bill_summary: Requires political parties and unaffiliated presidential candidates to submit elector nominees and alternate elector nominees with executed voting pledges. Designates the State Administrator of Elections to preside and serve as secretary at the presidential electors meeting. Establishes vacancy replacement procedures using alternate presidential electors or appointments by remaining electors. Prohibits the State Administrator from accepting ballots marked in violation of an elector's pledge. Vacates the office of any elector who refuses to vote or votes contrary to their pledge. Directs the State Administrator and Governor to prepare and transmit amended certificates of ascertainment if electors change.
responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections; State Board of Elections; Governor
stakeholders: presidential electors, alternate presidential elector nominees, political parties in Maryland, and unaffiliated presidential candidates
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the bill can be implemented with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns substantial administrative and oversight duties to the State Board and the State Administrator of Elections, including receiving presidential elector nominations and pledges, presiding over the electors' meeting, verifying ballots, administering substitute elector appointments, and preparing certificates of vote.

The bill mandates specific certification requirements for the Governor when submitting the State's certificate of ascertainment under federal law and requires the Governor to sign and deliver an amended certificate of ascertainment if substitute electors are appointed.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to file a petition for expungement of a disposition under a certain provision of law if the disposition was included in a case that was disposed of by the court with a no finding designation or designated by the court as having been terminated without finding.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Expungement - No Finding and Case Terminated Without Finding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes a person to file an expungement petition for specified criminal offenses under certain disposition conditions. Applies when a remaining charge was disposed of by a court with a no finding designation. Applies also when a remaining charge was included in a case designated as terminated without finding. Covers listed misdemeanors, listed felonies, and attempts, conspiracies, or solicitations of those offenses. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Individuals seeking expungement of criminal records for cases with charges disposed of with a no finding designation or terminated without finding
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $11,740 in FY 2027 only for the Judiciary to update expungement-related brochures, forms, and instructional videos. The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary by expanding eligibility for petitions for expungement under Criminal Procedure § 10-110, requiring revisions to court forms, brochures, and instructional videos, as well as operational adjustments in court case management systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS), which serves as the central repository for criminal records and is responsible for processing and complying with court-ordered expungements.
As the primary state law enforcement agency and a keeper of police records, MSP must comply with court orders to expunge police records covered under the expanded expungement criteria.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a merchant, in a certain transaction between the hours of 6 a.m. and 10 p.m., from prohibiting a person from making a cash payment to purchase an essential consumer good, requiring a person to purchase an essential consumer good by using a credit or debit card, or charging or collecting from a person a higher price than for an equivalent cashless transaction for making a cash payment for the purchase of an essential consumer good; establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice; etc.
Title: Consumer Protection - Retail Transactions for Essential Consumer Goods - Cash Payments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits merchants from refusing cash payments for in-person purchases of essential consumer goods totaling less than $300. Applies to sales between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., banning surcharges on cash transactions and mandatory card use. Defines essential goods to include food, water and beverages, personal hygiene items, health products, and fuel. Exempts remote transactions, vending machines, on-premises food consumption, specialty gourmet shops, and membership fuel sales. Authorizes merchants to refuse denominations over $20 or offer fee-free prepaid card conversion machines on site. Establishes civil fines up to $1,000 enforced by the Consumer Protection Division after two compliance warnings.
responsible_party: Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Retail merchants selling essential consumer goods to the public, consumers purchasing essential goods with cash, and retail establishments operating in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General can enforce the provisions using existing resources, and civil penalty revenues are not expected to be material.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General to enforce the new cash acceptance requirements, mandate compliance opportunities, and assess civil penalties for violations under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

Synopsis: Requiring a unit of State government to provide a certain debriefing of a contract award to certain persons on request; adding an exemption to the prohibition on an individual who assists in the drafting of specifications, an invitation for bids, or a request for proposals from submitting a bid or proposal or assisting in the submission of a bid or proposal; requiring a procurement contract to include a certain clause pertaining to certain contract modifications related to changes in State law; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Transparency and Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Requires State procurement officers to debrief unsuccessful offerors upon request before contract awards receive final approval. Mandates contract clauses authorizing contractor requests for equitable adjustments caused by changes in State law. Exempts individuals who provide information from solicitation drafting conflict-of-interest prohibitions if no unfair competitive advantage occurs. Extends dispute and claim resolution procedures beyond construction contracts to all State procurement contracts. Lengthens the deadline for contractors to file written notices of contract claims to 60 days. Requires contractors to certify claim accuracy and good faith before receiving payment on a contract claim.
responsible_party: Office of State Procurement; State procurement units
stakeholders: State procurement contractors, subcontractors, bidders, and offerors
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may experience indeterminate increases from potential contract award delays and bid protests, but implementation can be handled with existing agency resources and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of State Procurement, which is housed within the Department of General Services as the state's central procurement authority, with establishing statewide guidelines and procedures for procurement debriefings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the procedures, timelines, default denial determinations, and appeal mechanisms for bid protests and contract claims appealed to the Board.
The bill explicitly mandates that procurement officers seek the advice of the Office of the Attorney General on any legal issues raised in timely bid protests and contract claims.

As the state's highest procurement review body, the Board of Public Works is directly referenced regarding the requirement that debriefings for unsuccessful offerors occur before contract awards are presented to the Board for approval.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to develop, publish, and maintain a real property flood risk disclosure statement form that includes certain information about a property's flood risk and history; and requiring, beginning July, 1, 2027, a vendor of certain residential real property to provide the purchaser with a completed real property flood risk disclosure statement form before entering into a contract for the sale of the property.
Title: Sale of Residential Real Property - Required Flood Risk Disclosure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment to publish a real property flood risk disclosure form by June 1, 2027. Applies to residential real property improved by four or fewer single-family units, subject to specified exemptions. Requires vendors, beginning July 1, 2027, to provide purchasers a completed form before entering into a contract of sale. Requires vendors to provide a copy of any available FEMA elevation certificate for the property. Mandates disclosures on flood hazard zones, insurance, federal disaster aid, and past property flood damage.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Buyers and sellers of residential real property improved by four or fewer single-family units
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled by the Maryland Department of the Environment using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of the Environment to develop, publish, and maintain the real property flood risk disclosure statement form required for residential property sales by June 1, 2027.

The Department of Labor regulates and licenses real estate brokers, salespersons, and industry professionals through the Maryland Real Estate Commission, who must incorporate the new disclosure requirement into residential real estate transaction practices.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees consumer protection in real estate transactions and may handle enforcement or inquiries regarding deceptive practices or failure to provide mandatory property disclosures.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial system, which may hear civil disputes and litigation arising from real estate contract disputes or noncompliance with statutory disclosure mandates.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Baltimore County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on certain real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Baltimore County – Property Tax Credit – Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Baltimore County to grant a property tax credit against county property taxes. Covers real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 located at 730 Wampler Road. Requires the property tax credit to equal 100% of the property tax imposed on the property. Takes effect June 1, 2026. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Baltimore County
stakeholders: Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 and Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore County property tax revenues may decrease by approximately $9,600 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 if the credit is granted. County expenditures and State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes an optional local property tax credit on a specific parcel in Baltimore County. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is responsible for hearing appeals concerning real property valuations, exemptions, and property tax credits, giving it low administrative relevance in the event of an eligibility or application dispute.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including appeals arising from local taxing authority decisions and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding property taxes and credits.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting, or obtaining an individual for the purpose of appropriating the government benefits of an individual for the benefit of the person or another through deception, coercion, exploitation, or isolation; prohibiting a person from aiding, abetting, or conspiring with one or more persons to violate a certain provision of the Act; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Benefits Exploitation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: Prohibits knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting, or obtaining an individual through deception, coercion, exploitation, or isolation to appropriate government benefits. Prohibits knowingly benefiting from or aiding, abetting, or conspiring in benefits exploitation ventures. Establishes graduated penalties ranging from a misdemeanor to felonies based on aggregate benefit values. Subjects offenses involving $100,000 or more to imprisonment up to 20 years and fines up to $25,000. Treats each violation as a separate offense that may run concurrently or consecutively with related sentences.
responsible_party: Judiciary
stakeholders: Recipients of government assistance programs, elderly or disabled adults, and individuals accused of benefits exploitation
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,600 in FY 2027 only for one-time computer programming by the Judiciary. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal offenses and graduated penalties for benefits exploitation, requiring the Judiciary to implement one-time computer programming changes in FY 2027 costing approximately $1,600 and adjudicate new cases.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor and felony offenses, which will generate additional caseloads for the Office of the Public Defender to provide legal representation to indigent defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes prison terms ranging from up to 1 year for misdemeanors to up to 20 years for felonies, which impacts correctional facility operations and community supervision under DPSCS.

The Office of the Attorney General houses specialized units, such as the Senior and Vulnerable Adult Asset Recovery Unit and Medicaid Fraud Division, tasked with addressing the financial exploitation of vulnerable individuals and benefit fraud.

The bill specifically protects government assistance programs administered by DHS, including TANF, SNAP, TDAP, and Public Assistance to Adults (PAA), and aligns with DHS's role in protecting vulnerable adults and low-income individuals from economic abuse.

The bill defines government benefits to include Medicaid, which is administered by MDH, and addresses coercion involving the denial of medical care or improper provision of controlled dangerous substances.

The bill addresses coercion and financial control exerted over elderly adults, directly touching on the Department of Aging's mission to protect the rights, safety, and well-being of older Marylanders from exploitation.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating criminal violations, including trafficking-like recruitment, harboring, and exploitation of individuals for benefit theft.

Synopsis: Altering the date, from November 30 to October 1 each year, by which the Office of the Attorney General must report on certain activities of the Office's Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit and certain activities taken by the Department of the Environment and the Department of Natural Resources in response to findings of the Unit.
Title: Office of the Attorney General - Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit - Reporting Requirement

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the annual reporting deadline for the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit from November 30 to October 1. Requires the Attorney General to submit the report annually to the Governor and the General Assembly. Specifies that the report must cover the activities of the Unit during the previous fiscal year. Requires reporting on actions taken by the Department of the Environment or the Department of Natural Resources.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Maryland Department of the Environment, and Department of Natural Resources
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. The bill has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the annual reporting date and reporting period for the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit, which operates within the Office of the Attorney General.

The required annual report documents actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to findings and recommendations of the Unit, and the date change aligns with MDE's enforcement reporting timeline.
The annual report explicitly includes actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to the Unit's findings and recommendations.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the annual report submitted by the Attorney General.

Synopsis: Authorizing the installation of individual water submeters, used to determine the actual use of water, for each residential unit in an apartment house and mobile home parks; prohibiting the owner, operator, or manager of an apartment house, or mobile home park, or a contractor hired by the owner, operator, or manager, from imposing certain costs on a unit; authorizing the owner, operator, or manager of an apartment house or mobile home park to bill an occupant a certain amount under certain circumstances; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes owners, operators, managers, contractors, and local housing authorities to install individual water submeters in apartment houses and mobile home parks. Prohibits charging units more than actual water provider charges, allocated in proportion to actual usage. Restricts charges for common area usage, leaks, poor maintenance, and nonresidential areas, while permitting a one-dollar monthly administrative fee. Requires owners to maintain adequate records and permits estimated billing if a submeter fails. Prohibits billing occupants after two consecutive billing cycles if an inaccurate submeter remains unreplaced or unrepaired. Requires landlords mandating third-party water payments to use written leases and provide advance bill notices.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of Housing and Community Development; Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division); Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Owners, operators, managers, and contractors of apartment houses and mobile home parks; residential tenants and occupants; local housing authorities; water service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State agency operations and requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory agency tasked with adopting standards and regulations for the accuracy, testing, and recordkeeping of individual water submeters in consultation with DHCD.
DHCD is required to consult with MDE on the development of regulations and standards for water submeters, and must approve the installation of submeters by local housing authorities.

The Consumer Protection Division within the OAG is authorized to handle consumer complaints against apartment and mobile home park owners/operators regarding water submeter billing when local enforcement bodies are unavailable.
The Board of Public Works (or equivalent local authority) must approve the installation of individual submeters by local housing authorities.
The bill creates private causes of action for occupants and specifies that unpaid water bills under submetering may not be treated as unpaid rent in court eviction proceedings.

Synopsis: Continuing the Maryland Horse Industry Board in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2036, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: Maryland Horse Industry Board - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland Horse Industry Board by 10 years to July 1, 2036. Continues the board's statutory and regulatory authority under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the licensing and inspection of horse stables throughout the State. Preserves the Maryland Horse Industry Fund to support equine research, education, and promotion. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Horse Industry Board; Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Licensed horse stable operators, commercial equine feed purchasers and distributors, and the Maryland equine industry
fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the board from FY 2027 through FY 2036. The FY 2027 budget includes $435,471 in special funds and $12,298 in federal funds for board operations. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Horse Industry Board (MHIB) is housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. The bill directly extends the board's statutory authority, operations, licensing functions, and associated special funds through July 1, 2036.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Horse Industry Board is a statutory state regulatory and advisory board whose operational termination date is extended by 10 years under this legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Disabilities to establish affordable and accessible housing programs; authorizing the Department to establish one or more affiliated foundations to work with certain programs and units of the Department to solicit and accept funds, partner with individuals and entities, and promote certain activities that support certain projects; prohibiting an affiliated foundation from influencing determinations regarding eligibility for any program, benefit, or services administered by the Department; etc.
Title: Department of Disabilities - Housing Programs and Affiliated Foundations - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Disabilities to oversee and administer affordable and accessible housing programs. Authorizes the department to establish one or more affiliated foundations to support specified departmental programs and units. Prohibits an affiliated foundation from making or influencing policy decisions, program standards, or eligibility determinations. Permits department officials and employees to serve without compensation as directors or officials of an affiliated foundation. Requires the department to hire an independent certified public accountant annually to audit each affiliated foundation. Requires the Secretary of Disabilities to deposit contributions from an affiliated foundation into a separate special fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities; Office of the Attorney General; State Ethics Commission
stakeholders: individuals with disabilities, Maryland Department of Disabilities personnel, affiliated foundations, and private or public donors
fiscal_impact_summary: Department of Disabilities special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount from foundation contributions. State general fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate, minimal amount for required annual independent audits if costs cannot be absorbed with existing resources. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOD is the primary subject and implementing agency of the bill, which requires the department to administer affordable and accessible housing programs and authorizes it to establish and oversee affiliated foundations.

The bill explicitly tasks the State Ethics Commission with reviewing and approving foundation operating policies regarding conflicts of interest, evaluating notices of MDOD employees serving on foundation boards, and receiving annual implementation reports.
The bill requires the Office of the Attorney General to review and approve the operating policies developed by MDOD for form and legal sufficiency.
The bill requires MDOD to submit an annual report to the Governor by September 1 detailing the personnel serving in affiliated foundations and the implementation of operational policies.

Synopsis: Expanding the authority of the Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service to delegate certain functions to the Deputy Treasurer of the Service; increasing the threshold amount from $25,000 to $50,000 or less for estimated contract costs under which the Service may use the small procurement process; and altering the process for providing notice of the establishment or adjustment of certain rates charged for Service projects, products, or services.
Title: Maryland Environmental Service - Authorizations and Requirements - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Expands the authority of the Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service to delegate financial functions to the Deputy Treasurer. Increases the maximum expenditure threshold for small procurements by the Service from $25,000 to $50,000. Requires the Service to notify service district residents at least 60 days before establishing or adjusting district charges. Alters newspaper notice formatting for proposed charges and requires placement with legal notices. Requires the Service to provide supplemental notice via website posting, electronic messaging, or mail. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Service
stakeholders: Maryland Environmental Service contractors and vendors, and residents, property owners, and ratepayers in Maryland Environmental Service service districts
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on Maryland Environmental Service finances, though the Service may experience administrative efficiencies from procuring more goods and services under small procurement procedures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 227 is a departmental bill specifically governing the Maryland Environmental Service (MES). It expands the financial functions the MES Treasurer may delegate to the Deputy Treasurer, raises MES's small procurement expenditure threshold from $25,000 to $50,000, and updates public notice requirements for rate changes in MES service districts.

The bill references the State Treasurer's role in determining the type and coverage amount of the surety bond or insurance policy required for the Deputy Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from slaughtering or causing the slaughter of a racehorse in the State for certain commercial purposes; prohibiting a person from purchasing, selling, transferring, offering for sale, importing into the State, or transporting a racehorse if the person knows or reasonably should know that the racehorse will be slaughtered for certain commercial purposes; requiring certain fines collected by the State Racing Commission to be distributed to the racing Special Fund; etc.
Title: Horse Racing - Prohibited Acts - Slaughter of Racehorses for Commercial Purposes

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Prohibits slaughtering or causing the slaughter of a racehorse in the State for any commercial purpose. Bans purchasing, selling, transferring, offering for sale, importing, or transporting racehorses known to face commercial slaughter. Establishes misdemeanor criminal penalties and fines up to $5,000 for individual and entity violations. Authorizes the State Racing Commission and State Department of Agriculture to suspend or revoke violators' licenses. Distributes all fine revenue collected under the Act to the racing Special Fund. Permits humane euthanasia performed by a licensed veterinarian for reasons unrelated to commercial purposes.
responsible_party: State Racing Commission; State Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Racehorse owners, breeders, trainers, equine dealers, commercial transporters, and State Racing Commission licensees
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 from fines collected from violators, but the exact amount cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Labor. Its unit, the Maryland Racing Commission, is tasked with adopting implementing regulations (in consultation with the Department of Agriculture), authorized to suspend or revoke licenses for violations, and directs collected fine revenue into the horse racing Special Fund.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Maryland Department of Agriculture to revoke or suspend licenses it has issued upon finding a violation, and requires the Maryland Racing Commission to consult with the department when adopting implementing regulations.

Synopsis: Increasing, from $4,000,000,000 to $5,000,000,000, the limit on the amount of certain revenue bonds that the Maryland Transportation Authority may have outstanding and unpaid on June 30 each year; etc.
Title: Maryland Transportation Authority - Revenue Bond Limit - Increase

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Public Debt -see also- County & Balt City Bonds; State Bonds
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Increases the maximum allowable outstanding principal balance of Maryland Transportation Authority revenue bonds from $4.0 billion to $5.0 billion. Applies this debt limit to revenue bonds secured by toll revenue as of June 30 each year. Requires the maximum aggregate amount to be reduced by certain federal transportation loans or drawn credit lines. Authorizes the Authority to issue bonds to refinance prior transportation facility projects without General Assembly approval. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
stakeholders: Motorists and commercial drivers using Maryland toll facilities, bondholders, and transportation construction contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: MDTA nonbudgeted revenues increase significantly, potentially beginning in fiscal 2029, from proceeds of additional bond issuances. Nonbudgeted expenditures increase correspondingly to pay related debt service. Local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly increases the Maryland Transportation Authority's statutory cap on outstanding toll revenue-backed debt from $4.0 billion to $5.0 billion to finance capital projects and bridge reconstruction.
MDOT is the parent department of MDTA that requested this departmental legislation and coordinates overall state transportation capital programming and federal reimbursement tracking.
The State Treasurer acts as Maryland's chief financial officer overseeing state debt and bond activity, and served as an information source for the fiscal evaluation of this debt capacity increase.
DBM oversees statewide fiscal planning and capital budget evaluations, and was consulted as an information source regarding the fiscal impacts of adjusting authority debt limits.

Synopsis: Delaying the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program until the 2029-2030 financial aid award year.

bill_summary: Delays the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program until the 2029–2030 financial aid award year. Maintains central award notification and issuance by the Office of Student Financial Assistance through fiscal 2029. Postpones requirements for institutions of higher education to determine and offer grant awards using certified need rankings. Defers mandatory institutional reporting of award recipients and subsequent State reimbursements until the 2029–2030 award year. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance
stakeholders: Applicants for and recipients of Guaranteed Access Grants, Maryland public four-year institutions, locally funded community colleges, and participating nonpublic institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: Delays State and local higher education administrative expenditures associated with institutional grant processing until fiscal 2029. Any potential general fund appropriations intended to offset institutional costs are likewise postponed. Specific cost figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC requested this departmental legislation and oversees the Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA), which administers the Guaranteed Access Grant Program. The bill directly delays the transfer of grant notification and awarding responsibilities from MHEC to higher education institutions until the 2029–2030 award year.

This departmental bill directly impacts the commission's operational timeline and administrative responsibilities by delaying the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program until the 2029–2030 financial aid award year.

USM constituent institutions are directly impacted by the delayed transfer of administrative responsibilities, operational costs, and corresponding state revenues associated with notifying applicants and issuing Guaranteed Access Grant awards until FY 2029.

As an independent public institution of higher education, MSU's financial aid office is impacted by the postponement of responsibilities and funding related to the decentralization of Guaranteed Access Grant notifications and awards.

As a public four-year higher education institution, the college's financial aid operations and associated administrative costs are affected by the delayed transition of Guaranteed Access Grant responsibilities.

bill_summary: Expands tuition assistance provided by the Maryland Military Department for eligible active Maryland National Guard members. Authorizes assistance covering up to 100% of training assistance expenses directly related to required professional development resources. Adds private postsecondary vocational-technical, trade, or career schools recognized by designated State education and apprenticeship bodies. Repeals the requirement that private postsecondary vocational-technical schools provide a tuition waiver of at least 50%. Requires members who receive assistance for career courses to remain active for at least 2 years after completion.
responsible_party: Maryland Military Department
stakeholders: Active members of the Maryland National Guard and private postsecondary vocational-technical, trade, and career schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. Assistance is authorized only to the extent funds are provided in the State budget, which included $600,000 annually in fiscal 2025 through 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is the primary official responsible for certifying the eligibility of National Guard service members to receive tuition and training assistance and enforcing subsequent active service commitments.

Active members of the Maryland National Guard are the direct beneficiaries of the expanded tuition and training assistance for trade and career courses, and are subject to the associated mandatory service obligations.

The bill expands eligible institutions to include private postsecondary trade or career schools recognized and approved by MHEC, without requiring private schools to offer a minimum 50% tuition waiver.

The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC) and oversees workforce development programs; schools and training recognized by MATC are newly incorporated into the tuition and training assistance program.

Removes an exception that reduced an employee's pay step upon promotion based on another employee's service time. Entitles promoted police employees and deputy State fire marshals to their prior pay step in the new rank without exception. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: police employees and deputy State fire marshals in the Department of State Police
fiscal_impact_summary: No current State fiscal impact because the Department of State Police has not used the pay restriction on prior promotions. Future promotional costs are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing agency resources. No effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the promotional pay rates and step placements for police employees and deputy State fire marshals within the Department of State Police, and was introduced as a departmental request by the agency.
As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM reviews and approves State Police pay plans and oversees state compensation and personnel classifications.

fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected because the Department of Housing and Community Development can handle administrative changes with existing resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

Requires documentary evidence of negative test results for HIV antibodies, hepatitis B virus antigen, and hepatitis C antibodies. bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Maryland Heritage Area Authority and increases its quorum from nine to ten voting members. Adds the Secretary of Agriculture and the State Superintendent of Schools to the Authority. Replaces a Maryland Greenways Commission appointee with an expert in natural resource stewardship or climate resiliency. Authorizes the Authority to establish terms, conditions, and matching fund proportions for grants and loans. Repeals statutory 50% matching fund caps on grants for management plans, acquisition, development, and programming. Repeals requirements to send boundary maps to county clerks and to submit interagency program statements.
responsible_party: Maryland Heritage Area Authority; Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Local jurisdictions, heritage area management entities, and applicants for Maryland Heritage Areas Program grants and loans
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Overall funding under the Maryland Heritage Areas Program remains unchanged, though local jurisdictions may experience greater access to grants and loans due to the Authority's discretion to adjust matching fund requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA) is an independent unit within the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) and is staffed by the Maryland Historical Trust. MDP requested this departmental legislation to update the authority's membership, grant-making flexibility, and statutory requirements.

The bill adds the Secretary of Agriculture as a voting member of the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority and establishes a statutory responsibility for the Secretary to support and assist activities regarding agricultural resources within certified heritage areas.

The bill adds the State Superintendent of Schools as a voting member of the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority and assigns the Superintendent responsibilities regarding educational resources and their interpretation within certified heritage areas.

The Secretary of Commerce is a voting member of the Authority, and the bill modifies the statutory requirement for the Secretary regarding supporting tourism, economic development, and job creation in certified heritage areas.

The Secretary of Natural Resources is a voting member of the Authority and provides support for outdoor recreation and natural resources. The bill also alters an appointed seat previously tied to the Maryland Greenways Commission.
The Secretary of Transportation is a voting member of the Authority, and the bill updates requirements regarding transportation access, scenic byways, and signage within certified heritage areas.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development serves as a voting member of the Authority with statutory responsibilities regarding housing and neighborhood revitalization in certified heritage areas.
The Secretary of Higher Education serves as a voting member of the Authority and carries duties related to educational resources and their interpretation.
The Secretary of General Services has statutory duties under the bill to support and assist certified heritage area activities regarding the management and disposition of State property.
The Governor appoints ten public and local government members to the Authority with the advice and consent of the Senate, and the bill alters the qualifications for one of the appointed seats.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for appointed boards and commissions, including the modified public appointment for a member with expertise in natural resource stewardship or climate resiliency.

Requires the Department to provide guidance materials within 60 days after receiving notification. Specifies that guidance materials must address State laws, best practices, and resources supporting plan review or amendment. Directs the Department to develop and maintain guidance materials in consultation with other State agencies and offices. Replaces statutory references to "visions" with "planning principles" in local comprehensive planning and reporting laws.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: local planning commissions, county governments, and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Planning can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 240 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP). The bill requires local planning commissions to notify MDP when initiating a 10-year review of their comprehensive plans, mandates that MDP provide guidance materials to local jurisdictions within 60 days of notification, and directs MDP to develop and maintain these guidance materials in consultation with other state entities.

stakeholders: Licensed barbers, cosmetologists, professional land surveyors, real estate appraisers, appraisal management companies, home inspectors, and individual tax preparers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures are maintained through fiscal 2032 for the affected boards and commission. The Maryland Department of Labor and the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee can handle the reporting requirement with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 241 directly extends the statutory termination dates for five professional licensing boards and commissions operating within the Maryland Department of Labor and requires the Department to submit evaluation reports to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2030.

Defines confidential unemployment insurance information and establishes standards for safeguarding disclosed records. responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor

fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental bill from the Maryland Department of Labor that directly governs its administration of the Unemployment Insurance program, updates confidentiality standards for UI information to conform to federal law, and establishes disclosure protocols and penalties for departmental employees and third-party recipients.

The Department of Human Services administers Maryland's child support enforcement program. The bill directly alters and establishes data safeguarding and redisclosure requirements governing how child support enforcement units and their agents access and use confidential unemployment insurance information to enforce child support obligations.

bill_summary: Reorganizes and modifies the required elements of comprehensive and general plans across Maryland local jurisdictions. Establishes eight standardized plan elements: land, transportation, housing, economy, equity, resilience, place, and ecology. Incorporates prior standalone elements like water resources, sensitive areas, and municipal growth as required subelements. Directs the Maryland Department of Planning and other State agencies to provide local jurisdictions with data and technical assistance. Applies prospectively to local jurisdictions initiating plan amendments, revisions, or readoptions on or after October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of Commerce; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Charter counties, code counties, commission counties, and municipal corporations; local planning commissions; commercial watermen; property owners and developers; residents of overburdened and underserved communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies can implement the data, technical assistance, and review requirements using existing resources with no effect on state revenues. Local government expenditures may increase for certain jurisdictions that rely on contractual services or supplemental staff to conduct comprehensive plan reviews.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the requesting agency for this departmental legislation, MDP is the primary state entity tasked with implementing the bill. MDP must develop guidelines and best practices, coordinate state agency data and analysis, provide demographic and land use data, and provide technical assistance to local jurisdictions across the comprehensive plan elements.

MDE is directly assigned statutory duties to provide environmental justice data for the equity element, review mineral resources and sensitive areas subelements for consistency with department goals, and provide data, technical assistance, and plan reviews for the water resources subelement.

DNR is statutorily required to supply a statewide forest resource inventory every five years, coordinate with MDP and SHA on wildlife crossings and habitat connectivity, and review local jurisdictions' sensitive areas subelements.

MDOT is statutorily mandated to provide charter counties and local jurisdictions with the best available state-level transportation data and facilitate relevant data sharing from other state and federal agencies to inform the required transportation elements.

DHCD is required to provide local jurisdictions with the best available state-level housing data and collaborate with MDP to provide technical assistance regarding housing elements and fair housing assessments.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of Commerce to supply local jurisdictions with the best available state-level economic development data to inform the newly established economy element.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to provide local jurisdictions with the best available state-level labor force data to inform the newly established economy element.
SHA is specifically named in statute to coordinate with MDP and DNR to supply local jurisdictions with updated data on habitat connectivity concerns and planned wildlife crossings.

The bill requires local resilience elements to align with and be informed by the State Resilience Strategy and the State of Maryland Hazard Mitigation Plan, core plans overseen and administered by MDEM.

The bill incorporates optional priority preservation area subelements under the Land element referencing § 2-518 of the Agriculture Article and addresses prime agricultural land preservation policies.

The municipal growth subelement requires local jurisdictions to plan for public school capacity consistent with State rated capacity standards established by the Interagency Commission on School Construction.

bill_summary: Establishes liability for video tolls on the registered owner of a Class G (trailer) vehicle. Applies this liability when the registered owner of the towing motor vehicle cannot be determined. Extends video toll notice, citation, civil penalty, and collection procedures to Class G trailer owners. Authorizes trailer owners to transfer liability under specified circumstances, including vehicle theft or documented third-party towing. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to refuse or suspend vehicle registrations for unpaid toll violations.
responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority; Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Registered owners of Class G (trailer) vehicles, operators of motor vehicles towing trailers, and toll facility users
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues for the Maryland Transportation Authority increase significantly beginning in fiscal 2027, potentially by millions of dollars annually, from additional video toll and civil penalty collections. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Central Collection Unit and general fund revenues also increase to the extent delinquent accounts are referred for collection.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDTA is the primary implementing agency of the bill. It assesses video tolls and civil penalties, issues notices of toll due and citations, handles transfers of liability, and refers delinquent accounts to the Central Collection Unit, resulting in a significant increase in nonbudgeted toll revenues.

MVA is responsible for vehicle and trailer registrations and must provide registration and address records to MDTA, as well as enforce registration suspensions or refusals for delinquent Class G vehicle toll violators.
MDOT requested this departmental legislation and serves as the parent agency overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and coordinating transportation facilities and financing alongside MDTA.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), an operational unit within DBM, receives delinquent toll violation accounts referred by MDTA for collection, which impacts CCU special fund revenues, operating expenditures, and general fund fee reversions.
AOC supports the District Court, which has jurisdiction over individuals electing to stand trial to contest video toll citations and civil penalties.

bill_summary: Alters standards and requirements for granting variances under the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program. Prohibits local jurisdictions from accepting variance applications to authorize unallowed uses or adjust required mitigation. Establishes a rebuttable presumption that existing accessory structures demonstrate reasonable and significant use, excluding accessory dwelling units. Requires applicants to demonstrate substantial need and prove development cannot be located outside a habitat protection area. Requires local boards of appeals to hear variance appeals on the record and defer to administrative factual findings.
responsible_party: Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays
stakeholders: Property owners and developers seeking variances in the Critical Area, as well as local boards of appeals
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances and no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 247 is a departmental bill submitted on behalf of the Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays, which is housed within the Department of Natural Resources. The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to alter standards and requirements for local critical area land use variances overseen by the Commission.

bill_summary: Repeals the statutory requirement that photographs on identification cards, driver's licenses, and moped operator's permits be in color. fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures decrease by approximately $114,000 in FY 2027 and by $152,000 annually thereafter due to reduced printing and cartridge costs. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the direct implementing agency responsible for issuing driver's licenses, identification cards, and moped operator's permits. The bill eliminates the statutory requirement for color photographs on these credentials, reducing MVA's annual printing and materials expenditures by approximately $152,000.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and requested this departmental legislation. The bill results in an expenditure reduction for MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment to impose administrative penalties for violations concerning water appropriation, use, and dam safety. Caps administrative penalties at $5,000 per violation and $100,000 in total. Requires the department to provide written notice and offer an informal settlement meeting before seeking penalty recovery. Expands the department's authority to issue corrective orders and notices across all subtitle provisions. Directs collected administrative penalties to the Maryland Clean Water Fund or the Private Dam Repair Fund. fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Clean Water Fund and Private Dam Repair Fund increase by at least $50,000 in FY 2027 from new penalty collections. Special fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2027 with a matching $250,000 decrease in general fund expenditures to satisfy contingent budget provisions. Local governments and regulated entities experience no material fiscal impact assuming compliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill directly granting the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) expanded enforcement authority, including the ability to issue orders and impose administrative penalties up to $5,000 per violation for water appropriation, use, and dam safety violations, with funds deposited into the Maryland Clean Water Fund and the Private Dam Repair Fund.

The bill standardizes administrative notice and hearing procedures under the Administrative Procedure Act for orders and penalties related to water use and dam safety, potentially involving administrative law judges to adjudicate contested cases.

Circuit courts may receive petitions from the Department of the Environment to compel obedience to subpoenas or enforce contempt orders, and clerks of the circuit court are responsible for recording liens on real property for unpaid penalties.

DBM oversees the state budget and special funds. The bill restricts General Fund appropriations to the new grant fund in FY 2027 and may impact future PAYGO general fund expenditures and state budget planning.

bill_summary: Limits personal information collected, processed, and retained by State government units to the minimum necessary for legitimate purposes. Expands the statutory definition of personal information to include email account credentials, health data, and sensitive demographic data.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; units of State government; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Maryland residents; State government agencies and employees; third-party government contractors handling State data or information technology systems
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may increase for certain agencies needing additional personnel to fulfill compliance requirements, though most agencies are expected to implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency and departmental sponsor of the bill. It is responsible for adopting regulations, guidelines, model templates, and standard privacy and security contract requirements for all third-party state IT contracts.

State units maintaining personal records must submit annual reports to the Secretary of General Services, and DGS is explicitly tasked with adopting regulations to govern the form and method of this reporting.

The bill mandates that designated agency Privacy Officers across state government coordinate directly with the Office of the Attorney General to oversee compliance with data privacy and protection requirements.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is granted explicit statutory authority to adopt regulations exempting certain personal records based on recommendations from the Secretary of Information Technology, and DBM advises on statewide personnel and fiscal impacts.

The fiscal note specifically highlights that the Comptroller's Office anticipates an increased workload requiring additional staffing to implement the statutory data privacy and protection mandates, as it was previously exempt from the Governor's data privacy executive order.

MDOT is explicitly noted in the fiscal note as anticipating operational impacts and an increased workload that may exceed existing staff capacity to comply with the bill's data collection, retention, and privacy requirements.

The Department of Disabilities is specifically cited in the fiscal note as projecting an increased workload requiring additional staff resources to meet the new privacy officer, notice, and data handling requirements.
The legislation codifies and expands upon standards originally enacted by the Executive Department under Executive Order 01.01.2021.10 establishing the State Chief Privacy Officer.
The bill explicitly references public records accepted by the State Archivist for deposit in the Maryland Hall of Records as an exempt category from certain personal record requirements.
