fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate minimal increase in Maryland Department of Health general fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2027 from license fees capped at $100. Local health departments can absorb inspection and enforcement duties using existing budgeted resources, though regulatory costs may exceed license fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency responsible for setting the on-farm food service facility license fee, determining allowable foods, issuing licenses, and adopting regulations governing sanitation, toileting, food preparation, and public health requirements.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to consult with the Department of Agriculture when adopting regulations governing on-farm food service facilities, particularly regarding agricultural operations and structures.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health consult with the Department of the Environment to develop regulations concerning water access, wastewater management, and toileting facilities for on-farm food service facilities.

Synopsis: Altering the effective dates of enrollment in a Small Business Health Options (SHOP) Exchange plan for individuals who enroll during certain special enrollment periods.
Title: Health Insurance – Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Enrollment – Effective Dates

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Alters coverage effective dates for individuals enrolling in Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Exchange plans during specified special enrollment periods. Sets coverage to begin the first day of the month following receipt of plan selection for court-ordered dependents, if allowed and selected. Repeals provisions delaying effective dates to the second month for selections submitted after the fifteenth day. Establishes coverage effective dates on the first day of the month following plan selection for special enrollment periods involving death, divorce, or legal separation. Aligns Maryland health insurance statutory provisions with existing federal regulations.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Small employers, eligible employees, and dependents enrolled in Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Exchange plans
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies existing exchange operations that align with federal regulations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 273 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) to update and align the Maryland Insurance Article with federal regulations regarding SHOP special enrollment period effective dates.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange operates the Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Exchange in Maryland, directly administering the special enrollment periods and coverage effective dates modified by this bill.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists, in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law), by extending to July 1, 2032, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Extends the statutory and regulatory termination date for the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists by five years. Continues the board and its adopted regulations through July 1, 2032. Subjects the continuation to the evaluation and reestablishment provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the board's authority to license and discipline environmental health specialists. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: licensed environmental health specialists and applicants for licensure in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists through fiscal 2032. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This departmental bill extends the Board's statutory authority and termination date under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act through July 1, 2032, allowing the department to continue regulating and licensing environmental health specialists.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the termination date and statutory operating authority of the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists by five years to July 1, 2032.

Synopsis: Requiring a carrier that issues Medicare supplement policies to issue a Medicare supplement policy to an individual who meets certain criteria during certain special enrollment periods.
Title: Medicare Supplement Policies - Issuance - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: Requires carriers issuing Medicare supplement policies in the State to offer coverage under two new special enrollment periods. Mandates policy issuance to individuals losing Maryland Medical Assistance Program coverage who apply within 63 days. Applies to individuals enrolled in Medicare Part B for at least six months before Medicaid termination. Requires carriers to issue open policies to individuals eligible for Medicare before January 1, 2020. Eligible applicants must qualify under a federal special enrollment period and apply within 63 days.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Carriers issuing Medicare supplement policies in Maryland, individuals transitioning off the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, and Medicare beneficiaries eligible before January 1, 2020 who qualify for a federal special enrollment period
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational impact is minimal and absorbable within existing Maryland Insurance Administration budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulator of private health insurance carriers and Medicare supplement policies in Maryland and requested this departmental legislation. The agency will enforce carrier compliance with the new guaranteed issue special enrollment periods.

MDH administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill creates a special enrollment period for individuals disenrolling or terminating from Medicaid, requiring applicants to submit evidence of termination from the program.

Sponsors.Name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems

Synopsis: Altering the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program, including by establishing requirements regarding an automated external defibrillator (AED) coordinator, repealing certain provisions of law regarding regional council AED committees, and exempting certain law enforcement agencies from being required to obtain a certificate for an AED deployed in a patrol vehicle of the law enforcement agency; establishing certain certification qualifications for grocery stores and restaurants under the Program; etc.
Title: State Emergency Medical Services Board - Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program administered by the State Emergency Medical Services Board. Exempts law enforcement agencies from obtaining a certificate for an automated external defibrillator deployed in a patrol vehicle. Defines and establishes duties for automated external defibrillator coordinators designated by registered entities. Establishes specific certification qualifications for grocery stores and restaurants participating in the program. Repeals statutory provisions regarding regional councils and regional council automated external defibrillator committees.
responsible_party: State Emergency Medical Services Board; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
stakeholders: Entities registered in the Public Access AED Program, owners and operators of grocery stores and restaurants, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as the statutory changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS requested this departmental legislation and, alongside the State Emergency Medical Services Board, directly administers and oversees the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program governed by the bill.

The bill amends Section 21-330.3 of the Health - General Article regarding AED requirements for grocery stores and restaurants, which fall under the public health regulatory purview of the Department of Health.

The bill explicitly exempts law enforcement agencies from the requirement to obtain a certificate for an AED deployed in a patrol vehicle, directly affecting state and local police vehicle equipment protocols.

Synopsis: Altering the grounds on which the Maryland Insurance Commissioner may deny an applicant for registration as or refuse to renew, suspend, or revoke the registration of a third party administrator; and altering the violations for which the Commissioner may impose civil penalties against a third party administrator.
Title: Insurance – Third Party Administrators – Enforcement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Expands enforcement authority of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner over third party administrators. Authorizes the Commissioner to deny, suspend, revoke, or refuse registration for violations of state insurance laws. Authorizes registration actions when an applicant or registrant knowingly violates a Commissioner regulation or order. Authorizes civil penalties of up to $10,000 for each violation of the Insurance Article. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Third party administrators (TPAs), applicants for TPA registration, and plan sponsors, participants, and beneficiaries covered under plans administered by TPAs.
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State revenues or expenditures; the Maryland Insurance Administration can handle the enforcement requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration. It directly expands the enforcement and regulatory authority of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the administration over third-party administrators (TPAs), authorizing civil penalties and registration denials, revocations, or suspensions for violations of the Insurance Article or state insurance laws.

Synopsis: Requiring the Secretary of Aging to lead implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan which is a multisector plan on aging that transforms programs, services, policies, institutions, and systems to address the growing population of older adults in the State; requiring the Department to maintain a publicly accessible resource on the Department's website for monitoring implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan; and requiring the Department of Aging to staff the Commission on Aging.
Title: Human Services - Department of Aging and Commission on Aging (The Longevity Ready Maryland Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Secretary of Aging to lead implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan. Directs the Secretary to submit an updated comprehensive plan every four years beginning July 1, 2029. Mandates an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly on plan progress and activity center funding. Alters the membership, appointment process, and advisory duties of the Commission on Aging. Requires the Department of Aging to provide staff for the Commission.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Commission on Aging
stakeholders: older adults, family caregivers, area agencies on aging, and organizations advocating for older adults
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill generally codifies existing policies and procedures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Aging by requiring the Secretary of Aging to lead the implementation and reporting of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, updating the Secretary's powers and duties, and requiring the department to staff and support the restructured Commission on Aging.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the membership composition, meeting rules, attendance requirements, and advisory duties of the Commission on Aging in relation to the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan.

The bill modifies the gubernatorial appointment requirements for the Commission on Aging, establishing specific categories and qualifications for members that the Office of Appointments must vet and process.

The bill requires annual reporting and four-year comprehensive updates on the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan to be submitted to the Governor, and establishes appointments to the Commission on Aging to be made by the Governor.

Synopsis: Codifying in State law certain provisions of the Code of Federal Regulations related to mental health parity and clarifying the authority of the Maryland Insurance Administration to enforce certain laws; requiring health insurance carriers to collect and report on data in a certain manner; requiring health insurance carriers to provide certain benefits under certain circumstances; requiring health insurance carriers to explain differences in access to care under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Mental Health and Substance Use Disorders - Codification of Federal Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Codifies federal mental health parity standards into State health insurance law. Requires health insurance carriers to collect and evaluate data assessing how nonquantitative treatment limitations impact benefit access. Establishes that material differences in access serve as a strong indicator of noncompliance with parity requirements. Requires carriers to provide meaningful benefits and coverage for core treatments across all applicable benefit classifications. Requires carriers to submit comparative analyses and documentation of remedial actions upon request by the Commissioner. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to review compliance reports and issue administrative orders against noncompliant carriers.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers operating in Maryland and individuals receiving or seeking coverage for mental health and substance use disorders
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill and promulgate regulations using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) and directly strengthens MIA's authority to enforce mental health and substance use disorder parity requirements, review carrier comparative analyses and data reports, adopt regulations, and issue administrative orders or penalties.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note specifically evaluated the bill's requirements against state employee health plans and concluded there is no fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Altering provisions relating to criminal background investigations for certain individuals who care for or supervise children; requiring certain facilities to apply to the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository for a national and State criminal history records check for each employee, employer, individual, or volunteer; and altering provisions relating to the process under which a certain State or local law enforcement agency conducts a certain name-based check on certain individuals.
Title: Family Law - Child Care Providers - Criminal Background Investigations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Alters provisions governing criminal background investigations for individuals who care for or supervise children. Requires the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository to send State records to applicants and national records to authorized agencies. Mandates criminal history records checks for non-relative adults agreeing to provide care due to the sudden unavailability of a primary caretaker. Authorizes local departments to request national name-based checks by State or local law enforcement agencies for emergency out-of-home placements. Requires local departments to submit fingerprints within 15 calendar days after law enforcement conducts the name-based check.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Child care facilities, child care employees and volunteers, non-relative emergency caregivers, and children in out-of-home placements
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures likely increase minimally beginning as early as fiscal 2026 for background check fees and potential temporary foster care placements. Local expenditures may experience a minimal increase to process background checks. Revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS requested this departmental legislation. Its Criminal Justice Information System - Central Repository (CJIS-CR) is directly responsible for collecting fingerprints, processing fees, and conducting and disseminating State and national criminal history records checks (CHRC) in compliance with updated FBI standards.

DHS oversees child welfare, foster care, and local departments of social services. The bill alters requirements for background checks and emergency out-of-home placements (including safety plans involving non-relative caregivers), which carries direct operational and fiscal impacts for DHS when covering CHRC costs or placing children in foster care.

MSDE regulates and licenses child care centers, family child care homes, and informal child care subsidy providers, and receives criminal history record information from CJIS-CR for covered child care personnel and adult residents.

MDH licenses home health agencies and residential service agencies authorized to provide home- or community-based health services for minors, which are among the facilities required to obtain criminal history records checks under the bill.
DJS operates juvenile detention, correction, and treatment facilities, whose employees and employers are among the covered entities mandated to obtain criminal history records checks.
As the primary State law enforcement agency, MSP is authorized to conduct preliminary national name-based checks for emergency out-of-home child placements at the request of local departments.

Synopsis: Altering provisions relating to the reporting and investigation of abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and exploitation of vulnerable adults; and requiring the local department of aging to complete an investigation and make an indicated, not indicated, or undetermined finding within 60 days.
Title: Adult Protective Services – Modifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse; Dom. Viol.; Elder Abuse; etc
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Alters provisions governing the reporting and investigation of vulnerable adult abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and exploitation. Expands the definition of abuse to include psychological harm and sexual abuse by an individual in a relationship of trust. Authorizes mandated reporters to submit reports of suspected maltreatment through an online reporting portal. Requires local departments of social services to determine whether an alleged vulnerable adult is at risk of harm. Mandates that local departments complete investigations within 60 days and make an indicated, not indicated, or undetermined finding. Repeals the 10-day investigation completion deadline for cases involving an emergency.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services; local departments of social services
stakeholders: Vulnerable adults, individuals in relationships of trust with vulnerable adults, and mandated reporters including health practitioners, police officers, and human service workers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or expenditures, and it may help protect federal funding by ensuring compliance with federal Adult Protective Services standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 282 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services (DHS) to align Maryland's Adult Protective Services (APS) statutory definitions, reporting, and investigation standards with a federal 2024 rule, directly impacting DHS and local departments of social services.

The bill impacts the protection of vulnerable older adults, explicitly addresses long-term care ombudsman reporting requirements, and maintains statutory provisions allowing the Department of Aging to assist local departments in adult protective investigations.

State police officers are designated mandatory reporters of vulnerable adult abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and exploitation, and law enforcement agencies are statutorily called upon to assist local departments with adult protective investigations.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for operational impacts regarding vulnerable adult protective proceedings, guardianship reviews, and related judicial matters governed under the Family Law Article.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain licensed firearms dealer to notify the Secretary of State Police within 24 hours after the dealer first has knowledge that certain crimes have occurred or certain security features have been compromised; and providing that a person who violates the Act is subject to a civil penalty imposed by the Secretary of up to $250 for a first offense and up to $1000 for a second or subsequent violation.
Title: Public Safety - Licensed Firearms Dealers - Notification Regarding Compromising Events

NarrowSubjects.Name: Dealers -see also- Motor Vehicle Dealers and Salespeople

bill_summary: Requires a licensed firearms dealer to notify the Secretary of State Police within 24 hours of discovering specified compromising events. Applies when a burglary, attempted burglary, robbery, or theft involving a firearm or ammunition occurs at dealer premises. Applies when required security features fail, including video equipment, entry barriers, alarm monitoring, or physical breach barriers. Clarifies that this notification is in addition to any report made to local law enforcement or federal authorities. Establishes a civil penalty not exceeding $250 for a first violation and $1,000 for a second or subsequent violation. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: licensed firearms dealers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Civil penalty alterations are not anticipated to materially affect State revenues. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 284 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Police. It requires licensed firearms dealers to notify the Secretary of State Police within 24 hours of specific criminal events or security feature compromises, and authorizes the Secretary to impose updated civil penalties and enforce licensing compliance.

Synopsis: Requiring an individual to be a participant in the Ignition Interlock System Program as a condition of modification of a suspension or revocation of a license or issuance of a restricted license if the individual violated certain alcohol restrictions.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Ignition Interlock System Program - Required Participation

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Requires an individual to participate in the Ignition Interlock System Program to modify a license suspension or revocation. Applies this requirement to any driver who violates an alcohol restriction imposed under the Transportation Article. Mandates participation for individuals under age 21 who violate drug and alcohol impairment driving prohibitions. Directs the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue a restricted license to an otherwise eligible required participant. Requires the Administration to impose a one-year license suspension if a required participant fails to complete the program.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: drivers subject to license suspensions or revocations for alcohol restriction violations, including drivers age 21 and older
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations; hearing requests before the Office of Administrative Hearings are anticipated to decrease. No effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) establishes and administers the Ignition Interlock System Program (IISP) and driver's license suspensions, revocations, restrictions, and modifications. Under the bill, MVA directly implements the requirement that any individual who violates an alcohol restriction participate in the IISP as a condition of license modification or restricted license issuance.

The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and sponsored this departmental legislation to streamline participation in the Ignition Interlock System Program.

The bill allows individuals age 21 and older who violate alcohol restrictions to enroll directly in the Ignition Interlock System Program without appearing before an Administrative Law Judge, which is expected to decrease hearing requests before the Office of Administrative Hearings.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Superintendent of Schools to declare a prolonged state of emergency for an event that prevents regular, in-person attendance at a public school for at least 14 consecutive school days, subject to certain requirements; and requiring the State Board to adopt certain regulations including establishing minimum criteria for the adoption and implementation of virtual education plans by a county board during a prolonged state of emergency affecting the local school system.
Title: State Superintendent of Schools - Prolonged State of Emergency - Authority to Declare

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Superintendent of Schools to declare a prolonged state of emergency preventing in-person school attendance. Applies to emergencies lasting at least 14 consecutive school days due to disasters, health emergencies, or security threats. Requires the State Superintendent to consult the Governor and specified state agencies before issuing the written declaration. Authorizes a county board of education to transition affected public schools to virtual education under an approved plan. Allows the General Assembly, the State Board of Education, or the State Superintendent to terminate the emergency declaration.
responsible_party: State Superintendent of Schools; State Board of Education
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, teachers, county boards of education, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The State Superintendent of Schools and local school systems can implement the bill's provisions using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill directly concerns the State Superintendent of Schools and the State Board of Education, authorizing the State Superintendent to declare a prolonged state of emergency for public schools and oversee virtual education transitions.

The bill shifts the declaration authority for school-specific prolonged states of emergency from the Governor to the State Superintendent of Schools, while mandating that the State Superintendent consult with the Governor before making a declaration.

The bill identifies MDH as an agency the State Superintendent must consult if appropriate when declaring an emergency, and explicitly clarifies that the bill does not limit or interfere with the powers of the Secretary of Health during public health emergencies.

The bill explicitly lists the Maryland Department of Emergency Management as an entity the State Superintendent must consult, if appropriate, prior to issuing a declaration of a prolonged state of emergency.
The bill explicitly identifies the Department of State Police as an agency to be consulted by the State Superintendent if appropriate, particularly when emergencies involve specific security threats.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Central Collection Unit and the Child Support Administration to certify certain information about certain restitution, child support, and State debt obligors to a video lottery operator for purposes of enforcing a requirement to intercept certain prize payouts; requiring a video lottery operator to provide certain notice to a debtor that wins a prize to be paid by the operator and withhold all or part of the prize; authorizing certain debtors to appeal the proposed transfer; etc.
Title: Video Lottery Facility Payouts - Intercepts for Restitution Payments, Child Support Payments, and Debts Owed to the State

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery
Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments

bill_summary: Authorizes the Central Collection Unit to certify debts owed to the State to video lottery operators for prize interception. Requires video lottery operators to withhold prize payouts requiring federal form W-2G from certified debtors. Authorizes the Child Support Administration and Central Collection Unit to certify child support and restitution obligors directly to operators. Establishes an order of priority for honoring child support, restitution, and State debt interception requests. Allows debtors 15 days after notice to appeal a proposed prize transfer under the Administrative Procedure Act.
responsible_party: Central Collection Unit; Child Support Administration; State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: video lottery facility operators; individuals winning casino prizes who owe child support, court-ordered restitution, or State debts; recipients of child support and restitution payments; State agencies and community colleges collecting delinquent debts
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues increase annually across all funds by at least $3.0 million beginning in FY 2027 from intercepted casino prizes. Central Collection Fund special fund revenues increase by at least $510,000 annually from collection fees. Local community college revenues may increase from collections on delinquent debts referred to the Central Collection Unit. State expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly expands the authority of the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which is housed within DBM, authorizing it to certify debts and claims owed to the State to video lottery operators for prize interception. Furthermore, the Secretary of DBM may jointly adopt implementing regulations with the Director of the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, and CCU's dedicated special fund will receive increased fee revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SLGCA regulates video lottery operators and facilities across Maryland, requested this departmental bill, must establish and honor prize interception priority orders, and its Director is authorized to jointly adopt regulations with DBM.
The Child Support Administration (CSA) within DHS is authorized by the bill to certify child support obligors directly to video lottery operators for prize intercept enforcement.

OAH is responsible for adjudicating appeals from individuals disputing intercepted lottery facility winnings under the Administrative Procedure Act and will train administrative law judges on the provisions of the bill.

DJS refers overdue juvenile restitution accounts to the Central Collection Unit for collection, which can now be satisfied through video lottery prize interceptions under the specified statutory priorities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Division of Parole and Probation within DPSCS refers overdue criminal restitution accounts to the Central Collection Unit for interception and collection under the bill's framework.
AOC was consulted regarding court-ordered restitution and judicial enforcement of debt/restitution collections, though the bill is anticipated to have minimal operational impact on court operations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to provide certain student and workforce data to a third-party data center under certain circumstances; requiring each third-party data center to agree to comply with certain requirements relating to the data the center receives; requiring the Center to enter into a written data sharing agreement with certain third-party data centers; requiring the Center to submit a report to certain committees within 30 days of entering into a certain agreement; etc.
Title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center - External Data Sharing With Third-Party Data Centers for Multistate Reporting - Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to share data with third-party data centers. Limits data sharing to one third-party data center at a time for multistate research on student outcomes. Requires the data center to be FedRAMP-certified and maintain security standards at least as rigorous as the Center. Requires the Center to execute written data sharing agreements and submit reports to specified legislative committees. Repeals the Governing Board's authority to send student information to the United States Census Bureau.
responsible_party: Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center
stakeholders: Maryland students and workforce participants whose records are maintained in the Maryland Longitudinal Data System; third-party data centers and researchers conducting multistate student outcome research
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational expenditures can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources by the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 293 is a departmental bill directly governing the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center. It authorizes the MLDS Center and its Governing Board to share individual-level student and workforce data with a qualified third-party data center for multistate research and reporting, establishes data privacy and security criteria, requires written data-sharing agreements, mandates annual reviews and legislative reporting, and repeals previous authorization to share data with the U.S. Census Bureau.

Synopsis: Establishing the MDiplomaWorks pathway as an alternative method of earning a high school diploma in the State; providing the MDiplomaWorks pathway is a method to recognize and certify high school diploma achievement through demonstrated academic and career competencies, including workforce experience; and requiring, in calendar years 2027 and 2028, the Department of Labor to publish on its website information on the MDiplomaWorks pathway to inform potentially eligible applicants.
Title: Adult Education - High School Diploma Pathways - MDiplomaWorks Pathway

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the MDiplomaWorks pathway as an alternative method to earn a Maryland high school diploma. Bases diploma achievement on demonstrated academic and career competencies, including workforce experience. Restricts eligibility to Maryland residents without diplomas who have withdrawn from regular schooling and compulsory attendance. Requires participants to complete approved combinations of credentials, assessments, career coursework, and on-the-job training. Directs the Maryland Department of Labor to publicize the pathway in calendar years 2027 and 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland State Board of Education
stakeholders: Maryland residents without a high school diploma who have withdrawn from regular schooling and are exempt from compulsory attendance
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the pathway, publicize it, and adopt regulations using existing resources. State education aid and revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which was submitted as a departmental bill. It oversees the establishment and approval of the MDiplomaWorks pathway, adopts implementing regulations jointly with the State Board of Education, and is required to publicize information about the pathway.

The State Board of Education, supported by the Maryland State Department of Education, is required to jointly adopt regulations with the Secretary of Labor to govern the awarding of high school diplomas through the MDiplomaWorks pathway.

Synopsis: Exempting certain contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade from certain prohibitions on the provisions that may be included in State contracts.
Title: State Contracts - Prohibited Provisions - Exemptions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: Exempts certain contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade from statutory prohibitions on contract terms. Applies the exemption to contracts relating to the development of international business activities and opportunities. Relieves qualifying international trade agreements from prohibitions against indemnification clauses, binding arbitration, and out-of-state venues. Allows these contracts to include liability limits, automatic renewal terms, and non-State legal counsel provisions. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Office of International Trade
stakeholders: Office of International Trade; international contractors, vendors, and business entities contracting with the State
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill codifies existing contracting practices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill specifically exempts contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade within the Department of Commerce from certain prohibited state contract provisions, allowing the department to continue executing international business agreements and event contracts without violating state procurement statutes.

As the State of Maryland's central procurement authority overseeing state contracting rules and procedures under the State Finance and Procurement Article, DGS has an operational interest in statutory exemptions to standard contract requirements.
