Synopsis: Providing for command and control of State active duty personnel during mobilizations of the Maryland National Guard.
Title: Maryland Military Department – Supervision of State Active Duty Personnel

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Places members of the Maryland Military Department on State active duty under the operational command of the Adjutant General. Authorizes the Adjutant General to designate a National Guard officer to exercise operational command and control. Applies this command structure whether the commander is in State active duty or certain federal status. Expands coverage to all department units, including the National Guard, the Maryland Defense Force, and State operations. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
responsible_party: Maryland Military Department; Adjutant General
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland Military Department, including the Maryland National Guard, the Maryland Defense Force, and State operations personnel
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill codifies existing operational practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 301 is a departmental bill requested by the Military Department that explicitly establishes that members of the Department on State active duty are under the operational command and control of the Adjutant General or an officer designated by the Adjutant General.
The bill directly governs the command structure and operational control of Maryland National Guard members and designated officers during mobilizations and State active duty.

The Governor serves as Commander-in-Chief of the State militia with statutory authority to order personnel into State active duty, and the command authority in the bill applies in situations where the Governor is Commander-in-Chief.
The statute amended includes provisions regarding coordination with and emergency command authority over the Department of State Police when the militia is called into State active duty.

Synopsis: Providing that a manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch may not take an adverse action against a dealer for disclosing on its website that the advertised price of a vehicle is the manufacturer's minimum allowable advertised price and that the dealer may offer a lower price for the vehicle.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Prices Listed on Dealer Websites (Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits a vehicle manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch from taking adverse action against a dealer for specific website price disclosures. Protects dealers who disclose that an advertised vehicle price is the manufacturer's minimum allowable advertised price. Protects dealers who disclose on their website that they may offer a lower price for the vehicle. Applies these protections unless the dealer violates false advertising laws or public protection laws.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Motor vehicle dealers, manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration licenses and regulates motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and vehicle dealers under Title 15 of the Transportation Article, which governs the dealer-manufacturer relations and vehicle advertising standards amended by this bill.
The Department of Transportation oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and administers the Maryland Transportation Article amended by the legislation.

Synopsis: Authorizing an address in this State supplied by a commercial mail receiving agency to be designated as the principal office of a Maryland corporation, limited liability company, limited liability partnership, or limited partnership; and defining "commercial mail receiving agency" as a person that is authorized by the U.S. Postal Service to accept delivery of mail on behalf of another person as a business service.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Principal Offices - Private Mailboxes

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Authorizes business entities in Maryland to designate an address supplied by a commercial mail receiving agency as their principal office. Applies to Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, and limited partnerships. Requires the entity to maintain a valid commercial mail receiving agreement under U.S. Postal Service regulations. Defines a commercial mail receiving agency as a person authorized by the postal service to accept mail deliveries. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, limited partnerships, and commercial mail receiving agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase minimally in fiscal 2027 from filing fees when existing entities change their principal office address. There is no material impact on State Department of Assessments and Taxation operations or finances, and local government finances are unaffected.

Synopsis: Requiring each local school system to identify, in its regular safety evaluation, issues of accessibility for individuals with disabilities; and requiring local school systems to include in a certain annual report instances in which a public school facility became inaccessible for a student with a disability in a manner that could impede evacuations or emergency response.
Title: Public Schools - Individuals With Disabilities - Accessibility and Emergency Planning

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Requires each local school system to identify and develop solutions for accessibility issues for individuals with disabilities during regular safety evaluations. Mandates reporting of instances where a public school facility became inaccessible for a student with a disability in a manner that could impede emergencies. Directs local school systems to submit these reports annually to the Maryland Center for School Safety. Establishes that the submitted safety reports are confidential and exempt from inspection under the Maryland Public Information Act. Authorizes disclosure of the reports to members of the General Assembly upon request.
responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety; local school systems
stakeholders: students and individuals with disabilities in public schools, public school personnel, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Center for School Safety can implement the bill using existing resources. Local school system finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) is the primary state entity tasked with receiving, reviewing, and consulting on the local school systems' safety evaluations, updated emergency plans, and annual incident reports detailing school accessibility issues during emergencies.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public school systems statewide, houses the Maryland Center for School Safety, and maintains the Emergency Planning Guidelines for Local School Systems regarding accommodations for individuals with disabilities.

The bill's statutory framework requires local school safety coordinators to coordinate safety evaluations and public school facility assessments with the Interagency Commission on School Construction's facility assessment process.

As the state agency responsible for coordinating policies and improving services and accessibility for Maryland residents with disabilities, the bill's focus on school facility accessibility and emergency evacuation accommodations directly aligns with the department's mission.

Synopsis: Providing that a certain landlord may not refuse to rent to a prospective tenant who pays rent with the assistance of an income-based housing subsidy under certain circumstances, subject to a certain exception; establishing that a violation of the Act is a discriminatory housing practice and is subject to enforcement by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; and requiring that a certain landlord offer a certain tenant the option of having positive rental payment history reported to a certain consumer reporting agency.
Title: Landlord and Tenant - Discrimination in Housing for Income-Based Housing Subsidies and Positive Rental History Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: Prohibits residential landlords from denying housing to prospective tenants using income-based housing subsidies based on income or credit. Designates violations as discriminatory housing practices enforceable by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights. Authorizes landlords to verify a tenant has sufficient income to pay the tenant's portion of rent. Requires landlords owning six or more residential units to offer tenants optional positive rental payment history reporting. Authorizes landlords to charge electing tenants a fee capped at actual costs or $10 monthly. Requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations implementing the reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: residential landlords, prospective and current residential tenants, recipients of income-based housing vouchers and subsidies, and consumer reporting agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights and the Department of Housing and Community Development can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly expands the definition of discriminatory housing practices to include certain refusals to rent to prospective tenants who pay rent using income-based housing subsidies, making these violations subject to investigation and enforcement by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Housing and Community Development adopt regulations specifying the form and requirements for the mandatory offer of positive rental payment history reporting provided to tenants.

The Judiciary may adjudicate civil actions authorized under the state's fair housing laws for alleged discriminatory housing practices, though any impact on court workloads is projected to be negligible.
The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts contested case hearings for administrative complaints referred by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights regarding discriminatory housing practices.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination date of certain provisions of law that authorize a county board of education to provide transportation to and from school for certain students using a vehicle other than a certain type of school vehicle; and requiring the State Department of Education, in consultation with county boards of education and the Motor Vehicle Administration, to study the current regulations for vehicles other than a certain type of school vehicle and report the results to certain committees by January 1, 2027.
Title: County Boards of Education - Student Transportation - Sunset Repeal and Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Repeals the termination date of provisions authorizing county boards of education to transport certain students using alternative vehicles. Authorizes county boards of education to permanently use vehicles other than Type I and Type II school vehicles when appropriate. Requires the State Department of Education to review regulations governing alternative student transportation vehicles and drivers. Mandates consultation with county boards of education and the Motor Vehicle Administration during the regulatory review. Requires the Department to report its findings to specified legislative committees on or before January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Motor Vehicle Administration; County Boards of Education
stakeholders: public school students receiving transportation, county boards of education, and commercial student transportation contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: State implementation costs can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Local school system transportation expenditures may decrease or avoid future increases beyond fiscal 2026 by continuing the use of alternative vehicles.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for reviewing regulations regarding alternative school vehicles and drivers, consulting with stakeholders, and reporting findings to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027.

MVA is explicitly required by the bill to be consulted by the Maryland State Department of Education in reviewing the regulations for alternative student transportation vehicles and driver requirements.
The bill specifically directs MSDE to examine the Public Service Commission's regulations for transportation network operators to assess if school transportation regulations can be aligned with them.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which is statutorily required to participate in the regulatory review of alternative school transportation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Anne Arundel County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on real property that is located in a Rural Legacy Area, subject to certain land preservation programs, and for which the property owner has sold certain development rights under the Rural Legacy Program; applying the Act to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Property Tax Credit - Rural Legacy Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Forests and Parks -see also- MdNatlCapPkPlnCm; Plants; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Anne Arundel County to grant, by law, a county property tax credit. Applies the credit to real property located in a designated Rural Legacy Area. Requires that the property owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: governing body of Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: owners of real property located in a Rural Legacy Area in Anne Arundel County who have sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program
fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Anne Arundel County property tax revenues decrease by approximately $27,800 annually beginning in FY 2027 to the extent the credit is granted, with no effect on county expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a local property tax credit for landowners who have sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program, which is a state conservation program established under Title 5, Subtitle 9A of the Natural Resources Article and administered by the Department of Natural Resources.

Synopsis: Extending the deadline by which the Department of the Environment is required to submit a certain report on the synthetic turf industry and synthetic turf disposal from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027.
Title: Environment - Synthetic Turf Industry and Disposal Study - Deadline Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: Extends the deadline for the Department of the Environment to submit a synthetic turf study report to January 15, 2027. Moves the previous reporting deadline from July 1, 2026. Directs the department to submit findings to the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment and the House Environment and Transportation Committee. Requires the study to examine synthetic turf, existing synthetic turf fields, and the synthetic turf industry in the State. Mandates consultation with industry representatives, environmental and community stakeholders, and synthetic turf users. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Synthetic turf industry representatives, the Synthetic Turf Council, synthetic turf producers, retailers, and users including local governments, county school systems, higher education facilities, and professional sports organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Extending the reporting deadline does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the statutory deadline from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027, for the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to complete its study and submit a comprehensive report on the synthetic turf industry and disposal to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland Health Care Commission by reducing from nine to eight the number of members who are individuals who do not have any connection with the management or policy of a health care provider or payor and including an administrator of a hospital; and altering from five to four the number of Commission members who must be residents of different counties with a population of 300,000 or more.
Title: Maryland Health Care Commission - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the membership composition of the Maryland Health Care Commission. Reduces the number of members unconnected to health care provider or payor management from nine to eight. Adds one hospital administrator to the Commission. Decreases the required number of members residing in counties with 300,000 or more residents from five to four. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Hospital administrators, Maryland Health Care Commission members, health care providers, and health care payors
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as altering Commission membership does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership composition of the Maryland Health Care Commission by adding a hospital administrator and modifying the ratio of consumer/unaffiliated members and geographic representation requirements.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is an independent regulatory agency operating within the Maryland Department of Health, which provided information on the bill.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Maryland Health Care Commission and must adhere to the bill's updated composition and geographic distribution criteria.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing appointees for state commissions, including identifying qualified hospital administrators and candidates meeting geographic requirements.

Synopsis: Altering the composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board by removing a member who is chosen from a list of nominees provided by the Association of Independent Schools and increasing the number of members chosen from lists provided by the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities.
Title: Education - Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board - Composition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Alters the composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board. Removes the board seat for a certified nonpublic school classroom teacher nominated by the Association of Independent Schools. Increases the representation of the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities from one member to two. Requires the Governor to appoint one licensed special education teacher currently providing classroom instruction from association nominees. Requires the Governor to appoint one administrator or supervisory staff member from association nominees. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Governor; Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board
stakeholders: Association of Independent Schools; Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities; nonpublic school teachers and administrators
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the State Board of Education provide administrative and staffing support for the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, and the State Superintendent serves as an ex officio member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory membership composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, a state regulatory board governing teacher education and certification standards.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing nominations and appointments to state boards, including the revised seats on the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board.

The Governor is statutory authority responsible for appointing the members of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, subject to Senate advice and consent, following the altered composition criteria.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop and administer an anonymous reporting system to receive information related to a school or student safety concern; requiring the Center to develop operational guidelines and procedures, and to provide training relative to the system; requiring each local school system to participate in the anonymous reporting system, subject to a certain exception; requiring a certain custodian of records to deny inspection of information and materials related the system; etc.
Title: Education - Maryland Center for School Safety - Anonymous Reporting System

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop and administer an anonymous reporting system. Directs the system to coordinate receipt of school safety concerns while maintaining reporter anonymity. Requires the Center to develop operational guidelines and provide navigation training for school personnel. Requires each local school system to participate in the reporting system beginning July 1, 2027. Authorizes a local school system to opt out by December 1, 2026, if it operates a substantially similar system. Requires public records custodians to deny inspection of materials related to the reporting system.
responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, public school personnel, local school systems, parents, and emergency response personnel
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill codifies existing practice, and local school systems already comply with the requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 326 directly mandates the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop, administer, and establish operational guidelines and training for a statewide anonymous school safety reporting system.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education, and the bill impacts safety reporting and compliance across Maryland's public school systems overseen by the department.

Synopsis: Altering the number of members on the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County; and altering the membership of the Board to reflect the change in Baltimore County councilmanic districts.
Title: Education - Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: Reduces the membership of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County from 15 to 11 members. Increases the number of at-large members from one to two. Allocates one member to each of nine Baltimore County councilmanic districts instead of two from seven districts. Terminates the terms of specified current trustees on June 30, 2026. Reassigns continuing trustees to newly structured districts and establishes staggered terms for new appointments beginning July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Senate; Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County
stakeholders: Members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, the Community College of Baltimore County, and Baltimore County residents
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Minimal decrease in local reimbursement expenditures for trustee members begins in fiscal 2027 due to the smaller board size. Baltimore County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, which consists of members appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and managing appointments to state boards and commissions, and will need to implement the transition, seat redistricting, and new appointment schedule for the Baltimore County Community College Trustees.

SponsorPrimary: Prince George's County Delegation and Montgomery County Delegation

Sponsors.Name: Prince George's County Delegation and Montgomery County Delegation

Synopsis: Requiring an applicant for appointment as a commissioner of a bicounty commission to submit a certain statement to the Prince George's County Office of Ethics and Accountability; requiring the chief administrative officer for Prince George's County to transmit the financial disclosure statements of commissioners or appointed applicants of bicounty commissions to the Office; and requiring the Office, rather than the chief administrative officer for Prince George's County, to take certain actions regarding the statements.
Title: Bicounty Commissions - Public Ethics - Financial Disclosure Statements PG/MC 105-26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Transfers certain bicounty commission financial disclosure responsibilities to the Prince George’s County Office of Ethics and Accountability. Requires applicants seeking appointment from Prince George’s County to submit paper financial disclosure statements to the Office. Directs the county chief administrative officer to transmit statements of commissioners and appointed applicants to the Office. Requires the Office to retain statements, return unappointed applicants' statements, and notify the State Ethics Commission. Mandates that the Office maintain disclosure statements for public inspection and record examining individuals' identifying information.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Office of Ethics and Accountability; State Ethics Commission; Prince George’s County Chief Administrative Officer
stakeholders: Applicants for appointment and appointed commissioners of bicounty commissions from Prince George’s County, and members of the public examining financial disclosure statements.
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions of the Maryland Public Ethics Law governing financial disclosure statements for bicounty commissions filed electronically with the State Ethics Commission, including requirements for the Commission to delete electronic filings when notified that an applicant was not appointed.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a law enforcement officer from engaging in certain sexual acts, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with a student enrolled in a school where the law enforcement officer is assigned as a school resource officer; and providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction is subject to a term of imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine not exceed $3,000 or both.
Title: Criminal Law - School Resource Officers - Prohibition on Sexual Activity with Students

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Prohibits a law enforcement officer from engaging in sexual contact, vaginal intercourse, or a sexual act with a student. Applies this restriction to students enrolled in a school where the officer serves as a school resource officer. Classifies a violation as a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment up to three years, a fine up to $3,000, or both. Authorizes courts to impose sentences consecutive to or concurrent with sentences for other specified sexual crimes. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State's Attorneys; State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers assigned as school resource officers, Baltimore City school police officers, and students enrolled in schools with assigned resource officers
fiscal_impact_summary: Not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS), an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education, coordinates statewide school safety and oversees standards, training, and policy regarding School Resource Officers (SROs) pursuant to Title 7, Subtitle 15 of the Education Article, which is directly referenced in the bill.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and local school policies where School Resource Officers are deployed, and was consulted for the fiscal and policy note.

The Maryland State Police is the primary statewide law enforcement agency and employs law enforcement officers who may serve in roles subject to statutory standards of conduct and criminal prohibitions governing law enforcement officers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a misdemeanor offense punishable by up to three years of imprisonment and/or fines, impacting correctional operations and supervision overseen by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal offense with potential terms of incarceration, requiring OPD representation for indigent defendants charged under the statute.
The Maryland Judiciary is responsible for the trial and adjudication of individuals charged with misdemeanor offenses under the bill.

Synopsis: Increasing the number of members on the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation from 9 to 12.
Title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Increases the voting membership of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12. Requires the Governor to appoint the additional members with the advice and consent of the Senate. Expands the required number of lawyer board members from five to seven. Increases the required number of nonlawyer board members from four to five. Raises the vote threshold required to remove a voting member from seven to nine members.
responsible_party: Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation; Governor
stakeholders: Appointees and members of the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation from 9 to 12 voting members, all of whom are appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate. The Governor also fills any vacancies on the Board.

The Office of Appointments vets and manages the recruitment and appointment process for gubernatorial appointments to state boards, commissions, and councils, which will include identifying candidates for the three additional board positions created by this bill.

Synopsis: Altering and expanding the jurisdiction of the Maryland Capitol Police of the Department of General Services; and establishing that the Department has statewide jurisdiction over and full police authority for the enforcement of the criminal laws and parking and motor vehicle laws as to the operation, maintenance, and protection of certain State-owned or leased buildings and grounds and other public improvements or grounds designated by law or by the Board of Public Works.
Title: Department of General Services - Maryland Capitol Police - Statewide Jurisdiction

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: Expands the jurisdiction of the Maryland Capitol Police and the Department of General Services statewide. Increases the surrounding enforcement area around State-owned or State-leased buildings from 1,000 feet to 2,000 feet. Authorizes Maryland Capitol Police officers to investigate and enforce statewide criminal, asset forfeiture, and motor vehicle laws. Requires advance notification to the Secretary of State Police before conducting an investigation or enforcement action, absent an emergency. Requires the Maryland Capitol Police to enter a memorandum of understanding with the Baltimore Police Department before operating in Baltimore City.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Maryland Capitol Police; Department of State Police
stakeholders: Maryland Capitol Police officers, state and local law enforcement agencies, and individuals subject to law enforcement actions on or near State property or statewide
fiscal_impact_summary: Altering and expanding the jurisdiction of the Department of General Services and the Maryland Capitol Police is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Department of General Services (DGS) by expanding the statutory jurisdiction and police powers of the Maryland Capitol Police (MCP), a division within DGS, granting them statewide jurisdiction.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Capitol Police to provide notification to the Secretary of State Police in advance of exercising statewide investigative and enforcement powers (absent emergency/exigency) and post-action notification to local barrack commanders.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Capitol Police notify the Superintendent of the Natural Resources Police (or designee) after exercising statewide enforcement and investigative powers.
The bill requires post-enforcement notification to the Chief of Police of the Maryland Department of Health Secured Transport and Investigation Unit when Capitol Police exercise statewide authority.

The bill specifically identifies the Chief of Police of the Maryland Transit Administration Police Force as a recipient of notifications following investigations and enforcement actions conducted by the Capitol Police.

As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration (whose police force must be notified under the bill) and the manager of extensive state transportation facilities, MDOT is affected by expanded interagency police coordination.
The bill references the Board of Public Works' authority to designate other public improvements or grounds over which DGS and Capitol Police maintain jurisdiction and police authority.

The bill repeals an outdated, specific statutory reference to properties administered by the Maryland Department of Labor on June 30, 2019, replacing it with generalized statewide coverage for state-owned and leased facilities.

Synopsis: Entering into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact for the purpose of authorizing licensed school psychologists who hold multistate licenses to provide school psychological services in member states; establishing requirements for multistate licensure; establishing the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission; providing for the withdrawal from the Compact; etc.
Title: School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact

Synopsis: Establishing that certain firefighters, fire fighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, and members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal suffering from hypertension are presumed to have an occupational disease that is compensable under workers' compensation law and are presumed to be disabled if certain requirements are met.

bill_summary: Establishes a workers' compensation occupational disease and disablement presumption for specified paid public safety employees diagnosed with hypertension. Applies to paid firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, and State Fire Marshal members. Requires an authorized provider diagnosis, 90 consecutive days of prescribed medication, and two years of cumulative Maryland service. Disqualifies individuals from receiving disability retirement benefits for the same condition, unless authorized under a collective bargaining agreement. Prohibits claimants from receiving duplicative benefits for the same condition under multiple statutory provisions.
responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
stakeholders: Paid firefighters, paid firefighting instructors, paid rescue squad members, paid advanced life support unit members, and sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal employed by airport authorities, counties, fire control districts, municipalities, or the State; local governments and workers' compensation insurers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State, Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, and local government expenditures may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2027 due to expanded occupational disease presumptions and additional workers' compensation benefit payments. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the primary regulatory and adjudicative body administering Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law. The bill directly impacts the Commission by establishing a new compensability presumption for hypertension and requiring the Commission to adopt regulations defining an 'authorized provider.'

As the third-party administrator handling workers' compensation claims on behalf of the State of Maryland, the Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (operating through Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) would directly handle any additional workers' compensation claims and benefit payments resulting from the expanded hypertension presumption.

The bill explicitly covers sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, which operates within the Department of State Police, making its employees eligible for the occupational disease presumption.

The bill specifies that individuals who qualify for compensation under the new presumption generally may not receive disability retirement benefits for the same condition, which directly affects the administration and coordination of disability retirement benefits managed by the Agency.

The bill covers firefighters and emergency personnel employed by airport authorities or the State, which includes personnel at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport operated under MDOT.
The MAA employs airport firefighters and rescue personnel who would be covered under the bill's expanded occupational disease presumption for airport authority or State employees.

The Subsequent Injury Fund investigates and pays liabilities for workers' compensation claims involving preexisting health conditions combined with workplace conditions; expanded occupational disease claims can impact potential fund assessments and liabilities.

bill_summary: Authorizes an aggrieved party or the Office of the Attorney General to sue certain judicial officers for constitutional deprivations. Authorizes plaintiffs in an action to seek damages, declaratory relief, and injunctive relief. Permits courts to award reasonable fees and costs, including attorney's fees and expert witness fees, to prevailing plaintiffs. Requires filing an action within five years after the cause of action accrues. Authorizes prosecutors to direct law enforcement agencies to gather and retain identifying digital data upon receiving misconduct complaints. Restricts a plaintiff to obtaining that identifying digital data only under a court order.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; State Prosecutor; State's Attorney
stakeholders: Individuals deprived of constitutional or legal rights by federal officers; federal law enforcement officers authorized to carry firearms and make arrests; State and local law enforcement agencies; civil rights attorneys and law firms
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase if the Office of the Attorney General is awarded damages or recovers fees and costs. No impact on State expenditures is expected because existing budgeted resources are sufficient. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly empowers the Office of the Attorney General to initiate civil actions for damages and injunctive relief against judicial officers who violate constitutional and legal rights, and authorizes the office to direct state and local law enforcement agencies to gather and securely retain identifying digital data upon receiving a complaint.

The bill directly names the State Prosecutor as an authority empowered to receive complaints of judicial officer misconduct and direct appropriate state and local law enforcement agencies to collect and retain identifying digital data.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article for constitutional rights violations and requires court orders issued by state courts to release identifying digital data to plaintiffs.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police may be directed by the Attorney General, State Prosecutor, or State's Attorneys to gather and securely retain specified identifying digital data (such as license plate, GPS, and cell data) pursuant to complaints under the bill.

The State Treasurer's Office administers the Maryland Tort Claims Act and State Insurance Trust Fund; the fiscal note evaluates the potential impact on the office regarding claim investigations, state liability, and insurance adjusting workload.

The Department operates the Natural Resources Police, a state law enforcement agency that could potentially be directed to gather and retain digital data under the bill's provisions, and was consulted as an information source in the fiscal note.

The bill eliminates the requirement that urban agricultural property be located within a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which is a key land-use planning designation administered and tracked by the Department of Planning.

bill_summary: Requires certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover scalp cooling systems. Mandates this coverage for entities that provide coverage for chemotherapy to treat cancer. Defines a scalp cooling system as a reusable medical device used to prevent or reduce chemotherapy-related hair loss. fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. Local government expenditures may increase for fully insured health benefit plans.

Repeals the prohibition on issuing a permit to any person who begins construction without one. responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment

bill_summary: Repeals the 16-year maximum age cap for children receiving educational support in residential child care programs. Requires program operators to keep children enrolled in their previous school unless social services determines otherwise. Directs operators to provide academic assistance, study time, extracurricular support, and computer access for eligible students. Establishes mandatory training topics for applicants seeking certification as residential child and youth care practitioners. Exempts certified practitioners from new training requirements until their certificate renewal is due.
responsible_party: State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals; Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: children in residential child care programs, licensed operators of residential child care programs, and residential child and youth care practitioners
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in fiscal 2027 for the Department of Human Services to conduct staff training, update regulations, and modify contracts, with indeterminate but minimal ongoing monitoring costs in future years. Other state agencies can implement the bill with existing resources, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS licenses residential child care programs and oversees local departments of social services, which are tasked by the bill with determining whether keeping a child enrolled in their previous school is in their best interest. DHS also incurs a direct fiscal impact ($25,000 in FY 2027) to train staff, update regulations, and modify contracts.

MDH licenses residential child care programs and houses the State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals, which must update and administer the expanded training and certification requirements established in the Health Occupations Article.

DJS licenses residential child care programs and contracts with providers, and will need to ensure that its facilities and contracted operators comply with the updated educational support and practitioner certification standards.

The bill amends the Education Article regarding the enrollment, academic support, individualized education programs (IEPs), behavioral intervention plans, and school-provider coordination for school-aged children placed in residential child care programs.

Synopsis: Extending the reporting date and the termination date for a workgroup convened by the State Retirement Agency to study transfers of member service between State and local retirement and pension systems; and requiring the State Retirement Agency to report to the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee, the House Appropriations Committee, and the Joint Committee on Pensions and not the entire General Assembly.

responsible_party: State Retirement Agency

fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as extending the reporting and termination dates does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary implementing agency tasked with convening and staffing the workgroup to study service transfers between State and local systems and submitting the final report by the extended deadline of October 1, 2026.

Applies this terminology change to strategic planning and establishment decisions for parks interpreting underrepresented populations. Renames Freedman's State Historical Park in Montgomery County to Freedman's State Park. Renames Port of Deposit State Historical Park in Cecil County to Port Deposit State Park. Preserves the existing statutory historical purposes and educational missions of the affected parks. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Visitors to Maryland State parks, local governments and nonprofit organizations partnering with the State on partnership parks, and underrepresented communities whose history is interpreted in State parks
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances because signs and publications have not yet been produced for the renamed parks.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article governing the Maryland State Park System administered by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR), changing statutory references from 'State historical parks' to 'State parks' and renaming Freedman's State Historical Park and Port of Deposit State Historical Park.

Synopsis: Prohibiting provisions of the governing documents of a condominium or homeowners association from unreasonably restricting the governing body from installing or authorizing the installation of electric vehicle recharging equipment; establishing that the installation or authorization of electric vehicle recharging equipment by a governing body is subject to certain budget processes of the condominium or homeowners association for a common area renovation or alteration similar in cost or magnitude; applying the Act retroactively; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits governing documents of condominiums and homeowners associations from unreasonably restricting installation of electric vehicle recharging equipment. Applies this prohibition to common use and limited common use parking spaces. Subjects equipment installations to ordinary budget processes for similar common area renovations. Requires governing bodies to consider sufficient community parking availability before installing or authorizing equipment. Authorizes governing bodies to grant renewable licenses for up to three years on necessary common elements. Applies retroactively to governing documents recorded or adopted before October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: condominium unit owners, homeowners association lot owners, governing bodies of condominiums and homeowners associations, and electric vehicle owners in common ownership communities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration coordinates state clean energy policies and electric vehicle infrastructure initiatives. While the bill does not establish new grant programs or regulatory mandates for the agency, it directly impacts statewide electric vehicle recharging equipment deployment policies.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division handles inquiries, mediation, and enforcement related to common ownership communities (condominiums and homeowners associations) and consumer rights.

The bill establishes statutory standards rendering certain restrictive covenants void and enforceable in common ownership communities, which may be the subject of civil dispute litigation within the state court system.

Synopsis: Adding Class B (on-sale) beer and wine and Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor licenses to the list of alcoholic beverages licenses for which the prohibition against issuing multiple licenses for the same person or premises in Prince George's County does not apply.

Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue multiple qualifying licenses to the same person or premises. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license applicants, restaurant and hotel operators, and license holders in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County revenues increase by $365 per additional Class B beer and wine license and $2,305 per additional Class B beer, wine, and liquor license issued, but total revenue gains are indeterminate because the number of new licenses is unknown. County expenditures are unaffected as enforcement can be handled with existing resources. No state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill pertains to alcoholic beverages licensing. While it specifically alters local licensing restrictions administered by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry.

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission by two years to September 30, 2028. Adds two private sector members appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate. Requires the Commission to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly annually each December 1. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission; Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Private sector businesses engaged in bilateral trade with Ireland, the Irish–American community, and members of the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues or local finances. The Department of Commerce can continue to support the Commission using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission is established within the Department of Commerce, which provides staff and operational support for the commission. The Secretary of Commerce or their designee also serves as a member.
The Secretary of State or the Secretary of State's designee serves as an ex officio member of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership structure, reporting timeline, and termination date of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission, an executive advisory commission.

The Governor appoints members to the commission (including two additional private sector members created by the bill), has authority to remove appointed members, and receives the commission's annual report of findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments, which includes the new private sector seats on the commission.

bill_summary: Adds bacterial vaginosis to the list of infections eligible for expedited partner therapy. Authorizes licensed certified midwives to prescribe, dispense, or provide antibiotic therapy to partners without personal physical assessments. Replaces the statutory term sexually transmitted infection with an infection transmitted through sexual activity. Requires the Secretary of Health to adopt implementing regulations for public and private health care settings. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Patients diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis and their sexual partners, licensed certified midwives, authorized prescribing health care practitioners, and licensed pharmacists
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The Maryland Department of Health can update regulations and provider materials using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) oversees public health programs, health occupations licensing, and the Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT) program. bill_summary: Requires the Prince George’s County Board of Education to require high schools to provide free drink spiking detection products. Requires schools to provide drug detection strips if an incident requiring overdose-reversing medication was reported. Applies these mandates only if the detection products are provided to the schools at no cost. Authorizes schools to make detection products available in school-based health clinics or school libraries. Requires each county public high school to report product distribution quantities annually to Maryland’s Office of Overdose Response.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of Education; Maryland’s Office of Overdose Response
stakeholders: public high school students and public high schools in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as Maryland’s Office of Overdose Response can receive annual reports with existing budgeted resources. Prince George's County Public Schools expenditures may increase minimally to install product dispensers in clinics or libraries, while detection product mandates apply only if acquired at no cost.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article to require Prince George's County public high schools to make drink spiking and drug detection strips available to students under certain conditions, referencing overdose incident reporting submitted to the Maryland State Department of Education under existing law.

The bill involves distribution of drug detection strips and reporting to Maryland's Office of Overdose Response. The Maryland Department of Health manages the Overdose Response Program, which supplies free fentanyl test strips to authorized entities that schools may use to satisfy the bill's provisions.

The bill requires high schools to submit annual reports regarding distributed drug detection products directly to Maryland's Office of Overdose Response, an executive entity established within the Governor's coordinating offices.

Synopsis: Authorizing a party to the guardianship of the property of an alleged disabled person to request a stay of certain civil actions or proceedings on the filing of a petition for guardianship of the property of an alleged disabled person; requiring a certain party to the guardianship of the property of an alleged disabled person to provide certain notice to a court granting a stay and to parties to a civil action or proceeding; establishing that a stay may be in effect  for not more than 90 days, unless extended for good cause; etc.
Title: Petition for Guardianship of the Property of Alleged Disabled Person - Stay of Civil Actions and Proceedings
bill_summary: Authorizes a party to the property guardianship of an alleged disabled person to request a stay of specified civil actions. Covers actions for failure to pay rent, warrants of restitution, wrongful detainer, foreclosures, sheriff's sales, and property actions. Requires the requesting party to give notice of the petition and stay request to all parties. Limits the stay to 90 days after filing the petition, unless extended for good cause. Lifts the stay automatically upon the appointment of a guardian or denial of the petition. Requires serving the appointed property guardian to effectuate service of process for a stayed action.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: alleged disabled persons subject to property guardianship petitions, appointed guardians of property, landlords, mortgage lenders, and creditors
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill can be implemented with existing State resources with no material effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact. Small business plaintiffs such as landlords and creditors may experience delayed revenue or proceedings due to court stays.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland court system by authorizing parties to petition for stays in specific civil proceedings (such as failure to pay rent, wrongful detainer, and foreclosure actions) during guardianship proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for implementing these procedural changes and associated court case management programming.

The bill amends the Estates and Trusts Article regarding guardianship proceedings for alleged disabled persons, an area closely related to estate and fiduciary administration overseen in part by the Registers of Wills.

bill_summary: Extends the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances through December 31, 2027. Adds a representative of a Maryland historically Black college or university to the task force membership. Requires the task force to submit an updated report of findings and recommendations by October 31, 2026. Directs the task force to submit the updated report to the Governor and General Assembly. Continues task force staff support by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration; Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances
stakeholders: Historically Black colleges and universities in Maryland, Task Force members, and individuals affected by natural psychedelic substance policies
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Maryland Cannabis Administration can provide staff support and absorb minimal travel reimbursements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Cannabis Administration is mandated to provide staff support for the Task Force, and its Director (or designee) serves as an ex officio member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the operational timeline through 2027 and alters the membership requirements of the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances.
The Secretary of Health or the Secretary's designee is a designated member of the Task Force examining psychedelic substances and therapeutic uses.
The Secretary of Disabilities or the Secretary's designee is an ex officio member of the Task Force.
The Secretary of Veterans Affairs (Department of Veterans and Military Families) or the Secretary's designee serves as a member of the Task Force.
The Governor designates the chair of the Task Force, appoints several members (including the new HBCU representative), and receives the updated findings and recommendations report.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to the Task Force, including the newly added seat for an HBCU representative.

The University System of Maryland is explicitly listed among the entities eligible for a research appointment and also encompasses three state historically Black universities eligible for the new HBCU seat.
As a state agency and historically Black university, Morgan State University representatives are eligible to fill the newly created Task Force seat for an HBCU representative.

bill_summary: Establishes the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program in the Maryland Department of Agriculture starting July 1, 2028. Requires the Department, in consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment, to administer the program and seek funding. Directs the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 for the program beginning in fiscal year 2028. Authorizes grants to farmers, soil conservation districts, higher education institutions, nonprofits, partnering businesses, and qualifying consortiums. Supports projects developing or maintaining infrastructure, collection programs, education, or technical assistance for food waste reduction and composting. Requires the Department to submit an annual program report to the General Assembly beginning December 31, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Farmers, urban farmers, urban agricultural producers, soil conservation districts, institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, and partner businesses in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2028 for the mandated appropriation (covering administrative start-up costs), rising to $371,471 in FY 2029 for ongoing grant awards and administrative expenses, and $380,300 by FY 2031. State and local institutions of higher education and local soil conservation districts may receive indeterminate grant revenues and incur corresponding project expenditures beginning as early as FY 2029.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 429 establishes the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA). MDA is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the program, applying for external funding, awarding grants, and reporting annually to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly requires MDA to administer the grant program, identify and apply for funding, and prioritize grant applications in consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE).
The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 for the grant program in the State budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2028.

As the State's principal budget agency, DBM is responsible for preparing the Governor's annual budget and incorporating the $250,000 mandated appropriation established by the bill starting in fiscal year 2028.

Institutions of higher education are explicitly designated as eligible grant recipients under the program, potentially receiving funding for research and projects involving organics recycling, compost application, and food waste diversion.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is an eligible entity to apply for and receive grant funding under the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program.

As a public four-year higher education institution, Saint Mary's College of Maryland is eligible to receive grant awards under the program for qualifying organics recycling and food waste reduction projects.

Synopsis: Requiring a family child care provider who is a member of a reserve component to designate a substitute to provide family child care for not more than 45 working days in any 12-month period while the family child care provider is absent for required training and active service.
Title: Family Child Care Providers - Reserve Component Members - Substitute Provider
bill_summary: Requires a family child care provider who is a reserve component member to designate a substitute provider. Mandates that the substitute provide care during the provider's absence for required training and active service. Authorizes the provider to use the substitute for up to 45 working days in any 12-month period. Preserves the Maryland State Department of Education's authority to establish substitute requirements and necessary qualifications.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Family child care providers who are members of a military reserve component, designated substitute child care providers, and families with children in family child care homes
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill with existing resources; state revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE regulates and registers family child care homes and providers under the Education Article. The bill directly impacts MSDE's regulatory framework by allowing family child care providers who are reserve component members to use a substitute provider for up to 45 working days per year for required training and active service.

The bill provides protections and regulatory flexibilities for reserve component and National Guard members who operate child care businesses, supporting military service members and their families in balancing service obligations with small business ownership.

The legislation directly accommodates National Guard members called for required training and active service duties by expanding the allowed use of substitute child care providers to 45 working days per year.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly renames the agency to the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, updating its statutory references and advisory council framework.
The bill explicitly alters the composition of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing by adding the Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) as a statutory member.

bill_summary: Prohibits the State, units of local government, county sheriffs, and their agents from entering into immigration enforcement agreements. fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees state correctional facilities and detention operations whose officers and facilities are prohibited under the bill from participating in civil immigration enforcement agreements or 287(g) jail enforcement/warrant service models, and the department served as an information source for the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

responsible_party: Department of State Police; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers and commercial vehicle operators in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in general fund revenues from District Court fines. Enforcement can be handled with existing state and local resources, resulting in no material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle and traffic safety laws on state highways, MSP officers are responsible for enforcing the bill's prohibitions and issuing citations for dangerous accumulations of snow and ice.
The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding rules of the road and exposed vehicle surface safety, directly impacting the transportation statutory framework overseen by MDOT.

As the MDOT administration responsible for driver licensing, vehicle regulations, driving records, and traffic safety initiatives, MVA is affected by changes to vehicle operation standards and traffic violation records.
The District Court will process citations, collect fine revenues, and adjudicate contested cases resulting from violations of the new traffic prohibition.
MDTA operates Maryland's toll facilities and employs its own police force, which is empowered to enforce vehicle laws and citations on toll roads and bridges.

Synopsis: Altering a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for unreimbursed expenses paid or incurred by eligible teachers during a taxable year for the purchase of certain classroom supplies to include prekindergarten classroom teachers employed in publicly funded prekindergarten programs at eligible public providers or lead teachers or consulting teachers employed in a publicly funded prekindergarten program at an eligible private provider in the State; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Classroom Supplies Purchased by Teachers - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Expands the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for unreimbursed classroom supplies to certain prekindergarten teachers. Includes full-time prekindergarten classroom teachers in publicly funded programs at eligible public providers. Includes full-time lead teachers and consulting teachers in publicly funded programs at eligible private providers. Authorizes a subtraction of up to $250 for unreimbursed classroom supplies used by students or teachers. Excludes expenses subtracted from federal adjusted gross income under the Internal Revenue Code. Applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Full-time prekindergarten teachers at eligible public and private prekindergarten providers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease by approximately $80,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Local income tax revenues may decrease by approximately $50,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. The Comptroller's Office can administer the change using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's tax administration agency, the Comptroller is directly responsible for modifying state income tax forms and administering the expanded subtraction modification for eligible prekindergarten teachers.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees publicly funded prekindergarten programs and eligible providers defined under § 7-1A-01 of the Education Article whose teachers are made eligible by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a transportation network company to maintain a deactivation policy that provides the policies and procedures for the deactivation of operators; prohibiting a transportation network company from deactivating an operator for certain violations; authorizing a transportation network company to rely solely on a passenger report as the basis for deactivation under certain circumstances; requiring a transportation network company to allow an operator whose account is deactivated to withdraw certain earnings; etc.
Title: Transportation Network Companies - Deactivation of Operators

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
