Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires transportation network companies to maintain and publish a written plain-language deactivation policy for operators. Prohibits companies from deactivating an operator for violations not reasonably understood to be part of the policy. Restricts companies from relying solely on passenger reports for deactivation except under specified conditions. Mandates written notice of deactivation and allows deactivated operators to withdraw accrued earnings under certain circumstances. Establishes an appeals process allowing operators at least 30 days to appeal a deactivation decision.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Transportation network companies and transportation network operators in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 10 of the Public Utilities Article, which governs Transportation Network Companies (TNCs) and operators regulated and licensed by the Public Service Commission. While the bill places direct operational requirements on TNCs regarding deactivation policies and appeals, it alters the statutory and regulatory framework for for-hire passenger motor carriers under the Commission's jurisdiction.

The bill mandates that a TNC's deactivation policy is legally enforceable as a contractual term between the company and the operator, which may lead to breach of contract actions in the state court system, though it does not materially affect judicial finances or operations.

Synopsis: Increasing the minimum gross income amounts from charitable contributions at which a charitable organization must include a certain audit or a certain review with a registration statement; increasing the amount of cash receipts from charitable contributions the Secretary of State may accept an affidavit attesting to under certain circumstances; increasing the maximum amount of gross income of a charitable organization at which the Secretary of State may require an audit or review from $750,000 to $1,000,000; etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Charitable Organizations - Audit and Review Thresholds

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: Increases the gross income thresholds from charitable contributions that trigger independent CPA audits or reviews for charitable organizations. Raises the contribution threshold requiring an independent certified public accountant audit from $750,000 to $1,000,000. Raises the threshold requiring an independent certified public accountant review from $300,000 to $400,000. Increases the cash receipt limit for submitting an affidavit in place of an audit or review to $400,000. Authorizes the Secretary of State to require an audit or review if gross income is under $1,000,000.
responsible_party: Secretary of State
stakeholders: Charitable organizations soliciting or receiving contributions in Maryland; independent certified public accountants
fiscal_impact_summary: State implementation and online filing system update costs are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is the primary agency responsible for the registration and oversight of charitable organizations in Maryland. The bill directly alters the statutory thresholds for independent audits and reviews required for charitable organization registration statements filed with the Secretary of State.

Synopsis: Altering the name of the State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects to be the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects; altering the definition of "licensed landscape architects" to be "professional landscape architects"; altering certain qualifications for membership on the Board; altering certain duties of the Board; altering certain educational and experience requirements of applicants for a license to practice landscape architecture; etc.
Title: State Board of Professional Landscape Architects - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Renames the State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects to the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects. Alters experience qualifications for landscape architect Board members and updates institutional accreditation standards for licensure applicants. Authorizes the Board to issue an emeritus status license to eligible professionals with at least 25 years of experience. Establishes a two-year term from issuance for individual licenses and business permits. Repeals the permit exemption for businesses providing landscape architectural services to themselves or affiliated entities. Repeals the requirement for license applicants to pay examination fees directly to the Board.
responsible_party: State Board of Professional Landscape Architects; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Professional landscape architects, applicants for landscape architect licensure, business entities offering landscape architectural services, and retired landscape architects seeking emeritus status.
fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact; the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects can implement the provisions with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Landscape Architects is an occupational licensing unit housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly alters the board's name, composition requirements, exam procedures, licensing terms, and fee structures.

The bill alters the statutory qualification requirements for professional landscape architect members appointed by the Governor to the Board, directly impacting the vetting and candidate recommendation duties of the Office of Appointments.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members of the Board with the advice and consent of the Senate, and the bill modifies the statutory qualifications required for those appointments.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to adopt certain regulations regarding the consideration of remedies for investments in certain businesses that no longer meet the definition of a qualified business for purposes of provisions of law governing the Corporation; authorizing, rather than requiring, the Corporation to divest itself of an interest under certain circumstances; and authorizing the Corporation to pursue certain other remedies under those circumstances.
Title: Maryland Technology Development Corporation - Investments - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Public Corporations and Instrumentalities -see also- HBE
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to adopt regulations governing investment committee responsibilities. Mandates establishing a process for considering remedies, including divestment, when a business ceases to be a qualified business. Authorizes, rather than requires, the Corporation to divest itself of an equity investment within 15 years. Requires investment committee review and approval before divestment or pursuing another remedy in the Corporation's best interest.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
stakeholders: businesses receiving equity investments from the Maryland Technology Development Corporation
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances, though financial investment returns to the Maryland Technology Development Corporation may increase. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), requiring it to adopt regulations regarding investment committee responsibilities and providing flexibility regarding divestment and alternative remedies for its equity investments.

The Department of Commerce is Maryland's primary economic development agency and works closely with TEDCO initiatives, including programs funded through the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account referenced in the bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a law enforcement agency from making a certain request for verbal acknowledgement in an interaction with a person suspected to have been subjected to sexually assaultive behavior or who claims to have been subjected to sexually assaultive behavior.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Victims of Sexually Assaultive Behavior - Request for Verbal Acknowledgement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Prohibits a law enforcement agency from requesting a verbal acknowledgement during an interaction with a victim. Applies the prohibition to requests purporting to relieve an agency of an obligation. Prohibits requests purporting to preclude or define investigation scope or limit prosecution. Bars requests purporting to limit a victim's private right of action. Authorizes an affected victim to bring an action seeking injunctive or declaratory relief.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Victims of sexually assaultive behavior and Maryland law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's primary law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police officers and investigators are directly bound by the bill's prohibition on requesting verbal acknowledgments or waivers from victims of sexually assaultive behavior during investigations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which establishes the recommended standards and practices that law enforcement agencies must follow when a victim requests to limit or suspend an investigation. The department was also consulted for the bill's fiscal note.

The bill maintains the statutory provision permitting an affected victim to file a civil action seeking injunctive or declaratory relief in the state court system if a law enforcement agency violates the statute.

Synopsis: Establishing minimum adequate security standards for courtroom security at all courthouse facilities; requiring a court security officer to meet the qualifications for a special police officer; and requiring a minimum number of court security officers be present for certain types of proceedings.
Title: Courtroom Security - Minimum Adequate Security Standard

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Establishes a minimum adequate security standard for courtroom security at all courthouse facilities in the State. Requires court security officers to meet the qualifications for a special police officer. Directs entities responsible for courthouse security to use best efforts to meet specific staffing ratios beginning July 1, 2027. Mandates officers in criminal, family, or juvenile proceedings, custody cases, and across courthouse floors. Expands best-effort staffing requirements to cover all court proceedings beginning July 1, 2029.
responsible_party: Judiciary; local sheriffs' offices
stakeholders: Judges, court personnel, litigants, criminal defendants, county sheriffs' offices, and court security officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.6 million in FY 2027 only to provide security enhancement grants to local jurisdictions. Local government expenditures increase, significantly in some jurisdictions, beginning in FY 2027 for sheriffs' offices to hire an estimated 206 additional court security officers, partially offset by $5.6 million in local grant revenues in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly impacts court security operations across all Maryland courthouse facilities. The Administrative Office of the Courts serves as the administrative arm of the Judiciary, which is responsible for court security in the appellate and District courts and will administer state grant funding provided to local jurisdictions to support courtroom security enhancements.

Synopsis: Increasing from five to six the number of associate judges in the District Court in District 11 by increasing from two to three the number of associate judges appointed from Washington County.
Title: Washington County - Judgeships - District Court
bill_summary: Increases the number of District Court associate judges in District 11 from five to six. Requires three associate judges to be appointed from Washington County instead of two. Maintains the requirement that three associate judges be appointed from Frederick County. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: District Court judges, court personnel, and litigants in Washington County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $423,500 in FY 2027 to fund one new judgeship, one clerk, and two contractual bailiffs, increasing to $571,800 by FY 2031. Revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 493 creates an additional District Court judgeship in Washington County (District 11), along with associated court staff positions (courtroom clerk and contractual bailiffs), directly impacting judicial administration, operations, and general fund expenditures managed under the Judicial Branch.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and processing of candidates to fill judicial vacancies across Maryland, which includes the newly created District Court judgeship.
The Governor holds the constitutional authority to appoint judges to fill newly established judicial seats in the District Court.

Synopsis: Altering from not more than 7 to not more than 14 days after issuance, the time period during which a temporary protective order is effective: and altering the time period during which a final protective order hearing is to be held to not later than 14 days after the temporary protective order is issued.
Title: Family Law - Temporary and Final Protective Orders - Duration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse; Dom. Viol.; Elder Abuse; etc
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Alters the effective duration of temporary protective orders from seven days after service to 14 days after issuance. Requires the court to hold a final protective order hearing no later than 14 days after order issuance. Retains judicial authority to extend a temporary protective order up to six months to effectuate service. Maintains order effectiveness until the second open day if the court is closed on the expiration date. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Judiciary
stakeholders: Petitioners seeking domestic protective orders and respondents named in protective order proceedings
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by altering the effective duration of temporary protective orders issued by courts to 14 days after issuance and adjusting the statutory deadline by which the courts must schedule and conduct final protective order hearings.

Synopsis: Repealing the exemption from the certificate of need requirement for a change in bed capacity for intermediate care facilities that offer substance use disorder treatment services; providing a certificate of need is not required for a change in bed capacity at certain facilities offering certain treatment services if a written notice is filed with the Commission 45 days before the facility's establishment, the facility is consistent with the State Health Plan, will result in more efficient service delivery, and is in the public interest; etc.
Title: Certificate of Need - Intermediate Health Care Facilities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: Exempts qualifying intermediate care facilities providing medically managed residential substance use disorder treatment from certificate of need requirements. Requires facilities to submit written notice of intent to the Maryland Health Care Commission at least 45 days beforehand. Authorizes the Commission to approve exemptions that align with the State health plan and serve the public interest. Alters conditions under which licensed intermediate care facilities may change bed capacity without a certificate of need. Repeals the prior certificate of need exemption for certain residential or intensive substance-related disorder treatment facilities.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: intermediate care facilities offering substance use disorder treatment services and patients seeking residential substance use disorder treatment
fiscal_impact_summary: Workload on the Maryland Health Care Commission can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) administers the Certificate of Need (CON) program and is the primary entity responsible for receiving notices and determining whether proposed intermediate care facilities or changes in bed capacity meet the criteria for CON exemptions under the bill.

The Secretary of Health licenses the intermediate care facilities providing substance use disorder treatment affected by the bill, and MHCC is an independent commission housed within the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Altering eligibility for an exemption from the sales and use tax for the sale of precious metal bullion or coins by repealing a requirement that the sale occur at the Baltimore Convention Center.
Title: Sales and Use Tax - Precious Metal Bullion or Coins - Exemption
bill_summary: Expands the State sales and use tax exemption for sales of precious metal bullion or coins exceeding $1,000. Repeals the requirement that the transaction must occur at the Baltimore Convention Center to qualify. Alters the definition of refined precious metal to specify that its value primarily depends on precious metal content. Excludes jewelry or a work of art made of precious metal bullion or coins from the exemption. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Buyers and vendors of precious metal bullion or coins in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by $2.8 million in FY 2027, including a $2.5 million decrease in general fund revenues and a $0.3 million decrease in Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund revenues. Expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As Maryland's chief tax collector, the Comptroller of Maryland administers and enforces the state sales and use tax laws and oversees the collection and distribution of sales tax revenues affected by this exemption.

Synopsis: Altering the penalty for a subsequent conviction of sexual offense by a person in a position of authority; prohibiting a certain person in a position of authority from committing a certain violation involving a child at least 6 years younger than the person in a position of authority; prohibiting a person who has been previously convicted of a certain crime from committing a certain violation; adding sexual offense by a person in a position of authority as a predicate crime for sexual solicitation of a minor; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Sexual Offense by a Person in a Position of Authority

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the felony crime of sexual offense by a person in a position of authority involving a child under age 13. Establishes felony penalties for individuals with specified prior convictions who commit sexual offenses while in positions of authority. Designates these felony offenses as qualifying predicate crimes for sexual solicitation of a minor. Requires individuals convicted of these felony offenses to register as Tier III sex offenders. Classifies individuals convicted of misdemeanor sexual offense by a person in a position of authority as Tier I sex offenders.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Persons in positions of authority at schools or youth programs, minors, and victims of sexual offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected, though an unknown number of cases may shift from the District Court to the circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for operating Maryland's state correctional facilities, managing probation and parole, and overseeing sex offender registry requirements. The bill establishes new felony penalties of up to 10 and 20 years of imprisonment and designates offenders under these provisions as Tier III sex offenders.

The bill establishes new offenses and elevates certain misdemeanor sexual offenses to felonies, shifting caseloads from the District Court to the circuit courts and impacting judicial proceedings, caseload tracking, and sentencing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal cases. The creation of new felony offenses, heightened penalty thresholds, and mandatory lifetime Tier III sex offender registration directly affect defense workload, case exposure, and trial proceedings.

Synopsis: Including salary and wages in the compensation with regard to which full-time sworn law enforcement officers and court security officers in Baltimore City may collectively bargain; altering the person with whom the full-time sworn officers and court security officers are to seek recognition for the purposes of collectively bargaining concerning certain matters; etc.
Title: Baltimore City Sheriff's Office - Collective Bargaining - Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Expands collective bargaining subjects for full-time sworn law enforcement officers and court security officers in Baltimore City. Includes salary, wages, and merit step increases in bargainable compensation alongside city-administered benefits. Requires eligible officers to collectively bargain in good faith jointly with the Sheriff or designee and Baltimore City. Retains collective bargaining over leave, holidays, vacations, hours, working conditions, and job security. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Sheriff's Office; Baltimore City
stakeholders: Full-time sworn deputy sheriffs at the rank of lieutenant or below and court security officers in the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office, the Baltimore City Sheriff, and Baltimore City government
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Baltimore City expenditures may increase if negotiated personnel costs under collective bargaining agreements exceed what would have otherwise been spent; exact amounts cannot be reliably estimated in advance.

Synopsis: Increasing the annual salaries and providing for cost-of-living salary increases for the chair, certain part-time inspectors, and other members of the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners and Part-Time Inspectors - Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Increases the minimum annual salaries for members and inspectors of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners. Sets the board chair annual salary at not less than $21,240. Sets the annual salary for each other board member at not less than $17,700. Sets minimum annual salaries of $18,000 for the part-time deputy chief inspector and $8,260 for 18 part-time inspectors. Requires all listed salaries to include any cost-of-living increase available to nonrepresented Anne Arundel County employees.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County; Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: chair, members, part-time deputy chief inspector, and part-time inspectors of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners; Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County salary expenditures increase by at least $33,716 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 due to mandated salary increases, rising further with future cost-of-living adjustments. State revenues and expenditures are not affected.

Synopsis: Altering the titles of certain entertainment permits for certain alcoholic beverages license holders in Anne Arundel County; altering the authorized forms of entertainment that certain entertainment permit holders in the county may provide; and adding a 100-foot zoning distance requirement from any residential property applicable to certain entertainment permit holders in the county.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Entertainment Permits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc

bill_summary: Renames and alters entertainment permits for certain alcoholic beverages license holders in Anne Arundel County. Replaces the music permit with a background entertainment permit authorizing televisions and recorded or piped-in background music. Replaces the entertainment permit with a general entertainment permit authorizing background entertainment, trivia games, karaoke, and limited live music. Replaces the dancing permit with a full entertainment permit authorizing general entertainment, a stage area, a permanent dance floor, and floor shows. Requires outdoor entertainment areas under general or full entertainment permits to be at least 100 feet from residentially zoned property. Removes the statutory prohibition against dancing on licensed premises without an entertainment permit.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders in Anne Arundel County and residents of nearby residentially zoned properties
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this bill strictly modifies local alcoholic beverage entertainment permits administered by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and operation of licensed alcoholic beverage establishments.

Synopsis: Altering the license fee structure for Class C per diem beer, beer and wine, and beer, wine, and liquor licenses issued by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Class C Per Diem License Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Alters the fee structure for Class C per diem alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County. Maintains existing flat daily fees for events with an estimated attendance of fewer than 500 individuals. Restructures license fees for events with an estimated attendance of 500 or more individuals. Requires larger events to pay fees per day for each point of sale location serving alcohol. Sets large-event fees at $25 per point of sale for beer or beer and wine licenses. Sets large-event fees at $50 per point of sale for beer, wine, and liquor licenses.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Clubs and organizations hosting events with Class C per diem alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase by up to $7,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 from per-point-of-sale fees on events with 500 or more attendees. County expenditures and state finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry in the state. While this bill specifically modifies local per diem alcoholic beverages license fees set and collected by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation of alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education to develop and implement, by the 2027-2028 school year, a policy prohibiting the use of certain electronic communication devices by a student during the academic school day; and prohibiting the policy from restricting the  use of an electronic communication device for purposes of accommodations related to a disability, including for any purpose in a student's individual education program, to address a documented health issue, to access language translation tools, or to meet caregiving responsibilities.
Title: County Boards of Education - Student Electronic Communication Device Use Policy - Establishment (Joanne C. Benson Maryland Phone-Free Schools Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: Requires each county board of education to adopt a policy prohibiting student electronic communication device use. Mandates implementation not later than the 2027–2028 school year. Requires students to store devices and prohibits accessing social media platforms during the academic school day. Permits device use for disability accommodations, documented health issues, translation tools, or approved caregiving. Prohibits disciplinary suspension or expulsion solely for a violation of the policy. Directs local boards to report policy and enforcement data annually to the Maryland State Department of Education.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; County Boards of Education
stakeholders: Public school students, parents and guardians, public school teachers and administrators, and county boards of education in Maryland (excluding the Maryland School for the Blind and the Maryland School for the Deaf)
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and local school systems can implement the policy, regulation, and reporting requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary state oversight agency responsible for adopting regulations to implement the act, receiving electronic communication device policies and annual implementation data from local school boards, and publishing compiled reports and policies on its website.
The bill explicitly mentions the Maryland School for the Deaf to exempt it from the requirement to implement the student electronic communication device prohibition policy.

Synopsis: Revising, restating, and recodifying the laws of this State relating to the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.
Title: Code Revision - Health - Maryland Medical Assistance Program
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 865

NarrowSubjects.Name: Codes -see also- Annotated Code of Md; Building Codes
Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Revises, restates, and recodifies State laws governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program. Reorganizes statutory provisions relating to managed care organizations, advisory committees, and the Maryland Children's Health Program. Replaces outdated references regarding substance abuse with modern terminology referring to substance use disorders. Updates cross-references throughout the Health - General Article to reflect renumbered and newly codified sections. Clarifies that the enactment constitutes a nonsubstantive code revision without altering existing legal rights or duties.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees, Maryland Children's Health Program enrollees, participating managed care organizations, and Medicaid health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact because the bill constitutes a nonsubstantive code revision.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), the core subject of this code revision and recodification bill.
MHCC's Executive Director is an ex-officio member of the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee recodified by the bill, and the committee is tasked with reviewing data collected by MHCC.
HSCRC is referenced in provisions governing required hospital discharge data submissions for out-of-state hospitals treating Maryland Medicaid recipients.

The Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex-officio member of the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee, and Medicaid managed care organizations are required to track benefit information from DHS-administered assistance programs.
The Insurance Commissioner is consulted by the Secretary of Health to establish actuarially adjusted capitation payments for Medicaid managed care organizations.
MSDE is consulted by the Department of Health to define school-based clinics that provide care to Medicaid managed care enrollees.
The Department of Aging is designated as an entity from which the Secretary of Health must seek recommendations when appointing consumer members to the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee.
The Department of Disabilities is consulted for recommendations on consumer appointments to the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee.
OAH is designated in statute as the administrative body to hear appeals by managed care organizations regarding penalties imposed by the Department of Health.
The Comptroller receives fines and penalties collected by MDH from managed care organizations that fail to comply with program requirements.

Synopsis: Requiring governmental units that employ firefighters to compute overtime pay for each hour over 168 hours that a firefighter works during a 28-day work period; requiring counties and municipalities to provide certain payroll information to each employed firefighter; authorizing a firefighter or the firefighter's exclusive representative to initiate a certain grievance if a county or municipality does not provide the payroll information as required or wages due; etc.
Title: Employment Standards - Firefighters - Payment of Wages and Payroll Information

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires governmental units employing firefighters to compute overtime wages on hours worked exceeding 168 hours per 28-day period. Requires counties and municipalities to provide pay rate notices and pay period statements of hours, earnings, and deductions. Authorizes firefighters or their exclusive representatives to initiate grievances for missing payroll statements or unpaid wages due. Entitles firefighters to unpaid wages and damages up to three times the missing wage amount. Exempts collective bargaining agreements in effect before the October 1, 2028 effective date.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Office of Administrative Hearings
stakeholders: Firefighters employed by governmental units, Maryland counties and municipalities that employ firefighters, and the Maryland Aviation Administration
fiscal_impact_summary: Local government expenditures likely increase, potentially significantly in some jurisdictions, beginning in fiscal 2029 to pay additional overtime wages or hire more firefighters. State expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund are not materially affected, and the Maryland Department of Labor and Office of Administrative Hearings can implement the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Wage and Hour Law under the Labor and Employment Article regarding overtime computation for firefighters employed by governmental units, which the Maryland Department of Labor oversees and enforces.
MAA employs 99 state firefighters at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport who are directly covered by the bill's overtime pay calculation standards.
MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Aviation Administration, and any operational or overtime expenditure adjustments for state airport firefighters affect the Transportation Trust Fund.
OAH adjudicates contested wage payment cases and state employee grievances referred under labor laws and will need to train its administrative law judges on the bill's provisions.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to include in an annual report to certain committees of the General Assembly the amount of proceeds from a certain agricultural land transfer tax that are attributable to the taxation of certain instruments of writing that transfer title to parcels of land that are entirely woodland that were distributed to the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund during the immediately preceding fiscal year; and requiring the Department to report any uncertainties regarding certain amounts.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to expand annual reporting on the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund. Mandates reporting agricultural land transfer tax proceeds from entirely woodland parcels distributed during the preceding fiscal year. Requires the department to explain any uncertainties regarding required distribution amounts and actions necessary to resolve them. Directs the department to submit this report annually by September 30 to two legislative committees. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Private woodland owners participating in the Woodland Incentives Program, students seeking natural resources careers through the Mel Noland Fellowship Program, and the Department of Natural Resources
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the Department of Natural Resources can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Natural Resources to expand its annual reporting on the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund to include the amount of agricultural land transfer tax proceeds distributed to the fund and any uncertainties regarding those distributions.

The Comptroller receives remitted agricultural land transfer tax revenues and oversees state fund distributions, making the agency relevant to the accounting and resolution of any uncertainties regarding transfer tax proceeds credited to the fund.

Synopsis: Increasing from $50,000 to $100,000 the maximum amount of annual revenue a business may generate from the sale of cottage food products to be considered a cottage food business.
Title: Food Establishments - Cottage Food Businesses - Maximum Annual Revenue

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: Increases the maximum annual revenue limit for a cottage food business from $50,000 to $100,000. Allows qualifying residential kitchen operations to generate up to $100,000 annually without obtaining a commercial food manufacturer license. Regulates businesses producing or packaging nonhazardous cottage food products in a residential kitchen. Requires these businesses to continue complying with State labeling rules and food safety course requirements. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: cottage food business owners, home-based food producers, consumers, and retail food stores
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $52,434 in FY 2027 to hire one part-time registered sanitarian, increasing to $67,700 by FY 2031. General fund revenues face a potential minimal decrease starting in FY 2027 if businesses opt out of commercial food manufacturer licensing. Local health departments can handle any workload changes using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary regulatory agency overseeing cottage food businesses, including processing submissions, reviewing labels and food safety certifications, and issuing unique identification numbers under Health - General § 21-301. The bill directly impacts MDH by increasing its general fund expenditures to hire staff to manage the increased volume of cottage food businesses.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture promotes local agricultural products and oversees venues like farmers' markets where cottage food products are commonly sold directly to consumers. MDA was also consulted as an information source on the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to make available a professional development course on educator well-being and flourishing to school personnel and administrators on or before July 1, 2027; and requiring the Department to make the course available only if it can be provided at no cost or at a cost comparable to that which the Department pays for providing a commensurate course.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to offer an educator well-being and flourishing course by July 1, 2027. Makes the course available synchronously or asynchronously to all school personnel and administrators. Mandates the course only if the department can provide it at no cost or comparable cost. Requires instruction on eight dimensions of well-being identified by the federal Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration. Sets the course fee at a rate comparable to courses with equivalent professional development points. Terminates the statutory provisions on June 30, 2031.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Maryland school personnel and administrators
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland State Department of Education can use existing resources to provide an existing course, and statutory requirements are contingent on no-cost or comparable-cost availability. Local school system finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 546 directly requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to make available a professional development course on educator well-being and flourishing for school personnel and administrators, covering the eight dimensions of well-being.

Synopsis: Requiring the Secretary of Agriculture, by December 1, 2026, and each December 1 thereafter, to report to the Governor and the General Assembly on additional types of equipment that the Secretary recommends should qualify for the subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for enhanced agricultural management equipment; allowing a certain parent of a stillborn child a refundable credit of $1,000 against the State income tax for each birth for which a certain certificate has been issued; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Enhanced Agricultural Management Equipment Subtraction Modification and Parent of a Stillborn Child Credit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes a refundable $1,000 State income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child. Reduces the credit by $50 per $1,000 of income exceeding $100,000 for individuals or $150,000 for joint filers. Authorizes claiming the credit only for the taxable year in which the stillbirth occurred. Applies the tax credit to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026. Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to report annually to the Governor and General Assembly on additional qualifying agricultural equipment.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland income taxpayers who are parents of a stillborn child, agricultural producers, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will decrease beginning in fiscal 2028 due to the refundable income tax credit, but specific estimates are unquantified in the available fiscal note. The Maryland Department of Agriculture can complete annual reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller administers the state income tax system and is responsible for implementing the new refundable income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child as well as overseeing the subtraction modification for enhanced agricultural management equipment.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Agriculture to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly recommending additional types of equipment that should qualify for the enhanced agricultural management equipment subtraction modification.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the annual report required from the Secretary of Agriculture regarding recommended agricultural equipment qualifying for tax subtractions.

The bill establishes a tax credit contingent upon receiving a Certificate of Birth Resulting in Stillbirth issued under § 4-213.1 of the Health - General Article, which is maintained and issued by the Maryland Department of Health's vital records division.

Synopsis: Requiring the approval of a housing development project application by a local regulatory authority or the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission to be governed only by certain laws and regulations in effect at the time of submission of a complete application; granting the proponent of an approved housing development project certain vested rights related to use and development for the longer of 5 years or a period determined by the local regulatory authority of the Commission; etc.
Title: Land Use - Permitting - Development Rights (Maryland Housing Certainty Act)

bill_summary: Governs housing development application approvals under local laws and regulations in effect when a complete application is submitted. Requires regulatory authorities to determine whether an application is complete within 30 days of receipt. Grants approved housing development project proponents a vested development right for at least five years. Prohibits local governments from collecting development excise taxes or impact fees until project construction is complete. Exempts taxes or impact fees imposed to finance county debt incurred on or before January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland–National Capital Park and Planning Commission; local regulatory authorities
stakeholders: Housing developers, residential construction businesses, county governments, and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances. Local government revenues from residential development impact fees and excise taxes will be delayed until construction completion. Local government expenditures may increase in certain jurisdictions for personnel and tracking systems to implement required application review timelines and vested right durations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Land Use Article to regulate local land use application procedures, vesting of development rights, and local development impact fees. The Department of Planning provides guidance, technical assistance, and land use policy support to local governments as they implement these changes.

The bill directly impacts the regulatory predictability, timeline, and fee structure of residential housing development projects statewide, aligning with DHCD's core mission to promote housing development and affordability across Maryland.

Title: Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children - Establishment

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children to research resident deaths and unmarked graves. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to staff the Commission and administer its funding. Authorizes the Commission to conduct archaeological surveys, excavations, disinterments, and forensic DNA analyses without separate agency permits. Grants the Commission and its contractors unrestricted access to sealed juvenile, medical, and administrative records. Requires the Commission to submit an initial progress report by December 31, 2027, and a final report by December 31, 2029.
responsible_party: Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Descendants of deceased children buried at the facility, former residents of the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children, justice-involved youth, and African American communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,050,000 in FY 2027, reflecting funding included in the FY 2027 State budget for the cemetery project, with potential additional indeterminate expenses in FY 2028 and FY 2029. The Office of the Attorney General can provide staff using existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Attorney General as Chair of the newly established Commission, requires the Office of the Attorney General to provide staff, grants the office authority to procure goods and services and administer funding/grants, and authorizes the Attorney General to appoint public members and issue subpoenas.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services is an ex officio member of the Commission. The subject of the investigation, the former House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children, operated on the grounds of what is now DJS's Cheltenham Youth Detention Center, and DJS holds relevant records, historical ties, and related cemetery project funding.
The State Archivist is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission, and the investigation will extensively access and rely upon historical archives and records held by the agency.

The Director of the Maryland Historical Trust (a division of the Department of Planning) is an ex officio member of the Commission, and the Commission is explicitly required to consult with the Trust regarding methods and safety for disinterment and archaeological excavations.

The Commission is mandated to consult with the Maryland Department of Health regarding methods and safety for disinterment and excavation, and the investigation requires access to historical health, vital, and medical records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an executive commission (Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children) operating with a four-year sunset to study historical deaths and abuses and make formal recommendations.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.
MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, whose Chief Archaeologist is mandated to serve on the Commission.
The Secretary of General Services (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission.

The State Superintendent of Schools is a member of the Commission, and the Commission is charged with recommending educational initiatives to incorporate this history into the state's school curriculum.
The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission, and the department collaborates on cemetery conservation planning.
The Executive Director of the Gibson-Banks Center for Race and Law at the University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law is named as a statutory member of the Commission.
The Commission must submit an initial report by December 31, 2027, and a final report by December 31, 2029, directly to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to post a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates on the Maryland Department of Labor's website; and requiring the database to be searchable by street address, city, and county.
Title: Public Safety - Elevator Inspection Certificates - Searchable Database
bill_summary: Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to post a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates. Directs the Commissioner to publish the database on the Maryland Department of Labor's website. Mandates that the database allow users to search active certificates by street address, city, and county. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: owners and lessees of elevator units and members of the public seeking elevator inspection information
fiscal_impact_summary: Requirements can likely be implemented using existing budgeted resources. If existing online resources do not meet the bill's searchable database requirements, general fund expenditures may increase by an estimated $75,000 for a system module. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor to establish and maintain a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates on the department's website, potentially requiring up to $75,000 in expenditures to upgrade existing database capabilities.

Synopsis: Adding the Chair of the House Government, Labor, and Elections Committee to the Legislative Policy Committee; and updating the committees of the General Assembly that receive certain required reports and notices.

bill_summary: Updates the membership of the Legislative Policy Committee and names of standing legislative committees in State law. Adds the Chair of the House Government, Labor, and Elections Committee to the Legislative Policy Committee. Decreases the number of additional Delegates appointed to the Legislative Policy Committee from four to three. Updates statutory references to reflect the House Health Committee and Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment. Redirects specified agency reports and regulatory notices to the updated legislative committees.
responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly; Legislative Policy Committee
stakeholders: members of the Maryland General Assembly, standing legislative committees, and State agencies required to submit reports or notices to legislative committees
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances or governmental operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 554 updates several sections of the Health - General Article governing reporting and notice requirements for the Maryland Department of Health (including tobacco and cancer grant allocations, Medicaid long-term care eligibility modifications, and regulatory notices) to reflect the renamed House Health Committee.

The bill updates statutory provisions in the Insurance Article requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Board to submit proposed regulations and active purchasing/contracting strategy plans to the renamed House Health Committee.

The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article to update the legislative committees (House Health Committee and Senate Finance Committee) to which the Commissioner of Labor and Industry must submit notices and recommendations regarding the federal Bloodborne Pathogen Standard.

The bill updates the committee titles under the State Government Article for the legislative chairs who may formally request the State Archivist to review, evaluate, and provide recommendations on official State designations.

Synopsis: Providing that "department" does not include the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services for purposes of certain provisions prohibiting a department from refusing to issue an occupational license or certificate based on a certain conviction under certain circumstances; establishing a predetermination review process for occupational licenses and certificates in certain departments of State government; authorizing a department to charge a criminal history review fee of up to $100; etc.
Title: Occupational Licensing and Certification - Criminal History - Predetermination Review Process

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes a predetermination review process to evaluate whether an individual's criminal history disqualifies them from occupational licensure. Makes the department's predetermination binding unless a subsequent direct and material adverse change occurs in the criminal history. Authorizes departments to charge a criminal history review fee up to $100, subject to an income waiver. Excludes mortgage loan originator applicants and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services from these provisions. Requires five State departments to report predetermination requests and associated implementation costs by October 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: individuals with criminal histories seeking State occupational licenses or certifications; applicants for mortgage loan originator licensure
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $50,800 in FY 2027, $22,500 in FY 2028, and $23,500 in FY 2029 for the Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland Department of Agriculture. State special fund revenues experience an indeterminate but minimal net impact depending on review fee collections and application volumes. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is one of the primary departments required to establish the binding predetermination review process for occupational licenses and submit a report by October 1, 2028. The fiscal note identifies an increase in special fund expenditures for MD Labor to hire contractual staff to administer the process.

MDA is explicitly subject to the predetermination review requirements and reporting mandate under the bill, with the fiscal note noting an increase in special fund expenditures for programming updates for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners.

MDH is directly named as an implementing department that must offer the predetermination review process across its occupational licensing boards and submit an implementation report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

MDE is designated as an implementing department responsible for conducting predetermination reviews for occupational licenses or certificates under its jurisdiction and submitting a reporting update by October 1, 2028.

DHS is designated as an implementing department responsible for conducting predetermination reviews for applicable occupational certificates or licenses under its jurisdiction and reporting on its implementation by October 1, 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly amends the law to exclude DPSCS from the statutory definition of 'department' subject to these occupational licensing review and non-denial requirements.

Synopsis: Repealing the restriction on the number of wine festival licenses that the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County may issue annually; and repealing a prohibition on issuing a wine festival license for use in the 24th legislative district.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Wine Festival Licenses PG 316-26
bill_summary: Repeals the annual limit of one wine festival license that the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County may issue. Authorizes the Board to issue multiple wine festival licenses each year to eligible retail and winery license holders. Allows the Board to select multiple festival weekends, Friday through Sunday, each year. Removes the prohibition on holding a wine festival within the 24th legislative district. Requires the primary focus of each wine festival to remain the promotion of Maryland wine.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County
stakeholders: holders of retail, Class 3 winery, and Class 4 limited winery licenses in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State operations or finances. Prince George's County local revenues increase minimally from issuing up to three additional wine festival licenses annually at a fee of $75 each.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates aspects of the alcohol industry and collects alcoholic beverage excise and sales taxes. Although this legislation specifically pertains to local wine festival licenses administered by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it touches upon alcoholic beverage distribution and sales involving state-licensed wineries and wholesalers.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor, in each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030, to appropriate to the Maryland Child Care Credential Program $5,687,000.
Title: Maryland Child Care Credential Program - Extension of Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appropriate $5,687,000 annually for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program from fiscal 2028 through 2030. Reestablishes mandated state funding for the credentialing program. Supports awards for staff credentials, child development associate credentials, and administrator credentials. Authorizes the Office of Child Care to award achievement bonuses, training reimbursements, and training vouchers. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Office of Child Care
stakeholders: child care providers, staff, and administrators pursuing or holding child care credentials
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.7 million annually from fiscal 2028 through 2030 to fund the mandated appropriation for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Child Care Credential Program is administered by the Office of Child Care within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which oversees credentialing, achievement bonuses, training reimbursements, and vouchers for child care providers.

The Department of Budget and Management prepares and oversees the state budget, which must incorporate the bill's statutory mandated appropriation of $5,687,000 annually for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.
The bill explicitly mandates the Governor to include an appropriation of $5,687,000 for the program in the state budget bill for each of fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition against intentionally inflicting bodily harm, permanent disability, or death on an animal owned or used by a law enforcement unit; prohibiting a person from harassing, interfering with, injuring, or killing or causing serious physical injury to an emergency response animal; and establishing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to imprisonment for up to 2 years, or a fine of up to $10,000, or both upon conviction.
Title: Criminal Law - Emergency Response Animal - Prohibited Actions Against

bill_summary: Repeals the felony offense of intentionally inflicting bodily harm, permanent disability, or death on a law enforcement animal. Prohibits intentionally harassing, interfering with, injuring, or killing an emergency response animal. Defines emergency response animals to include specified police dogs, police horses, and search and rescue dogs. Establishes misdemeanor penalties including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to $10,000. Allows the defense of necessity and an affirmative defense against unlawful police use of force.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State and local law enforcement units
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, emergency response animal handlers, search and rescue personnel, and individuals accused of offenses against emergency response animals.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not materially affected. Minor case-flow shifts may occur between the circuit courts and the District Court, but penalty adjustments will not significantly alter revenues or incarceration expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police utilizes trained law enforcement animals (such as K-9 units) in its daily policing, detection, and tracking duties, and investigates criminal violations involving interference with or injury to law enforcement animals.
The bill alters criminal penalties from a felony to specific misdemeanor offenses, impacting judicial caseload distribution between the District Court and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters sentencing, establishing misdemeanor terms of imprisonment ranging up to five years, which impacts state correctional and local detention operations and community supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new misdemeanor criminal offenses carrying potential terms of incarceration and sets specific affirmative defenses, directly affecting the representation of indigent defendants charged under this section.

The Department of Natural Resources Police employs trained K-9 units for conservation law enforcement and frequently participates in search and rescue efforts covered under the definition of emergency response animals.
The bill protects search and rescue dogs engaged in state-directed search and rescue operations, which fall under coordinated emergency response efforts managed and supported by MDEM.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel on criminal law enforcement and handles any subsequent appellate litigation arising from convictions or legal challenges regarding the Maryland Use of Force Statute defense.

bill_summary: Establishes consumer protection and disclosure requirements for registered cemetery operators and licensed crematories providing pet cremation services. Requires providers to distribute detailed written descriptions of available pet cremation services to owners, veterinarians, and the Department of Agriculture. Mandates written certification verifying the cremation date and identity of pet cremains returned to pet owners. Directs providers to maintain holding facilities that preserve dignity and to retain detailed cremation records for at least five years. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with reviewing and updating regulations for the Irreplaceable Natural Areas Program, determining threatened and endangered species listings and delistings, designating essential habitats, and regulating the taking of species and migratory birds.

Under statutory provisions referenced in the bill, the Secretary of Natural Resources is required to consult with the Secretary of Agriculture regarding conservation programs for nongame, endangered, or threatened wildlife and plants. Additionally, the bill addresses depredation permits for black vultures, a species known to cause agricultural and livestock damage.

MDOT manages extensive state infrastructure and capital projects that may face regulatory delays, modifications, or increased compliance costs resulting from expanded definitions of harm and the designation of essential habitats for protected species.
DGS oversees the planning, construction, and management of state facilities and capital programs, which may be affected by strengthened protections for endangered and threatened species habitats.
The bill touches upon existing statutory provisions directing the Governor to review and utilize state programs in furtherance of endangered and threatened species conservation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 587 establishes a workgroup focused on the procurement and contract approval authority for capital expenditures by the Department of Transportation (MDOT). The Secretary of Transportation serves on the workgroup, and MDOT is tasked with jointly providing staff for the workgroup.

The bill centers on studying whether and how the Board of Public Works (BPW) should exercise contract approval and oversight authority over transportation capital expenditures, and mandates that BPW jointly staff the workgroup alongside MDOT.

The workgroup is tasked specifically with reviewing and evaluating the approval authority structure, contract awards, change orders, and potential BPW oversight for capital expenditures made by the Maryland Transportation Authority.
The Comptroller of Maryland, or the Comptroller's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority.
The State Treasurer, or the State Treasurer's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority.
The Governor appoints four members to the workgroup, designates the chair, and receives the workgroup's final report and recommendations by December 1, 2026.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the state highway network and standard traffic control specifications affected by the bill.

The bill sets legal conditions under which citations may be issued for standing in inherently dangerous roadways, which are processed through the District Court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill establishes restrictions and requirements on when police officers can issue citations for standing on specified roadways and highways within Wicomico County, which affects Maryland State Police troopers patrolling the area.

bill_summary: Expands an existing computer-related offense to include acts intended to interrupt or impair critical infrastructure. Prohibits unauthorized computer acts that deny authorized access to or interrupt critical infrastructure or a public safety answering point. Establishes a felony penalty of up to 10 years of imprisonment, a fine up to $50,000, or both. Defines critical infrastructure as physical or virtual systems vital to public safety, security, transportation, health, or utilities.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the custody and supervision of individuals sentenced to terms of incarceration. The bill expands criminal penalties and creates a new felony offense with sentences up to 10 years imprisonment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

DoIT manages cybersecurity, statewide IT networks, and digital infrastructure for state executive agencies, which are classified as critical virtual systems protected under the statute.
GOHS coordinates statewide strategy for disaster prevention, emergency readiness, and the protection and resilience of Maryland's critical infrastructure.

bill_summary: Conforms the Maryland Uniform Simultaneous Death Act to the uniform act adopted by the Uniform Law Commission. Deems an individual to have predeceased another if survivorship by at least 120 hours is not established. Divides survivorship property equally or proportionally among co-owners who do not survive each other by 120 hours. Establishes evidentiary rules for proving death and presumes death after five continuous years of unexplained absence. Shields third-party payors from liability for good-faith distributions made before receiving written notice of conflicting claims. Exempts distributions where application causes escheat to the State or contradicts express governing instrument terms.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is responsible for the administrative probate of decedents' estates and serving as clerk to the Orphans' Court. This bill substantively alters the legal rules governing survivorship (establishing a 120-hour survival requirement) which directly governs how estates are administered and how assets are distributed when related individuals die simultaneously or in close succession.

The bill establishes procedural and evidentiary standards for determining survivorship and death in judicial proceedings, and explicitly provides that payors may deposit disputed assets with the court having jurisdiction over probate proceedings, directly impacting court procedures and administration.

fiscal_impact_summary: Local revenues for St. Mary's County and the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 from higher fines and penalties. State operations and local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that the required depository and fidelity bond given by the Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer of the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission must be in a form approved by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

The bill modifies criminal penalty thresholds, civil infraction citation procedures, and judicial enforcement remedies handled by the District Court in St. Mary's County, which is supported administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

bill_summary: Authorizes the use of stop sign monitoring systems in school zones within the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville. Requires local authorization by local law enacted after reasonable notice and a public hearing before system deployment. Imposes a civil penalty of up to $40 on vehicle owners or drivers recorded failing to stop. Directs citation revenues toward program administration costs and local public safety programs. Requires each city to report program costs, revenues, and safety outcomes to state officials by December 1, 2028. Sunsets the pilot program on June 30, 2029.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers in the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville, pedestrians and students in local school zones, and municipal law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2030 from contested citations. Indeterminate increase in revenues and expenditures for the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville to the extent that each city elects to deploy stop sign monitoring systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the State Highway Administration to authorize the use of stop sign monitoring systems if placed on State highways in school zones, and mandates that SHA prominently place signage providing notice that the systems are in use on State highways.

The District Court (supported by AOC) is tasked with prescribing a uniform citation form, establishing civil penalty procedures, adjudicating contested citations, and coordinating citation processing and evidence sharing with local enforcement agencies.

The MVA is authorized to refuse vehicle registration or reregistration or suspend registration if penalties are unpaid and uncontested, and is prohibited from recording the violation as a moving violation or assessing points on driving records.

MDOT is the parent department overseeing both the State Highway Administration and the Motor Vehicle Administration, both of which have specific statutory roles and operational impacts under the bill.
The bill requires the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville to report comprehensive program implementation and evaluation data to the Governor by December 1, 2028.
Under statutory automated enforcement provisions referenced in the fiscal note, any citation revenues exceeding 10% of total local revenues must be remitted to the Comptroller.

Synopsis: Altering the collective bargaining process for certain State employees, including by requiring the selection of a neutral arbitrator to oversee certain aspects of collective bargaining and establishing a process of arbitration in the event of impasse in negotiations between certain parties; requiring that each budget bill submitted by the Governor contain the appropriations necessary to implement all terms and conditions of employment in certain memoranda of understanding for the next ensuing fiscal year; etc.
Title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026
