bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution requiring the Governor to budget funds for all State employee memoranda of understanding. Establishes a binding arbitration process to resolve collective bargaining impasses for certain State employees. Requires bargaining parties to select a neutral arbitrator if negotiations do not conclude by September 15. Expands mandatory collective bargaining subjects to include health benefits and fringe benefits other than pension benefits. Makes statutory collective bargaining changes contingent on voter approval of the constitutional amendment in November 2026.
responsible_party: Office of the Governor; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: State employees and exclusive employee bargaining representatives; State institutions of higher education; Maryland Environmental Service
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by at least $150,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2028 for arbitration services and personnel, with potentially significant impacts on personnel expenditures beginning in fiscal 2029 depending on arbitration awards. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the principal personnel and fiscal agency for Maryland state government. It leads collective bargaining on behalf of the State, oversees state employee compensation and health benefits (which are expanded under the bill), manages arbitration proceedings and costs, and prepares the annual state budget bill where funding for agreements must be included.

The bill proposes an amendment to Article III, Section 52 of the Maryland Constitution requiring the Governor to include appropriations in the annual budget bill to implement all terms of MOUs and binding arbitration awards for State and higher education employees.

MES is explicitly governed by the bill's collective bargaining and arbitration provisions. The proposed constitutional amendment and statutory changes require the Governor to fund MES memoranda of understanding in the state budget bill, which could fundamentally affect MES's nonbudgeted operational status.

USM and its Chancellor are explicitly subject to the bill's provisions regarding collective bargaining, memoranda of understanding, and the constitutional requirement that the Governor include appropriations in the budget bill to fund employee agreement terms.

Morgan State University's governing board is explicitly designated as a bargaining party under the statute, and its employee memoranda of understanding are subject to the required budget appropriations under the proposed constitutional amendment.

St. Mary's College of Maryland's governing board is explicitly named as a bargaining representative party, and its negotiated agreements are subject to the bill's collective bargaining provisions and mandated budget inclusion.

PERB administers collective bargaining laws for State and higher education employees and retains jurisdiction over unfair labor practice complaints that may arise during collective bargaining or the neutral arbitration process.
The State Board of Elections is responsible for administering the statewide general election ballot question in November 2026 for voter adoption or rejection of the proposed constitutional amendment.

MDOT oversees state transportation employees, including the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department and MDTA personnel covered under Title 3 collective bargaining, with specific carve-outs and arbitration procedures preserved in the bill.

The OAG provides legal advice to the Governor, DBM, and state agencies regarding the implementation of binding arbitration, collective bargaining statutory interpretations, and the ballot question language for the constitutional amendment.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for property tax payment deferrals in Anne Arundel County to include members of certain reserve components and certain members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Residential Property Tax Payment Deferrals - Eligibility
bill_summary: Expands eligibility for residential property tax payment deferrals in Anne Arundel County. Applies the deferral to permanently and totally disabled homeowners who qualify for federal benefits as service members. Includes members of reserve components, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Public Health Service. Requires qualifying homeowners to have resided in the dwelling for at least five consecutive years. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: permanently and totally disabled homeowners in Anne Arundel County who are service members, including members of reserve components, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Public Health Service
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County property tax revenues may experience a potential minimal decrease during deferral periods depending on participation, with revenues recouped upon repayment. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands property tax payment deferral eligibility in Anne Arundel County for disabled individuals by broadening the definition from United States armed forces to service members, including reserve components, NOAA, and the Public Health Service. DVMF is responsible for assisting and advocating for Maryland service members, veterans, and their families regarding benefits and resources.

The bill amends eligibility criteria related to permanent and total disability qualifications for residential property tax payment deferrals in Anne Arundel County, touching upon state policies and relief options available to individuals with disabilities.

Synopsis: Providing for the annual salaries of the Comptroller, the Treasurer, the Attorney General, and the Secretary of State.

bill_summary: Establishes statutory annual salary schedules for the Comptroller, the Treasurer, the Attorney General, and the Secretary of State. Sets salaries for the Comptroller, Treasurer, and Attorney General at $175,000 for terms beginning in January 2027. Increases those three salaries to $180,000 in the second and third years and $185,000 in the fourth year. Sets the Secretary of State's salary at $120,000 in 2027, increasing to $128,000 by the fourth year. Applies salary adjustments to terms of office beginning January 2027 in accordance with constitutional requirements.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland State Treasurer; Maryland Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Secretary of State
stakeholders: The Comptroller of Maryland, the Maryland State Treasurer, the Attorney General of Maryland, and the Maryland Secretary of State
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,800 in FY 2028, growing to $43,000 in FY 2031 to cover statutory salary and fringe benefit increases for the four constitutional officers. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the Comptroller for the term beginning in January 2027.
HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the State Treasurer for the term beginning in January 2027.
HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the Attorney General for the term beginning in January 2027.
HB 607 directly establishes and increases the statutory annual salary schedule for the Secretary of State for the term of appointment beginning in January 2027.

As the State's principal budget and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for managing executive branch salary schedules, fringe benefits, and incorporating general fund expenditure increases into future state budgets.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill implements the formal recommendations submitted by the Governor's Salary Commission regarding constitutional officer compensation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland and a judge who serves as an administrative judge for a circuit court or the District Court to receive an annual stipend in addition to the judge's annual salary; and altering the compensation of the Chairman of the Worker's Compensation Commission to be at least equal to the salary of the Chief Judge of the District Court.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland to receive an annual stipend in addition to annual salary. Permits a judge serving as an administrative judge for a circuit court or the District Court to receive the stipend. Alters the minimum annual salary of the Chairman of the State Workers' Compensation Commission. Requires the Chairman's salary to at least equal the salary of the Chief Judge of the District Court. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Judiciary; State Workers' Compensation Commission
stakeholders: Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland, administrative judges of the circuit courts and District Court, and the Chairman of the State Workers' Compensation Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: State Workers' Compensation Commission special fund expenditures increase by $22,300 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to align the Chairman's salary with that of the Chief Judge of the District Court. Fiscal impacts of judicial administrative stipends are accounted for under separate enacted joint resolutions. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by authorizing annual stipends for the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland and judges serving as administrative judges for a circuit court or the District Court, whose administrative and financial operations are supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill directly modifies the compensation structure for the Chairman of the State Workers' Compensation Commission to equal at least the salary of the Chief Judge of the District Court, resulting in an annual increase in special fund expenditures of approximately $22,300 beginning in FY 2027.

Synopsis: Requiring a qualified organization to hold a gaming permit whenever the qualified organization operates a certain gaming device in St. Mary's County; authorizing the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to adopt certain regulations; and requiring the Board to designate a person to administer the issuance of gaming permits in the county.

bill_summary: Requires a qualified organization to hold a gaming permit whenever operating a gaming device in St. Mary's County. Defines a gaming device as a mechanism for playing a game of chance, excluding slot machines. Requires the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to designate a person to administer gaming permit issuance. responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County
stakeholders: Qualified organizations operating gaming devices in St. Mary's County, including volunteer fire companies and bona fide religious, fraternal, civic, war veterans', and charitable organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. St. Mary's County can administer permits and enforce provisions with existing resources, and county revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's regulatory body for gaming operations, the Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency tracks gaming policy in the state, although the permitting and administration under this bill are delegated directly to St. Mary's County.

Under current law in this subtitle, Maryland State Police officers are authorized along with local law enforcement to inspect records of gaming devices and proceeds held by qualified organizations in the county.

bill_summary: Requires property improvements for shoreline erosion protection to consist of living shorelines or nonstructural measures unless demonstrated infeasible. Directs the Department of the Environment to adopt waiver regulations and develop a scoring system for evaluating waiver requests. Requires the Department to conduct site visits within 45 days upon owner request during waiver reviews. Requires the Department to notify local soil conservation districts and provide an opportunity for recommendations on waiver requests. Directs the Department to engage stakeholders on waiver alterations and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Riparian and waterfront property owners, local soil conservation districts, and marine contractors and businesses involved in shoreline stabilization projects
fiscal_impact_summary: MDE can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State and local expenditures for shoreline stabilization projects may increase beginning in fiscal 2027. MDE special fund revenues from application fees may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 if more structural projects are pursued. Specific dollar amounts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for administering the living shorelines and nonstructural shoreline stabilization regulations, developing and publishing a waiver evaluation scoring system, conducting site visits upon request, notifying local soil conservation districts, leading stakeholder engagement, and reporting progress to the General Assembly.
The bill amends and replaces provisions in the Natural Resources Article and requires MDE to consult with DNR in adopting regulations related to shoreline stabilization and waiver procedures.

The bill mandates that MDE provide local soil conservation districts with written notice and the opportunity to make recommendations on waiver requests. Local soil conservation districts coordinate closely with and are overseen through agricultural conservation programs under MDA.

The Board of Public Works possesses statutory authority over State wetlands licenses (often delegated to MDE), is referenced in the underlying tidal wetlands statute, and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an occupant from using the occupant's self-service storage facility beyond the term of a rental agreement after delivery of a notice of nonrenewal; requiring an operator to give an occupant at least 30 days after delivery of a notice of nonrenewal to remove the occupant's personal property from the self-service storage facility; requiring an operator to give an occupant notice of intent to dispose of the occupant's personal property at least 10 days before the operator disposes of that personal property; etc.

bill_summary: Expands the definition of self-service storage rental agreements to include electronic agreements. Prohibits occupants from using a self-service storage facility beyond the lease term after receiving nonrenewal notice. Requires operators to give occupants at least 30 days and until term end to remove property. Authorizes operators to dispose of remaining personal property after providing at least 10 days' notice. Requires a second notice by verified mail when an emailed notice receives no confirmation within five days. Requires rental agreements to include a statement advising occupants to remove property upon nonrenewal.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Owners and operators of self-service storage facilities, and occupants renting space in self-service storage facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces Maryland's consumer protection laws under the Commercial Law Article and served as an information source regarding the bill's changes to self-service storage rental agreements, notices, and disposal procedures.

bill_summary: Enacts the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact to create an expedited pathway for multistate podiatric licensure. Authorizes an eligible podiatrist to obtain an expedited license to practice podiatric medicine in member states. Requires applicants to meet specified examination, education, residency, certification, and criminal background check standards. Establishes the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission to administer compact operations and promulgate binding rules. Requires member boards to report disciplinary actions and share investigative information through a coordinated database. Conditions Maryland's participation on the enactment of substantially similar legislation in four other states.
responsible_party: State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners; Maryland Department of Health; Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission
stakeholders: Podiatrists seeking expedited multistate licensure, podiatric patients in Maryland and member states, and the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures and revenues for the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners likely increase by an indeterminate amount upon entry into the compact due to annual commission assessments, coordinated database requirements, and expedited license application fees. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enacts an interstate licensure compact governing podiatrists, directly impacting the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners housed within MDH. The department is directly responsible for notifying the Department of Legislative Services once four states enact similar legislation, and BPME will handle the licensure requirements, database reporting, background checks, and associated special fund revenue/expenditures.

The bill creates Maryland's membership in a new multistate compact and interstate body, the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission, which falls directly under the collective classification of interstate compacts and commissions in which Maryland participates.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to MDH and its licensing boards. The bill specifically requires the approval of the Attorney General or appropriate legal counsel regarding the legal defense of Interstate Commission representatives in civil liability actions.

The Interstate Commission must submit annual reports and financial statements to the Governor, and the Governor receives official statutory notices regarding any member state defaults, terminations, or withdrawals from the compact.

bill_summary: Alters voter registration qualifications for legal counsel appointed or retained by a local board of elections. Authorizes each local board of elections to appoint or retain counsel who is a registered voter of the State. Removes the requirement that board counsel must reside as a registered voter in the board's specific county. Maintains the requirement that counsel must be admitted to practice law in Maryland. Takes effect immediately upon enactment as an emergency measure.
responsible_party: Local boards of elections
stakeholders: Local boards of elections and Maryland-admitted attorneys seeking appointment as board counsel
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections oversees the administration of election laws and the activities of local boards of elections throughout the state. This bill alters the statutory qualifications required for counsel appointed or retained by local boards of elections.

Extends the authorization for converted medical cannabis dispensaries to deliver medical cannabis until July 1, 2027. responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
stakeholders: micro dispensary licensees, converted medical cannabis dispensary licensees, registered cannabis agents, on-site consumption establishment employees, and cannabis training program providers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Cannabis Administration can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

bill_summary: Establishes the Purple Star Colleges Program to recognize colleges that provide strong services and support for military-connected students. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to administer the program and adopt implementing regulations. Requires participating colleges to designate a uniformed services liaison and establish a dedicated resource webpage. Requires qualifying colleges to maintain student-led transition programs and offer staff professional development. Identical listing for MHEC, which serves as the primary agency responsible for administering and regulating the Purple Star Colleges Program.
MSDE oversees the Purple Star Schools Program, and the bill amends the statutory definition of 'military-connected student' under this existing program.
DVMF advocates for and supports veterans, active-duty service members, and their families, aligning closely with the bill's focus on military-connected students and collegiate support services.
USM member institutions are public higher education institutions eligible to voluntarily seek Purple Star College designation by meeting required support service and staffing criteria.
As a public university, Morgan State may elect to participate in the program and seek designation as a Purple Star College by providing the required military-connected student supports.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College is eligible to seek designation as a Purple Star College under the program.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health

Local government and higher education finances have no material direct fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 625 designates the Department of Agriculture as the agency responsible for collecting annual contributions from qualifying animal research facilities, enforcing penalties for noncompliance, and distributing the collected funds to the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

The bill repeals the statutory provisions in the Health - General Article that tasked the Maryland Department of Health with collecting contributions from research facilities, thereby relieving MDH of this duty.

TEDCO administers the Human-Relevant Research Fund, which receives the contributions collected under the bill to fund research into alternatives to animal testing. Changes in collection effectiveness directly affect the fund's revenues and grant/loan expenditures.

Public higher education research institutions under USM that report animal research under USDA APHIS Form 7023 are subject to the required fee assessments, will submit payments to MDA instead of MDH, and are eligible to apply for grant and loan funding from the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to mandate specific police training curriculum across Maryland. Applies to entrance-level training and commission-determined in-service training at State, county, and municipal police training schools. Directs the curriculum to cover training regarding individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, and autism. Mandates instruction on locating wandering individuals, searching near water bodies, and using sensory-aware approaches. Includes training on reunification, documentation, and interagency coordination. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
stakeholders: State, county, and municipal police officers and trainees; State, county, and municipal police training schools; individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, or autism
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations. Local expenditures may experience a minimal increase to conduct additional training if local schools do not already provide it. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which establishes training standards and curriculums for law enforcement statewide, is housed within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency operating its own training academy, the Maryland State Police must incorporate the required curriculum on autism, dementia, and developmental disabilities into its entrance-level and in-service officer training programs.

The Department oversees the Maryland Natural Resources Police, whose sworn officers must complete police training programs that adhere to MPTSC standards, including the new training requirements for searching near water and locating missing individuals.

Mandates the Maryland State Department of Education to establish a centralized background check processing unit by June 30, 2027. Lowers the age threshold from three years to two years for probationary child care teacher qualification rules. Repeals the statutory cap on the number of Deputy State Superintendents of Schools. Requires the Department to review background check procedures and report findings by October 1, 2028.

fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education is anticipated to implement the bill's requirements with existing budgetary resources, resulting in minimal state fiscal impact. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency under the bill. It removes the statutory cap on Deputy State Superintendents, requires MSDE to establish a centralized unit by June 30, 2027 to manage child care background checks, alters probationary qualifications for child care teachers, and mandates a comprehensive review and report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references and relies upon DPSCS's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) to process and disseminate the criminal history records checks to MSDE's centralized unit, requiring ongoing operational coordination between the two agencies.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Secretary of Health to issue clinical recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services. Mandates a 30-day comment period and health commission analysis before adopting certain non-immunization preventive recommendations. Authorizes licensed pharmacists to administer Secretary-recommended vaccines to individuals at least seven years old. Requires health insurance carriers to cover recommended preventive services and child wellness immunizations without cost sharing. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Health to issue, publish, and distribute recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services, and directly expands the scope of vaccines pharmacists may administer based on the Secretary's determinations.

The Insurance Commissioner and MIA are responsible for enforcing health insurance coverage mandates and cost-sharing prohibitions updated by the Secretary of Health's recommendations, and MIA will experience a minimal special fund revenue increase from rate and form filings.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Health to obtain an impact analysis from the Maryland Health Care Commission pursuant to § 15-1501 of the Insurance Article before adopting recommendations for certain preventive services.
This is an Administration priority bill ('The Vax Act') introduced by request of the Governor to protect public health standards and preventive care access in Maryland.

bill_summary: Repeals multiple obsolete or unnecessary state boards, commissions, and reporting requirements across various state agencies. Eliminates the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board, the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board, and the Commission on Trauma-Informed Care. Transfers renewable fuels credit certification and payment responsibilities directly to the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Authorizes reasonable compensation and expense reimbursement for Interagency Council on Homelessness members who have experienced homelessness. Replaces specialized intervention service reports with annual third-grade literacy proficiency reporting by local school boards. Alters membership compositions, reporting deadlines, and term lengths for various statutory advisory bodies.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Housing and Community Development; Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Members of affected state boards and commissions; certified ethanol and biodiesel producers; public school students requiring literacy support; individuals experiencing homelessness serving on the Interagency Council on Homelessness; state and local government agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on state or local finances; the bill is largely procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM requested this departmental bill as part of its Government Modernization Initiative to streamline executive branch efficiency by repealing obsolete boards, commissions, and mandated reporting requirements.

The bill repeals the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board and transfers all authority for certifying, approving, and administering renewable fuel tax credits directly to the Department of Agriculture, and removes the Secretary from the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council.

The bill repeals several MDH reporting mandates (hepatitis C, cancer registry, mental health registry), consolidates youth camp epinephrine reporting, alters minority health disparities reporting, shifts health preceptor tax credit reporting deadlines, compiles Pre-K notification reports, and removes the Secretary from several oversight bodies.

The bill replaces the specialized intervention services report with a new Grade 3 literacy proficiency reporting mandate, repeals reports on youth suicide prevention and the Geographic Cost of Education Index adjustment, and removes MSDE from the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee.

The bill repeals the Two-Generation Family Economic Security Commission and the Commission on Trauma-Informed Care within DHS, eliminates the Multidisciplinary Alternative Response Advisory Council, alters the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, and modifies Pre-K enrollment reporting requirements.

The bill repeals the Partnership for Workforce Quality Advisory Board, alters member terms and staggering for the Maryland Life Sciences Advisory Board, modifies the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission membership and strategic planning duties, and removes Commerce from the Customer Council and Green Purchasing Committee.

The bill designates the Secretary of Housing and Community Development as Chair of the Interagency Council on Homelessness, removes term limits on the chair, authorizes DHCD to administer a compensation policy for council members with lived experience of homelessness, and alters reporting dates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board, requiring the Secretary of DPSCS to operate the CJIS Central Repository without the advisory board, and alters Customer Council membership.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly repeals, restructures membership for, or alters reporting requirements of numerous state boards, advisory councils, and commissions across state government.
The bill repeals the requirement for DNR to publish on its website a list of park maintenance projects costing over $25,000 and repeals the annual report on nutria eradication.
The bill repeals the annual reporting requirement on the Oil Contaminated Site Environmental Cleanup Fund and alters the membership of the Hart-Miller-Pleasure Island Citizens Oversight Committee.
The bill modifies the membership of the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee housed within the Transportation Article and adjusts agency representation on other interagency bodies.
The bill repeals the annual statutory reporting requirement for the Maryland Department of Labor regarding voter registration efforts at one-stop career centers.

The bill directly implements efficiency recommendations spearheaded by the Government Modernization Initiative, an effort established in coordination with GOPI to eliminate government waste, redundancy, and unnecessary mandates.

The bill modifies gubernatorial appointment structures and terms (such as for the Maryland Life Sciences Advisory Board and Hart-Miller-Pleasure Island Oversight Committee) and adjusts reporting requirements to the Governor.

The bill updates statutory citations and requires MHCC to continue analyzing information for the Health Care Disparities Policy Report Card published by MDH's Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership of the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board, which is established and housed within GOCPP.
The bill alters the statutory deadline from January 31 to March 1 for MDH to report to the Comptroller on tax credit certificates issued for medical preceptor programs.
The bill adjusts the membership and statutory references for the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council involving the MCA Director and social equity office.

Extends the maximum timeframe to obtain required practical work experience from three years to six years. Repeals the statutory 120-semester-hour examination requirement and the 150-semester-hour licensure requirement. Authorizes licensure with a master's degree or a bachelor's degree plus 30 semester credits and 2,000 hours of experience. Authorizes licensure with a bachelor's degree in accounting and 4,000 hours of practical work experience.
responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
stakeholders: certified public accountant license applicants, certified public accountants, and accounting firms
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Public Accountancy can implement the bill with existing resources. Special fund revenues may increase minimally to the extent additional individuals apply for licensure. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, which oversees the occupational licensing and regulation of certified public accountants. The Department of Labor is responsible for implementing the bill's altered educational and experiential pathways for CPA licensure.

Requires the Office of Home Energy Programs to update the redetermination process annually. Aligns state redetermination eligibility with federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program reporting standards for older adults. Streamlines the enrollment process for eligible energy customers aged 60 to 64. Takes effect July 1, 2026.

stakeholders: Eligible energy assistance customers aged 60 and older, particularly those aged 60 to 64; local administering agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Human Services and local administering agencies can handle administrative changes using existing budgeted resources. Total program funding is not directly affected, though an increase in participating households could lead to downward adjustments in benefit amounts to remain within available funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS requested this departmental legislation and houses the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which is directly responsible for administering energy assistance programs and implementing the uniform redetermination process for eligible older adults.

The bill expands streamlined enrollment and redetermination protections to individuals aged 60 to 64, directly aligning with the population of older adults served and advocated for by the Department of Aging.
MEA oversees state energy policy and the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which partially funds the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) accessed through OHEP.
PSC regulates public electric and gas utilities whose low-income residential customers participate in the energy assistance programs affected by the redetermination process.

Authorizes the Authority to award grants and loans for the management of certified heritage areas. Authorizes the Authority to require matching funds in whatever proportion the Authority considers appropriate. Repeals statutory 50% limits on project costs covered by certified heritage area grants. Alters the operating expense cap for transferred funds to up to 7% or $600,000, whichever is greater.
responsible_party: Maryland Heritage Areas Authority; Maryland Department of Planning; Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Local jurisdictions and entities managing certified heritage areas, Maryland Department of Planning personnel, and businesses supporting heritage area projects
fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on overall State finances, but redirects up to $6.0 million annually from Program Open Space State land acquisition to the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund beginning in FY 2027. Redirected funds cover two new Maryland Historical Trust positions totaling $202,318 in FY 2027. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase from additional grant and loan awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA) and the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) are housed within the Department of Planning, which directly administers the Maryland Heritage Areas Program, receives operating expense allowances under the fund, and requires additional personnel to manage the expanded grant funding.

Program Open Space (POS) is administered by DNR. The bill directly impacts DNR by increasing the transfer of POS State share funding to the MHAA Financing Fund by up to $6 million annually, redirecting funds away from State land acquisition and capital improvements on DNR land.

The bill redirects up to an additional $6 million from the State's share of Program Open Space funds designated under statute for recreation and open space purposes shared by DNR and the Historic St. Mary's City Commission.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to invest and reinvest moneys in the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund and credit investment earnings back to the fund.
DBM oversees the State budget and budget amendments authorizing the transfer of Program Open Space funds to the MHAA Financing Fund and reviewed the legislation as a contributing agency.

Synopsis: Altering the calculation of certain funding for the State Library Resource Center for fiscal year 2028 and each fiscal year thereafter.

bill_summary: Increases the per capita minimum funding calculation for the State Library Resource Center beginning in fiscal year 2028. responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
stakeholders: State Library Resource Center (Central Library of the Enoch Pratt Free Library System), local public library systems, and Maryland library patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $628,856 in FY 2028, rising to $2,817,159 in FY 2031 due to the mandated per-resident funding increase and projected population growth. State revenues are not affected. Local library systems benefit programmatically, but local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency coordinates the State Library Network and administers state funding for public library systems, including the State Library Resource Center and the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled, both of which are directly impacted by the bill's funding formula changes.

The bill creates an increased statutory mandated general fund appropriation starting in FY 2028, which the Department of Budget and Management must incorporate into state budget planning and execution.

bill_summary: Prohibits a person in St. Mary’s County from standing in certain roadways, shoulders, median dividers, or intersections. fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or St. Mary’s County operations or finances. The State Highway Administration can implement the bill's consultation and sign-approval provisions using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires St. Mary's County or its municipalities to consult with the State Highway Administration (SHA) to determine whether a State roadway is inherently dangerous, comply with SHA traffic control device manuals for signage, and obtain SHA approval before installing signs on State highways.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the State Highway Administration, which has direct statutory responsibilities for consultation, standard-setting, and sign approval under the bill.

The Maryland State Police enforce traffic and motor vehicle laws on State highways, including in St. Mary's County, and are directly subject to the bill's restrictions prohibiting police officers from issuing citations unless specified signage conditions are met.
The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for fiscal analysis as the judicial branch would process any contested traffic citations issued pursuant to this new prohibition.

Protects licensed funeral establishments, registered reduction operators, and crematory permit holders acting in good faith from civil liability. Covers transferring unclaimed cremains, hydrolyzed remains, or soil remains of veterans or eligible dependents to veterans service organizations. Protects veterans service organizations acting in good faith from civil liability for receiving those unclaimed remains. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Office of Cemetery Oversight; State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors
stakeholders: registered reduction operators, licensed funeral establishments, crematory permit holders, veterans service organizations, veterans, and eligible dependents of veterans
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected, with no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which regulates crematories, reduction facilities, and registered reduction operators under the Business Regulation Article referenced in the bill.

The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which regulates licensed funeral establishments and jointly regulates reduction facilities and crematory permit holders.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families oversees veterans' cemeteries and receives unclaimed remains of eligible veterans or dependents when veterans service organizations do not take possession.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to provide civil immunity from liability for qualifying transfers and receipts of remains, which directly affects tort claims filed in state courts.

Synopsis: Clarifying the membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain employees of certain Maryland Department of Health facilities; and clarifying that certain participating employees who are appointed, promoted, or transferred are members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System as a condition of employment.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Membership - Clarifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires certain employees at seven Maryland Department of Health facilities to join the Correctional Officers' Retirement System. Covers individuals serving as CAMH Specialist I – CI and CAMH Specialist II – CI on or after July 1, 2026. Permits affected members with 20 combined years of eligibility service to retire with normal service retirement benefits. Directs the Board of Trustees to transfer prior service credit from the Employees' Pension System or Employees' Retirement System. Allows members with pre-July 1, 2008 pension credit to opt out of the service transfer by June 1, 2027. Requires the board to grant the higher ordinary disability benefit calculated under either applicable retirement system.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals employed as CAMH Specialist I – CI or CAMH Specialist II – CI at seven specified Maryland Department of Health facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because the bill affects a very limited number of employees (approximately 12 positions). No effect on revenues, local finances, or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS). The bill requires the agency to manage the transfer of service credit, process election forms for affected members, and calculate retirement and disability benefits under the revised statutory provisions.

The bill directly modifies retirement system membership for specific Maryland Department of Health employees (CAMH Specialist I and II classifications at specified state health facilities), making their membership in CORS a mandatory condition of employment.

As the state's central personnel agency overseeing state employee job classifications, benefits, and fiscal planning, DBM is affected by changes governing retirement system enrollment and benefits for state positions.

Synopsis: Renaming the Children's Cabinet Fund to be the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund; requiring the Governor, for fiscal years 2028 through 2030, to include an appropriation in the annual budget bill to the Fund of an amount at least equal to the appropriation to the Fund in fiscal year 2027; and requiring, in fiscal year 2031, the Governor to provide an appropriation to the Fund of $500,000 above the appropriation for fiscal year 2030, to be used for grants to the local management boards.
Title: Children's Cabinet Fund - Renaming and Funding for Grants to Local Management Boards

NarrowSubjects.Name: Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.

bill_summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund to be the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund. Mandates annual budget appropriations for grants to eligible local management boards for fiscal years 2028 through 2031. Requires funding for fiscal years 2028 through 2030 to at least equal the fiscal year 2027 appropriation. Requires an additional $500,000 above the fiscal year 2030 funding level for fiscal year 2031. Specifies that grant money must supplement rather than supplant existing funding for eligible local management boards.
responsible_party: Governor's Office for Children; Children's Cabinet
stakeholders: eligible local management boards; children, youth, and families receiving interagency services
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in FY 2031 to fulfill the mandated appropriation to the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund. Local revenues and expenditures for local management boards increase by $500,000 in FY 2031 from additional grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office for Children serves as the fiscal agent for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and staffs the Children's Cabinet, which administers the fund and awards grants to Local Management Boards.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for developing the annual state budget and overseeing budget execution, which is directly impacted by the bill's statutory mandated appropriations to the fund for fiscal years 2028 through 2031.
The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2028 through 2031.
The bill amends the Education Article to conform statutory cross-references to the newly renamed Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund, with which the department collaborates on rate-setting processes.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to conform statutory cross-references to the renamed Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund regarding funds used to provide services to children with disabilities.

Synopsis: Removing the maximum amount that Baltimore City is authorized to establish for civil and criminal fines and penalties for violating certain ordinances, rules, or regulations.
Title: Baltimore City - Ordinance Enforcement - Fines and Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil and criminal fine or penalty Baltimore City may establish from $1,000 to $5,000. Applies this cap to violations of any ordinance, rule, or regulation established by the city. Retains the provision specifying that imprisonment may not exceed 12 months. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
stakeholders: Individuals and property owners who violate Baltimore City ordinances, rules, or regulations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Baltimore City revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent that higher civil or criminal fines and penalties are imposed and collected. City expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the state court system, including the District Court and Circuit Court, which handle contested civil citations and criminal ordinance violations originating from Baltimore City. While the fiscal note indicates no material fiscal impact on state operations, the judiciary was consulted regarding potential court impacts resulting from altered penalty structures.

Synopsis: Establishing in Anne Arundel County a Class GC (golf course) license that authorizes the holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption at a golf course with at least nine holes; and establishing in Anne Arundel County sports activity venue licenses that authorize the holder to sell beer and wine or beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption at a certain sports activity venue.
Title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages – Golf Course License and Sports Activity Venue Licenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: Establishes Class GC golf course licenses and sports activity venue alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue licenses to qualifying nine-hole golf courses and commercial sports facilities. Permits license holders to sell designated alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption Monday through Sunday without a Sunday permit. Sets the annual license fee at $1,200 for full-service licenses and $740 for beer and wine licenses. Requires sports venue licensees to serve prepared food, certify servers in alcohol awareness, and implement consumption monitoring policies.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Owners and operators of qualifying golf courses and commercial sports activity venues in Anne Arundel County, their employees, and venue patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase beginning in FY 2027 to the extent new licenses are issued at annual fees of $740 or $1,200. Specific revenue totals are unavailable. State finances and Anne Arundel County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers state sales taxes. While the bill specifically establishes local alcoholic beverages licenses administered by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates generally to the state's alcoholic beverages statutory framework under the Comptroller's broader regulatory subject area.

Synopsis: Requiring certain health systems to comply with certain insurance provisions regarding notice of termination of contracts; altering the notification requirements a carrier is required to provide an enrollee regarding changes to the carrier's provider panel; altering the notice requirements a carrier is required to provide to the Insurance Commissioner for certain material changes to the carrier's provider panel; requiring certain notice if a carrier and health system intend to terminate certain contracts; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers to notify enrollees when primary care or behavioral health providers are terminated. Extends transitional care rights to eligible behavioral health patients for up to 90 days after termination. Mandates that carriers notify the Insurance Commissioner at least 60 days before certain provider network terminations. Requires carriers and health systems to adhere to contract terms for 90 days following contract termination or nonrenewal. Establishes a 90-day special enrollment period for individual market enrollees whose regular treating provider is terminated.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health systems, hospitals, primary care and behavioral health providers, and individual health insurance enrollees
fiscal_impact_summary: Additional workload for the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties of up to $5,000 per day for failure to timely file access plan updates. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary implementing agency for this departmental legislation. The bill establishes notification requirements to the Insurance Commissioner for material changes to provider networks, authorizes the Commissioner to assess daily fines for late updates, and requires the Commissioner to develop a uniform form for enrollee requests for transitional care.

MHBE operates the Individual Exchange (Maryland Health Connection) and is directly affected by the statutory requirement establishing a new 90-day special enrollment period for enrollees whose regular providers are terminated from their plan's network.

MDH oversees health care facilities, health systems, and Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs), which are subject to carrier provider panel notification and transitional care standards. The bill also adds a compliance section directly into the Health - General Article.

Synopsis: Transferring the authority to regulate certain crematories and reduction facilities from the Office of Cemetery Oversight to the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors; altering the circumstances under which the Governor may remove an appointed member of the Board; altering the quorum of the Board; and specifying that the Board may take action with a simple majority vote of the quorum.
Title: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors – Board Operations and Regulation of Crematories and Reduction Facilities
