bill_summary: Transfers regulatory oversight of crematories and reduction facilities from the Office of Cemetery Oversight to the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors. Requires individuals and business entities operating crematories or reduction facilities to obtain registrations and permits from the Board. Increases maximum civil penalties to $10,000 per violation and $1,000 per day for continuing violations. Alters Board quorum standards, member removal grounds, and disciplinary appeal procedures. Mandates the Board to employ at least two inspectors and create a permanent inspector position by fiscal 2028. Directs the Board to convene a stakeholder workgroup and submit recommendations by December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors; Office of Cemetery Oversight
stakeholders: crematory operators, reduction facility operators, funeral directors, morticians, registered cemeterians, and consumers of death care services
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors special fund expenditures increase by at least $101,200 in FY 2027 to hire an additional inspector, with ongoing personnel costs in future years. Board special fund fee revenues increase by an indeterminate amount, while Office of Cemetery Oversight special fund revenues decrease by approximately $6,000 biennially beginning in FY 2027. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors is a regulatory board within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill transfers full regulatory authority over crematories and reduction facilities to the Board, requires the Board to employ inspectors, establishes new registration and permit systems, and incurs operational and fiscal impacts on the Board's special fund.

The Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO) is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill removes regulatory oversight of crematories and reduction facilities from OCO, transfers duties and records to the Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, alters the OCO Advisory Council composition, and results in a loss of special fund revenue for OCO.

The bill mandates the creation of a new state Position Identification Number (PIN) beginning in fiscal year 2028 for a full-time inspector position within the Board, requiring coordination with DBM regarding personnel and state budget allocations.
The bill amends statutory standards and grounds under which the Governor may remove appointed members of the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors.

The bill repeals Business Regulation Section 5-803 and updates statutory references concerning the transfer of unclaimed cremated and reduction remains of veterans to the Department of Veterans and Military Families.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a certain controller from knowingly selling the personal data of a consumer to a certain governmental unit that has engaged in or supported civil immigration enforcement under certain circumstances; requiring a custodian of a public record to take reasonable steps to determine whether a public record is accessed for enforcing immigration law; requiring an entity that operates a certain message switching system to take certain actions regarding system access; etc.
Title: Data Privacy - Consumer Data, Public Records, and Message Switching System (Data Privacy Act)
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 874

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Prohibits data controllers from knowingly selling consumer personal data to governmental units that recently engaged in civil immigration enforcement. Limits controller and processor compliance with subpoenas or law enforcement cooperation concerning immigration enforcement without a valid warrant. Requires public record custodians to take reasonable steps to determine whether persons seek records to enforce immigration law. Directs custodians to deny inspection of personal information, photographs, and facial recognition searches for immigration enforcement without a warrant. Extends law enforcement database access bans and verification requirements to message switching systems. Requires governmental entities to develop and publish procedures preventing the sale and redisclosure of sensitive data.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Department of State Police; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of Information Technology; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Maryland residents and consumers, commercial data controllers and processors, public records custodians, state and local law enforcement agencies, and government agencies seeking access to records or personal data.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase significantly for the Judiciary to implement operational procedures, additional staff, or programming changes to determine the purpose of data requests. Local government expenditures may increase for certain custodians to scrutinize public records requests, but specific figures are unavailable. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is explicitly mandated under Public Safety § 3-529 to adopt regulations governing access to message switching systems and law enforcement databases, and under General Provisions § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and submit annual reports to the General Assembly regarding immigration-related data and facial recognition requests.

MVA is explicitly required under General Provisions § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and procedures restricting access to personal information and facial recognition searches for immigration enforcement, and to submit an annual report to the General Assembly tracking such requests.

MSP is specifically mandated under General Provisions § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and procedures governing immigration-related data and facial recognition requests, and to report annually on these requests to the General Assembly.

The fiscal note specifically highlights that the Judiciary/AOC faces a significant operational and expenditure impact because court records are publicly accessible, necessitating new procedures, programming, and potential staffing to screen all public record requests to determine if they are sought for immigration enforcement.

Under State Government § 10-1702, DoIT is statutorily designated to consult with every governmental entity in the state as they develop and publish procedures to prevent the sale and redisclosure of personal records and sensitive data.

The bill amends the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act enforced by the OAG's Consumer Protection Division, specifically authorizing the Division to post consumer education materials and enforce prohibitions on selling or disclosing personal data for immigration enforcement.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), which is subject to extensive regulatory, procedural, and reporting mandates under the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing specified organizations that are affiliated with a professional National Football League team that plays its home games in Baltimore City to conduct raffles, subject to certain limitations; and extending for a period of 4 years and one month to June 30, 2029 the termination date of certain provisions of law authorizing certain organizations that are affiliated with a professional Major League Baseball team that plays its home games in Baltimore City to conduct certain raffles.
Title: Baltimore City - Raffles - Organizations Affiliated With Professional Baseball and Football Teams

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City organizations affiliated with a professional National Football League team to conduct raffles. Extends the termination date for raffles affiliated with professional Major League Baseball teams to May 31, 2031. Requires organizations to obtain an annual written permit from a designated Baltimore City agency. Restricts football raffle sales to between 4.5 hours before kickoff and the third quarter. Mandates age-verification measures and geofencing to limit electronic ticket sales to a specified geographic area.
responsible_party: Baltimore City designated agency; Baltimore City Police Department
stakeholders: organizations affiliated with Major League Baseball and National Football League teams in Baltimore City; attendees and raffle ticket purchasers at Baltimore home games
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, though lottery revenues may see a minor substitution effect. Baltimore City finances are not materially affected, and the Baltimore City Police Department can issue permits using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency oversees gaming policy in the state. The bill expands allowable raffle operations at professional sporting events in Baltimore City, and the fiscal note evaluates the potential substitution effects of these raffles on State lottery revenues.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain provisions of law governing information technology plans apply to certain public institutions of higher education; establishing a policy of the State that State and higher education employee e-mail systems and resources are intended to support State business and may not serve as a public forum; requiring certain policies, plans, and standards to include provisions to implement systems that automatically filter spam e-mail from certain email accounts; etc.
Title: Information Technology – State and Higher Education E–Mail – Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes that State and higher education employee email systems must support State business and cannot serve as a public forum. Requires State units and public higher education governing boards to protect employee email services from spam email. Mandates the implementation of systems that automatically filter spam email from employee email accounts. Excludes from spam email bulk emails related to State business from vendors, partners, and exclusive representatives. Requires information technology policies to permit incidental personal use with de minimis resource impact consistent with professional norms. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Secretary of Information Technology; governing boards of public institutions of higher education
stakeholders: State employees; public higher education employees; units of State government; public institutions of higher education; State vendors, partners, and exclusive representatives
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances because the bill generally codifies existing practice. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT and the Secretary of Information Technology are the primary regulatory authorities responsible for setting IT guidelines, reviewing and approving IT policies, standards, and plans submitted by State agencies and higher education institutions, and overseeing statewide email security and IT master planning.

The bill explicitly amends State law to apply IT plan requirements to USM, requiring its governing board to develop and submit IT policies, standards, and plans regarding email spam filtering and acceptable State business use to the Secretary of Information Technology.

The bill explicitly amends State law to bring Morgan State University under the IT plan and email security requirements of § 3.5-305, requiring its governing board to submit IT policies and plans to the Secretary of Information Technology.

The bill explicitly amends State law to include St. Mary's College of Maryland under the IT plan and email security requirements of § 3.5-305, requiring its governing board to submit IT policies and standards regarding email spam filtering to the Secretary of Information Technology.

As the central personnel and human resources agency for State government, DBM is affected by statewide policies governing employee IT usage norms, allowable incidental personal use of State email, and standards for conducting State business.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition on awarding the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship after June 30, 2030; and repealing the limitation on renewing the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship if the scholarship recipient received an initial scholarship before June 30, 2030.
Title: Higher Education - Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship - Repeal of Termination Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals the June 30, 2030 deadline for awarding initial Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans Scholarships. Eliminates the restriction limiting post-2030 scholarship renewals to individuals who received an initial scholarship earlier. Authorizes the Maryland Higher Education Commission to award new and renewal scholarships indefinitely. Preserves scholarship eligibility for qualifying veterans, active service members, reservists, and their spouses and children. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Maryland resident veterans, active duty service members, and activated reservists of the Afghanistan and Iraq conflicts, as well as their spouses, children, and stepchildren
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $750,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2031 to maintain the scholarship program beyond its former sunset date. No effect on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship program and the associated scholarship fund, which will now continue awarding initial scholarships beyond June 30, 2030.
As the state's central higher education coordinating board that manages state financial aid programs, it oversees the administration and ongoing operation of the scholarship program and fund.
DVMF advocates for Maryland veterans, active-duty service members, and their families, assisting them in accessing state educational benefits including this scholarship.

USM institutions enroll eligible scholarship recipients, and the statutory formula capping the maximum scholarship award is directly tied to tuition, mandatory fees, and room and board at USM institutions.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold and maintain the special, nonlapsing Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.
The Comptroller has a statutory duty to account for the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law regarding priority registration at public institutions of higher education, resources and support at community colleges, senatorial and Delegate scholarships, and preferences in hiring by the Public Service Commission to the spouses of active service members and veterans; etc.
Title: Uniformed Services Spouses Act

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Expands educational benefits, scholarship eligibility, and employment preferences to spouses of active service members and certain veterans. Requires public institutions of higher education to grant course priority registration to eligible spouses and certain veterans. Requires community colleges to include veterans' spouses in specialized advising services and campus resource centers. Authorizes senatorial and Delegate scholarships for out-of-state study to be awarded to spouses of active service members. Expands State personnel test credits and sanitary commission hiring preferences to include additional eligible veterans and spouses.
responsible_party: Public institutions of higher education; community colleges; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Department of Budget and Management; Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
stakeholders: Spouses of active service members; spouses of veterans; veterans with other than dishonorable discharges; students at Maryland public institutions of higher education and community colleges; applicants for State and local government employment
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not materially affected and implementation costs can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM administers the State Personnel Management System and must update the JobAps system, testing guides, and administrative materials to implement the expanded definition of eligible veterans and military spouses for selection test credits.

MHEC coordinates statewide postsecondary education policies and administers state financial aid programs, including the senatorial and delegate scholarships whose eligibility criteria are expanded to include spouses of active service members domiciled in Maryland.
The bill amends the Public Utilities Article to authorize hiring and promotion preferences for spouses of active service members and adjusts the discharge criteria for eligible veterans.
USM institutions are public institutions of higher education that must adopt policies and grant priority course registration to eligible service members, qualifying veterans, and their spouses.
As an independent public university, Morgan State must adopt policies granting priority registration to eligible service members, qualifying veterans, and their spouses.
As an independent public honors college, St. Mary's must establish policies to grant priority course registration to eligible service members, veterans, and military spouses.

DVMF is the primary state agency responsible for assisting Maryland's veterans, active service members, and their families in securing benefits, higher education access, and support services impacted by this legislation.
The bill amends provisions in the Labor and Employment Article regarding hiring and promotion preferences for veterans and military spouses by private and local employers.

Synopsis: Altering membership criteria for a Class C (veterans' organization) alcoholic beverages license in Anne Arundel County by including certain members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service, and repealing a requirement that members of the veterans' organization served in a war; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class C (Veterans' Organization) Licenses - Membership
bill_summary: Alters membership criteria for Class C veterans' organization alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County. Requires eligible organizations to consist only of individuals who served in the uniformed services. Expands eligibility to veterans of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service. Repeals the requirement that members must have served during a war. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: veterans' organizations and clubs in Anne Arundel County and their members, including veterans of the uniformed services, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Public Health Service
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Local government finances and operations in Anne Arundel County are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers relevant provisions of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, though local retail licenses in Anne Arundel County are handled by the local board of license commissioners.

The bill updates criteria for veterans' organizations to align with the broader definition of uniformed services (including NOAA and PHS) and removes wartime service restrictions, which touches on the community and advocacy scope of veterans' affairs in Maryland.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time within which the Securities Commissioner in the Office of the Attorney General may exercise a power under certain provisions of law governing the sale of franchises; altering the period of time within which an action for liability under a certain provision of law pertaining to franchise offers for sale must be brought; prohibiting a franchisor and certain others from inhibiting the right of franchisees to associate for certain purposes;  etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law - Alterations (Franchise Reform Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Alters the timeframe for the Securities Commissioner to bring franchise enforcement actions from three years to five years. Modifies the statute of limitations for franchisee civil liability claims against franchisors. Prohibits franchisors from restricting franchisees from joining trade associations or freely associating for lawful purposes. Authorizes franchisees to sue in circuit court for injunctive relief, damages, and attorney's fees for association violations. Establishes the Maryland Franchise Disclosure Document Renewal Fast-Track Review Pilot Program through September 30, 2032. Requires the Securities Commissioner to report on the pilot program by September 30, 2031.
responsible_party: Securities Commissioner in the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Franchisees, franchisors, and prospective franchise buyers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $305,500 in FY 2027 to hire three staff positions in the Office of the Attorney General, rising to $413,400 by FY 2031; costs may potentially be mitigated by the Securities Act Registration Fund. Revenues are not materially affected. Local governments experience no material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law is administered and enforced by the Securities Commissioner within the Office of the Attorney General. The bill expands the Commissioner's enforcement timeline, mandates the creation and administration of the Maryland Franchise Disclosure Document Renewal Fast-Track Review Pilot Program, imposes extensive reporting requirements on the office, and results in a direct fiscal impact requiring additional staff positions and general fund expenditures.

The bill modifies the statute of limitations for civil liability lawsuits and creates a new private right of action permitting franchisees to sue in circuit court for injunctive relief, damages, and attorney's fees if their rights of association are violated, directly impacting the operations and caseload of the Maryland Judicial Branch.

Synopsis: Legalizing the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and any supplement to the extent to which that code or supplement contains laws enacted by the General Assembly.
Title: Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws - 2025 Edition - Legalization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Codes -see also- Annotated Code of Md; Building Codes
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte

bill_summary: Legalizes the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and its supplements. Applies to the extent that the code or supplements contain laws enacted by the General Assembly. Requires all Maryland courts and public officials to recognize the code as evidence of enacted law. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Government
stakeholders: Baltimore County officials, Maryland state and local courts, legal practitioners, and Baltimore County residents

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization, a temporary advisory body tasked with analyzing cost drivers, developing cost-based reimbursement methodologies, and reporting findings before terminating on June 30, 2028.
The bill requires multiple interim and annual reports detailing behavioral health rate methodologies, delivery systems, and implementation progress to be submitted to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring an intake officer to file a petition alleging that a child under the age of 13 years is a child in need of supervision if the child is alleged to have committed an act that results in the death of a victim; and requiring a law enforcement officer to forward a complaint alleging that a child under the age of 13 years committed an act that resulted in the death of a victim to the Department of Juvenile Services for appropriate action.
Title: Juvenile Law - Child in Need of Supervision - Mandatory Petition (NyKayla Strawder Memorial Act)

bill_summary: Requires law enforcement officers to forward certain complaints to the Department of Juvenile Services. Applies when a child under age 13 allegedly commits an act resulting in a victim's death. Requires a juvenile intake officer to file a petition alleging the child is in need of supervision. Designates the legislation as the NyKayla Strawder Memorial Act. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services; Law Enforcement Agencies
stakeholders: Children under age 13 alleged to have committed acts resulting in the death of a victim, their parents or guardians, and crime victims and their surviving families
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 776 directly impacts the Department of Juvenile Services (DJS) by requiring DJS intake officers to file a petition alleging that a child is in need of supervision (CINS) if the child is under age 13 and alleged to have committed an act resulting in the death of a victim, removing intake discretion for informal adjustment or refusal in these cases.

The bill requires mandatory filing of CINS petitions in the juvenile court for specified cases involving children under 13, directly impacting juvenile court caseloads and judicial proceedings administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill establishes a statutory requirement under the Criminal Procedure Article that law enforcement officers, including Maryland State Police troopers, must forward complaints alleging an act by a child under 13 that resulted in the death of a victim to the Department of Juvenile Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Mandatory formal CINS petitions in juvenile court require legal representation for the children involved, which is routinely handled by the Office of the Public Defender in indigent juvenile proceedings.

Synopsis: Requiring the governing body of Washington County and of a municipal corporation in Washington County to grant a 100% property tax credit against the county and municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated, and used to provide housing to veterans; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.

bill_summary: Requires the governing bodies of Washington County and municipal corporations in Washington County to grant a property tax credit. Sets the credit equal to 100% of the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on eligible real property. Applies the tax credit to real property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated. Restricts eligibility to property used to provide housing to veterans. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Washington County; municipal corporations in Washington County
stakeholders: Platoon 22, Incorporated; veterans housed by Platoon 22, Incorporated; Washington County; City of Hagerstown
fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Local property tax revenues decrease annually beginning in fiscal 2027 by approximately $4,000 for Washington County and approximately $5,000 for the City of Hagerstown. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates a local property tax credit for property owned by Platoon 22, Inc. that is used to provide housing to veterans, aligning with the Department of Veterans & Military Families' mission to support and advocate for veterans' housing and welfare.

responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: shellfish aquaculture leaseholders and commercial shellfish businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Department of Natural Resources' authority to approve the placement of shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation by extending the statutory termination date of this regulatory program from June 30, 2027, to June 30, 2030.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain members and former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System assigned as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit to receive credit for certain military service if the member receives military service credit in another retirement system; and prohibiting an individual from receiving credit more than one time.

Prohibits an individual from receiving service credit under the section more than once. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members and former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System who are or were assigned as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit
fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or revenues because the bill applies to a very small number of individuals. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and is directly responsible for processing applications and granting military service credits under the State Personnel and Pensions Article.

The Maryland State Police operates the State's law enforcement Aviation Command, directly employing the helicopter pilots who are members of LEOPS eligible for the expanded military service credit under this bill.
The Department of Budget and Management serves as the central personnel and fiscal agency, monitoring state employee benefits, retirement plans, and state employer pension contribution rates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce administers the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA) and is directly responsible for authorizing eligible fund managers to receive management fees and setting annual caps under this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Although the program is directly administered by Commerce, this office coordinates policies and initiatives affecting small, minority, and women-owned business enterprises across Maryland.

bill_summary: Establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Secretary of Aging. Authorizes expenditures for expenses aligning with that mission, including partnership development and departmental programs, services, or activities. Prohibits the Governor from reducing an appropriation for the fund approved by the General Assembly. Requires the Secretary to submit an annual fund administration report to specified legislative committees by January 1.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging; Secretary of Aging
stakeholders: Older adults and seniors in Maryland, caregivers, families, and local area agencies on aging
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in State special fund revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 from investment earnings, collected fees, and other accepted contributions. Potential increase in local area agency on aging revenues and expenditures to the extent funds become available.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to support the Department of Aging's mission and requires the Secretary of Aging to administer the fund and report annually on its receipts and expenditures.

The bill statutorily tasks the State Treasurer with holding the Aging Resilience Fund separately, investing the money in the fund, and crediting interest earnings directly to the fund under an exemption to the General Fund interest sweep.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the newly created Aging Resilience Fund.

The bill limits executive authority by explicitly prohibiting the Governor from reducing an appropriation for the Aging Resilience Fund in the State budget under Section 7-213 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

As the State's central agency responsible for budget development and execution, DBM is impacted by restrictions on budget reductions under Section 7-213 and the requirement that fund expenditures conform to the State budget.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant, by law, a tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain dwellings that are subject to a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity and a certain covenant or agreement that ensures affordable pricing of the dwelling; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Building Homes Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant a property tax credit on qualifying dwellings. Applies to dwellings with a mortgage or deed of trust provided by a nonprofit entity. Requires a covenant or legally binding agreement of at least 20 years enforcing income and equity or appreciation restrictions. Caps the credit at the difference between taxes on the full assessed value and the homeowner's first mortgage obligation. Allows local governing bodies to set credit duration, additional eligibility criteria, and application procedures. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
stakeholders: Homeowners of qualifying affordable dwellings, nonprofit mortgage lenders, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 to the extent local jurisdictions enact the credit; specific figures are unavailable because revenue loss depends on local adoption and eligible property sales. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes an optional local property tax credit to incentivize and support affordable homeownership through nonprofit-provided mortgages and long-term affordability covenants. While the fiscal impact is local and the credit is administered by local governments, the policy directly aligns with DHCD's mission and initiatives to promote affordable homeownership and community stability.

Synopsis: Specifying the intern fellowships that exist in the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program; increasing the maximum scholarship award amount under the Program from $5,000 to $6,000; and requiring the Governor, beginning in fiscal year 2028, to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation for the Program that is at least a 125% of the appropriation provided in fiscal year 2026.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: Specifies three intern fellowships in the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program. Includes the Governor's Summer Internship, Sondheim Maryland Nonprofit Leadership Internship, and Sondheim Public Service Law Fellows programs. Increases the maximum scholarship award under the program from $5,000 to $6,000. Requires the Governor to provide an annual budget appropriation starting in fiscal year 2028. Mandates funding for the University of Maryland, Baltimore County of at least 125% of fiscal 2026 levels.
responsible_party: The Shriver Center; University of Maryland, Baltimore County
stakeholders: College and graduate students pursuing public service internships; public and nonprofit host entities; University of Maryland, Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $87,500 annually beginning in fiscal year 2028 to satisfy the mandated 125% appropriation requirement for the University of Maryland, Baltimore County. No direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Shriver Center at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC), a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, administers the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program. The bill directly mandates funding for UMBC to support the program and its fellowships.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific statutory appropriation in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2028 equal to at least 125% of the program's FY 2026 appropriation.

As the principal budget agency for the State, DBM is responsible for preparing the Governor's budget and incorporating the mandated appropriation for the internship scholarship program beginning in FY 2028.
The program is codified under Title 18 (Student Financial Assistance) of the Education Article, which falls within MHEC's policy purview over higher education scholarships and financial aid programs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI is recognized in the bill's preamble as a cornerstone of the State's public service initiatives, aligning closely with the bill's objective of expanding public service pathways and internships for students.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, in coordination with certain entities, to evaluate the use of blockchain technology for securely recording and verifying real property ownership and leases and to assess its potential for use by law enforcement and courts in resolving real property disputes involving squatting; and requiring the Department, by December 31, 2026, to report the results of the study to evaluate certain uses of blockchain technology to the Governor and the General Assembly.

bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to evaluate blockchain technology for property lease and title recordation. responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Maryland Judiciary; Maryland State Police; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: real property owners, tenants, alleged squatters, law enforcement agencies, and state courts
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected; any potential costs associated with the study workgroup are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General is explicitly required by the bill to coordinate with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and other entities to conduct the study and submit the final report on blockchain-based real property title and lease recordation.

The Maryland State Police is specifically mandated to coordinate on the study and report, particularly evaluating how blockchain technology could assist law enforcement in resolving real property disputes involving squatting.

The Administrative Office of the Courts represents the Maryland Judiciary, which is explicitly named in the bill to coordinate on the study evaluating the potential use of blockchain technology by courts in resolving real property disputes.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the final study and recommendations required to be submitted by December 31, 2026.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Aging to make grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging to support social connection for individuals in aging-in-place programs through events or gatherings at multigenerational third places; and defining "multigenerational third place" as a community space other than a personal home or workplace that supports social connection, events, or gathering among individuals of different ages.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of Aging to make grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging. Defines a multigenerational third place as a community space other than a home or workplace supporting connection. Authorizes grant funding for operational costs, including administrative and rental costs, for senior villages. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: nonprofit organizations, area agencies on aging, senior villages, and seniors participating in aging-in-place programs
fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on state finances, as the bill alters the authorized uses of existing funds and the Maryland Department of Aging can implement changes with existing resources. Local governments operating area agencies on aging may receive grant revenues, with local expenditures increasing correspondingly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the grant program administered by the Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA), authorizing the department to award aging-in-place grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging for multigenerational third places and related senior village operational costs.

Synopsis: Altering the cap on a certain assessment allocation percentage required to be calculated by the Board of Directors of the Industry Automobile Insurance Association; authorizing the Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund to establish an affordability program subject to certain requirements and modification under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Affordability Program and Industry Automobile Insurance Association Assessments
bill_summary: Reduces the cap on the Industry Automobile Insurance Association's assessment allocation percentage for private passenger auto from 3% to 1%. Authorizes the Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund to establish a private passenger auto insurance affordability program. Requires approval from the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and caps overall rate inadequacy at 20% of net written premium. Restricts program eligibility to qualified policyholders with household incomes not exceeding 250% of the federal poverty level. Prohibits the Commissioner from disapproving or modifying the program based on noncompliance with statutory capital requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; Maryland Insurance Administration; Industry Automobile Insurance Association
stakeholders: Eligible Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund policyholders with household income not exceeding 250% of the federal poverty level, private passenger automobile insurers, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. Nonbudgeted Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund revenues likely decrease in fiscal 2028 and 2029 due to the continuation of discounted premium rates, but specific figures cannot be reliably predicted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs MAIF by authorizing its Executive Director to establish an automobile insurance affordability program for qualifying policyholders and reducing the cap on the assessment allocation percentage for its private passenger auto division from 3% to 1%.

The bill assigns regulatory and oversight responsibilities to the Insurance Commissioner and MIA to review, approve, and require modifications to MAIF's affordability program and ensure rates are not excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory.

bill_summary: Alters the maximum annual salary for clerks of the circuit courts and registers of wills. Caps the maximum salary at Grade 26, Step 20 of the State Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale. Requires the Board of Public Works to set each official's salary within that statutory limit. Prohibits mid-term salary scale adjustments from applying to incumbent officials until their next term begins. Repeals an obsolete $12,000 minimum annual salary for the Baltimore City register of wills. Applies salary adjustments to terms of office beginning on or after October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Maryland Judiciary; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Clerks of the circuit courts and registers of wills across Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2027, State general fund expenditures increase by $403,800 for the Judiciary to cover clerk salary increases, rising to $692,300 annually thereafter. State general fund revenues decrease by $386,300 in FY 2027 due to increased register of wills compensation paid from fee and inheritance tax collections, decreasing by $662,100 annually thereafter. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the maximum annual statutory salary for the 24 elected registers of wills by tying it to Grade 26, Step 20 of the State salary scale, and repeals an obsolete salary provision for the Baltimore City register.

The bill increases the maximum salary for clerks of the circuit courts, directly impacting the Judiciary's operational budget with projected general fund expenditure increases of over $400,000 in FY 2027 and nearly $700,000 annually thereafter.

The Board of Public Works is the statutory body required to determine and fix the specific annual salaries for each circuit court clerk and register of wills within the newly established statutory cap.

The Comptroller oversees the remittance of taxes and fees from the registers of wills, authorizes transfers to cover expense or salary deficiencies in registers' offices, and manages the remittance of excess revenues that flow into the general fund.

DBM maintains the State of Maryland Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale (specifically Grade 26, Step 20) that establishes the salary ceiling under the bill and oversees state personnel compensation schedules and fiscal planning.

stakeholders: Employees of county boards of education and members of the Maryland State Board of Education
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill is procedural in nature.

The bill directly impacts the Governor's statutory appointment authority by permitting the Governor to appoint an employee of a county board of education to the State Board of Education.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, including the newly eligible county board employee seat on the State Board of Education.

bill_summary: Requires applicants for for-hire and locally licensed taxicab driver licenses to verify completion of human trafficking awareness training. Mandates training on recognizing, responding to, and reporting suspected human trafficking to appropriate authorities. Requires transportation network operators to complete training within 30 days after first providing a prearranged ride. Bars transportation network companies from letting operators provide services if they fail to complete the training. Protects drivers, operators, and applicants from civil or criminal liability for good-faith reporting or responding to suspected human trafficking.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: taxicab drivers, for-hire drivers, transportation network operators, transportation network companies, and local taxicab licensing authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission increase by $10,000 in fiscal 2027 only for online application software modifications, offset by an equal increase in special fund assessment revenues on public service companies. Local governments can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory agency responsible for licensing passenger-for-hire drivers, taxicab drivers, and transportation network operators. The bill requires PSC to verify human trafficking awareness training documentation for applicants and entails a $10,000 IT modification expenditure in FY 2027.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents utility and passenger transportation consumers before the Public Service Commission and was consulted as an informational source regarding the regulatory impacts of the bill.

The bill provides civil and criminal immunity to for-hire drivers, taxicab drivers, and transportation network operators who report or respond to suspected human trafficking in good faith, which could marginally affect court proceedings.

bill_summary: Reestablishes the Commission to Advance Lithium–Ion Battery Safety in Maryland with altered membership and an expanded mandate. Requires the Office of the State Fire Marshal to provide staff for the Commission. Requires the Commission to study battery fire safety, recycling practices, extended producer responsibility, and transportation risks. Requires an interim progress report to the Legislative Policy Committee by December 1, 2026. Requires a final report with recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal; Commission to Advance Lithium–Ion Battery Safety in Maryland
stakeholders: Lithium-ion battery and vehicle propulsion battery manufacturers, battery recycling and solid waste facilities, first responders and firefighters, electric utilities, commercial and property casualty insurers, towing and recovery professionals, and the Maryland Port Administration
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $70,700 in FY 2027 and $30,100 in FY 2028 for the Office of the State Fire Marshal to hire one contractual employee to staff the Commission. Revenues are unaffected. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal, an agency within the Department of State Police, is mandated to staff the Commission, which requires hiring a contractual employee resulting in a direct general fund fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reestablishes and sets the mandate and membership for the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland.
The bill designates a seat on the Commission for a representative of the Maryland Port Administration and specifically tasks the Commission with studying battery risks at the Port of Baltimore.

The Secretary of the Environment appoints multiple members to the Commission, including a representative of the Land and Materials Administration, and the Commission studies battery recycling, disposal, and solid waste issues.
The Director of MEA appoints a representative from MEA and battery industry representatives, and the Commission reviews grid-scale battery energy storage and safety standards.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner appoints members representing the property casualty and commercial insurance sectors, and the Commission is mandated to study the impacts of battery risk on insurance providers and coverage.
The Secretary of Transportation appoints members to the Commission, and the Commission evaluates lithium-ion battery risks on roads, rail, and tunnels throughout the state.

fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures beginning as early as fiscal 2027 for additional scholarship awards and increased award amounts covering total cost of attendance. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for tracking State revenues, paying State bills, and administering tax refunds. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is the administrative body that hears appeals regarding property tax valuations and disputes concerning eligibility for property tax exemptions.

bill_summary: Prohibits an enrollment freeze in the Child Care Scholarship Program from applying to specified vulnerable children and families. Exempts recipients of Temporary Cash Assistance, federal TANF, Supplemental Security Income, siblings of enrolled children, and homeless children. Requires the State Department of Education to establish an enrollment waitlist when a freeze occurs. Prioritizes qualified applicants by financial need, child care employment, children under age three, and waitlist tenure. Requires the Department to develop an updated application and review job training eligibility standards.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Low-income families seeking child care assistance, children experiencing homelessness, recipients of TCA, TANF, or SSI, child care facility employees, and child care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $350,000 in FY 2027 to reprogram administrative tracking and portal systems. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE administers the Child Care Scholarship Program and is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to establish and manage a waitlist during enrollment freezes, exempt specific populations, develop a new application, review job training eligibility methodology, submit a report to the General Assembly, and reprogram tracking and portal systems at an estimated cost of $350,000.

DHS administers Maryland's Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) programs. The bill specifically exempts individuals and families enrolled in TCA and TANF from any enrollment freeze under the Child Care Scholarship Program, necessitating program alignment and data coordination for eligible recipients.

DBM is responsible for state budget oversight and fiscal planning. The bill impacts program funding mechanics, waitlist operationalization, and requires state general fund expenditures for IT modifications.

responsible_party: Home Builder Registration Unit, Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly impact State or local government finances or operations.

MSILC works in conjunction with the Maryland State Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which is housed within the Maryland State Department of Education, to develop, monitor, and implement the State Plan for Independent Living.

bill_summary: Prohibits operating certain freight trains in the State unless the train has a crew of at least two individuals. Applies to freight trains sharing a rail corridor with high-speed passenger or commuter trains. Excludes freight operations involving hostler service or utility employees in yard service. Establishes civil penalties up to $10,000, increasing to $25,000 for repeat willful violations within three years. Conditions implementation on New York, Pennsylvania, and Virginia enacting substantially similar legislation on or before October 1, 2056.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Railroad companies operating freight trains in Maryland, freight train crew members, and passenger rail operators sharing rail corridors
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances under current federal rules. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the Railroad Safety and Health Program and its Commissioner is tasked with assessing civil penalties for violations of the freight train crew size requirements. The department is also required to monitor and notify the Department of Legislative Services when the multi-state contingency is satisfied.

The bill impacts freight rail operating in shared corridors with commuter rail. Under an Access Agreement with freight rail operator CSX, MDOT could face up to $6.0 million annually in State Transportation Trust Fund obligations if federal crew size rules are modified or invalidated.

The Maryland Transit Administration operates MARC passenger commuter trains that share tracks and infrastructure with CSX freight trains. An existing Access Agreement between MTA and CSX includes staffing reimbursement stipulations tied to state-mandated crew size laws.

The Public Service Commission possesses regulatory oversight over railroad carriers and by statute funds the Department of Labor's Railroad Safety and Health Program through annual assessments on public service companies.

Synopsis: Altering certain apprenticeship requirements relating to public works contracts to require certain contractors and subcontractors to employ a certain number of qualifying new apprentices or journeyworkers necessary to meet a certain applicable percentage for the project; altering which projects are subject to certain apprenticeship requirements; altering certain provisions of law that authorize contractors and subcontractors to make certain payments to a certain apprenticeship program in lieu of employing certain apprentices; etc.
Title: Public Works Contracts - Apprenticeship Requirements (Maryland Workforce Apprenticeship Utilization Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Public Works -see also- Brg&Tun; Hwys; PublBlgFac; etc.

Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires contractors and subcontractors on covered public works projects to employ qualifying apprentices or journeyworkers for specified labor hours. Sets the initial apprenticeship utilization requirement at 20% for bids advertised on or after January 1, 2027. Requires the Secretary of Labor to set the applicable percentage every other December 31 beginning in 2028. Redefines covered projects to align with all projects subject to State prevailing wage law. Applies these public works apprenticeship standards to the University System of Maryland and Baltimore City Community College. Authorizes alternative payments to the State Apprenticeship Training Fund or qualified apprenticeship programs not exceeding 25 cents per hour.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Contractors and subcontractors on public works projects subject to prevailing wage laws, registered apprentices and journeyworkers, qualified apprenticeship programs, the University System of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund increase starting in fiscal 2027 as contractors make payments in lieu of meeting apprentice utilization targets, though a reliable estimate is not feasible. State general fund revenues may increase minimally from penalties. State and local public works project costs could increase if contractor competition declines, or decrease if apprentice labor replaces higher-wage tradespeople. State agencies can implement the requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for the bill. The Secretary of Labor is responsible for setting the applicable apprenticeship utilization percentage, administering and auditing the State Apprenticeship Training Fund (SATF), reviewing contractor waiver requests and monthly reporting, adopting implementing regulations, and assessing penalties.

The bill explicitly removes certain procurement exemptions to apply Title 17, Subtitle 6 (Apprenticeship Requirements for Public Works Contracts) directly to University System of Maryland procurements and capital projects.
The bill explicitly subjects public works procurements by Morgan State University to State apprenticeship utilization requirements and prevailing wage apprenticeship standards.
The bill's provisions amending procurement laws under § 11-203 apply the public works apprenticeship utilization requirements directly to Saint Mary's College of Maryland.

As the state's principal agency for public works, capital improvements, and facility construction, DGS will be required to ensure that contractors and subcontractors comply with the new apprentice and journeyworker utilization percentages and verification requirements.

MDOT awards and manages significant public works and infrastructure contracts that are subject to prevailing wage laws and will have to incorporate the revised apprentice and journeyworker utilization standards into contract administration.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves higher education capital improvement and service contracts exceeding statutory thresholds and approves procurement policies affected by the bill.
Under § 17-602(d), the Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.
Under § 17-602(d), the State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the State Apprenticeship Training Fund separately.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees capital construction and maintenance of correctional facilities subject to public works procurement and prevailing wage requirements, directly impacting its contractor utilization standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The board retains dispute and contract claim authority over procurement contracts awarded by the universities and community colleges referenced under § 11-203.

Synopsis: Extending the deadline for the report of findings and recommendations from the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing from June 1, 2025, to December 1, 2028; and extending the termination date for the Workgroup from June 30, 2026, to December 31, 2028.

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to December 31, 2028. Alters the workgroup reporting deadline to December 1, 2028. Requires the workgroup to submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly. Continues the workgroup study on specialized case management and support programs for affected individuals. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (ODHH) staffs and supports the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, whose operations, reporting deadline, and termination date are extended by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the lifespan, reporting deadline, and mandate of an active statutory body—the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing—through December 31, 2028.

The bill requires the Workgroup to submit its report of findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2028, and the staffing entity (ODHH) is a coordinating office within the Executive Department.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning on July 1, 2026, a county or municipality to notify the Department of the Environment within 10 business days  after a county or municipality accepts the permit application for a new building that has a proposed gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more.
Title: Environment - Permit Applications for New Buildings - Notice (Large Buildings for Tomorrow Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.

bill_summary: Requires a county or municipality to notify the Maryland Department of the Environment after accepting certain building permit applications. Mandates notification within 10 business days after accepting an application for a new building of 35,000 square feet or more. Excludes parking garage space from the gross floor area threshold calculation. Requires notices to include the address, permit number, square footage, building type, planned energy sources, and owner contact information. Applies prospectively to construction with utility service requests, development applications, or permit applications filed after the effective date.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: counties, municipalities, and owners and developers of proposed new buildings with a gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment and local governments can implement the notification requirement using existing resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires local governments (counties and municipalities) to provide notice to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) within 10 business days of accepting a permit application for any new building with a proposed gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more. MDE will receive and track these notices to support its Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for certain local law enforcement officers if the Seat Pleasant Police Department becomes a participating governmental unit; and providing that a certain individual is entitled to eligibility service and creditable service that was earned before the effective date of the Seat Pleasant Police Department's participation in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System - Seat Pleasant Police Department

bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for permanent full-time Seat Pleasant police officers. Applies only if the Seat Pleasant Police Department becomes a participating governmental unit in the system. Grants past eligibility and creditable service to qualifying officers employed before the participation effective date. Covers local law enforcement officers employed in permanent full-time positions before, on, or after the date. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System; Seat Pleasant Police Department
stakeholders: Permanent full-time local law enforcement officers of the Seat Pleasant Police Department and the City of Seat Pleasant
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. If Seat Pleasant elects to participate, its municipal pension liabilities increase by $2,104,315. Net local employer pension contributions increase by an estimated $541,380 annually beginning as early as fiscal 2028, reflecting a $680,330 contribution offset by a $138,950 new entrant credit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). If the Seat Pleasant Police Department participates as a governmental unit, the agency will be responsible for administering member enrollment, crediting past service, and managing contribution accounts.

Synopsis: Increasing from three to five the membership of the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County; requiring the Governor to appoint members to the Board from a list of individuals recommended by the Anne Arundel County delegations to the General Assembly; altering eligibility requirements for Board membership; and requiring the Board to adopt and publish a certain ethics policy.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Board of License Commissioners - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Increases the membership of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from three to five. Requires the Governor to appoint members from lists recommended by the county General Assembly delegations. Authorizes the Governor to request a new list of recommendations at any time. Prohibits more than three members from the same political party and two from the same legislative district. Requires the Board to adopt and publish a written conflict of interest and recusal policy. Sets the initial terms for the two additional members to begin May 2, 2027.
responsible_party: Governor; Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Members and prospective appointees of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners, alcoholic beverage license holders and applicants in Anne Arundel County, and Anne Arundel County taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $39,995 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 to fund salaries, fringe benefits, and incidental expenses for two new board members. State operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Governor to appoint members to the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from recommendations submitted by county legislative delegations, and grants the Governor authority to request new lists of recommendations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and executing appointments to state and local boards and commissions, directly encompassing the gubernatorial appointments altered by this bill.

The bill mandates that the Board adopt and publish a written policy concerning conflicts of interest and recusal, intersecting with the State Ethics Commission's role in ethics laws and standards for public officials.

Synopsis: Extending the presumption of compensability under the workers' compensation law to include, subject to certain conditions, Carroll County correctional deputies who suffer from heart disease or hypertension resulting in partial disability or death; and altering a certain definition of "public safety employee" so as to apply a certain workers' compensation provision relating to permanent partial disability benefits to correctional deputies employed by Carroll County.
Title: Workers' Compensation - Heart Disease and Hypertension Presumption and Permanent Partial Disability - Carroll County Correctional Deputies

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Extends the workers' compensation occupational disease presumption for heart disease and hypertension to Carroll County correctional deputies. Conditions the presumption on heart disease or hypertension being more severe than pre-existing conditions. Requires correctional deputies employed on or before September 30, 2026, to submit medical reports by December 31, 2026. Classifies Carroll County correctional deputies as public safety employees for enhanced permanent partial disability benefits. Applies the public safety employee designation prospectively to claims arising on or after October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Carroll County Sheriff's Office
stakeholders: Carroll County correctional deputies and Carroll County
fiscal_impact_summary: Carroll County expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2027 due to enhanced permanent partial disability benefits and increased occupational disease claims; exact costs cannot be reliably estimated. State operations, finances, and revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission is the state agency responsible for administering Maryland's workers' compensation laws and adjudicating claims. It will oversee and adjudicate any workers' compensation claims filed by Carroll County correctional deputies under the newly established occupational disease presumption and enhanced permanent partial disability benefit provisions.

The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions that combine with workplace injuries or occupational diseases. Because the bill establishes specific requirements evaluating pre-existing heart disease and hypertension conditions, the Fund could be involved in contested claims involving pre-existing disabilities.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that the Governor include in the annual budget bill a $350,000 appropriation to the State's Consumer Health Information Hub; requiring the Hub to carry out certain duties to the extent funding is available; and repealing the termination date for certain provisions of law related to consumer health information and the State's Consumer Health Information Hub.
Title: Consumer Health Information - Termination Date and Mandatory Funding for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub - Repeal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Repeals the June 30, 2026 termination date for the State's Consumer Health Information Hub. Repeals the requirement that the Governor include an annual $350,000 appropriation to the Hub. Requires the Hub to carry out its statutory health literacy duties to the extent funding is available. Continues the requirement that the Hub submit an annual implementation report to designated legislative committees by July 1. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy
stakeholders: University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy, State and local government agencies, health systems, nonprofit and community-based organizations, and Maryland health care consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances or operations, as the $350,000 mandated annual appropriation was scheduled to sunset after fiscal 2026 and the Hub must operate to the extent funding is available.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State's Consumer Health Information Hub is housed within the University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy (part of USM). The bill eliminates the Hub's June 30, 2026 termination date while repealing its $350,000 annual mandated appropriation, directing it to carry out its operations to the extent funding is available.

The bill amends the Health - General Article governing statewide consumer health information and health literacy, an area closely coordinated with the Maryland Department of Health, which collaborates with the Hub on evaluating health communication and literacy initiatives.
The bill explicitly repeals the statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include a $350,000 appropriation for the Hub in the annual state budget bill.
As the agency responsible for preparing the state budget and managing mandated appropriations on behalf of the Governor, DBM is impacted by the repeal of the annual $350,000 mandated appropriation.

The Hub's codified statutory duties specifically include supporting public reporting of vital public health information, including health care quality reports from the Maryland Health Care Commission.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Wicomico County and the governing body of a municipal corporation in Wicomico County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain real property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.
Title: Wicomico County - Property Tax Credit - Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.

bill_summary: Authorizes Wicomico County or a municipal corporation in Wicomico County to grant a property tax credit. Applies to property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc., for development, rehabilitation, and transfer to a private owner. Requires the organization to intend to relinquish ownership in the near future. Excludes property occupied by administrative or warehouse buildings owned by the organization. Requires an annual report documenting local property holdings and transactions if a jurisdiction grants the credit. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Governing Body of Wicomico County; governing bodies of municipal corporations in Wicomico County
stakeholders: Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc.; Wicomico County; municipal corporations in Wicomico County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. Wicomico County and municipal property tax revenues decrease by a minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent credits are granted. Expenditures are not directly affected.
