bill_summary: Authorizes qualifying transit-oriented developments served by frequent rail transit to receive enterprise zone designations. Requires the Maryland Economic Development Corporation to prioritize redeveloping government-owned land near qualifying rail stations. Prohibits local governments from imposing minimum off-street parking mandates within 0.25 miles of qualifying rail stations. Requires local zoning to allow mixed-use development within 0.5 miles of qualifying rail stations. Restricts local land use limitations on certain transportation land subject to an approved transit-oriented development plan.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Economic Development Corporation; Department of Commerce; Sustainable Growth Subcabinet
stakeholders: Local governments; residential and commercial real estate developers; businesses and residents near qualifying rail transit stations; Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate state and local impact. State general fund expenditures increase in future years to reimburse local governments for enterprise zone property tax credits. State income tax revenues to the general fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and Higher Education Investment Fund decrease in future years. Local property tax revenues decrease from enterprise zone credits, and development impact fees and excise taxes are delayed if contingent provisions take effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is directly tasked with reviewing and concurring with local adequate parking studies within 45 days, approving transit-oriented development (TOD) plans that limit local zoning restrictions on contiguous transit land, and managing TOD joint developments and leases on transportation-owned properties.

The bill statutorily requires MEDCO to prioritize projects that redevelop land contiguous to rail transit stations owned by the State, Baltimore City, or WMATA when issuing loans under the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program.

Commerce oversees the Enterprise Zone program, and the bill expands the definition and process to automatically designate qualifying transit-oriented developments as enterprise zones outside the statutory cap on annual designations by the Secretary.

As the MDOT modal agency operating rail transit stations (including Light Rail, Metro Subway, and MARC), MTA's stations and surrounding state-owned properties are the core geographic focus of the bill's land use, parking, and transit-oriented development mandates.

The Comptroller administers state income tax collections and tax credits, which will experience future revenue reductions in the General Fund, TTF, and HEIF due to expanded enterprise zone tax credits created under the bill.

MDP guides state land use policies and plays a central administrative role with the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, which receives local enterprise zone election filings and coordinates state TOD designations.

DHCD is the primary agency for community revitalization and housing finance; the bill facilitates mixed-use and residential housing expansion around transit hubs to support statewide affordable housing goals.
The legislation was introduced as an Administration priority bill to implement the Moore-Miller State Plan and Executive Order 01.01.2025.19 targeting transit-oriented development and housing supply.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a food retailer and a third-party delivery service provider from engaging in the practice of dynamic pricing or using consumer personal data to set a price for consumer goods or services; prohibiting a food retailer and a third-party delivery service provider from using protected class data to offer, advertise, or sell a consumer good or service under certain circumstances; making a certain violation of the Act an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice that is subject to enforcement and penalties; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits food retailers and third-party delivery service providers from using dynamic pricing to set higher prices for tax-exempt food. Bans these entities from using personal data to increase tax-exempt food prices for a single consumer. Prohibits using protected class data to deny or withhold accommodations, advantages, or privileges from consumers. Requires the Consumer Protection Division to provide alleged violators a 45-day notice period to cure violations. Excludes violations from criminal penalties and prohibits private civil lawsuits.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Food retailers operating establishments of at least 15,000 square feet, third-party delivery service providers, and Maryland consumers purchasing food
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General increase at least minimally beginning in FY 2027 to cover contractual training and technical expertise costs. The bill is not anticipated to have a material impact on State revenues or local government finances and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of dynamic pricing and data protection restrictions as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General. The fiscal note anticipates an increase in general fund expenditures for the agency.
HB 895 is an Administration bill introduced at the request of the Governor to advance executive policy priorities regarding consumer protection and predatory pricing regulation.

Synopsis: Establishing the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund in the Military Department to provide funds for State active duty mobilization of the National Guard.
Title: Military Department - National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund
bill_summary: Establishes the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund in the Military Department. Requires the Adjutant General to administer the fund. Restricts fund usage to personnel, equipment, and operational expenses of the National Guard during State active duty mobilization. Credits any investment earnings of the fund to the General Fund of the State. Mandates timely replenishment of expended money to maintain operational effectiveness for future mobilizations.
responsible_party: Military Department; Office of the Adjutant General
stakeholders: Maryland National Guard personnel ordered to State active duty
fiscal_impact_summary: Accelerates general fund expenditures to capitalize the fund, likely with at least $1.0 million in fiscal 2027, with special fund revenues increasing correspondingly. Special fund expenditures increase starting in fiscal 2027 based on mobilizations. Ongoing general fund expenditures will accelerate as needed to replenish the fund. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund in the Office of the Adjutant General within the Military Department and designates the Adjutant General as the administrator of the fund.
The fund is specifically established to pay for the personnel, equipment, and operations of the Maryland National Guard during State active duty mobilizations.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the new special fund separately and invest the money in the fund in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill specifically mandates that the Comptroller shall account for the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund.
State active duty mobilization of the National Guard is ordered by the Governor as commander-in-chief, which triggers expenditures from the newly created fund.
The fund relies on State budget appropriations and replenishments managed through the executive budget process, which DBM oversees and coordinates.

bill_summary: Alters, renames, and transfers multiple State economic development programs, financing funds, and tax credits. Redesignates the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account as the Strategic Closing Fund within the Department of Commerce. Transfers the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Zone and Build Our Future Grant programs to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation. Extends the Job Creation, Research and Development, and Employer Security Clearance Costs tax credits. Exempts sales of certain information technology services and digital products between affiliated group members from sales and use tax. Reallocates video lottery terminal proceeds and increases financing caps for small business development programs.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Maryland Economic Development Corporation; Comptroller of Maryland; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland business entities, small businesses, minority- and women-owned businesses, technology companies, film production entities, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State net fiscal impact is negative $37.3 million in FY 2027, with general fund revenues decreasing by $35.5 million and special fund revenues decreasing by $1.8 million due to sales and use tax exemptions. In FY 2028, general fund revenues decrease by $60.2 million and general fund expenditures increase by $10.6 million. Local highway user revenues decrease by an estimated $0.4 million annually beginning in FY 2028, and local property tax revenues are moderately affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Commerce is the primary state department impacted by the bill. It oversees the vast majority of altered economic development programs and tax credits, including the Strategic Closing Fund, MEDAAF, MSBDFA, SMWOBA, Job Creation Tax Credit, R&D Tax Credit, and Film Production Activity Tax Credit.

The bill directly transfers the administration and management of both the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone Program and the Build Our Future Grant Program from Commerce to MEDCO, expanding MEDCO's operational responsibilities, grant-making authority, and reporting requirements.

The Comptroller administers the state sales and use tax, which is amended to exempt certain affiliated group information technology and digital product sales (resulting in tens of millions in annual revenue reductions). The Comptroller also accounts for several established special funds, processes income and corporate tax credits, distributes VLT proceeds, and must submit a report on tracking tax credit carryforwards.

The Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold, invest, and report on the moneys of the newly restructured and consolidated special funds under the bill, including the Strategic Closing Fund, Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund, Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Fund, and Build Our Future Grant Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees video lottery terminal operations and prepares transmittals that govern the statutory distribution of VLT proceeds, which this bill alters by redirecting $5.0 million to the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund.

DBM oversees state budget execution and fiscal planning, which will be affected by major shifts in general and special fund expenditures, budget amendments for fund transfers, and backfilling lost education revenues.
Transportation Trust Fund revenues and local highway user revenue grants are reduced by the extension and alteration of corporate income tax credits included in the bill.

This is an Administration initiative establishing key statewide economic competitiveness policies. The Governor proposes funding for the Strategic Closing Fund, submits budget amendments, and receives multiple required program evaluation reports.

Higher education institutions serve as anchor qualified institutions for RISE zones and are eligible recipients for up to 50% of grant funds appropriated under the Build Our Future Grant Program; additionally, the Higher Education Investment Fund is fiscally affected by corporate tax credit extensions.

As a public research university, Morgan State can serve as a qualified institution under the RISE Zone Program and is eligible to receive infrastructure grants under the Build Our Future Grant Program.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an agent of a private home detention monitoring agency, an employee of a courthouse, or an employee of a correctional facility from engaging in certain activities promoting or otherwise soliciting business for a private home detention monitoring agency on the grounds of a courthouse or correctional facility.

bill_summary: Prohibits private home detention monitoring agencies and their agents from soliciting business on courthouse or correctional facility grounds. Extends this solicitation ban to courthouse employees and correctional facility employees. Bans distributing, displaying, or wearing items advertising private home detention monitoring agency services on those grounds. Establishes misdemeanor penalties with fines up to $2,500 for first offenses and $5,000 for subsequent offenses. Requires license suspensions of 30 days for first offenses and 90 days for subsequent offenses for licensed violators. Requires referral of convicted licensed offenders to the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

bill_summary: Prohibits a law enforcement agency from assigning an officer to non-administrative duties unless issued protective body armor. Requires issued armor to meet current National Institute of Justice ballistic standards and unexpired manufacturer dates. Requires agencies to replace protective body armor before the expiration or suggested replacement date indicated by the manufacturer. Directs agencies to notify the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission if armor is unreplaced 31 days past expiration. Requires the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to withhold available grant funds from noncompliant agencies.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $55,300 in fiscal 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health to purchase protective body armor for its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit. No material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates GOCPP to withhold and manage grant disbursements to law enforcement agencies that fail to comply with protective body armor replacement and notification requirements, and GOCPP administers the State Protective Body Armor Fund.

The bill has a direct fiscal impact on MDH, requiring $55,305 in general fund expenditures in FY 2027 to purchase compliant protective body armor for 45 officers in its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit (STIU).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is tasked by the bill with receiving failure-to-replace notifications from law enforcement agencies and transmitting them to GOCPP. The department's Division of Parole and Probation also qualifies for body armor grant funding.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, MSP must ensure all active non-administrative officers are issued compliant, unexpired body armor and adhere to statutory replacement deadlines.
DNR employs the Maryland Natural Resources Police, which is subject to the bill's body armor issuance, compliance, and replacement standards for sworn officers.
MDTA operates a dedicated police force that must comply with the bill's body armor replacement timelines and standards.
MDOT oversees modal administrations that maintain sworn police forces (such as the Maryland Transit Administration Police), which must comply with the bill's body armor requirements.
The Comptroller's Office employs sworn enforcement officers who are subject to the bill's protective body armor equipment mandates.
Morgan State University maintains a campus police department subject to the bill's requirements governing body armor issuance, replacement, and reporting.
USM institutions operate campus police departments that employ sworn officers who must be equipped with compliant, unexpired protective body armor.
The Department of Labor has regulatory and enforcement personnel identified in state law enforcement surveys affected by protective equipment guidelines.

bill_summary: Prohibits applying sewage sludge with regulated PFAS concentrations of 50 parts per billion or more to agricultural or marginal land. Restricts applying sludge with regulated PFAS concentrations between 25 and 50 parts per billion starting October 1, 2028. Authorizes generators to commingle sewage sludge for up to two years to reduce PFAS levels below 25 parts per billion. Requires generators exceeding 25 parts per billion of PFAS to complete source tracking studies and develop five-year mitigation plans. Authorizes local jurisdictions and pretreatment authorities to establish pretreatment standards and set rates and fees for industrial users.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Sewage sludge generators, publicly owned treatment works, industrial wastewater dischargers, local pretreatment authorities, and owners and operators of agricultural or marginal land
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $248,100 in FY 2027 for three new positions, with ongoing personnel and operational costs increasing in subsequent years. Beginning in FY 2029, local government expenditures and nonbudgeted state expenditures may increase significantly for sewage sludge testing, mitigation, or alternative disposal. Local revenues may increase from rates and fees imposed on industrial users.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for adopting regulations, establishing monitoring protocols and reporting levels, providing technical assistance to sewage sludge generators and local jurisdictions, reviewing and approving mitigation plans, and evaluating pretreatment controls for industrial users.

MES is explicitly defined in statute as a sewage sludge generator and operates approximately 90 wastewater treatment plants across Maryland. The bill will impact MES operations by requiring compliance with PFAS testing, monitoring frequencies, and potential mitigation measures, leading to potential increases in nonbudgeted expenditures and contract revenues.

Under the Maryland Environment Article provisions governing sewage sludge, MDE cannot adopt regulations dealing with the land application of sewage sludge without the approval of MDA. Because the bill establishes strict new limits on applying sewage sludge to agricultural land, MDA has direct regulatory and policy oversight involvement.

fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2027 only for contractual services to complete the study. There is no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 956 directly mandates the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to conduct a comprehensive study on buildings in the State that are more than 40 years old and contain condominiums, and report its findings to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026. The fiscal note estimates a $75,000 general fund expenditure for DHCD in FY 2027 to procure contractual services to complete the study.

Synopsis: Requiring each local school system to designate a local point of contact for certain communications, to comply with, and certify compliance with, the State minimum cybersecurity standards, and to conduct a cybersecurity maturity assessment every 2 years; requiring the Office of Security Management within the Department of Information Technology to annually review and, if necessary, update the State minimum cybersecurity standards; requiring the Department to advise local school systems on certain functions; etc.
Title: Cybersecurity - Standards and Compliance - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Requires each local school system to designate a point of contact for cybersecurity communications. Mandates local school systems to comply with State minimum cybersecurity standards beginning in 2027. Directs each local school system to conduct a cybersecurity maturity assessment every two years. Requires biennial compliance certification to the Office of Security Management starting June 30, 2027. Requires the Office of Security Management to annually review and update State minimum cybersecurity standards as necessary. Directs the Department of Information Technology, on request, to advise local school systems on compliance and remediation.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Office of Security Management
stakeholders: local school systems in Maryland, local school IT and cybersecurity personnel, and public school students and staff
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources with no revenue impact. Local school system expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2027 for technology upgrades, contracted services, and staff needed to achieve compliance, though total statewide costs are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT, through its Office of Security Management and the State Chief Information Security Officer, is the primary implementing agency. The bill requires DoIT to annually review and update State minimum cybersecurity standards, receive contact designations and biennial compliance certifications from local school systems, and advise local school systems on compliance, assessments, and remediation.

MSDE oversees the 24 local school systems across Maryland. The bill amends the Education Article to establish cybersecurity compliance, point-of-contact designation, and biennial assessment mandates across all local school systems.

Synopsis: Altering the prohibition on a register of wills or court granting letters in administrative or judicial probate to certain individuals who are not citizens or permanent residents of the United States.
Title: Registers of Wills - Appointment of Personal Representatives

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: Alters restrictions on appointing noncitizens as personal representatives in estate administration. Authorizes registers of wills and courts to grant letters of administration to lawful permanent residents of the United States. Permits individuals who are neither citizens nor permanent residents to receive letters under specified conditions. Requires those individuals to be domiciled in the United States. Requires those individuals to be the decedent's spouse, ancestor, descendant, or sibling. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Registers of Wills; Orphans' Courts
stakeholders: Noncitizens and lawful permanent residents seeking appointment as personal representatives, along with decedents' families and heirs
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory qualifications under Estates and Trusts § 5-105 for individuals to whom a register of wills may grant letters of administration to serve as personal representatives of an estate.

The bill affects the granting of letters in judicial probate proceedings handled within Maryland's court system (specifically Orphans' Courts), which the Administrative Office of the Courts administratively and operationally supports.

Synopsis: Requiring the owner or possessor of a weight and measure used for the retail sale of electricity as a vehicle fuel to display certain information in a conspicuous manner; requiring all electricity possessed, offered, or exposed for sale and sold at retail as a vehicle fuel to be measured and sold in units of kilowatt-hours; authorizing the owner or possessor of a weight and measure used for the retail sale of electricity as a vehicle fuel to charge certain fees for certain services; etc.
Title: Electric Vehicle Fuel Sold at Retail - Equipment Requirements, Units of Measure, and Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Requires owners of weights and measures used for retail vehicle electricity sales to conspicuously display local contact information. Mandates that all electricity sold at retail as vehicle fuel be measured and sold in kilowatt-hours. Limits customer charges during a charging session strictly to the kilowatt-hours of electricity dispensed. Authorizes the owner or possessor to charge a fixed or time-based fee for related services. Requires any service fee to be applied at charging conclusion and itemized on the receipt.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Retail electric vehicle fuel sellers, electric vehicle charging station operators, and electric vehicle drivers
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct, material impact on State finances or local government operations, as the bill largely codifies existing standards and regulatory requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 11 of the Agriculture Article governing weights and measures, which is directly administered and enforced by the Maryland Department of Agriculture's Weights and Measures Program.
The Public Service Commission regulates retail electric service and public utilities in Maryland and provided information regarding the regulation and sale of electricity as vehicle fuel.
The Maryland Energy Administration coordinates state energy policy and electric vehicle infrastructure initiatives, and served as an information source for the legislation.
The Comptroller regulates motor fuel industries and tax collection, was considered in earlier versions of the bill regarding retail pricing, and was consulted for the fiscal note.
The Department of General Services manages state-owned facilities, vehicle fleets, and electric vehicle charging infrastructure across state properties, and was consulted for the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund  to provide grants that advance agricultural fairs and education in the State; requiring interest earnings of the Fund to be credited to the Fund; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $200,000 to the Fund each year; requiring the Comptroller to pay $100,000 to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Inc, and $100,000 to the Maryland FFA Association from the Fund for agricultural education programs; etc.
Title: Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund - Establishment ( Charles J. Otto Agricultural Education Promise Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund to advance agricultural fairs and education. Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $200,000 to the Fund in the State budget. Requires the Comptroller to pay an annual grant of $100,000 to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Inc. Requires the Comptroller to pay an annual grant of $100,000 to the Maryland FFA Association. Repeals a $75,000 annual grant to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Inc., from the horse racing Special Fund.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland State Treasurer
stakeholders: Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Inc.; Maryland FFA Association; youth participating in agricultural education; horse racing special fund grantees
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $200,000 annually beginning in FY 2028 due to the mandated appropriation, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures for grant distributions. Horse racing special fund revenues increase by $75,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to the repealed grant distribution, making those funds available for other existing statutory grantees. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller to administer the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund, account for its monies, and disburse the annual statutory grants to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation and the Maryland FFA Association, as well as administer adjustments to the horse racing Special Fund distributions.

The bill codifies the new grant fund within the Agriculture Article of the Maryland Annotated Code to promote and advance agricultural education, youth agricultural programs, and agricultural fairs across the state.
The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established special fund separately, manage its investments, and exempt its interest earnings from accruing to the General Fund.
The bill creates a mandated annual General Fund appropriation of $200,000 beginning in fiscal year 2028, impacting state budget preparation and long-term fiscal planning managed by DBM.
The bill imposes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $200,000 to the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund in the state budget bill.
The bill amends the Business Regulation Article concerning distributions from the horse racing Special Fund, which is regulated under the Maryland Racing Commission within the Department of Labor.

Synopsis: Prohibiting licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and third parties directed by licensed massage therapists or registered massage practitioners from placing, publishing, or distributing certain advertisements; and requiring that if an advertisement for massage therapy services lists the name of a licensed massage therapist or registered massage practitioner, the name displayed on the advertisement must be consistent with the name of the individual on the Board issued license or registration.
Title: Health Occupations - Massage Therapy - Advertising

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Prohibits licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and acting third parties from advertising prostitution, escort, or sexual services. Bans massage therapy advertisements on websites known for sexual services and ads indicating sexual activity is included. Requires advertisements to display the provider's full licensed name and license or registration number. Exempts multi-practitioner businesses from listing each provider unless individual names are specified. Mandates removal of noncompliant physical signs or billboards visible to the public before May 1, 2027. Directs the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to adopt regulations defining prohibited language and reporting procedures.
responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, massage therapy businesses, third-party advertisers, and massage therapy clients
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill and adopt required regulations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates advertising for licensed massage therapists and registered massage practitioners, requiring the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners—an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health—to adopt regulations defining prohibited language and establish violation reporting procedures.

Synopsis: Requiring the Secretary of Human Services to establish and maintain a Guardianship Assistance Program to promote the placement and maintenance of children in permanent guardianship homes by providing guardianship assistance to guardians of minor children; establishing the State Foster Youth Ombudsman in the Department of Human Services; requiring the Ombudsman to provide legal expertise in child welfare, custody and guardianship matters, and appeal and due process; etc.
Title: Family Law and Human Services - Guardianship Assistance Program and State Foster Youth Ombudsman - Establishment (Kanaiyah's Law)

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Requires the Secretary of Human Services to establish and maintain a Guardianship Assistance Program providing monetary and medical assistance. Establishes eligibility criteria for guardians who execute voluntary assistance agreements following six months of foster care placement. Allows approved assistance to continue until age 21 for qualifying individuals participating in education, work, or job training. Authorizes local departments of social services to terminate assistance if certain violent or registered sex offenders reside in the home. Establishes the State Foster Youth Ombudsman within the Department of Human Services to advocate for youth in out-of-home care.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Youth in foster care and out-of-home care, legal guardians of minor children, caregivers and adoptive parents, and local departments of social services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $37,500 in FY 2028 and by $50,000 annually thereafter to fund the State Foster Youth Ombudsman position, assuming a vacant position is repurposed; costs would rise to $120,000 in FY 2028 and $154,000 annually if a new position is created instead. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 980 directly tasks the Secretary of Human Services and DHS with establishing and maintaining the Guardianship Assistance Program, adopting implementing regulations, and creating and staffing the State Foster Youth Ombudsman position within the department.

The bill requires creating a new State Foster Youth Ombudsman position within the Management Service of the State Personnel Management System, which requires DBM approval for position classification and the repurposing of a vacant Position Identification Number (PIN).

Synopsis: Extending from 1 p.m. to 11 p.m., rather than 9 p.m., the hours during which a holder of a Class HC (health club) beer and wine license in Harford County may sell alcoholic beverages.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class HC (Health Club) License - Hours of Sale

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: Extends the hours of sale for Class HC beer and wine licenses in Harford County. Permits 6-day and 7-day license holders to sell beer and wine for on-premises consumption until 11 p.m. Replaces the prior closing time of 9 p.m. while maintaining the 1 p.m. opening time. Applies to qualifying health club facilities that feature swimming pools or pickleball courts. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Holders of Class HC beer and wine licenses in Harford County and health club patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: No state effect. The bill does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers related excise taxes. While local licensing and hours of sale are primarily overseen by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners, the bill touches on alcohol regulation within the state.

Synopsis: Establishing the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund in the Maryland Department of Labor; requiring that investment earnings be credited to the General Fund of the State; requiring the Secretary of Labor to annually calculate costs; authorizing the Department to set fees; requiring providers of travel services to file with the Department proof of professional liability and errors and omissions liability insurance in the amount of at least $1,000,000; etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Travel Services - Special Fund, Fees, and Surety Requirement (Don't You Worry (Wurie) Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds

bill_summary: Establishes the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor. Requires sellers of travel and independent agents to annually file proof of professional liability and errors and omissions insurance. Mandates coverage of at least $1,000,000 and sets an initial $300 annual filing fee. Requires each seller of travel to annually file a list of affiliated independent agents. Prohibits receiving payment for travel services unless the provider meets all annual filing requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: sellers of travel; independent travel agents; consumers purchasing travel services
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by at least $99,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 from filing fees. State expenditures increase by $106,513 in FY 2027 ($101,000 special funds and $5,513 general funds) for one executive director and start-up costs, with ongoing special fund expenditures averaging around $100,000 annually. Minimal increase in general fund revenues from interest earnings. No material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing and regulating agency under the bill. It is responsible for administering the newly established Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund, collecting annual filing fees, verifying insurance filings from sellers of travel and independent agents, establishing fee structures, adopting regulations, and conducting enforcement.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Labor to pay all collected registration fees to the Comptroller, who is statutorily directed to distribute those fees into the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund.

The bill specifies that the new special fund is subject to audit under § 2-1220 of the State Government Article, and the fiscal note notes that the Office of Legislative Audits can incorporate the fund into its regular audits of MD Labor using existing resources.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to notify a person who files a charter document if the Department does not accept the document; requiring the Department to accept a corrected charter document under a certain circumstance; authorizing certain governing bodies of certain corporations to take certain actions without a meeting of the governing body subject to certain conditions;  repealing the authority of certain persons to maintain a suit in a State court; etc.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to notify a filer if a charter document is rejected. Mandates the Department record a corrected charter document as of the original filing date if refiled within 30 days. Authorizes boards of registered open-end investment companies to act without a meeting by majority consent under specified conditions. Authorizes corporate boards, bankruptcy trustees, and receivers to execute bankruptcy relief orders without stockholder approval. Repeals misdemeanor penalties for officers and agents of foreign corporations doing business in Maryland without registering or qualifying.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland corporations, registered open-end investment companies, foreign corporations doing business in Maryland and their officers, limited partnerships and general partnerships, and corporate charter document filers
fiscal_impact_summary: State Department of Assessments and Taxation operations can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a criminal misdemeanor offense for officers and agents of unregistered foreign corporations and amends the standards under which a foreign corporation may maintain a civil suit in Maryland courts, directly touching judicial proceedings administered and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class 7 micro-brewery license to the holder of a Class B-D-7 license in the 46th alcoholic beverages district, subject to a certain limitation; requiring the Board to establish a standard template for certain memoranda of understanding by January 1, 2027; authorizing certain holders of certain Class D licenses in the 46th alcoholic beverages district to apply for a 7-day sales privilege under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Baltimore City – Alcoholic Beverages – 46th Alcoholic Beverages District

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class 7 micro-brewery license in the 46th district. Authorizes the Board to transfer a Class B-D-7 license from the 40th district into the 46th district. Authorizes certain Class D license holders in the 46th district to apply for a seven-day sales privilege. Requires the Board to establish a standard template for neighborhood association memoranda of understanding by January 1, 2027. Requires the Board to adopt regulations establishing tiered penalties for license violations. Extends expiration dates for three specified alcoholic beverages licenses to July 1, 2027, for renewal or transfer.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants in Baltimore City, local neighborhood associations in Baltimore City, and patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Baltimore City finances and operations are not materially affected; revenues collected from the $15,000 one-time fee for a seven-day Class D sales privilege are dedicated to enforcing required memoranda of understanding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters alcoholic beverages regulations and licensing in Baltimore City, including provisions regarding manufacturer/wholesaler donations and tax remittance. Although implementation is managed locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and there is no direct state fiscal effect, the Comptroller oversees state alcohol regulation and excise tax collection.

Synopsis: Authorizing the holder of a Class 9 limited distillery license to manufacture, rectify, or bottle more than one brand of alcoholic beverage; and authorizing the holder to manufacture or rectify up to 31,000 gallons of product of an entity other than the holder.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 9 Limited Distillery License - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages Manufacturing -see also- Breweries; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the holder of a Class 9 limited distillery license to produce more than one brand of alcoholic beverage. Repeals the requirement that a licensee maintain only one brand at any one time for each product. Allows the licensee to manufacture or rectify product for another brand or entity. Prohibits the licensee from manufacturing or rectifying more than 31,000 gallons of product each calendar year for another brand or entity. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
stakeholders: Holders of Class 9 limited distillery licenses and alcoholic beverage brands contracting for manufacturing or rectifying services
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters regulations and production limits governing Class 9 limited distillery licenses for manufacturing and rectifying spirits. According to the agency summary, the Comptroller is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state excise taxes on alcoholic beverages.

Synopsis: Requiring a police officer who is on duty at a polling place to obey the authority of the State Administrator, the Deputy State Administrator, or a local election director; providing that, in a polling place, certain individuals have the authority to keep the peace and order the arrest of certain persons; requiring a local election director, while serving in a polling place, to protect certain rights of challengers and watchers; etc.
Title: Election Law - Authority at Polling Places, Early Voting Centers, and Counting Centers - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Administrator, Deputy State Administrator, and local election directors to order arrests at polling places. Requires on-duty police officers at polling places to obey orders issued by these officials. Allows political committees and specified independent spenders to designate accredited challengers, watchers, and canvass observers. Expands the designation and presence of accredited challengers and watchers to early voting centers. Prohibits challengers and watchers from physically handling voting equipment. Requires designating persons to submit certificates of accredited challengers or watchers to local boards before entry.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections; State Administrator of Elections; local election directors
stakeholders: Election judges, local election directors, police officers on duty at polling places, accredited and nonaccredited challengers and watchers, canvass observers, candidates, political parties, political committees, and independent spenders
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Election Law Article to govern the authority of the State Administrator of Elections, Deputy State Administrator, and local election officials at polling places, early voting centers, and counting centers. It also tasks the State Board with prescribing forms for accredited challengers and watchers.

The bill explicitly requires police officers on duty at polling places to obey orders from the State Administrator, the Deputy State Administrator, or local election directors to maintain peace or effectuate arrests, providing statutory protection for officers executing such orders.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain facilities from involuntarily transferring or discharging a resident to certain housing or before receiving certain confirmations; altering the information required to be included in a certain notice or new notice; requiring that a certain notice or new notice be provided to certain residents at least a certain period of time before an involuntary discharge or transfer; establishing time requirements that apply to the discharge or transfer of a resident if a new notice of involuntary discharge or transfer is provided; etc.
Title: Nursing Facilities - Involuntary Discharge or Transfer

NarrowSubjects.Name: Long-Term Care -see also- Continuing Care; Nursing Homes
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Nursing Homes -see also- AsstLiving; ContinCare; LTCare
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Prohibits nursing facilities from involuntarily transferring or discharging a resident to temporary housing or unconfirmed receiving facilities. Requires discharge notices to provide contact details for hearing requests, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, and Disability Rights Maryland. Repeals the shortened notice exception previously permitted when a resident resided in a facility for under 30 days. Establishes revised notice requirements and waiting periods ranging from seven to 30 days when transfer details change. Requires post-discharge care plans to identify the resident's post-discharge address and provide a safe, secure, and sustainable environment.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Residents of Maryland nursing facilities, nursing facility operators and staff, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, and Disability Rights Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates nursing facilities, prepares the standardized involuntary discharge notice form, receives copies of all involuntary discharge notices, and adopts regulations establishing requirements for post-discharge plans of care and hearing procedures.

The Department of Aging oversees the statewide Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, which is required under the bill to be provided with written notice of any proposed involuntary discharge or transfer and whose contact information must be provided to residents.
Administrative Law Judges within the Office of Administrative Hearings conduct hearings and issue binding orders regarding proposed involuntary transfers and discharges of nursing facility residents.

Synopsis: Authorizing a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to delay or deny a disbursement from the account of a certain individual or the account on which a certain individual is a beneficiary; requiring a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to provide certain financial records to certain entities; authorizing a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to contact certain individuals; and providing certain fiduciary institutions immunity from certain liability.
Title: Fiduciary Institutions - Exploitation of Seniors and Vulnerable Adults - Protections and Required Referral (Vulnerable Adult Banking Protection Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Authorizes a fiduciary institution to delay or deny disbursements from an account of an eligible adult if financial exploitation is suspected. Requires the institution to notify adult protective services, law enforcement, or a State's Attorney within four business days. Directs the institution to send written notice of delays to authorized account parties, excluding suspected exploiters. Authorizes institutions to extend disbursement delays and notify designated trusted contacts under specified conditions. Requires fiduciary institutions to provide relevant financial records to investigating authorities upon referral or request. Grants fiduciary institutions civil and administrative immunity when acting in good faith and exercising reasonable care.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; State's Attorneys; law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Maryland residents at least 65 years old and vulnerable adults; fiduciary institutions including banks, credit unions, and savings associations; trusted contacts and authorized account parties; adult protective services staff and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local social service agencies and law enforcement agencies can likely handle the bill's requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the Adult Protective Services (APS) program housed within local departments of social services overseen by DHS. Fiduciary institutions are required to report suspected financial exploitation to APS, provide relevant financial records, and APS may request or order extensions or terminations of disbursement delays.

The bill amends the Financial Institutions Article and governs fiduciary institutions, which fall under the regulatory and supervisory authority of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor.

The bill authorizes fiduciary institutions to notify law enforcement agencies of suspected financial exploitation, provides law enforcement access to confidential financial records, and allows law enforcement to request extensions of disbursement delays.

The bill authorizes courts of competent jurisdiction within the Judicial Branch to issue orders terminating or extending disbursement delays related to suspected vulnerable adult financial exploitation.

The bill establishes statutory protections against the financial exploitation of adults aged 65 and older and vulnerable adults, aligning closely with the Department of Aging's mission to advocate for the rights and welfare of older Marylanders.

Synopsis: Authorizing a county or municipality to establish a local suicide fatality review team to coordinate with certain local child fatality review teams and the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee; authorizing a team to review suicide deaths in the county, identify  factors associated with suicide, promote coordination among certain entities, and develop recommendations to prevent suicide; providing that certain information acquired by a local team is confidential and exempt from disclosure under the Maryland Public Information Act; etc.
Title: Public Health - Local Suicide Fatality Review Teams - Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Vital Records -see also- Death; Divorce; Marriage

bill_summary: Authorizes a county or municipality to establish a multidisciplinary and multiagency local suicide fatality review team. Permits two or more counties to establish a single multicounty local team under a memorandum of understanding. Requires local teams to meet at least quarterly, collect data, and coordinate with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee. Exempts team meetings discussing individual suicide cases from the Open Meetings Act. Designates team records and proceedings as confidential, privileged, and exempt from disclosure under the Maryland Public Information Act. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to a $500 fine and 90 days imprisonment for unauthorized disclosures.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Suicide Fatality Review Committee
stakeholders: County and municipal governments, local health departments, health care providers, law enforcement agencies, and individuals affected by suicide
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational impacts can likely be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. Local government and local health department expenditures may increase indeterminately beginning in fiscal 2027, estimated at $30,000 to $50,000 per jurisdiction that chooses to establish a review team.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is authorized to adopt regulations establishing protocols, procedures, and data security standards for local suicide fatality review teams. Local health officers play a primary role in forming and appointing members to the teams, and the teams coordinate closely with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly integrates local teams with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee, requiring local teams to follow its guidance, establish operating protocols with it, and submit case reports, data, and policy recommendations.

The bill specifies that the director of the local department of social services (or their designee) must be included on local review teams, and local teams are authorized to request and receive confidential social services records.
The bill requires local suicide fatality review teams to include county superintendents of schools (or their designees), directly involving local public school leadership overseen by MSDE.
Local review team membership includes State law enforcement officers, and local teams are authorized to request and examine police investigative data regarding suicide fatalities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Local teams must include emergency medical services providers from the county and may request records or statements from first responders involved with decedents.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for developmental disabilities services to individuals who received certain services in another state and relocated to the State; and requiring the Department to begin the determination process before an individual establishes residency in the State under certain circumstances.
Title: Developmental Disabilities Services - Expedited Eligibility Determinations for Recently Relocated Individuals (Ralph's Act)

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide expedited Medicaid eligibility determinations for certain individuals relocating to Maryland. Applies to qualifying dependents whose caretaker died or became incapacitated after receiving out-of-state waiver services for ten years. Requires the dependent's Maryland family member to have resided in the State for at least two years. Mandates that the Department complete each expedited eligibility review within 60 business days after receiving a complete application. Places eligible individuals into the crisis resolution category for waiver services based on their prior out-of-state care.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities who relocate to Maryland after losing an out-of-state caretaker, and their Maryland family members
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can likely implement the expedited determinations with existing resources, though redirection of staff may delay other applications. If application volume expands, costs could increase by approximately $80,000 annually for one additional staff position split between general and federal funds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (specifically the Developmental Disabilities Administration) is directly responsible for administering the Community Pathways waiver and implementing the expedited eligibility determinations and priority placements required by the bill.

As the principal state agency responsible for coordinating and improving the delivery of services and policies for individuals with disabilities across Maryland, the bill aligns closely with the department's core advocacy and interagency policy focus.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law establishing that certain noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in certain employment contracts are null and void as being against the public policy of the State to licensed architects employed by certain employers that relocate the majority of its employees outside the State or have its principal place of business outside the State.

bill_summary: Voids noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in employment contracts concerning certain licensed architects. Applies to employers employing more than 30 qualifying workers on the architect's first day of employment. Requires a majority of those initial workers to report in Maryland or work remotely within the State. Invalidates provisions if the employer lacks an in-state principal place of business on the enforcement date. Also invalidates provisions if the employer lacks a majority Maryland workforce on that enforcement date. Applies only to employment contracts executed on or after October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Licensed architects and employers of licensed architects with more than 30 employees
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1016 amends Title 3 of the Labor and Employment Article regarding noncompete and conflict of interest clauses, specifically applying protections to licensed architects whose employers relocate out of state. The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for enforcing state labor laws and regulating occupational licensing for professions, including architects.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State or a unit of local government from approving the construction or operation of a building, structure, or other real property for use as a detention facility by a private entity; establishing that a building, structure, or other real property is considered proposed for use as a detention facility, regardless of how the use is descried in an application or permit request under certain circumstances; establishing a certain penalty; authorizing the Attorney General to bring a civil action to enforce the Act; etc.
Title: Correctional Services - Private Detention Facilities - Zoning Requirement

bill_summary: Prohibits the State and local governments from approving the construction or operation of private detention facilities. Prohibits private entities from operating or occupying real property as a detention facility. Excludes licensed health care facilities, residential child care programs, and child placement agencies meeting specified treatment purposes. Authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil enforcement actions and seek injunctive relief. Subjects violating private entities to a civil penalty not exceeding $10,000 for each day of violation. Establishes contingent zoning and public notice requirements if a court invalidates the detention facility ban.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Private entities seeking to construct or operate detention facilities, local governments, and individuals held in civil or criminal custody
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government operations or finances. Indeterminate potential increase in State general fund revenues if civil penalties up to $10,000 per day are assessed against violating entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions in court to enforce the prohibition on private detention facilities and seek injunctive relief and civil penalties. Additionally, the Office of the Attorney General is tasked with notifying the Department of Legislative Services if the primary provisions are declared unenforceable in court.

The bill provides for civil actions, injunctive relief, and daily civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation to be adjudicated in State courts, which could result in a minimal operational and caseload impact for the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation directly amends the Correctional Services Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland regarding the statutory definitions, approval, and operation of detention facilities within the state.

bill_summary: Repeals the option for an eyelash extension limited license applicant to qualify solely by examination. Requires applicants instead to satisfy statutory training requirements before obtaining a license. Retains the option to serve as a registered apprentice for at least 3 months. Retains the alternative option of completing at least 100 hours of approved school instruction. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Board of Cosmetologists
stakeholders: Applicants for a limited license to provide eyelash extension services, cosmetology apprentices, and approved cosmetology schools
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Cosmetologists can implement the licensing changes with existing resources. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Cosmetologists is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill directly alters qualification and training requirements for limited licenses to provide eyelash extension services administered by the Board.

Synopsis: Authorizing a merchant to round the portion of the price of a certain  transaction for which a customer pays using cash in a certain manner or round the amount of change due to a customer in a certain manner; providing that certain provisions of the Act shall preempt existing regulations, rules, and ordinances that conflict with certain provisions of the Act; and altering the definition of "taxable price" for certain purposes to clarify the exclusion from tax of a certain amount collected due to rounding the price.

bill_summary: Authorizes merchants doing business in the State to round cash transaction prices or change due. Rounds prices ending in 1, 2, 6, or 7 cents down to the nearest five cents. Rounds prices ending in 3, 4, 8, or 9 cents up to the nearest five cents. Authorizes merchants to round cash transactions totaling under 5 cents up to 5 cents. Excludes cash transactions paid with exact change from these rounding authorizations. Excludes amounts under 5 cents added or subtracted from rounding from the sales and use tax taxable price.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Merchants doing business in Maryland and cash-paying retail customers
fiscal_impact_summary: Does not materially affect State or local operations or finances. The Maryland Department of Labor can handle implementation and compliance with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Business Regulation Article authorizing the Secretary of Labor to adopt regulations to carry out the provisions regarding cash rounding and handle any compliance guidance or related wage and business regulatory matters.

The bill amends the Tax - General Article governing the State sales and use tax administered by the Comptroller by altering the definition of 'taxable price' to exclude amounts added or subtracted due to cash transaction rounding.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Office of the State Prosecutor to investigate a threat made against a judge or judge-elect.
Title: Office of the State Prosecutor - Investigation of Threats - Judges

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Prosecutor to investigate violations of law prohibiting threats against a judge or judge-elect. Allows the State Prosecutor to investigate on their own initiative or upon specific official requests. Permits investigation requests from the Governor, Attorney General, General Assembly, State Ethics Commission, or a State's Attorney. Applies to prohibited oral and written threats to take life, kidnap, or cause physical injury. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Office of the State Prosecutor
stakeholders: Maryland judges, judges-elect, and individuals investigated for or accused of making threats against judges
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations, workloads, or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1030 directly expands the investigatory authority of the Office of the State Prosecutor by authorizing the State Prosecutor to investigate threats made against a judge or judge-elect under § 3-708 of the Criminal Law Article.
The bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly affects judicial officers by empowering the State Prosecutor to investigate criminal threats against judges and judges-elect.

Synopsis: Requiring an individual to be registered with the State Board of Physicians to perform limited X-ray machine operations in the State; establishing certain disciplinary procedures for limited X-ray machine operators; recodifying certain provisions of law related to registered cardiovascular invasive specialists and supervised medical graduates; and authorizing a physician assistant to perform X-ray duties under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: Requires individuals to register with the State Board of Physicians to perform limited X-ray machine operations. Establishes training, examination, criminal history records check, and continuing education requirements for registrants. Establishes disciplinary procedures and authorizes civil penalties up to $5,000 for unauthorized practice violations. Authorizes physician assistants to perform extremity X-ray duties under direct supervision as an approved advanced duty. Recodifies statutory provisions governing delegated duties for registered cardiovascular invasive specialists and supervised medical graduates.
responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Limited X-ray machine operators, physician assistants, delegating physicians, physician offices, and hospitals with cardiac catheterization laboratories
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Board of Physicians are not expected to materially change, as the board can absorb registration processing using existing resources and fee/penalty impacts are minimal. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians is a licensing and regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the Board by requiring it to establish and administer a registration and renewal program for limited X-ray machine operators, adopt regulations, set fees, and enforce disciplinary procedures.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and prosecutorial support to the Board of Physicians. The bill explicitly tasks the OAG with filing certified docket entries and certifications of convictions involving moral turpitude to initiate mandatory suspensions and revocations of registrations.

Synopsis: Authorizing a majority of the board of a surviving credit union to approve a proposed merger without the affirmative vote of a majority of the members of the surviving credit union, subject to certain requirements.

bill_summary: Authorizes the board of a surviving credit union to approve a proposed merger without a vote of its members. Requires the board of each merging credit union to set a date for a member vote. Permits the board of a surviving credit union to hold a member vote optionally. Requires a merger plan to state the field of membership type of the surviving credit union. Mandates approval by a majority of voting members of each merging credit union, unless waived by the Commissioner. Modifies certificate of merger filing requirements when member approval is not required and not obtained.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: credit unions, credit union boards of directors, and credit union members
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, which regulates state-chartered credit unions and oversees the approval of credit union mergers and consolidations governed by the Financial Institutions Article.

Synopsis: Altering the composition of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf from 19 members to 13 members and requiring that at least 7 members be deaf.

bill_summary: Decreases the membership of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf from 19 to 13 members. Increases the minimum number of board members who must be deaf from 6 to 7. Terminates the terms of the first six board members whose terms expire after July 1, 2026. Requires the Governor to prioritize appointing members who are deaf upon the termination of an appointed member.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf; Governor
stakeholders: members of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf and deaf individuals in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal decrease in State expenditures for the Maryland School for the Deaf due to lower meal costs for quarterly board meetings. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the governance and composition of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf, reducing membership from 19 to 13 and increasing the required minimum representation of deaf members to 7.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Board of Trustees with the advice and consent of the Senate and is directed under the bill to prioritize the appointment of deaf members as seats expire.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for state boards and commissions, which includes the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office coordinates policies promoting the welfare of deaf residents in Maryland and often collaborates or provides expertise on representation and appointments affecting the deaf community.

bill_summary: Authorizes a circuit court to approve specific transactions for a minor or disabled person without appointing a guardian. Applies when a legal basis exists for the court to assume jurisdiction over the person's property. Permits court orders that grant access to financial records. Permits court orders that establish eligibility for government assistance programs. Requires the court to consider creditors, dependents, and continuing protection needs before approving an arrangement. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Circuit Courts of Maryland
stakeholders: Minors and disabled persons requiring property management, their families, caregivers, and creditors
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Estates and Trusts Article to expand the statutory authority of circuit courts to authorize or direct specific transactions—such as accessing financial records and establishing eligibility for government assistance programs—for minors or disabled persons without appointing a guardian.

Synopsis: Providing that the Department of Natural Resources may authorize the reduction of the deer population on certain property with deer damage using certain methods; altering the time restrictions for Sunday deer hunting in certain counties during deer firearms season; repealing certain time restrictions that apply to the hunting of game birds and mammals on certain Sundays on private property in Wicomico County; authorizing the Department to allow a person to hunt deer on each Sunday of the deer bow hunting season in Baltimore City; etc.
