bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to reduce deer populations on contiguous properties of at least 10 acres with documented damage. Permits property owners or their agents to shoot deer on Sundays under department-issued permits. Expands Sunday hunting hours in Kent, Talbot, and Wicomico counties. Authorizes the Department to allow Sunday deer bow hunting in Baltimore City. Replaces county-specific Sunday hunting statutes with statewide department regulations from July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2030. Requires the Department to report on deer management and outdoor recreation safety by December 1, 2029.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: hunters, private landowners, agricultural producers, outdoor recreationists, and businesses affected by deer damage or hunting activity
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances, as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1063 directly impacts the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) as the primary regulatory and implementing agency. The bill authorizes DNR to permit deer population reduction on properties with documented damage, requires DNR to map applicable areas and make maps publicly available, modifies county-specific Sunday hunting allowances, requires DNR to adopt comprehensive Sunday hunting regulations starting July 1, 2027, and mandates multiple annual reporting requirements to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations that consider certain best management practices for stormwater management for agritourism; requiring Montgomery County and the Montgomery Soil Conservation District, in consultation with the Department, to review certain processes for reviewing and approving certain stormwater management plans and submit their findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2026; etc.
Title: Environment - Stormwater Management for Agritourism

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: Requires the Department of the Environment, in consultation with the Department of Agriculture, to define agritourism in stormwater regulations. Requires these regulations to consider best management practices for stormwater management for agritourism. Specifies practices include creating standard plans for temporary parking areas and using pasture, meadows, and cropland for runoff treatment. Requires Montgomery County and the Montgomery Soil Conservation District jointly to review local agritourism stormwater plan approval processes. Requires Montgomery County and the district to report findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Montgomery County; Montgomery Soil Conservation District
stakeholders: agricultural landowners and farm operators conducting agritourism activities, county stormwater management authorities, and Montgomery County farmers
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government operations can absorb the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency tasked with adopting stormwater management regulations, defining agritourism in consultation with MDA, considering agritourism best management practices, and consulting with Montgomery County on its review.

MDE is statutorily required to consult with the Department of Agriculture to define 'agritourism' under the stormwater management regulations, directly tying into MDA's agricultural oversight and soil conservation missions.

The Governor's Office receives the required report detailing findings and recommendations on agritourism stormwater management plan review processes from Montgomery County and the Montgomery Soil Conservation District.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility under the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include students attending the University of Maryland Eastern Shore and enrolled in certain degree programs.
Title: Higher Education - Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program - Eligible Institutions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility under the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include certain students at the University of Maryland Eastern Shore. Covers students enrolled in physician assistant studies, pharmacy, physical therapy, or veterinary medicine doctoral and master's degree programs. Requires scholarship recipients to be Maryland residents who demonstrate financial need. Sets scholarship awards between $1,000 and $5,000 per school year for up to eight semesters. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Maryland resident graduate students at the University of Maryland Eastern Shore in eligible degree programs, and participating institutions of higher education
fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State expenditures or revenues, as program funding is determined by the annual State budget ($1.2 million in the proposed fiscal 2027 budget). Reallocating existing funds to include the University of Maryland Eastern Shore will reduce funding allocations to currently participating institutions. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can administer the changes with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission administers the Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program, adopts regulations for its implementation, and calculates and allocates program grant funds to eligible institutions based on enrollment.
The Commission is directly tasked with administering the scholarship program, issuing regulations, establishing guidelines, and reallocating grant funding across participating institutions.

The bill directly impacts the University of Maryland Eastern Shore, a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, by making several of its graduate and professional degree programs eligible to receive scholarship fund allocations.

Synopsis: Requiring each public senior higher education institution and community college to submit a report on contraception access to the Maryland Higher Education Commission each year; requiring the Commission to submit a report on contraception access to the General Assembly each year beginning October 1, 2026; and requiring each community college to provide students with access to all methods of over-the-counter contraception.
Title: Higher Education Institutions - Over-the-Counter Contraception - Access and Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.

bill_summary: Requires each public senior higher education institution and community college to submit an annual campus contraception access report. Mandates reporting to the Maryland Higher Education Commission on access methods, quantities provided, and student consultations. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to submit an annual summary report to the General Assembly. Requires each community college to provide students with access to all methods of over-the-counter contraception. Consolidates existing community college contraception reporting requirements into the new annual submission.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students attending Maryland public senior higher education institutions and community colleges, public senior higher education institutions, and community colleges
fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City Community College and local community college expenditures and revenues likely increase at least minimally to make all methods of over-the-counter contraception available on campus. The Maryland Higher Education Commission and most public senior higher education institutions can implement the reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory body tasked with implementing the reporting requirements under the bill, including providing reporting forms to public senior higher education institutions and community colleges and submitting an annual consolidated report to the General Assembly.

MHEC is directly responsible for developing the form for institutions and community colleges to report on over-the-counter contraception access, receiving the submissions, and compiling an annual report to the General Assembly.
Constituent institutions of USM are public senior higher education institutions directly subject to the bill's annual reporting requirements regarding campus over-the-counter contraception access.

Morgan State University is explicitly designated as a public senior higher education institution required to track and submit an annual report to MHEC on campus over-the-counter contraception provision and student consultation.
St. Mary's College of Maryland is specifically enumerated as a public senior higher education institution required to annually report over-the-counter contraception access data to MHEC.

The Maryland Department of Health is authorized under the bill to provide technical assistance to community colleges in developing contraception access plans and collaborating with vending machine contraception providers.

bill_summary: Establishes the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board within the Maryland Transit Administration. Repeals the existing Baltimore Regional Transit Commission. Requires the Maryland Transportation Commission to determine qualifications, appointments, compensation, and leave for up to 12 agency management positions. Directs the Department of Transportation to contract for a study on creating a statewide rail authority by December 1, 2026. Mandates that the Maryland Transit Administration reallocate staff and establish five specific administrative positions for the new boards.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration; Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Transportation Commission
stakeholders: Transit riders in the Baltimore metropolitan area, MARC and commuter bus passengers, Maryland Transit Administration management employees, and transit labor unions
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by a net of $319,456 in FY 2027, accounting for five board staff positions and a $100,000 technical study, offset by $375,000 in savings from repealing the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission. Future net expenditure increases range from $210,500 in FY 2028 to $310,100 in FY 2031, with potential further annual increases up to several hundred thousand dollars depending on management compensation determinations. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reforms the Maryland Transit Administration by establishing the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board within the agency, repealing the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission, mandating staff allocations, and restructuring management personnel qualifications and compensation.

MTA is a modal administration within MDOT. The bill requires MDOT to jointly provide staff for the new oversight boards, coordinates budget timelines with MDOT's process, includes the Secretary on the boards, and requires MDOT to contract with the Baltimore Metropolitan Council to conduct a technical study on creating a rail authority.

The bill requires the Maryland Transportation Commission to notify the Secretary of Budget and Management of proposed salary adjustments for up to 12 MTA management personnel positions, requiring DBM to review and determine within 10 days whether the adjustments pose an adverse impact on special fund expenditures.
The bill grants the Governor statutory authority to appoint members and designate chairs for both the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission and establishes two new advisory and governing boards within MTA (the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board), while assigning new compensation and appointment duties to the Maryland Transportation Commission.
The office will be tasked with recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for multiple seats and chairs across the newly established transit oversight boards.

Synopsis: Requiring, by January 1, 2028, each health care facility that performs surgical procedures to adopt and implement policies that require the use of a smoke evacuation system during a surgical procedure that may generate surgical smoke.

bill_summary: Requires health care facilities that perform surgical procedures to adopt and implement smoke evacuation policies by January 1, 2028. Mandates the use of a smoke evacuation system during any surgical procedure that may generate surgical smoke. Applies to hospitals, limited service hospitals, related institutions, ambulatory surgical facilities, and freestanding medical facilities. Defines surgical smoke as gaseous by-products produced by energy-generating devices. Defines smoke evacuation systems as equipment that captures and filters surgical smoke at its site of origin.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of Health Care Quality
stakeholders: Hospitals, limited service hospitals, related institutions, ambulatory surgical facilities, freestanding medical facilities, surgical staff, and surgical patients
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected, as the Office of Health Care Quality can monitor and ensure compliance within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations have no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds requirements under the Health - General Article requiring licensed health care facilities to adopt smoke evacuation policies. The Maryland Department of Health, through its Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), inspects and regulates these facilities and will be responsible for monitoring and ensuring compliance with the new mandate.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain insurers and dental plan organizations from prohibiting an assignment of benefits to a provider who is a dentist by an insured or refusing to directly reimburse a nonpreferred provider who is a dentist; requiring a nonpreferred provider who is a dentist and who seeks an assignment of benefits from an insured or enrollee to provide certain information to the insured or enrollee before performing a health care service and submit a disclosure form to document the assignment of benefits; etc.
Title: Health Insurance and Dental Plan Organizations - Dentists - Assignment of Benefits and Reimbursement of Nonpreferred Providers

bill_summary: Prohibits certain insurers and dental plan organizations from barring an assignment of benefits to a dentist. Prohibits these entities from refusing to directly reimburse a nonpreferred provider dentist under an assignment of benefits. Requires nonpreferred dentists seeking an assignment of benefits to provide cost and billing disclosures to patients before treatment. Requires nonpreferred dentists to document assignments using disclosure forms developed by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner. Authorizes insurers and dental plan organizations to deny direct reimbursement under specified circumstances, such as prior payment.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Licensed dentists, dental plan organizations, health insurers, insureds, and dental plan enrollees in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. MIA can handle any resulting operational workload with existing budgeted resources. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding assignment of benefits and reimbursement by health insurers and dental plan organizations. It directly impacts the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA), as the Insurance Commissioner is mandated to develop disclosure forms, review form and rate filings, and regulate compliance, resulting in a minimal increase in special fund revenues.

Synopsis: Altering the process through which health care providers apply to participate on a carrier's provider panel, including certain notice requirements; repealing the authorization for a carrier to charge a certain application fee; requiring carriers to use certain information to update the carriers' provider directory at a certain frequency; altering the credentialing applications that the Commissioner may designate for a certain credentialing system and the circumstances under which the designation may be made; etc.

bill_summary: Shortens carrier deadlines to process health care provider applications and send acceptance or rejection notices. Repeals authorization for carriers to charge an application fee for provider panel credentialing. Requires carriers to establish dedicated telephone and email contacts for credentialing inquiries. Requires carriers to use the online credentialing system as the primary source for updating provider directories. Mandates reimbursement of group practices at participating rates for nonparticipating providers with tort claims immunity. Alters designation standards for uniform credentialing systems and establishes annual reporting requirements for the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health care providers, group medical practices, and insured health plan enrollees
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Maryland Insurance Administration can be handled with existing budgeted resources, with no impact on State revenues or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA), headed by the Insurance Commissioner, is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing health insurance carriers, enforcing carrier compliance with provider panel and credentialing requirements, adopting required regulations for online credentialing systems, and submitting annual reports to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Establishing that insureds and any other persons covered by certain health insurance policies, contracts, or certificates are entitled to reimbursement for the services rendered by a graduate-level counseling, social work, or psychology clinical intern under certain circumstances; providing the services are reimbursable if provided at an outpatient health care facility by a graduate level counseling clinical, social work clinical, or psychology clinical intern under the direct supervision of a licensed practitioner; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Graduate-Level Clinical Interns - Required Reimbursement

Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Requires certain health insurance policies to reimburse for services rendered by graduate-level clinical interns under specified circumstances. Covers graduate-level counseling, social work, and psychology clinical interns enrolled in graduate programs. Mandates that covered services be provided at outpatient health care facilities under direct clinical supervision. Specifies that supervising clinicians must bill for the services provided by the interns. Applies to health benefit policies and contracts issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Insured individuals receiving mental health services, graduate-level counseling, social work, and psychology clinical interns, supervising licensed mental health professionals, outpatient behavioral health clinics, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 only from $125 rate and form filing fees. Expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing health insurers in Maryland. The bill amends the Insurance Article to mandate reimbursement for services rendered by graduate-level clinical interns, requiring MIA to review and approve updated policy forms and rate filings from health insurance carriers.

MDH oversees health professional licensing boards (including the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, whose supervisor regulations are specifically cross-referenced in the bill) and regulates outpatient health care facilities where reimbursable services will be provided.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Calvert County to grant a property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on certain real property that was formerly used solely as a tobacco barn; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Calvert County - Property Tax Credit - Tobacco Barns

Tobacco and Nicotine -see also- Cigarettes; Smk&Vap

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Calvert County to grant a property tax credit on certain former tobacco barns. Qualifying property must be located on land subject to a tobacco buyout agreement. Alternatively, qualifying property must qualify for an agricultural use assessment and support an approved agricultural activity. Authorizes the county to provide by law for the amount, duration, and administration of the credit. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: governing body of Calvert County; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: owners of real property formerly used solely as tobacco barns in Calvert County
fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County property tax revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent the tax credit is granted, but specific figures are unavailable because the county lacks an inventory of eligible properties. State finances and county expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes Calvert County to establish a property tax credit for real property formerly used solely as a tobacco barn. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is tasked with hearing disputes concerning real property valuations, exemptions, and property tax credits, making it potentially relevant in the event of administrative appeals regarding credit eligibility, though any operational or fiscal impact is minimal.

Synopsis: Requiring the collector for each county to include in the written materials sent with each property tax bill a website address or quick-response code for a county government webpage that lists each property tax credit that is available to taxpayers in the county and includes an explanation of how to apply for the tax credits.
Title: Property Tax Credits - Notice Through Property Tax Bill

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the tax collector for each county to include specific digital resources with property tax bills. Mandates inclusion of a website address or quick-response code in written materials sent with each bill. Directs the link or code to connect to a county government webpage. Requires the webpage to list each property tax credit available to taxpayers in the county. Mandates that the webpage provide a brief explanation of how to apply for the tax credits.
responsible_party: County Tax Collectors
stakeholders: property taxpayers in Maryland; county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. County expenditures are not expected to be significantly impacted by the requirement to include a webpage address or QR code, and county revenues are not directly affected.

Synopsis: Specifying that certain documentation may establish lawful authority to sell certain telecommunications equipment as junk or scrap metal; requiring certain junk dealers, scrap metal processors, and antique dealers to register and provide a description including certain information of purchased telecommunications equipment with a certain law enforcement official; prohibiting certain individuals from destroying telecommunications infrastructure in a certain manner; and providing certain penalties for violations of the Act.
Title: Telecommunications Infrastructure - Protections

bill_summary: Prohibits a person from recklessly or willfully and maliciously defacing, damaging, or destroying telecommunications infrastructure. Establishes a misdemeanor penalty of imprisonment up to 6 months, a fine up to $500, or both. Exempts telecommunications company employees, authorized agents, and political subdivisions exercising supervision and control. Expands the definition of junk or scrap metal to include specified telecommunications equipment and infrastructure. Prohibits junk dealers and scrap metal processors from purchasing telecommunications equipment without documentary proof of lawful selling authority.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Judiciary
stakeholders: junk dealers; scrap metal processors; telecommunications companies; individuals selling telecommunications scrap metal
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. Minimal small business effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense for defacing, damaging, or destroying telecommunications infrastructure, which directly affects the judicial branch through the adjudication and processing of new criminal charges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense carrying penalties of up to six months of imprisonment, the Office of the Public Defender would be responsible for providing legal defense to eligible indigent defendants charged under the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees pretrial detention facilities in Baltimore City and community supervision through the Division of Parole and Probation, which may be impacted by individuals sentenced or detained under the newly created misdemeanor.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating crimes involving property destruction, infrastructure damage, and monitoring compliance with scrap metal and stolen property laws.

The Public Service Commission regulates public utilities and telecommunications providers in Maryland, whose critical network equipment and infrastructure are protected under the provisions of the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing a temporary to-go event permit in Worcester County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to issue a temporary to-go event permit to a holder of a Class B liquor license or a Class D license under certain circumstances; establishing a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license in the county; authorizing the Board to issue a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license to certain municipalities in the county; etc.
Title: Worcester County - Alcoholic Beverages - Temporary To-Go Event Permit and Class C Per Diem Municipal To-Go Beer, Wine, and Liquor License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Establishes a temporary to-go event permit and a Class C per diem municipal to-go license in Worcester County. Authorizes the Board to issue the license to the Town of Berlin, Pocomoke City, or the Town of Snow Hill. Restricts permit eligibility to Class B and Class D establishments located within or immediately adjacent to designated event areas. Authorizes permit holders to sell alcoholic beverages in approved to-go cups carried into the event area. Sets daily fees of $45 for the municipal license and $20 for the temporary event permit. Requires the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to adopt implementing regulations.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County
stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages licensees in Worcester County, the Town of Berlin, Pocomoke City, and the Town of Snow Hill
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in Worcester County revenues beginning in fiscal 2027 from the $45 per day Class C municipal license fee and $20 per day temporary permit fee; local monitoring can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland and oversees alcoholic beverage taxation. While the bill's provisions are administered locally by the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates directly to the regulation and retail sale of alcoholic beverages.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain local detention center officers of Allegany County in the event Allegany County becomes a participating governmental unit in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System; and providing that certain local detention center officers who join the Correctional Officers' Retirement System and receive certain service credit shall no longer be members of the Employees' Pension System.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Allegany County
bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for Allegany County local detention center officers if the county participates. Grants eligibility service and creditable service in the retirement system for past employment with the county. Terminates membership and benefit rights in the Employees' Pension System upon joining the retirement system. Exempts transferring officers from standard statutory requirements to pay contribution rate differences for prior service. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Allegany County
stakeholders: Allegany County local detention center officers and Allegany County government
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. If Allegany County elects to participate in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System, local pension liabilities increase by approximately $2.4 million, and net annual local employer pension contributions increase by $164,546 beginning in FY 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). SRA is responsible for administering the transfer of membership, creditable service, and pension assets and liabilities for the Allegany County detention center officers.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to organize the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps; requiring the Department to notify each health officer for a county of a certain procurement to offer the opportunity for the county health department to join the procurement; requiring the Department of Legislative Services to develop a process to assess the health equity impacts of relevant legislation; requiring the Department to convene a workgroup to review local health department recruiting and classification processes; etc.

bill_summary: Reorganizes Maryland's public health governance and extends the Commission on Public Health through June 30, 2028. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to organize the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps for statewide emergency volunteer coordination. Establishes the Public Health Workforce Development Fund administered by the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission. Authorizes county health officers to enter into certain health care service agreements if the Secretary does not respond within seven days. Requires the Department of Legislative Services to develop a process to assess health equity impacts of relevant legislation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Commission on Public Health; Maryland Community Health Resources Commission; Department of Legislative Services; Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: county health officers; local health departments; public health workforce; clinical and nonclinical emergency volunteers; Maryland hospital boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the Public Health Workforce Development Fund, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures. State expenditures increase minimally in fiscal 2027 and 2028 to maintain staffing for the extended Commission on Public Health. Local health department revenues may increase to the extent they receive workforce development funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for significant portions of the bill. It is required to organize the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps, maintain its volunteer tracking system, designate a surge coordinator, consult with local health departments on EHR procurements, submit quarterly updates to the Commission on Public Health, co-manage transfers to the new Public Health Workforce Development Fund, and convene a workgroup on local health department recruiting and classification.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the governance, membership, staffing, reporting duties, and sunset date of the Commission on Public Health; establishes a joint workgroup on local health department recruitment; and alters the composition of the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Health Services Cost Review Commission, in conjunction with MDH, to transfer money from the Population Health Improvement Fund to the newly established Public Health Workforce Development Fund under the AHEAD Model State Agreement.

The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) is added as a member of the Commission on Public Health, and DBM must participate in a newly mandated workgroup convened by MDH to examine local health department recruiting and classification efficiencies.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission on Public Health to advise on public health IT and data systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI oversees the Maryland Corps Program, and the bill alters the statutory membership of the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board by adding a county health officer appointed by the Governor.
The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the moneys of the newly created Public Health Workforce Development Fund, with interest earnings credited back to the fund.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established Public Health Workforce Development Fund.

The bill modifies the Governor's appointment authority for public members of the Commission on Public Health, adds a gubernatorial appointee (a local health officer) to the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board, and mandates annual report submissions to the Governor.

Synopsis: Altering requirements for providing notice to interested parties when a county or municipal corporation files a complaint for a judicial in rem foreclosure on certain vacant and abandoned property.
Title: Judicial In Rem Tax Foreclosure - Notice Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Alters notice requirements for judicial in rem tax foreclosures on certain vacant and abandoned property. Requires a county or municipal corporation to serve the foreclosure complaint on each interested party under the Maryland Rules. Repeals the mandate to send notice by first-class and certified mail within five days after filing. Applies when filing an in rem foreclosure complaint in the appropriate circuit court. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Circuit Courts; Maryland Counties and Municipal Corporations
stakeholders: Property owners, mortgagees, and other interested parties in vacant and abandoned real property subject to tax foreclosure; Maryland counties and municipal corporations
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1110 alters the notice and service procedure for judicial in rem tax foreclosure complaints filed in Maryland circuit courts, requiring service to be made in accordance with the Maryland Rules rather than specific statutory mailing requirements. As the administrative support entity for the state court system, the Administrative Office of the Courts is directly affected by changes governing circuit court filings and procedural service rules.

bill_summary: Requires health care providers who evaluate and manage pregnancy or postpartum care to screen for perinatal behavioral health conditions. Mandates health insurance carriers and Medicaid to cover perinatal behavioral health screenings at well visits. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to identify screening tools, resource networks, and provider training programs. Requires health occupations boards to grant two continuing education credits for each hour of approved training. Requires carriers to provide members standing referrals to behavioral health care providers during pregnancy and postpartum. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to study coverage impacts and report by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum patients; infants; health care providers evaluating perinatal care; hospitals; health insurance carriers; Medicaid recipients
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. The Maryland Department of Health, Medicaid, the Maryland Health Care Commission, and relevant health occupations boards can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and no likely expenditure increase for local governments purchasing fully insured plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with identifying approved screening tools for perinatal behavioral health conditions, identifying and developing provider training programs with health occupations boards, disseminating educational materials to local WIC agencies, and ensuring Medicaid coverage for required screenings.

The bill mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct a formal study and analysis on the impact of requiring coverage and prohibiting cost-sharing for perinatal behavioral health condition screenings, reporting findings to legislative committees by December 1, 2026.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating health insurance carriers subject to the coverage mandate, reviewing amended rate and form filings, and collecting filing fee revenues.

The bill text includes provisions establishing a refundable state income tax credit of $1,000 for parents of a stillborn child, which falls directly under the Comptroller's jurisdiction for tax administration, processing, and refund issuance.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and assesses whether mandated health insurance coverage requirements impact the State plan.

bill_summary: Authorizes Foreign Service members and their spouses relocating to Maryland on assignment to practice under an out-of-state professional license. Requires individuals to submit assignment notices, maintain good standing, and have actively used the license within the preceding two years. Limits authorized practice strictly to the discipline and scope permitted by the out-of-state license. Prohibits State licensing authorities from requiring a Maryland license unless an individual practices outside that authorized scope. Excludes the practice of law and professions practicing under interstate compacts from these provisions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Insurance Administration; Public Service Commission; State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission; Department of State Police; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Members of the U.S. Foreign Service and their spouses relocating to Maryland on assignment or detail, regulated occupational and professional practitioners, and Maryland employers
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $45,000 in FY 2027 ($30,000 in general funds for the Maryland State Department of Education and $15,000 in special funds for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners) for one-time software modifications. State general and special fund licensing fee revenues decrease indeterminately beginning in FY 2027. Local finances are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts numerous occupational and professional licensing boards housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (including architects, accountants, cosmetologists, electricians, engineers, real estate appraisers, and home improvement contractors), as well as financial and labor regulatory divisions.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees dozens of health occupations licensing boards (such as nursing, physicians, pharmacy, dentistry, and social work) and laboratories, all of which are required to permit practice under the bill's portability provisions.

The bill applies to licensing programs administered by the Department of Agriculture, including the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners, pesticide applicators, and fertilizer applicators. The fiscal note estimates a $15,000 software modification expense and lost licensing fee revenue.

The bill exempts qualifying Foreign Service members and spouses from certain certification requirements to teach or provide school counseling. MSDE anticipates general fund expenditures of up to $30,000 in FY 2027 to update its teacher licensure platform.

The bill alters licensing and certification provisions for programs under MDE's jurisdiction, such as waterworks and waste systems operators, well drillers, marine contractors, on-site wastewater professionals, and radiation machine inspectors.

MSP licenses security guards, private detectives, and security systems technicians, administers vehicle inspection mechanic licensing via the Automotive Safety Enforcement Division, and oversees explosives and electrical inspector certifications via the State Fire Marshal.

MVA is the licensing authority for vehicle salespersons, automotive dismantlers and recyclers, title service agents, drivers' schools, and driving instructors, which are subject to the bill's portability exemptions.
MIA is the licensing authority for insurance producers, advisers, bail bondsmen, public adjusters, and motor club service providers, all of which are impacted by the license portability mandate.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees the licensing and certification of emergency medical services (EMS) providers under Education Article § 13-516, which is amended to recognize authorization under the bill.
The PSC licenses energy salespersons and vendors, as well as master plumbers/gasfitters under its utility jurisdiction, which are subject to reciprocal authorization under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes qualified Foreign Service members and spouses holding out-of-state licenses to work as video lottery employees and sports wagering employees without separate State licensure.

The bill exempts qualified individuals authorized under the bill from certain registration and administrative supervision requirements for rehabilitation counselors and vocational evaluators registered with the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services licenses private home detention monitoring agencies, which are amended to recognize authorizations under the bill.

Clerks of the Circuit Court issue various commercial and trader licenses under Business Regulation Article Title 17 that are amended by the bill; the fiscal note notes that the Judiciary anticipates potential minimal reductions in license fee collections.
The Comptroller administers and issues licenses for transient vendors under Business Regulation Article § 17-20A-02, which is amended by the bill.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, whose professional licenses (vehicle sales, driving schools, etc.) are directly impacted by the bill.

Title: Health Occupations - Pharmacists - Vaccination Orders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes licensed pharmacists to order specified vaccines for individuals at least three years old without personally administering them. Limits eligible orders to influenza vaccines, COVID-19 vaccines, or vaccines used during a public health emergency. Requires pharmacists ordering vaccines for minors to inform adult caregivers about pediatric primary care visits. Mandates that pharmacists report all ordered vaccinations to the state ImmuNet Program. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: licensed pharmacists, adult caregivers, and vaccine recipients aged three and older
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state or local government finances. The changes are technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Pharmacy, the State Board of Physicians, and the State Board of Nursing, which regulate health occupations and establish vaccination protocols. MDH also maintains the ImmuNet statewide immunization registry where pharmacists must report ordered vaccinations.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study residential-in-commercial-zone laws. Defines these laws as legislation requiring local jurisdictions to allow multifamily residential or mixed-use developments in commercial zones. Directs the Department to assess impacts on infrastructure, local economic goals, housing production, and existing mixed-use communities. Mandates recommendations on development standards, including parking, density limits, building heights, and urban, suburban, and rural considerations. Requires the Department to report its findings to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: local governments, commercial property owners, multifamily and mixed-use housing developers, and housing advocates
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in fiscal 2027 only for contractual services to assist with the study. Local government finances and State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Housing and Community Development conduct a study of residential-in-commercial-zone (RICZ) laws, develop recommendations, and submit a final report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026, resulting in an estimated $75,000 fiscal impact for contractual services.

The Department of Housing and Community Development is required to submit its completed study findings and policy recommendations regarding residential-in-commercial-zone laws to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

The study directly evaluates statewide land use planning, commercial zoning overrides, infrastructure impacts, and local economic development, which fall within the Department of Planning's advisory and policy domain.

Synopsis: Clarifying the Consumer Price Index used to determine the cost-of-living adjustments for retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System in certain years.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System – Cost–of–Living Adjustments – Clarification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the missing October 2025 Consumer Price Index value for State Retirement and Pension System calculations. Sets the October 2025 value as the average of the September 2025 and November 2025 values. Applies this calculated value to determine cost-of-living adjustments effective July 1, 2026, and July 1, 2027. Addresses the lack of an official federal report caused by the federal government shutdown. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System and participating governmental units
fiscal_impact_summary: Likely has no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities and contribution rates, with no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1138 directly governs the calculation of cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) for retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary entity responsible for administering these retirement allowances and implementing the revised Consumer Price Index formula.

Synopsis: Altering the dates by which certain local employers are required to pay the State Retirement and Pension System a certain amount of the charges certified to the local employer; clarifying the interest rate a county government is charged for certain delinquent amounts owed to the State Retirement and Pension System; clarifying that an eligible governmental unit that satisfies certain requirements is eligible to participate in certain systems of the State Retirement and Pension System under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Administration and Clarification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Alters administrative procedures and participation requirements for participating governmental units in the State Retirement and Pension System. Sets a 7.75% annual interest rate on delinquent payments owed by county governments. Requires eligible governmental units to make pension enrollment available to all eligible employees. Deems eligible employees who fail to submit election documentation as enrolled in the applicable pension system. Shifts the third quarterly payment deadline for certified local employer charges from April 1 to April 16. Repeals immediate vesting rights for the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: county governments; local employers; participating governmental units; eligible employees of participating governmental units including law enforcement officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians, and local detention center officers; and the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Local government expenditures increase if a county government fails to make timely pension payments and incurs the 7.75% annual interest penalty on delinquent amounts. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill directly amends the administration of SRPS plans, including rules for participating governmental units (PGUs), enrollment deadlines, default election mechanisms, prior service credit determinations, and receipt of local payments.

The bill explicitly directs the State Comptroller to exercise setoff and withhold delinquent amounts plus a clarified 7.75% annual interest penalty from funds due to delinquent counties or local employers and remit those payments to the SRPS Board of Trustees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals Section 29-304(19) of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, removing the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs from the list of state officials entitled to immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

Synopsis: Establishing a Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures to study and evaluate the revenue structure of the county and municipal governments within the State; and requiring the Task Force to submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
Title: Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures. Requires the Task Force to evaluate county and municipal government revenue structures across Maryland. Directs the evaluation of current and optional revenue sources, interstate practices, and cost-of-living impacts. Requires recommendations regarding local government authority to increase revenue sources. Mandates a final report to the Governor and specified General Assembly committees by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures; Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: county and municipal governments in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal State expenditure impact, as the Department of Legislative Services can likely provide staff support within existing budgeted resources and member expense reimbursements are absorbable. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee, is explicitly designated as a member of the newly created Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures.
The Secretary of Budget and Management, or the Secretary's designee, is explicitly designated as a member of the Task Force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures, a temporary advisory body established to evaluate county and municipal revenue structures and report recommendations.
The Task Force is required to submit a final report of its findings and recommendations regarding local revenue modernization to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

Synopsis: Altering eligibility for certain services and programs offered by the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to include certain persons acting on behalf of a deceased homeowner or an heir or a legatee of a deceased homeowner; establishing a Legacy Protection Program administered by the Ombudsman to allow heirs who inherit a dwelling to become the record title holder of the dwelling, prevent tax sales of dwellings inherited by heirs, and allow heirs to remain in their homes; etc.
Title: Property Taxes - Tax Sales, Legacy Protection Program, and Tax Credits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect

Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Establishes the Legacy Protection Program in the State Department of Assessments and Taxation under the State Tax Sale Ombudsman. Requires the Ombudsman to provide grants to qualified legal services organizations and eligible heirs for probate costs. Requires the Governor to appropriate $250,000 annually and counties to collectively pay $500,000 annually to the program fund. Grants the homeowners' and homestead property tax credits to certain eligible heirs for up to three taxable years. Expands State Tax Sale Ombudsman assistance to estates, personal representatives, and heirs of deceased homeowners.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; State Tax Sale Ombudsman
stakeholders: Heirs and legatees inheriting residential dwellings, estates and personal representatives of deceased homeowners, county governments, and legal services organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2028, State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually, and Legacy Protection Fund special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $750,000 annually. County expenditures collectively increase by $500,000 annually beginning in FY 2028. Indeterminate potential decreases in State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local property tax revenues begin in FY 2027 due to expanded eligibility for the homeowners' and homestead property tax credits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to collaborate with the Registers of Wills to develop a step-by-step guide to probating an estate and becoming the record title holder of a dwelling. Furthermore, the newly created program provides direct grants to heirs to pay probate fees and inheritance taxes administered and collected by the Registers of Wills.

The bill establishes the Legacy Protection Fund and requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately, invest its moneys, and credit interest earnings to the fund pursuant to an exemption from standard interest accrual to the General Fund.

The bill specifies that the Comptroller must account for the newly created Legacy Protection Fund and process interest earnings allocations under Section 6-226 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The bill establishes a statutory mandated annual appropriation of $250,000 to the Legacy Protection Fund starting in FY 2028, impacting state budget preparation and fiscal management.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $250,000 from the interest on overdue State property tax to the Legacy Protection Fund in the annual state budget bill.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for the bill's fiscal note regarding impacts on the judicial system, as county land records maintained by the circuit court clerks determine record title holder status.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Comptroller to settle a claim of the State that is in arrears, regardless of how long the claim has been in arrears, under certain circumstances.
Title: State Finance - Claims of the State - Settlement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments

bill_summary: Authorizes the Comptroller to settle State claims in arrears against businesses that permanently ceased operations regardless of elapsed time. Eliminates the two-year waiting period previously required before settling claims against these defunct businesses. Requires the Comptroller to verify that the State cannot collect the claim through legal process before settling. Authorizes the Comptroller to abate all or part of the principal or interest due. Requires discharging the debtor and surety once the agreed settlement sum is paid into the State Treasury.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: business entities that have permanently ceased operations, their sureties, and taxpayers with unresolved State liabilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State tax revenues (general funds and special funds) increase by potentially $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 from earlier settlement of claims. General fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office increase by $74,124 in FY 2027 and by $98,500 in FY 2031 to hire one revenue administrator. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures and local income tax and highway user revenues may increase by indeterminate amounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency for HB 1149. The bill authorizes the Comptroller to settle delinquent State claims against business entities that have permanently ceased operations without waiting for the claims to be two years in arrears, and requires additional personnel expenditures to process the anticipated increase in settlements.

The Department of Transportation is fiscally impacted because a portion of corporate income tax revenues flows into the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will experience expenditure increases for local highway user revenue grants as claims are settled sooner.
Under the statute amended by the bill, agreed-upon settlement sums from resolved claims are paid directly into the State Treasury, which is managed and safeguarded by the Treasurer's Office.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of State Police to conduct a study regarding the employment and use of special police officers; and requiring the Department to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2026.
Title: Department of State Police - Special Police Officers - Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Department of State Police to study and recommend policies on employing and using special police officers. Mandates that the study examine commissioning, employment requirements, operations, training, equipment, jurisdiction, and regulatory oversight. Directs the Department to survey requirements in surrounding states and analyze public and private employer best practices. Requires consultation with special police officers, employers, law enforcement associations, prosecutors, state officials, and training academies. Directs the Department to submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Special police officers, public and private employers of special police officers (including county and municipal governments), security training academies, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Department of State Police can implement the study using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1152 directly tasks the Department of State Police (including its Licensing Division) with conducting a comprehensive study on the employment, commissioning, training, and regulatory oversight of special police officers, and submitting a final report with recommendations by December 1, 2026.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to consult with a representative of the Office of the Secretary of State in carrying out the study regarding special police officers.

The bill requires the Department of State Police to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2026, relevant to the Governor's statutory authority to appoint and deputize special police officers.

Title: Calvert County - Procurement - Long-Term Contracts for Infrastructure and Asset Management
