bill_summary: Authorizes Calvert County to enter into contracts for infrastructure or asset management programs. Requires covered infrastructure or assets to have a life cycle of not less than 15 years. Limits the initial contract term to not more than 20 years. Includes water towers, flow meters, and other water and sewer assets as eligible infrastructure. Permits contracts to include planning, design, construction, operation, maintenance, modification, revitalization, and decommissioning.
responsible_party: Calvert County Government
stakeholders: Calvert County Government and contractors providing infrastructure and asset management services in Calvert County
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Calvert County government finances, though it may generate operational efficiencies.

Synopsis: Altering a certain benefit amount for certain fire and rescue volunteers in Calvert County.
Title: Calvert County - Length of Service Award Program - Benefits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Increases death and burial benefits under the Calvert County Length of Service Award Program. Raises the maximum benefit to $14,000 for qualified volunteers who complete 25 certified service years. Increases the benefit to up to $560 per certified service year for volunteers receiving specified service benefits. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Calvert County Government
stakeholders: Volunteer fire, rescue, and emergency medical services personnel in Calvert County and their beneficiaries
fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County expenditures may increase by approximately $16,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 due to higher death and burial benefit payments. State operations and local revenues are unaffected.

Synopsis: Altering the statutory reference to the name Calvert Memorial Hospital to be CalvertHealth Medical Center, Inc., and its successors.
Title: Calvert County - CalvertHealth Medical Center
bill_summary: Alters the statutory reference to Calvert Memorial Hospital in the Public Local Laws of Calvert County. Replaces the obsolete name with CalvertHealth Medical Center, Inc., and its successors. Authorizes the Calvert County Commissioners to appropriate an amount determined by them to the medical center. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Calvert County Commissioners
stakeholders: CalvertHealth Medical Center, Inc. and Calvert County Commissioners
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. The bill is procedural in nature and does not affect Calvert County finances.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Public Service Commission to require a water company, sewage disposal company, or water and sewage disposal company to adopt a certain limited-income mechanism subject to the approval of the Commission; and requiring the Commission to study the feasibility of requiring certain companies to adopt a limited-income mechanism to benefit limited-income customers and to report its findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
Title: Water Companies, Sewage Disposal Companies, and Water and Sewage Disposal Companies - Limited-Income Mechanisms

NarrowSubjects.Name: Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Water -see also- Coastal Bays; Riv,Str,Lks; Wastewater; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to study limited-income mechanisms for eligible limited-income customers. Evaluates water companies, sewage disposal companies, and water and sewage disposal companies in the required study. Requires the Commission to report study findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026. Authorizes the Commission, effective July 1, 2027, to require these companies to adopt approved limited-income mechanisms. Permits mechanisms to take the form of programs, tariff provisions, credits, rates, or riders.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Water companies, sewage disposal companies, water and sewage disposal companies, eligible limited-income residential utility customers, and other rate-paying utility customers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State expenditures are likely not materially affected because most State agencies are not served by the affected companies, and there is no effect on State revenues. Local government expenditures could be affected if rates increase as early as fiscal 2028 to fund adopted limited-income mechanisms, but specific figures cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing regulatory agency under the bill. The bill requires the Commission to study the feasibility of requiring water and sewage disposal companies to adopt limited-income mechanisms, submit a report by December 1, 2026, and authorizes the Commission to require such companies to implement limited-income mechanisms starting July 1, 2027.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers, including water utility customers, in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding utility rate structures, consumer affordability, and limited-income assistance mechanisms.

The Department of Human Services administers the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which is referenced in the statute to certify eligible limited-income customer qualifications if required by an approved mechanism.
The Public Service Commission is required to report its findings on the feasibility of limited-income mechanisms for water and sewage disposal companies to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

Synopsis: Requiring certain apprenticeship programs utilized in certain State procurements to have at least a 25% completion rate, as determined by the Maryland Department of Labor.
Title: State Procurement - Apprenticeship Program Accountability and Completion

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires specified apprenticeship programs used in State procurement to have a completion rate of at least 25%. Applies the completion rate standard to apprenticeship programs that have graduated at least one apprenticeship cohort. Directs contractors awarded covered procurements valued at $1,000,000 or more to utilize registered apprenticeships or eligible internship programs. Requires public work and capital construction contractors choosing apprenticeship payments to fund only programs meeting the standard. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Labor to determine and verify program completion rates.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Contractors and subcontractors on State procurements and public works, registered apprenticeship program sponsors, and apprentices.
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate potential increase in State Apprenticeship Training Fund special fund revenues beginning in FY 2027 if more contractors choose fund contributions over program participation. State and local project procurement costs may increase if fewer eligible contractors bid, though payment alternatives mitigate this effect. State agencies and local governments can implement requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing and enforcing agency under the bill. It is responsible for verifying that registered apprenticeship programs meet the new 25% completion rate requirement, overseeing prevailing wage and apprenticeship compliance, and administering the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.

DGS houses the Chief Procurement Officer, who is statutorily directed to establish criteria and adopt regulations defining 'covered procurements' that require the use of registered apprenticeship or eligible internship programs.

The Secretary of Information Technology is explicitly required to be consulted by the Chief Procurement Officer in adopting regulations and defining covered procurements for state information technology contracts under Title 3.5.

The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily designated under § 17-602 to account for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund, which receives contractor payments and penalty revenues affected by the bill.
The State Treasurer's Office is statutorily designated under § 17-602 to hold the State Apprenticeship Training Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.

Synopsis: Altering the matters on which the student member of the Howard County Board of Education may vote.
Title: Howard County Board of Education - Student Member - Voting Ho. Co. 7-26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Expands the voting rights of the student member of the Howard County Board of Education. Authorizes the student member to vote on budgetary matters, school consolidation, student transportation, and student suspensions and expulsions. Permits the student member to vote on geographical attendance areas, donations, condemnation, and real property acquisition and disposition. Prohibits the student member from voting on architect employment, superintendent appointment and salary, and staff appointments. Prohibits the student member from voting on staff discipline, employee appeals, and collective bargaining. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of Education
stakeholders: the student member and students of the Howard County Public School System
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the changes are procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's public education system and the 24 local school systems. Although this legislation specifically affects the local governance and voting authority of the student member on the Howard County Board of Education with no state fiscal impact, MSDE holds broad administrative and policy oversight over local school boards in Maryland.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that a certain individual designate a certain representative as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Howard County Economic Development Authority; altering the frequency of certain Board meetings from at least once each month to at least once every other month; and amending the title of certain staff for the Authority.
Title: Howard County - Economic Development Authority - Alterations Ho. Co. 14-26
bill_summary: Alters governance provisions for the Board of Directors of the Howard County Economic Development Authority. Repeals the designation of an ex officio nonvoting member by the Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council chair. Decreases required board meeting frequency from monthly to at least once every other month. Designates the Executive Director of the Authority as Chief Executive Officer instead of Chief Administrative Officer. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Howard County Economic Development Authority
stakeholders: Board of Directors and staff of the Howard County Economic Development Authority, Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council, and Howard County government
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Howard County operations or finances.

Synopsis: Requiring, in the submission of the annual budget to the Howard County Council, the Howard County Executive to include the percentage of the county's general fund revenue, excluding one-time expenses, that is allocated to the operating budget of the Howard County Board of Education and operating costs associated with the Howard County school system; requiring that a copy of the budget be placed on the county board's public-facing website, in an easily identifiable location; etc.
Title: Howard County - Board of Education Budget - Percentage of County General Fund Revenue Ho. Co. 10-26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Howard County Executive to indicate the percentage of county general fund revenue allocated to public school operating costs. Applies this reporting requirement to the annual budget submission to the Howard County Council. Requires the approved county school budget to include the percentage of general fund revenue appropriated. Excludes one-time expenses from the general fund revenue calculation. Mandates reporting on pensions, employee and retiree benefits, debt service, school safety, and transportation costs.
responsible_party: Howard County Executive; Howard County Council; Howard County Board of Education
stakeholders: Howard County Public School System, Howard County Board of Education, and Howard County taxpayers
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Howard County can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources, and county revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1176 amends Section 5-102 of the Education Article regarding the submission and contents of local school board budgets. Under this section, copies of the approved local school board budget containing the newly required percentage allocations must be submitted to the State Superintendent of Schools, who leads the Maryland State Department of Education.

Synopsis: Requiring a municipality that is seeking to annex land that is located in a different legislative district than a legislative district in which the municipality or any part of the municipality is located to notify the members of the General Assembly for the district in which the land is located and for the district to which the land is being annexed by electronic communication and the United States Postal Service.
Title: Municipalities - Annexation - Limitations

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte

bill_summary: Requires a municipality seeking to annex certain land to notify specified members of the General Assembly. Applies when the land is located in a different legislative district than the municipality. Requires written notice after the municipality introduces an annexation resolution. Mandates notice delivery by electronic communication and United States Postal Service to affected legislators. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
responsible_party: Maryland Municipalities
stakeholders: Maryland municipalities seeking to annex land, and members of the General Assembly representing legislative districts affected by municipal annexations
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning oversees state land use policy, coordinates with local governments on comprehensive planning and growth management, and monitors municipal boundary changes and annexations.

Synopsis: Requiring instead of authorizing the Board of Architects to deny, reprimand, or suspend a license to practice architecture or a permit to operate a business through which an individual may practice architecture under certain circumstances; authorizing the Board to establish an electronic portal to allow the anonymous reporting of a suspected violation of certain provision of law relating to the practicing of architecture; requiring a code official to verify a licensee's credentials; etc.
Title: State Board of Architects - Grounds for Discipline and Anonymous Complaints

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Architects to deny, reprimand, suspend, or revoke a license under specified circumstances. Expands disciplinary grounds to include misrepresenting that an individual holds an architecture license or permit. Directs the Board to notify each county code official when a license is suspended or revoked. Requires county code officials to verify an architect's seal and license before processing building permits. Authorizes the Board to establish an electronic portal for anonymous and confidential violation reporting.
responsible_party: State Board of Architects
stakeholders: Licensed architects, applicants for architecture licensure, architecture firms, and county building code officials
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations can absorb requirements using existing resources. Discretionary special fund expenditures may increase minimally if the State Board of Architects elects to build an electronic reporting portal. State and local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing). The bill alters disciplinary standards, requires notifications to county code officials, and authorizes the board to establish an electronic reporting portal.

Synopsis: Altering provisions relating to children who are placed in an out-of-home placement by a local department of social services under a voluntary placement agreement; requiring, by October 1, 2029, the Department of Human Services and the Maryland Department of Health to jointly submit a report to certain entities concerning children who are placed in an out-of-home placement under a voluntary placement agreement; and establishing that certain child support due to the State before the effective date of the Act is uncollectable.
Title: Family Law - Children in Out-of-Home Placement - Voluntary Placement Agreements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Group Homes -see also- Foster Care; JuvFacil; SubsAbTrt
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Trauma Informed Approach -see also- Mental&Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Alters procedures for placing children in out-of-home care under voluntary placement agreements. Requires local departments of social services to schedule assessment meetings within five business days of receiving requests. Mandates written eligibility determinations within five business days following the assessment meeting. Prohibits requiring parents to relinquish legal custody or guardianship of a child to access services. Prohibits referring families entering voluntary placement agreements to child support enforcement. Declares previous child support balances owed to the State under voluntary placement agreements unenforceable and uncollectable.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Children with developmental disabilities or mental illnesses, their parents and legal guardians, local departments of social services, and behavioral health providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $94,700 in FY 2027, growing to $127,700 by FY 2031, for the Department of Human Services to hire one program manager. Special fund revenues from child support foster care offsets may decrease. Montgomery County expenditures increase by approximately $162,000 annually for personnel and technology upgrades.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary state agency responsible for child welfare and out-of-home placements. The bill establishes new assessment and determination timelines for local departments of social services regarding voluntary placement agreements (VPAs), alters child support enforcement referral policies and order modifications via the Child Support Administration, mandates staff training, requires data collection and website publishing, and requires a joint report with MDH.

MDH is required to consult with the Social Services Administration on annual training for local department staff regarding VPAs for children with developmental disabilities or mental illnesses, coordinates with local behavioral health authorities receiving direct referrals for Medicaid-eligible children seeking psychiatric residential treatment, and must co-author a joint report evaluating hospital discharge delays and VPA reform implementation.

The bill impacts juvenile and family court proceedings by restricting the court from ordering child support in certain VPA cases, mandating filings of motions to modify existing child support orders, and requiring judicial best-interest findings for children remaining in VPA placements beyond 180 days.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals regarding state and local property tax matters, including potential disputes over personal property assessment and exemption qualifications under the Tax - Property Article.

Title: Prince George's County - Tax Increment Financing - Extraordinary Development District - Alterations PG 425-26

bill_summary: Expands the definition of extraordinary development district to include the site of a qualifying immersive entertainment venue. Authorizes Prince George's County or its revenue authority to use bond proceeds to acquire, construct, or rehabilitate the venue. Authorizes the Maryland–National Capital Park and Planning Commission to pledge specified taxes as bond security upon adopting required resolutions. Establishes that exterior visual effects displayed on an immersive entertainment venue are not considered signs under county zoning ordinances. Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to grant waivers or exceptions to provisions requiring State approval for the venue.
responsible_party: Prince George's County; Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Prince George's County; Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission; private developers and operators of immersive entertainment venues
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Prince George's County revenues and expenditures increase beginning as early as fiscal 2026 from bond proceeds, tax revenues, and subsequent debt service payments. A portion of Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission property tax revenues within the district may be redirected, though specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1247 adds § 8-706 to the Transportation Article, granting the Secretary of Transportation specific statutory authority to issue waivers or exceptions to state outdoor advertising approval requirements for an immersive entertainment venue.

The State Highway Administration oversees and enforces outdoor advertising regulations along state highways under Title 8, Subtitle 7 of the Transportation Article, which the bill makes eligible for Secretary-granted waivers for qualifying venues.

The bill amends the Economic Development Article regarding tax increment financing mechanisms intended to facilitate major private tourism, arts, and entertainment infrastructure investments, and the Department was consulted as an information source.
The bill amends provisions within the Land Use Article concerning zoning classification and tax increment agreements, and the Department of Planning provided information for the fiscal analysis.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace to study and make recommendations regarding the expansion of part-time State employment opportunities for individuals who are challenged by the traditional full-time employment structure; and requiring the Department of Budget and Management, taking into consideration the Workgroup's findings and recommendations, to develop and distribute guidance to State agencies on expanding part-time employment opportunities.
Title: Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace - Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace to study and recommend expanding part-time State employment opportunities. Requires the workgroup to focus on removing employment obstacles for individuals challenged by full-time employment. Directs the Department of Budget and Management to provide staff for the workgroup. Requires the workgroup to report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by September 15, 2027. Requires the department to distribute guidance to State agencies on expanding part-time employment by December 31, 2027.
responsible_party: Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace; Maryland Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: State agencies, State personnel, and individuals challenged by traditional full-time employment structures, including caregivers, individuals with disabilities, and older adults
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected. The Department of Budget and Management can staff the workgroup and issue guidance using existing budgeted resources, and any member travel reimbursements are minimal and absorbable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary agency tasked with staffing the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace. The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves on the workgroup, and DBM is required to develop and distribute guidance to State agencies on expanding part-time employment opportunities based on the workgroup's findings.

The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is a designated member of the workgroup, and the workgroup is specifically tasked with outlining steps to encourage the expansion of part-time employment within the Department of Transportation.

The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland (or designee) serves on the workgroup, and the workgroup is specifically tasked with outlining steps to encourage the expansion of part-time employment within USM.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary study entity, the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace, charged with evaluating policies, studying economic and operational effects, and reporting recommendations to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace to examine inclusive employment opportunities.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated as a member of the workgroup to assist in studying state employment barriers and opportunities for individuals with disabilities.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.
The Comptroller of Maryland (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace.

The Governor is tasked with designating the chair of the workgroup and appointing a representative from a State employees union, with discretionary authority to appoint additional community representatives and a labor economist.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and coordinating appointments to state task forces and workgroups, including the appointments authorized under this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring that the requirements for the certification of recovery residences established by a credentialing entity prohibit a certified recovery residence from refusing services to an individual receiving medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder or requiring an individual to cease receiving or modify how the individual receives medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder as a condition to receive services from a certified recovery residence.

bill_summary: Requires certification standards established by a credentialing entity to prohibit certified recovery residences from refusing services. Applies this protection specifically to individuals receiving medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder. Prohibits certified recovery residences from requiring individuals to cease or modify treatment before receiving services. Authorizes credentialing entities to revoke certificates of compliance from noncompliant recovery residences. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration
stakeholders: individuals receiving medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorder and operators of certified recovery residences
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local revenues or expenditures because the bill codifies existing Behavioral Health Administration nondiscrimination policies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), primarily through its Behavioral Health Administration (BHA), oversees and approves the credentialing entity that establishes certification standards, inspects, and certifies recovery residences under Title 19, Subtitle 25 of the Health - General Article.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study and make recommendations on the availability and affordability of housing in Montgomery County; and requiring the Department to issue two interim reports and its final report of the findings and recommendation by February 1, 2029, to certain entities in Montgomery County and the Montgomery County Delegation to the General Assembly.
Title: Department of Housing and Community Development - Montgomery County Study MC 19-26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to study housing availability and affordability in Montgomery County. Requires the Department to make recommendations to increase housing availability and affordability in the county. Mandates that the study identify housing makeup by unit type, development prospects, and regulatory and market impacts. Requires the Department to confer with specified Montgomery County agencies regarding data collection and analysis. Requires interim reports by February 1, 2027, and February 1, 2028, and a final report by February 1, 2029.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Residents, housing developers, and local government agencies in Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 for the Department of Housing and Community Development to hire an external consultant to conduct the study. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to conduct a multi-year study on housing availability and affordability in Montgomery County, consult with local agencies, and submit annual interim and final reports. The fiscal note indicates an increase in general fund expenditures of $50,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 to hire a consultant.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain local zoning authority to designate and maintain certain property in a zoning classification that restricts the uses in a certain manner under certain circumstances; requiring the appropriate authority to maintain certain property in a certain  zoning classification that restricts the uses in a certain manner under certain circumstances; requiring, prior to any development on certain property, a certain local zoning authority to hold a hearing and make a decision in consultation with certain entities; etc.

bill_summary: Requires local zoning authorities to maintain Patuxent Research Refuge and Beltsville Agricultural Research Center lands in open space zoning classifications. Continues non-commercial, non-industrial, and non-residential zoning restrictions if the federal government sells, leases, licenses, or encumbers these properties. Prohibits converting central natural areas within either property to agriculture, active recreation, forestry, or other plant harvesting. Requires local authorities to hold a public hearing prior to any development on refuge or center property. Mandates a final determination in consultation with state environmental and natural resources departments that development will not substantially impact central natural areas.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Council; District Council for Prince George's County; Maryland Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Anne Arundel County and Prince George's County zoning authorities, federal land managers for the Patuxent Research Refuge and Beltsville Agricultural Research Center, and prospective land developers or purchasers
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that local zoning authorities and the district council must consult with the Department of Natural Resources prior to approving any development on Patuxent Research Refuge or Beltsville Agricultural Research Center lands to ensure there is no substantial impact on central natural areas.

The bill explicitly requires local zoning authorities and the district council to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment before rendering a final decision on any proposed development on Patuxent Research Refuge or Beltsville Agricultural Research Center land.

The Department of Planning serves as the state's primary agency for land use planning and policy guidance; while not given direct regulatory mandates under the bill, it monitors state and local land use and zoning legislation.

Synopsis: Establishing the Neighborhood Development and Social Connection Program within the West North Avenue Development Authority to provide technical support and grants to certain organizations to implement programs that foster social connections and activities in the West North Avenue Corridor; authorizing the West North Avenue Development Authority, in conjunction with certain entities, to use funds from the Continuing CORE Partnership Fund to assist with the expeditious removal of blighted property within Baltimore City; etc.
Title: West North Avenue Development Authority - Neighborhood Social Connection and Development Program - Establishment (WNADA Neighborhood Social Connection and Development Act)

bill_summary: Establishes the Neighborhood Social Connection and Development Program within the West North Avenue Development Authority. Authorizes the Authority to annually set aside up to $150,000 in existing funds for program grants. Requires participating organizations to collaborate with West North Avenue Corridor residents on planned events and projects. Expands the purpose of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund to include assisting the Authority with blight removal. Requires the Authority to submit annual comprehensive grant-awarding reports beginning December 1, 2027.
responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority; Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Residents, community development corporations, neighborhood associations, volunteer groups, and nonprofit organizations within the West North Avenue Corridor in Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures in total are not expected to change, though the West North Avenue Development Authority may redirect up to $150,000 annually from existing funds to award grants. State revenues, the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund, and Baltimore City operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the statutory purpose of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund, which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development, to assist the West North Avenue Development Authority in expeditiously removing blighted property in Baltimore City.

The Maryland Stadium Authority is a statutory partner named alongside the Department of Housing and Community Development, Baltimore City, and the West North Avenue Development Authority in utilizing the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund for blight removal.
The bill requires the West North Avenue Development Authority to submit an annual report to the Governor on its comprehensive grant-awarding activities under the program.

Synopsis: Adding applications promoting certain workforce housing to the types of applications that certain regulations governing the application process for the catalytic revitalization project tax credit must emphasize.
Title: Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit - Alterations

bill_summary: Requires regulations governing the catalytic revitalization project tax credit application process to emphasize applications that promote workforce housing. Defines workforce housing to include rental housing affordable to households earning between 50% and 100% of area median income. Includes homeownership housing affordable to households earning between 60% and 120% of area median income. Expands the homeownership income threshold up to 150% of area median income in designated Maryland Mortgage Program target areas. Directs the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to adopt implementing regulations in consultation with the Department of Commerce.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Developers and property owners applying for catalytic revitalization project tax credits, and households seeking workforce housing.
fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on overall State or local revenues or expenditures. The Department of Housing and Community Development can update regulations using existing budgeted resources, though the allocation of tax credit awards among projects may shift.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary agency administering the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit and is responsible for updating its program regulations to emphasize applications that promote workforce housing.
Section 6-904 of the Housing and Community Development Article requires the Secretary of DHCD to consult with the Department of Commerce when adopting regulations for the tax credit program.
As the State's tax collection and enforcement authority, the Comptroller administers the claiming of the catalytic revitalization project tax credit against the State income tax.

Synopsis: Requiring the University of Maryland, College Park, with assistance from the Department of Human Services, to conduct a feasibility study for establishing and operating the Supporting Our Caregiver Infrastructure Program; and requiring the University of Maryland, College Park, to submit a final report of its findings, conclusions, and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly by July 1, 2028.
Title: Supporting Our Caregiver Infrastructure Program - Feasibility Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: Requires the University of Maryland, College Park to study establishing a universal monthly payment program for caregivers. Directs the Department of Human Services to assist by identifying potential funding sources and operating costs. Requires the university to examine economic impacts, tax revenues, and appropriate stipend amounts in consultation with the Comptroller. Directs the Department of Human Services to consult with the Maryland Department of Aging, Maryland Department of Health, and local agencies. Requires the university to submit a final report to specified General Assembly committees by July 1, 2028.
responsible_party: University of Maryland, College Park; Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Caregivers supporting qualified family members who are elderly, have Alzheimer's disease, or have developmental or functional disabilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures increase by $490,000 in FY 2027 only for the University of Maryland, College Park to conduct the study and complete the report. Revenues are unaffected. The Department of Human Services and the Office of the Comptroller can perform required tasks using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the University of Maryland, College Park (a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland) as the lead entity responsible for conducting the feasibility study, exploring caregiver stipend amounts, and submitting the final report, resulting in an estimated $490,000 fiscal impact in FY 2027.

The Department of Human Services is explicitly tasked with assisting the University of Maryland, College Park with the study by identifying funding sources, determining administrative and operating costs, and conducting interagency consultations.

The study must be conducted in consultation with the Office of the Comptroller to examine the economic impact of caregiver stipends on state and local economies, tax revenues, and public benefits participation.
The Department of Human Services is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Aging in conducting the feasibility study for the caregiver infrastructure program.
The Department of Human Services is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Health as part of the feasibility study.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations that authorize a residential service agency to provide training to a licensed nurse that provides private duty nursing services after employment; authorizing a residential service agency to employ a licensed nurse who does not meet certain requirements under certain circumstances; and requiring a residential service agency to provide training and a competency evaluation for certain nurses.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations authorizing a residential service agency to train licensed nurses after hire. Authorizes a residential service agency providing private duty nursing to employ licensed nurses who lack department-established clinical experience. Requires the agency to implement an approved training program and assign a preceptor until competency is demonstrated. Mandates clinical supervision by a qualified registered nurse and competency evaluations documented in the nurse's personnel file. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: residential service agencies providing private duty nursing services, licensed nurses, and patients receiving private duty nursing care
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $204,800 in FY 2027 ($152,300 general funds and $52,600 federal funds) for two staff positions within the Maryland Department of Health and Medicaid, offset by $52,600 in federal fund revenues. No effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with adopting regulations for on-site nurse training programs at residential service agencies (RSAs), approving training programs and competency evaluations via the Office of Health Care Quality, and conducting provider audits through Medicaid, which incurs direct fiscal and staffing impacts.

Synopsis: Authorizing a holder of a barbershop and beauty salon license in Anne Arundel County to provide to a customer during any one visit not more than 1.7 ounces of liquor for on-premises consumption in addition to beer and wine.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Barbershop and Beauty Salon License
bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners to issue barbershop and beauty salon beer, wine, and liquor licenses. Expands the existing beer and wine license to include liquor. Authorizes license holders to provide up to 1.7 ounces of liquor to a customer during one visit. Restricts service to customers receiving barbering or cosmetology services or attending a fund-raising event. Permits service during normal business hours until 9 p.m., including Sundays without a separate Sunday license.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: barbershop and beauty salon owners, permit holders, and customers in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County revenues and expenditures are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes barbershop and beauty salon alcoholic beverage licenses for holders of barbershop and beauty salon permits issued under the Business Occupations and Professions Article, which are regulated and licensed by boards within the Maryland Department of Labor.
The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers excise and sales taxes related to alcoholic beverage sales and consumption.

bill_summary: Renames the African American Heritage Preservation Program to be the Speaker Adrienne A. Jones African American Heritage Preservation Program. Repeals the authority of the Secretary of Human Services to appoint the executive director of the Maryland Commission for Women. Designates the executive director as a skilled service employee rather than a special appointee. Expands the Commission's statutory duties regarding research on disparities, legislative advocacy, and partner organization programs. Authorizes the Commission to appoint advisory committees in all fields affecting women in the State. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Commission for Women; Maryland Historical Trust; Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture
stakeholders: Women in Maryland, statewide women's organizations, local commissions for women, and the executive director of the Maryland Commission for Women
fiscal_impact_summary: Negligible impact on the Department of Human Services to reclassify the executive director position. The Maryland Commission for Women can implement requirements within existing budgeted resources, and renaming the preservation program has no state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission for Women is housed within the Department of Human Services. The bill alters the commission's statutory duties and modifies personnel provisions governing its executive director, specifying that the position is in the skilled service rather than a special appointment.

The Maryland Historical Trust, which is overseen by the Department of Planning, administers the African American Heritage Preservation Program that the bill renames to the Speaker Adrienne A. Jones African American Heritage Preservation Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory powers, duties, research mandates, and leadership appointment provisions of the Maryland Commission for Women.
The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article (§ 6-212) to update the name of the program prioritized for funding within sustainable communities.

As the central personnel and human resources agency administering the State Personnel Management System, DBM oversees job classifications and changes affecting positions transitioned into the skilled service.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to include certain additional information in an annual report submitted to the General Assembly regarding children and foster youth in the State child welfare system; and requiring the State Department of Education, in cooperation with the Department of Human Services, to develop and submit a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026, on improving outcomes for students in the State child welfare system.

bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Education to include college enrollment and six-year graduation rates in an annual child welfare report. Mandates the department include, where appropriate, comparison data for students not in the child welfare system. Directs the department and the Department of Human Services to submit an educational outcomes report by December 1, 2026. Requires the report to identify service gaps and provide recommendations to improve foster youth outcomes. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Department of Human Services
stakeholders: children and foster youth in the State child welfare system
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education and the Department of Human Services can implement the reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland State Department of Education to include new college enrollment and six-year graduation metrics for foster youth in its annual child welfare report, provide comparison data, and collaborate with the Department of Human Services to submit a comprehensive report on improving educational outcomes for students in foster care.

As the state's child welfare agency, DHS is a joint recipient of the annual reporting data under Family Law § 5-1312 and is statutorily required to cooperate with MSDE in developing and submitting the 2026 report to the General Assembly regarding services and educational outcomes for foster youth.

MLDSC is the state entity responsible for linking student records between K-12 and postsecondary education. Reporting on the number of foster youth who enroll in college and graduate within six years relies directly on longitudinal data matching systems maintained by MLDSC.

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Department of Education to establish a sliding fee copayment scale for the Child Care Scholarship Program. Exempts families with household incomes at or below the federal poverty line from paying child care copayments. Repeals the statutory process and special fund for granting presumptive eligibility under the program. Requires the department to identify, inform, and assist applicants qualifying for publicly funded prekindergarten or Head Start. Mandates at least 90 days of notice before the department implements the new copayment system.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Child Care Scholarship Program applicants and recipients, low-income families with young children, and participating child care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $749,700 in FY 2027 for one staff position and one-time IT system modifications, with ongoing expenditures between $118,200 and $134,800 annually through FY 2031. Copayment revenue and presumptive eligibility repeals may offset costs to serve more families without increasing net program spending. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) directly administers the Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program. The bill authorizes MSDE to implement a sliding fee scale and partial scholarships, alters copayment requirements, repeals presumptive eligibility provisions, requires MSDE to coordinate Pre-K and Head Start options for applicants during enrollment freezes, and imposes reporting requirements, resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of $749,700 in FY 2027.

Permits disclosure to administrators of government-operated child care centers or centers in State-occupied buildings. Allows disclosure to coaches, team administrators, or managers of youth sports programs for minors. responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: applicants and volunteers for youth-serving positions, youth sports programs, government child care centers, organizations caring for or supervising children, and individuals with indicated findings of child abuse or neglect
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Department of Legislative Services projects the Department of Human Services can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary implementing agency responsible for maintaining child abuse and neglect records and the centralized confidential database. The bill directly expands DHS's authority to disclose reports and records of indicated child abuse or neglect to certain child care administrators, youth sports organizations, and child supervision entities for employment and volunteer suitability determinations.

MSDE regulates and oversees child care centers and programs referenced in the bill under Title 9.5 of the Education Article, and the agency was consulted in the preparation of the fiscal note regarding personnel screening and child care facility administration.

Synopsis: Altering, beginning in taxable year 2027, the homeowners' property tax credit application cycle to be year-round for each taxable year; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2027.
Title: Homeowners’ Property Tax Credit – Year–Round Application
bill_summary: Alters the homeowners' property tax credit application cycle to operate year-round for each taxable year. Extends the standard application filing deadline from October 1 to February 14 of the taxable year. Repeals the provision authorizing late applications for good cause through October 31. Establishes property tax payment due dates for credits granted on applications received after October 1 but on or before February 14. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2027.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Homeowners eligible for the property tax credit and local governments providing local supplemental credits
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $168,200 annually beginning in fiscal 2028 due to additional credits granted. Local revenues decrease in counties and municipalities that provide local supplemental property tax credits to the extent that more homeowners become eligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board adjudicates appeals of property tax determinations made by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), including disputes regarding property tax credits and exemptions. Altering the application cycle and deadlines for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit may impact the volume or timing of taxpayer eligibility appeals.

As the State's principal fiscal agency responsible for budget development and supervision, DBM is impacted by the projected ongoing increase of approximately $168,200 in annual General Fund expenditures starting in FY 2028 to fund additional homeowners' property tax credits.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative review body for tax disputes, hearing appeals from final decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board regarding property tax assessments and credits.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Information Technology to procure the services of a third-party entity to conduct a certain independent study related to the staffing, capability assessment, and workforce alignment of information technology and cybersecurity professionals in the State; and requiring the Department of Information Technology to submit the study to the Governor and the General Assembly by November 1, 2027.
Title: Department of Information Technology - Information Technology Staffing and Capability Assessment - Independent Study
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 871

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to procure a third-party entity to conduct an independent staffing study. Mandates an assessment of information technology and cybersecurity staffing needs across Executive Branch principal departments. Directs the study to analyze capability gaps, evaluate department technology environments, and recommend updated staffing models. Requires recommendations for updated job classifications and pay scales informed by State and local government compensation data. Requires the department to submit the completed study to the Governor and General Assembly by November 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: Information technology and cybersecurity professionals in Maryland State government and principal departments of the Executive Branch
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $250,000 in each of fiscal 2027 and 2028, totaling $500,000 across the two-year period, to procure the study. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency responsible for procuring the third-party study, assessing IT and cybersecurity staffing needs, managing the $500,000 fiscal expenditure, and reporting findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee compensation, salary structures, and job classifications, which the mandated study directly evaluates for IT and cybersecurity positions.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments subject to the IT staffing assessment and is a designated recipient of the final study and recommendations.

Synopsis: Establishing that, under the Maryland Trust Act, a certain in terrorem clause contained in a trust is void under certain circumstances.
Title: Maryland Trust Act - In Terrorem Clause - Void

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Voids any trust provision purporting to penalize an interested person for contesting the trust if probable cause exists. Invalidates trust provisions that penalize an interested person for instituting other proceedings relating to the estate. Aligns trust penalty enforceability with existing Maryland law governing no-contest clauses in wills. Applies prospectively only to causes of action arising on or after July 1, 2026. Prohibits retroactive application to any cause of action arising before the effective date.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: settlors, trustees, and beneficiaries or interested persons involved in Maryland trusts
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill voids in terrorem clauses in trusts if probable cause exists for instituting proceedings, directly impacting trust litigation, estate disputes, and judicial proceedings heard within the Maryland court system.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administration and serves as clerk to the Orphans' Court, which frequently interacts with estate and testamentary trust proceedings affected by in terrorem provisions.

Synopsis: Establishing an expedited processing fee for certain documents filed with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation; and requiring the Department to process documents filed at least 1 hour before the Department's close of business within 1 hour after the documents are received.
Title: State Department of Assessments and Taxation - Expedited Document Processing and Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Establishes a 1-hour expedited processing tier and a $1,000 fee for specified documents filed with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Requires the Department to process eligible documents within 1 hour after receipt. Applies this timeframe to documents filed at least 1 hour before the Department's close of business. Requires filed documents to first receive preclearance acceptance from the Department. Takes effect January 1, 2028.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Business entities and law firms filing corporate and organizational documents with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation on an expedited basis
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues likely increase beginning in fiscal 2028 from expedited filing and preclearance fees, but the exact increase is indeterminate. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill with existing resources. No local government fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Altering the examination fee for a new commercial bank charter; requiring a certain nondepository trust company to include certain disclosures in its articles of incorporation; exempting from certain provisions of law a certain nondepository trust company authorized to provide certain services by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation; authorizing a certain nondepository trust company to request that the Commissioner reduce the capital stock requirements under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Financial Institutions - Payment Stablecoin Services - Establishment and Regulation (Maryland Stablecoin Act)

bill_summary: Establishes a regulatory framework for payment stablecoin services institutions and State issuers under the Maryland Stablecoin Act. Designates the Office of Financial Regulation as the State payment stablecoin regulator. Authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to issue operating certificates to qualifying nondepository trust companies and credit union service organizations. Prohibits certificate holders from extending credit, accepting consumer deposits, or accepting insured deposits. Lowers the examination fee for a new commercial bank charter from $15,000 to $7,000. Requires commercial banks and credit unions to notify the Commissioner before offering stablecoin-related services or seeking federal issuer authorization.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation; Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: nondepository trust companies, credit union service organizations, commercial banks, credit unions, and stablecoin users
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. The Office of Financial Regulation can implement the regulatory framework using existing budgeted resources. Revenue reductions resulting from lowering the commercial bank charter examination fee from $15,000 to $7,000 are expected to be minimal and recuperated through annual regulatory assessments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of Financial Regulation (OFR), a principal regulatory division within the Maryland Department of Labor, with serving as the State Payment Stablecoin Regulator under the federal GENIUS Act of 2025. OFR is responsible for evaluating applications, issuing certificates, establishing assessments, conducting oversight, and enforcing compliance for payment stablecoin service institutions and state issuers.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning April 1, 2028, manufacturers of menstrual hygiene products to include a list of all ingredients listed in order of predominance and displayed prominently in conspicuous type on each consumer-facing package of menstrual hygiene products sold in the State.
Title: Consumer Protection - Menstrual Hygiene Products - Labeling Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg

bill_summary: Requires manufacturers of menstrual hygiene products to list all ingredients on each consumer-facing package sold in Maryland starting April 1, 2028. Mandates that ingredients appear in order of predominance and be displayed prominently in conspicuous type. Authorizes manufacturers to list a confidential substance by its common name to protect confidentiality. Defines menstrual hygiene products as disposable or reusable products used to absorb or contain menstruation or vaginal discharge. Designates a violation as an unfair or deceptive trade practice subject to Consumer Protection Division enforcement and penalties.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Manufacturers and consumers of menstrual hygiene products sold in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties, and the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General can handle enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that a failure to comply with menstrual hygiene product ingredient labeling requirements is an unfair or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

Synopsis: Requiring certain centers where mammography testing is performed to include in the screening results letter that is sent to a patient, as required by federal law, a notice of the presence of arterial calcification as observed during the patient's mammogram.
Title: Public Health - Mammograms - Arterial Calcification Notice

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Requires centers performing mammography testing to include a notice regarding breast arterial calcification in screening results letters. Mandates specific language explaining that breast arterial calcification may indicate an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Advises patients with breast arterial calcifications to discuss cardiovascular risks and potential additional testing with their physician. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations modifying the notice if medical evidence changes. Prohibits construing the notice requirement to create a standard of care or basis for a cause of action.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Patients receiving mammography screening, mammography testing centers, and physicians
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local government finances and operations are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1364 amends the Health - General Article regarding mammography result notices and grants the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) discretionary authority to adopt regulations modifying the required notice language if medical evidence changes.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness; requiring certain health occupations boards to grant a certain number of hours for every hour of continuing education for menopause and menopause-associated symptoms; requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated conditions; requiring the Maryland Commission for Women to conduct a certain evaluation; etc.
Title: Health Occupations, Public Health, and Insurance - Menopause - Provider Training Coverage Requirements, Policy Initiatives, and Access to Care

bill_summary: Requires certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover evaluation and management of menopause. Mandates that health occupations boards grant at least two hours of continuing education credit for each hour completed on menopause. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to identify an approved menopause training program in consultation with professional associations. Alters the membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness by adding menopause expertise and women's representation. Requires the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Commission for Women to submit policy and access reports by October 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Commission for Women; Maryland Insurance Administration; State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness
stakeholders: Individuals experiencing perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal symptoms; licensed health care providers who evaluate and manage menopause; commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; health occupations licensing boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,300 in FY 2027 and $30,200 in FY 2028 for the Maryland Department of Health to retain contractual staff and vendor support for required evaluations and reports. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2027 from filing fees. Local government expenditures may increase minimally for fully insured employee health benefit plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency. MDH is tasked with identifying approved menopause training programs for health professional licensees, overseeing health occupations boards updating continuing education rules, administering the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, and conducting two comprehensive studies and reports to the General Assembly regarding community health worker outreach and clinical education.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates commercial health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans subject to the bill's new insurance coverage mandate for the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated symptoms, requiring policy form reviews and complaint handling.

The Maryland Commission for Women is administratively housed within the Department of Human Services. The bill adds the Commission's Executive Director to the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness and tasks the Commission with evaluating state policy initiatives and submitting a report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory membership and composition of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness and assigns formal evaluation and reporting duties to the Maryland Commission for Women.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must evaluate compliance and fiscal impacts associated with state-mandated health insurance coverage expansions.
MDH must consult with institutions of higher education to evaluate methods for increasing clinical and postgraduate education opportunities regarding menopausal evaluation and treatment.
MHEC oversees postsecondary education standards and contributed to the fiscal note analysis regarding MDH's consultation with higher education institutions on clinical training programs.

Synopsis: Establishing a Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care to envision and make recommendations regarding establishing a comprehensive, patient-centered  health care system in the State; and requiring the Commission to submit a preliminary report by December 1, 2027, and a final report of the Commission's findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2029.
Title: Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care in Maryland

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care to envision a comprehensive health care system for Maryland. Requires the Commission to study delivery models, provider reimbursement rates, coverage scope, and network barriers. Directs the Commission to submit preliminary reports in 2027 and 2028 and a final report by December 1, 2029. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide staff for the Commission. Conditions the Commission's implementation on securing private funding before June 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Maryland health care consumers, health care practitioners, health insurers, hospitals, and local health departments
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in special fund revenues and expenditures from fiscal 2027 through 2030 if the Maryland Health Care Commission secures sufficient private funding to support commission operations; no effect in fiscal 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHCC is the primary implementing agency tasked with providing staff support for the Commission, determining required funding levels, and securing the private funding upon which the bill is contingent.

The Secretary of Health and the Deputy Secretary of Health Care Financing (Medicaid) serve as statutory members on the Commission, which focuses on reforming the statewide health care delivery system.
The Executive Director of the Health Services Cost Review Commission serves as a designated member of the Commission to advise on hospital financing, cost containment, and system reform.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is a statutory member of the Commission, which is tasked with studying coverage, health benefit designs, and health insurance access.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is a designated member of the Commission, which will examine health insurance regulation, network adequacy, and high-deductible plans.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Commission.
The Governor jointly designates the Commission chair with legislative presiding officers, appoints several key members to the body, and receives the required preliminary and final reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a multi-year temporary advisory body (the Commission on Re-Imagining Health Care in Maryland) scheduled to operate through May 31, 2030.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting the numerous gubernatorial appointees specified in the legislation.

Synopsis: Establishing the Audit and Finance Compliance Unit in the Department of Budget and Management; requiring the Governor to implement systems and processes to monitor certain efforts; requiring the Unit to monitor efforts of Departmental Units to correct certain audit findings and provide guidance, coordination, and technical assistance; authorizing the Unit to implement steps to address and prevent audit findings; requiring the Unit to provide direct assistance to Departmental Units with four or more repeat audit findings; etc.
Title: Department of Budget and Management - Audit and Finance Compliance Unit - Establishment

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Audit and Finance Compliance Unit in the Department of Budget and Management to monitor Executive Branch audit compliance. Requires the Governor to implement systems and processes to monitor Executive departmental units correcting Office of Legislative Audits findings. Directs the unit to assist Executive departmental units with four or more repeat audit findings or unsatisfactory audits. Requires the unit to establish a specialized team to review resolution timelines, perform sample tests, and monitor progress. Mandates that the unit submit an annual report on audit findings to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by October 1. Authorizes specified legislators, executive officials, and the unit to view unredacted cybersecurity audit findings.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Office of the Governor
stakeholders: Executive Branch departmental units subject to Office of Legislative Audits reviews, state internal auditors and compliance personnel, and legislative oversight committees.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $216,971 in FY 2026 and $2,288,120 in FY 2027 to support nine new regular positions and contractual services under contingent budget appropriations. Out-year expenditures range from $2.14 million to $2.35 million annually through FY 2031. There is no effect on revenues or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1369 establishes the Audit and Finance Compliance Unit within the Department of Budget and Management (DBM). DBM is the primary implementing agency, responsible for staffing the unit, providing technical assistance to other executive units, and producing annual compliance reports, with an expenditure impact of approximately $2.29 million and nine new positions.

The entire statutory framework created by the bill centers on monitoring, remediating, and reporting on audit findings and recommendations issued by the Office of Legislative Audits (OLA), including handling unredacted cybersecurity findings.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor implement systems and processes to monitor executive departmental units' efforts to resolve audit findings, and authorizes the Governor, Chief of Staff, and Deputy Chiefs of Staff to review unredacted cybersecurity audit findings.

DoIT, through the State Chief Information Security Officer, plays a key role in tracking and remediating cybersecurity and repeat audit findings across state agencies, and manages the information technology tracking tools used to monitor audit compliance.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission, in collaboration with the Office of Health Care Quality within the Maryland Department of Health, to develop a process to receive and publish certain inspection information on the Commission's Maryland Quality Reporting website; establishing the Maryland Health Centralization Commission to provide advice and recommendations relating to the relationship between the Department and the health occupations boards; requiring each health occupations board to annually report certain information; etc.
Title: Public Health - Office of Health Care Quality Information and Maryland Health Centralization Commission
