bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Health Centralization Commission to recommend ways to increase collaboration between the Department of Health and health occupations boards. Requires the Maryland Health Care Commission and the Office of Health Care Quality to publish facility inspection dates and quality metrics online. Directs each health occupations board to annually certify compliance with State minimum cybersecurity requirements to the Secretary of Information Technology. Mandates each health occupations board to designate a liaison and provide requested information to the commission within 10 business days. Requires the commission to convene by July 1, 2026, and submit annual findings and recommendations beginning December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Centralization Commission; Maryland Health Care Commission; Office of Health Care Quality; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Information Technology; Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: State health occupations boards, licensed health care practitioners, health care facilities inspected by the Office of Health Care Quality, and Maryland health care consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources, with no impact on State revenues. The bill has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission, in collaboration with the Office of Health Care Quality, establish a process to receive inspection dates and quality metrics and publish them on its Maryland Quality Reporting website.

The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), its Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), and its affiliated health occupations boards. MDH leadership sits on the newly created Maryland Health Centralization Commission to improve departmental collaboration and oversight of the boards.
The bill requires each health occupations board to annually certify to the Secretary of Information Technology that their IT systems comply with State minimum cybersecurity requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates an advisory entity, the Maryland Health Centralization Commission, to advise the General Assembly and develop recommendations regarding health occupations boards.

The bill directly responds to recent OLA audit findings concerning regulatory services and health occupations boards, and the newly established commission is tasked with ensuring boards remedy audit findings.
The bill requires annual reports detailing findings, recommendations, and draft legislation from the Maryland Health Centralization Commission to be submitted to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and the Maryland Children's Health Program to provide a prior authorization determination regarding a transfer on request of a special pediatric hospital within 3 business days after the request is received; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations on or before December 31, 2026, establishing a retrospective review process for special pediatric hospitals.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children's Health Program, and Health Insurance - Transfers to Special Pediatric Hospitals - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs
Physicians -see also- MedExmnrs; Pediatr; Psychiatrists etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Maryland Children’s Health Program to issue prior authorization determinations for transfers to special pediatric hospitals. Mandates delivery of the determination within three business days after receiving a request from a special pediatric hospital. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations establishing a retrospective review process by December 31, 2026. Requires the regulations to include peer-to-peer reconsideration of medical necessity determinations requested by a pediatric specialty hospital. Mandates retrospective reviews for denials of hospital admissions or reimbursements issued on or after January 1, 2025. Specifies that the retrospective review process must be conducted by a licensed physician.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: special pediatric hospitals and pediatric patients enrolled in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program or Maryland Children's Health Program
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to modify utilization control agent contracts and conduct retrospective reviews, funded 50% from general funds and 50% from federal fund revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP). HB 1376 directly mandates that MDH provide prior authorization determinations for transfers to special pediatric hospitals within three business days upon request and adopt regulations by December 31, 2026, establishing a retrospective review process.

Synopsis: Establishing the Redirecting Safe Prescription Drugs Pilot Program; requiring the Secretary of Health to collaborate with the federal Drug Enforcement Agency and certain drop-off sites in the State to separate and redirect certain prescription medications to a State repository program; and requiring each drop-off site participating in the Pilot Program to ensure that any prescription medications collected are packaged in a certain manner and transferred to a repository.
Title: Prescription Drug Repository Program - Redirecting Safe Prescription Drugs Pilot Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Redirecting Safe Prescription Drugs Pilot Program to expand medication access for underserved populations. Requires the Secretary of Health to collaborate with the federal Drug Enforcement Agency and four registered drop-off sites. Directs participating drop-off sites to separate eligible, unopened, noncontrolled prescription medications collected during National Prescription Drug Take Back Day. Requires participating sites to transfer eligible medications to a State repository and provide collected controlled substances to the DEA. Requires the Secretary of Health to report collection data to the State Board of Pharmacy and the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: Underserved patients needing prescription medications, participating drop-off sites, and licensed drug repositories in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Pharmacy can handle oversight and reporting responsibilities with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Secretary of Health to administer the Redirecting Safe Prescription Drugs Pilot Program, collaborate with the federal Drug Enforcement Administration and participating drop-off sites, and report findings to the Maryland State Board of Pharmacy (housed within MDH) and the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Altering the minimum commission rate from 10% to 5% of the total premium that the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund is required to pay to a fund producer of a policyholder to whom a policy is issued for private passenger auto insurance; and prohibiting the Fund from paying a commission to a fund producer for a policy written directly by the Fund without the involvement of a fund producer.
Title: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund - Fund Producer Commission Rate

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Lowers the statutory minimum commission rate paid by the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund from 10% to 5%. Applies this reduced minimum commission rate to private passenger auto insurance policies issued by the Fund. Maintains the existing maximum commission cap of 15% of the total premium. Prohibits the Fund from paying a commission on policies written directly without producer involvement. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
stakeholders: fund producers licensed to sell Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund policies, small business insurance agencies, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
fiscal_impact_summary: MAIF nonbudgeted expenditures decrease beginning in FY 2027, potentially by several hundred thousand dollars annually, to the extent MAIF lowers commission rates paid to producers. State operations, state revenues, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1387 directly governs the operations and statutory obligations of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF). It alters the minimum commission rate MAIF must pay to producers for private passenger auto insurance policies from 10% to 5% and prohibits commissions on direct-written policies, leading to a notable decrease in MAIF's nonbudgeted operating expenditures.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the state's insurance industry, licenses insurance producers, and enforces provisions under the Insurance Article, making the regulatory framework regarding producer commissions relevant to its oversight authority.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "abuse" to include female genital mutilation for the purposes of a provision of law requiring certain persons to provide notice of suspected abuse or neglect of a child or make a written report of suspected abuse or neglect of a child; altering the actions regarding female genital mutilation in which a person is prohibited from engaging; increasing the penalties for a violation of certain provisions related to female genital mutilation; etc.
Title: Public Health - Female Genital Mutilation

Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Expands the statutory definition of child abuse to include female genital mutilation for mandatory reporting provisions. Prohibits knowingly performing, attempting, conspiring, or transporting an individual under age 18 for female genital mutilation. Increases maximum criminal penalties for violations to 10 years imprisonment and a $10,000 fine. Requires health occupations licensing boards to revoke the license of an individual convicted of violations. Authorizes victims of female genital mutilation to file civil actions for actual, compensatory, and punitive damages. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to publish annual reports and distribute culturally appropriate educational materials.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; health occupations licensing boards
stakeholders: Minors at risk of female genital mutilation, victims of female genital mutilation, licensed health care practitioners, mandatory child abuse reporters, and parents or legal guardians of minors
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $39,500 in FY 2027, $40,900 in FY 2028, and $17,900 in FY 2029 for a part-time contractual health policy analyst at the Maryland Department of Health to establish data collection, publish educational materials, and prepare annual reports. The position terminates on December 1, 2028. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill's provisions, including collaborating to develop, publish, and distribute educational materials, coordinating with health occupations boards to enforce mandatory license revocations, submitting an annual report to the General Assembly, and incurring direct fiscal expenditures for personnel.

The bill alters the definition of child abuse to include female genital mutilation under Family Law provisions, directly impacting local departments of social services that receive and investigate mandatory abuse reports. In addition, the Social Services Administration within DHS is explicitly required to consult with MDH on the annual report.

The bill creates a specific civil cause of action for victims in the circuit courts with an extended statute of limitations, and also alters felony criminal provisions, impacting court caseloads and judicial administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill increases the maximum criminal penalty for female genital mutilation from 5 to 10 years of imprisonment, potentially increasing the length of stay for individuals committed to State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings and will be responsible for defending individuals charged under the expanded criminal prohibitions and increased felony penalties.

MSP is a primary law enforcement agency responsible for investigating felony violations, receiving mandatory reports of child abuse involving female genital mutilation, and consulting on data collection for MDH's annual report.

The bill explicitly mandates that educational materials on female genital mutilation be distributed to schools, and educators are designated mandatory reporters of child abuse under the impacted reporting statutes.
OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and health occupations licensing boards regarding license revocations, regulatory actions, and defense of state actions.

Synopsis: Requiring, to make a claim under a warranty for certain agricultural equipment, a consumer to provide written notice to certain parties to report a nonconformity, defect, or condition occurring in certain agricultural equipment; requiring certain parties to correct the nonconformity, defect, or condition in a certain manner; and requiring certain parties to provide a consumer with the opportunity to replace agricultural equipment or receive a refund under certain circumstances.
Title: Consumer Protection - Agricultural Equipment Warranties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Establishes warranty protections and repair procedures for consumers purchasing or holding warranties on new agricultural equipment. Requires consumers to report nonconformities by written notice via certified mail during the warranty period. Mandates manufacturers, factory branches, or authorized dealers to repair reported nonconformities free of charge within 30 days. Requires manufacturers to provide replacement equipment or a full refund if repairs fail after a reasonable number of attempts. Authorizes civil actions and bad-faith damages up to $5,000 against noncompliant manufacturers or distributors. Designates violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Purchasers, owners, and operators of agricultural equipment, as well as manufacturers, factory branches, distributors, and authorized dealers of agricultural equipment
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General can handle enforcement and complaint investigations using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of the Agricultural Equipment Warranty Enforcement Act as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.
The bill creates a private civil right of action allowing consumers to sue equipment manufacturers or authorized dealers in Maryland courts, with provisions for bad-faith damages up to $5,000.

The bill establishes warranty protections and remedy procedures for purchasers of agricultural equipment used in the business of farming, directly affecting the economic viability and operations of the agricultural community that the department supports.

Synopsis: Authorizing the suspension or revocation of a shellfish aquaculture harvester permit or shellfish aquaculture harvester registration card for certain violations; prohibiting a person whose permit or registration card has been suspended or revoked in accordance with the Act from engaging or working in any aquaculture activity during the suspension or revocation; authorizing a certain leaseholder and the Department of Natural Resources to complete a process to remove gear or transfer a shellfish aquaculture lease; etc.
Title: Shellfish Aquaculture - Penalties - Suspension or Revocation of Permit or Registration Card

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to suspend or revoke shellfish aquaculture harvester permits or registration cards for specified violations. Authorizes permit or registration card suspension for up to five years for a first violation and revocation for subsequent violations. Prohibits an individual whose permit or registration card is suspended or revoked from working in any aquaculture activity. Establishes a process and deadlines for certain sole leaseholders to remove gear or transfer their lease before termination. Authorizes the State to seize and forfeit gear and equipment if a leaseholder fails to complete the process.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: shellfish aquaculture harvester permit and registration card holders and shellfish aquaculture leaseholders
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in general and special fund expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 to cover Office of Administrative Hearings costs for permit or registration card suspension or revocation proceedings. Revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating shellfish aquaculture leases, issuing harvester permits and registration cards, conducting administrative proceedings, and executing lease transfers or gear forfeitures.
OAH conducts the required administrative hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act prior to the suspension or revocation of shellfish aquaculture permits or registration cards.
The bill penalizes violations of delivery timeframes established by the Maryland Department of Health's Vibrio Parahaemolyticus Control Plan (COMAR 10.15.07.06).
The circuit courts under AOC may receive and adjudicate petitions for judicial review filed by individuals aggrieved by DNR's final administrative decisions.

Synopsis: Establishing and altering requirements related to criminal history records checks for certain licenses and certificates issued by certain health occupations boards, including the State Board of Acupuncture, the State Board of Dental Examiners, the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, the State Board of Nursing, the State Board of Examiners in Optometry, the State Board of Pharmacy, the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners, and the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists.
Title: Health Occupations - Criminal History Records Checks

Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants

bill_summary: Establishes and alters criminal history records check requirements for multiple health occupations licensing boards. Requires initial applicants, certain renewal applicants, and reinstatement applicants to submit fingerprints and fees to the Central Repository. Directs the Central Repository to forward criminal history record information and any subsequent updates to boards and applicants. Prohibits specified boards from issuing, renewing, or reinstating credentials before receiving required record information. Adds failure to submit to a records check as grounds for licensee discipline for multiple professions.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State Board of Acupuncture; State Board of Dental Examiners; State Board of Dietetic Practice; State Board of Environmental Health Specialists; State Board of Examiners in Optometry; State Board of Examiners of Psychologists; State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors; State Board of Nursing; State Board of Pharmacy; State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners; State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners; State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals
stakeholders: Applicants, licensees, and certificate holders across regulated health occupations (including acupuncturists, dentists, dental hygienists, dental radiation technologists, dietitian-nutritionists, environmental health specialists, forensic nurse examiners, medication technicians, optometrists, pharmacists, and physical therapists)
fiscal_impact_summary: DPSCS general fund revenues and expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2028 from conducting additional criminal history records checks, with potential revenues up to $946,512 depending on renewal timing. Affected health occupations boards can absorb administrative requirements using existing budgeted resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends licensing, renewal, and disciplinary requirements for twelve health occupations boards housed within the Maryland Department of Health, requiring them to receive and review criminal history records checks for applicants and licensees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that applicants submit fingerprints and fees to the department's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) to conduct state and national criminal history checks and report subsequent arrest information to licensing boards, resulting in notable operational and revenue impacts beginning in FY 2028.

Synopsis: Requiring units of State government to provide certain documentation to the Board of Public Works and the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee if the unit decides not to pursue certain liquidated damages; authorizing the Secretary of Budget and Management to set the pay scale for certain chief financial officer positions in order to assist with recruitment and retention; requiring the Secretary to establish certain minimum qualifications for chief financial officers that consider certain qualifications; etc.
Title: State Procurement and Personnel - Liquidated Damages Documentation Requirements and State Fiscal Leadership Capacity

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Budget and Management to set pay scales for certain chief financial and chief information officers. Excludes the University System of Maryland from these executive pay and qualification requirements. Requires the Department of Budget and Management to adopt minimum qualification regulations for chief financial officers by November 1, 2026. Requires qualifying chief financial officers to provide annual financial reports and an attestation letter to the Comptroller's Office. Requires units waiving liquidated damages to submit documentation to the Board of Public Works. Mandates sending the same liquidated damages documentation to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Board of Public Works; Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee; Office of the Comptroller
stakeholders: chief financial officers and chief information officers in Executive Branch units; State procurement units; State contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may increase from general and special funds beginning in fiscal 2027 if higher pay scales are established for chief financial officers and chief information officers. The fiscal 2027 budget includes $4.0 million in the Dedicated Purpose Account that may be used for this purpose. Liquidated damages provisions are procedural and have no direct fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing minimum qualifications for Chief Financial Officers by regulation and setting the pay scales for both CFO and Chief Information Officer positions across qualifying executive branch units.

The bill mandates that CFOs of major executive branch agencies submit necessary financial entries, schedule of expenditures of federal awards information, and an attestation letter directly to the Office of the Comptroller for the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report.
State units that decide not to pursue liquidated damages on procurement contracts must provide written documentation explaining the rationale for their decision directly to the Board of Public Works.

As an executive branch department receiving over $1.75 billion annually, MDH is directly subject to the bill's requirements regarding CFO qualifications, reporting to the Comptroller, and adjusted CFO/CIO pay scales.

As a major agency exceeding the $1.75 billion funding threshold, MSDE is directly impacted by the CFO minimum qualification mandates, financial reporting and attestation requirements to the Comptroller, and potential pay scale adjustments for its fiscal and IT leadership.

MDOT exceeds the $1.75 billion threshold and conducts significant procurement contracting; it is directly impacted by the CFO/CIO provisions as well as the broadened liquidated damages reporting requirements.

DHS meets the $1.75 billion annual funding threshold and will be subject to new CFO qualification standards, reporting and attestation obligations to the Comptroller, and altered executive salary scales.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Identified as one of the state agencies meeting the fiscal threshold, DPSCS is directly impacted by the revised CFO qualifications, financial reporting requirements, and executive compensation provisions.

DoIT coordinates IT strategy and leadership across the executive branch, making it relevant to the bill's establishment of statutory standards and pay scale authorizations for Chief Information Officers.

Synopsis: Repealing the deadline by which a certain fee must be paid by the holder of a Class A beer and light wine license or a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license to exercise certain Sunday sales privileges; and altering the deadline by which a license holder must present to the Board certain proof that all of the license holder's personal property taxes due to Baltimore City and the State have been paid.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Repeals the September 30 deadline for Class A alcoholic beverages license holders in Baltimore City to pay supplementary Sunday sales fees. Maintains the required supplementary license fee of $120 for each Sunday sales privilege exercised between Thanksgiving and New Year's Day. Moves the annual deadline from October 30 to March 30 for license holders to present paid personal property tax certificates. Requires the Board to immediately suspend renewal licenses without a hearing for failing to meet the tax certification deadline. Mandates the immediate reinstatement of suspended licenses without a hearing once the required certificate is presented.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of Liquor License Commissioners
stakeholders: Holders of Class A alcoholic beverages licenses and renewal licenses in Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill is not expected to materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland. While the bill specifically adjusts administrative deadlines for local Baltimore City alcoholic beverages licenses and verification of personal property taxes, it touches areas within the broader regulatory and tax enforcement purview of the Comptroller.

Synopsis: Adding two student members to the Somerset County Board of Education; altering who appoints an individual to fill a vacancy on the board to be the County Commissioners of Somerset County instead of the Governor; increasing the annual compensation for the chair and regular members of the board to be $6,000 and $5,000, respectively; and altering the actions the board may take during an executive session.
Title: Somerset County Board of Education - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: Adds one nonvoting student member from each public high school to the Somerset County Board of Education. Requires the County Commissioners of Somerset County, rather than the Governor, to appoint individuals to fill board vacancies. Increases annual compensation to $6,000 for the board chairman and $5,000 for other nonstudent members for future terms. Authorizes the county board to take actions in executive session under specified Open Meetings Act provisions. Prohibits student members from attending executive sessions unless invited by an affirmative majority vote of the county board.
responsible_party: Somerset County Board of Education; County Commissioners of Somerset County
stakeholders: Somerset County Board of Education members, Somerset County public high school students, and Somerset County taxpayers
fiscal_impact_summary: Somerset County expenditures increase by $3,450 in FY 2027, $6,900 in FY 2028, $9,550 in FY 2029, and $12,200 annually beginning in FY 2030 due to phased-in school board salary increases. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes the Governor's statutory authority to appoint qualified individuals to fill vacancies on the Somerset County Board of Education, transferring this appointment power to the County Commissioners of Somerset County.

Because the bill transfers the authority to fill vacancies on the local school board from the Governor to the Somerset County Commissioners, the Office of Appointments will no longer recruit or vet candidates for these vacancies.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the public education system and local school boards across Maryland's 24 jurisdictions, and the bill amends the governance structure and compensation of the Somerset County Board of Education under the Education Article.

Synopsis: Requiring the Interagency Commission on School Construction to distribute funds to public charter schools for capital improvements to public charter school facilities;  beginning in fiscal year 2028, requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation for the capital improvements to public charter school facilities that is equal to the total aggregate student enrollment in the Maryland Public Charter School Program for the prior fiscal year multiplied by $200; etc.
Title: Maryland Public Charter School Program - School Facilities - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Primary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Schools
Public Debt -see also- County & Balt City Bonds; State Bonds
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: Requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction to distribute funds directly to eligible public charter schools. Authorizes funding for capital improvements to public charter school facilities, debt service, or rent or lease payments. Restricts eligibility to public charter schools that had an unqualified audit in the prior fiscal year. Requires recipient charter schools to report project status to the Commission before receiving subsequent annual funds. Mandates an annual State budget appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2028 of $200 per charter school student.
responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction
stakeholders: Maryland public charter schools, charter school students and operators, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $116,835 in FY 2027 for administrative staff, rising to approximately $5.2 million in FY 2028 due to the mandated $200 per pupil facilities appropriation ($5.0 million) and administrative expenses. Out-year expenditures grow with inflation and projected charter school enrollment. Federal fund revenues may increase if the State obtains competitive federal charter facility grants. Direct local fiscal impact is minimal because disbursements go directly to charter schools.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) is the primary implementing agency responsible for adopting regulations, distributing funds directly to eligible public charter schools for capital improvements, debt service, or lease payments, and monitoring project reporting and compliance.

MSDE oversees the state's public education system, including the Maryland Public Charter School Program, and tracks the student enrollment data used to calculate the annual per-pupil facilities appropriation.

DBM oversees state budget preparation and execution, which is directly affected by the bill's statutory mandated General Fund appropriation of approximately $5.0 million or more annually starting in fiscal 2028.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor include an appropriation in the annual state budget bill equal to $200 multiplied by aggregate public charter school enrollment beginning in fiscal year 2028.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop and maintain a caregiver resource webpage with information and resources to support certain caregivers in the State.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - Caregiver Resource Webpage - Establishment
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 873

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and maintain a centralized caregiver resource webpage. Mandates plain-language resources covering children, adults, and older adults with functional limitations or special health needs. Requires information on respite, financial assistance programs, safety planning, and technology data privacy considerations. Requires coordination with the State Department of Education, Department of Aging, and Developmental Disabilities Administration. Directs the department to review and update the webpage at least annually.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Caregivers in Maryland providing care or assistance due to an individual's age, disability, chronic illness, cognitive impairment, or other functional limitation, as well as the individuals receiving care.
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local governmental finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health (and its Developmental Disabilities Administration) to develop, host, review, and maintain a centralized caregiver resource webpage on its website.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to coordinate with the Department of Aging to develop the webpage, which must include resources for older adults and individuals with dementia or cognitive impairments.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to coordinate with the Maryland State Department of Education to include resources and school-based supports for children with disabilities and special health care needs.
The Department of Human Services staffs the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, which oversees family caregiver support services and was consulted as an information source on the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a municipality to submit to the State Board of Elections the qualifications to be a candidate for each office on the ballot in a municipal election, the list of qualified candidates for each office on the ballot in a municipal election, the date of a special election and each office on the special election ballot, and certain information on voting procedures and locations in a municipal election on or before certain dates; requiring the State Board to post the information on the State Board's website immediately on receipt; etc.
Title: Municipal Elections - Reporting of Information to the State Board

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Requires municipalities to submit candidate qualifications for each municipal office to the State Board of Elections before filing deadlines. Mandates reporting of special election dates, ballot offices, and candidate qualifications within 15 business days of scheduling. Requires municipalities to submit qualified candidate lists and voting instructions within 10 business days after filing deadlines. Requires municipalities using ranked-choice voting to submit their ballot tabulation regulations to the State Board. Directs the State Board of Elections to publish all submitted election information immediately on its website.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, municipal election candidates, and municipal voters
fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact as the State Board of Elections can implement the bill with existing resources. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1448 directly mandates that the Maryland State Board of Elections receive municipal election candidate qualifications, candidate lists, voting procedures/locations, and ranked-choice voting regulations from municipalities and publish this information immediately on its website.

Synopsis: Establishing the Suitland Development Authority in Prince George's County; requiring the Authority to support and develop a neighborhood revitalization plan in coordination with certain residents; authorizing the Authority to modify certain boundaries, subject to a certain vote; requiring the Authority to take certain actions regarding the finances of the Authority; and requiring the Authority, by December 15, 2027, to report its neighborhood revitalization strategy to the Governor and certain legislative committees.
Title: Economic Development - Prince George's County Suitland Development Authority - Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Suitland Development Authority in Prince George's County as an instrumentality of the State. Requires the Authority to develop a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan in coordination with community residents. Authorizes the Authority to acquire property, issue grants, manage funds, and modify target area boundaries. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $500,000 to the Authority, which must become self-sustaining by fiscal 2036. Creates the Suitland Development Authority Fund to finance administrative costs, consulting fees, and employee salaries. Exempts the Authority from general state procurement law and specified state and local taxes on projects.
responsible_party: Suitland Development Authority; State Treasurer; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Residents, commercial property owners, and businesses along the Suitland Road and Silver Hill Road corridor in Prince George's County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $10.0 million annually from FY 2027 through FY 2035 to capitalize the authority, with corresponding special fund revenues and expenditures. The statutory $500,000 mandated appropriation begins in FY 2028 and continues in perpetuity after the authority becomes self-sustaining in FY 2036. Prince George's County expenditures increase if local funding is provided, while local revenues may shift due to tax exemptions and future property development.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the newly established Suitland Development Authority and is eligible to serve as cochair. The authority's core mission aligns directly with Commerce's economic development objectives.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Suitland Development Authority and is eligible to serve as cochair, directly connecting the agency to the authority's housing and neighborhood revitalization plan.

The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Suitland Development Authority and is eligible to serve as cochair, as the revitalization plan specifically addresses transportation along the Suitland Road and Silver Hill Road corridor.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Board of Directors of the Suitland Development Authority and is eligible to serve as cochair.
The bill establishes the Suitland Development Authority Fund and statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Suitland Development Authority Fund and administers state tax exemptions provided to the authority.

The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $500,000 for the authority in the state budget bill and requires the authority to submit its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report to the Governor by December 15, 2027.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, which includes administering the bill's mandated annual appropriation of $500,000 to the authority.

Because the authority is subject to Title 12, Subtitle 4 of the State Finance and Procurement Article as a procurement-exempt unit, it must submit its written procurement policies and procedures to the Board of Public Works for review.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Circuit Administrative Judge of the Fourth Circuit to establish a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program in the juvenile court in Washington County.
Title: Washington County - Juveniles - Truancy Reduction Pilot Program
bill_summary: Authorizes the Circuit Administrative Judge of the Fourth Circuit to establish a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program in Washington County. Applies the program specifically to the juvenile court in Washington County. Conditions program implementation on funding provided in the annual State budget. Authorizes the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland to accept gifts or grants for program implementation. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Circuit Administrative Judge of the Fourth Circuit; Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Truant children and their parents or legal guardians in Washington County, the Washington County juvenile court, and Washington County public school officials
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $155,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 for Judiciary grant funding. Washington County grant revenues and expenditures increase by $155,000 annually for program implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Circuit Administrative Judge of the Fourth Circuit to establish a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program in Washington County. The Administrative Office of the Courts (Judiciary) will administer the program and provide an estimated $155,000 annually in grant funding through its Office of Problem-Solving Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The establishment of a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program impacts the Office of the Public Defender operationally due to potential increases in juvenile caseloads and representation of parents facing truancy-related charges.

As the state agency overseeing juvenile justice, youth supervision, and court interventions for youth involved in the juvenile court system, the department has an operational interest in juvenile truancy interventions and court dispositions.

Synopsis: Expanding the definition of a qualified property for purposes of the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program.
Title: Department of Housing and Community Development - Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program - Qualified Properties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Expands the definition of a qualified property under the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program. Includes residential properties located in areas meeting department-established criteria for neighborhoods that have been historically redlined. Adds properties in areas that have undergone urban renewal under the department's criteria. Retains requirements that properties be newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated formerly vacant structures. Requires eligible properties to be built or rehabilitated for sale to owner-occupants at an affordable price.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Affordable housing developers and prospective owner-occupant homebuyers in historically redlined neighborhoods or areas that underwent urban renewal
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program, which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development. The bill authorizes the Department to establish criteria to identify neighborhoods that have been historically redlined or undergone urban renewal to qualify properties for the program.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning in 2026, the Maryland Department of Health to conduct the in-State cost-of-dispensing survey at least every 3 years;  and requiring the Department to report the results of the survey to the General Assembly by December 1 in each year the survey is required.
Title: Medical Assistance Programs - Drug Dispensing - Cost-of-Dispensing Survey

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct an in-State cost-of-dispensing survey at least once every three years. Sets the start of the triennial survey requirement for calendar year 2026. Directs the Department to report survey findings to the General Assembly. Requires this report on or before December 1 of each year a survey is conducted. Applies these provisions to drug dispensing under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Retail pharmacies and pharmacy providers participating in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program
fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures increase by $81,000 (50% general funds, 50% federal funds) in FY 2027 and FY 2030 to conduct the cost-of-dispensing survey. Federal fund revenues increase by $40,500 in those same years. Survey reporting can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1470 directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health conduct an in-State cost-of-dispensing survey for the Medical Assistance Program at least once every three years beginning in 2026 and report the findings to the General Assembly, resulting in periodic operational and fiscal impacts on Medicaid expenditures.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland's Future Board under the Department of Commerce to develop, evaluate, and revise a visionary plan for the future of Maryland by January 1, 2027; requiring the Board to make recommendations for projects based on the plan to the Governor and the General Assembly by August 1, 2027 and each August 1 thereafter; establishing the Maryland's Future Fund; and requiring the Comptroller to study economic growth trends for certain industries and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland's Future Board in the Department of Commerce to develop, annually evaluate, and revise a visionary plan. bill_summary: Restructures State energy assistance programs, utility ratemaking standards, and clean energy initiatives to reduce ratepayer costs. Modifies the EmPOWER Maryland Program by removing gas companies and lowering electric greenhouse gas reduction targets. Lowers the large load customer demand threshold from 100 megawatts to 25 megawatts. Mandates that high-voltage transmission line owners participate in a regional transmission organization. Directs the Public Service Commission to implement a successor net energy metering program capped at 6,000 megawatts. Authorizes residential customers to install one portable solar energy generating system per electric meter.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Maryland Energy Administration; Department of Natural Resources; Department of Human Services; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: residential electric and gas ratepayers, electric and gas utility companies, data center operators, solar energy developers, and energy efficiency contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $201.4 million in FY 2027, including $100.0 million for PSC rate relief grants and $100.0 million for MEA renewable energy auctions funded by the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. Special fund spending increases by $198.2 million in FY 2028 due to ongoing auctions and mandated appropriations, while general fund expenditures increase by at least $10.0 million annually from FY 2029 through FY 2031 for the Urban Trees Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places extensive regulatory, administrative, and reporting mandates on the PSC, including establishing utility rate-setting restrictions, developing and implementing a successor net energy metering program, regulating large load customers/data centers, expanding CPCN requirements to underground transmission lines, restructuring EmPOWER Maryland, and publishing new online dashboards and annual rate reports.

The bill significantly impacts MEA by mandating two annual competitive low-bid renewable energy auctions ($100 million each in FY 2027 and FY 2028) using SEIF alternative compliance payment revenues, transferring primary administration of DRIVE Act on-site clean energy incentives/rebates to MEA, reallocating RGGI proceeds within SEIF, and requiring consultation on multiple studies and dashboards.

As the independent advocate for residential utility customers, OPC is tasked with participating in rate proceedings, consulting on annual utility rate reports, bringing actions before PSC for inaccurate rate information, and participating in the stakeholder proceeding regarding the successor net metering program.

The bill directly impacts DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), which must evaluate additional CPCN applications resulting from expanded transmission line reviews and altered definitions of large capacity energy resources, conduct a study on streamlined energy permitting and priority sites, and receive an altered allocation of SEIF funding.

The bill formally transfers statutory administration of the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) from the PSC to the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) within DHS and requires DHS consultation on an automatic community solar enrollment study.

The bill authorizes BPW, upon the recommendation of the Secretary of General Services, to waive the mandatory termination for convenience clause in multi-year State procurement contracts for renewable energy generation projects.

As the State's lead procurement agency, DGS is empowered to recommend waivers to BPW for termination for convenience clauses in multi-year renewable power purchase contracts to facilitate project financing and reduce State energy costs.

The bill's restructuring of SEIF clean energy program accounts affects the dedicated funding stream currently supporting the Trust's Urban Trees Program and Climate Corps program, necessitating $10 million annually in replacement general funds starting in FY 2029.

DHCD administers low-income energy efficiency programs under the EmPOWER Maryland Program; while its targets and funding allocations remain intact, the broader restructuring of EmPOWER surcharges and goals directly intersects with its energy efficiency portfolio.
MDE is required to consult with DNR on the energy development streamlined permitting study and is operationally affected by adjustments to greenhouse gas reduction goals and EmPOWER program targets.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to seek judicial enforcement against local governments that fail to comply with residential solar permitting software implementation and inspection timeline requirements.

The bill mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations of unencumbered RGGI proceeds from SEIF in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2028 and authorizes budget amendments to transfer funds for residential customer rate relief.

Requires the committee to review State long-term real estate plans annually and meet at least three times each year. Mandates an annual committee report to the Governor, Board of Public Works, and General Assembly. Expands oversight requirements for State real property acquisitions and high-value State leases. The bill places new requirements on real property acquisitions and leases approved by BPW, requiring reporting and justifications to the Legislative Policy Committee, and establishes the advisory committee in part to advise BPW.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent advisory entity, the Real Estate Advisory Committee, charged with reviewing state real estate plans and advising on commercial real estate trends and best practices.

As an agency that manages state property, facilities, and leases, MDOT is responsible for producing and disseminating required information and justification to the Legislative Policy Committee for qualifying real estate transactions.

As an entity managing significant real property and facility leases, USM is identified in the fiscal analysis as responsible for compiling and submitting required property lease and acquisition justifications under the expanded reporting requirements.
The Governor sits on the Board of Public Works which is subject to the bill's property approval provisions, and receives the advisory committee's mandatory annual reports.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is directly advised by the new committee and subject to expanded oversight and submission requirements before approving certain high-value leases and property transactions.

The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is directly advised by the new committee and subject to expanded reporting and approval conditions for high-value state real estate leases.

bill_summary: Prohibits the use of unlicensed settings for children in out-of-home placement programs. Expands the definition of unlicensed settings to include pediatric hospital overstay patients. Establishes the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel within the Governor's Office for Children. Requires pediatric overstay coordinators to convene Rapid Response Placement Teams to locate appropriate placements. Authorizes the Department of Human Services to execute emergency procurements for in-state or out-of-state placements. Establishes the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.
responsible_party: Governor's Office for Children; Department of Human Services; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: children and youth in out-of-home placements, pediatric hospital overstay patients, foster parents, hospitals, child welfare service providers, and local departments of social services
fiscal_impact_summary: Governor's Office for Children special fund expenditures increase by $204,600 in fiscal 2027 for new staff, reflecting the phase-in of one contractual position and one permanent position. Costs annualize in subsequent years through fiscal 2031, with the contractual position terminating in fiscal 2030. The Maryland Department of Health and the Department of Human Services can absorb operational requirements within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly houses the newly established Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, creates the Senior Advisor for Children and Families within the office to oversee the panel and placement teams, and requires the office to provide administrative and staff support for both the panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families, resulting in a direct fiscal and operational impact.

The bill directly regulates DHS's out-of-home placement program by prohibiting placements in unlicensed settings and pediatric overstays, alters the duties and reporting of DHS's pediatric overstay coordinator, authorizes DHS to execute emergency procurements for youth placements, and mandates joint reporting with the Department of Health.

The bill alters requirements and data collection for MDH's pediatric overstay coordinator, designates MDH's notification system for hospitals, requires joint capacity-building reporting with DHS, and places the Secretary of Health on the review panel and advisory council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes multiple new state entities, including the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, Rapid Response Placement Teams, and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families, and its working subgroup.

The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is mandated to serve as a member of both the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.

The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is named as a statutory member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its specialized assessment and data subgroup.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner (or designee) is designated to serve on the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its subgroup, which examines insurance parity and rate reform barriers.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission (or designee) is mandated to serve on the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its working subgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families and its working subgroup.

The Governor appoints the Senior Advisor for Children and Families (who serves at the Governor's pleasure), appoints various stakeholder members to the Review Panel and Advisory Council, and receives annual reports and recommendations.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to examine carriers issuing patterns of adverse decisions on emergency department claims. Authorizes the Commissioner to obtain independent review of carrier decisions at the carrier's expense. Requires the Commissioner to include post-acute care data in the annual appeals and grievances summary report. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission and Health Services Cost Review Commission to conduct two studies by January 1, 2027. Requires the commissions to quantify hospital and post-acute bed capacity and evaluate transitions from acute to post-acute care.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Health Care Commission; Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: health insurance carriers, private review agents, hospitals, post-acute care facilities, and patients receiving emergency or post-acute services
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal state fiscal impact. Studies by the Maryland Health Care Commission and Health Services Cost Review Commission, as well as additional workload for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA), can likely be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. MIA special fund revenues may increase minimally to recoup carrier examination costs. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1563 authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to conduct market examinations of carriers demonstrating a pattern of adverse decisions or grievances regarding emergency department claims/authorizations, mandate independent external reviews at the carrier's expense, and incorporate post-acute care adverse decision and grievance data into the annual appeals and grievances summary report.

The bill directly mandates that MHCC, in conjunction with HSCRC and industry representatives, conduct two major studies due January 1, 2027: one quantifying bed capacity in hospitals and post-acute settings and recommending a standardized bed reporting and auditing process, and another analyzing options to facilitate clinically appropriate transitions from acute to post-acute care.

HSCRC is mandated to partner with MHCC to conduct both required studies regarding hospital and post-acute care bed capacity, annual bed collection and auditing mechanisms, and acute to post-acute patient care transitions, submitting joint reports to the Governor and legislative committees.

MHCC is an independent regulatory agency housed within the Maryland Department of Health, and MDH was consulted as an information source regarding state health facility oversight and regulations implicated by the emergency department and post-acute care study requirements.

The Governor is designated as a recipient of the mandated study findings and recommendations from MHCC and HSCRC regarding hospital bed capacity auditing and acute to post-acute transitions due by January 1, 2027.

bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the Minority Business Enterprise Program and its related procurement requirements to July 1, 2031. Establishes new legislative findings based on the 2025 disparity study to support the program. Requires State procurement units to submit quarterly reports on minority business participation and small business awards. Directs the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to establish a small business certification review process. Expands the definition of small business to include qualifying joint ventures.
responsible_party: Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; Department of Social and Economic Mobility; Board of Public Works
stakeholders: certified minority business enterprises; small businesses; veteran-owned small business enterprises; State procurement units; prime contractors; applicants and licensees for cannabis, offshore wind, video lottery terminal, and sports wagering operations
fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal effect. State procurement agencies can implement the altered reporting deadlines and new quarterly reporting mandates using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reauthorizes the Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) Program, requires OSBA to establish a small business certification review process, modifies OSBA's reporting schedules and mandates new quarterly tracking, and adjusts OSBA's duties regarding cannabis, offshore wind, and gaming licensees.

The bill requires annual procurement reports to be submitted to BPW, involves BPW in criteria adoption and approval of reporting forms, regulates public-private partnership approvals under MBE guidelines, and oversees the designated MBE certification agency.

OAG is statutorily required to consult on MBE plans and disparity evaluations for cannabis, offshore wind, sports wagering, and public-private partnerships, participate in criteria development for noncompliant prime contractors, and handle contractor debarment referrals.

DGS houses the Office of State Procurement, which must jointly adopt criteria for contractor debarment with OSBA, assist in developing small business reserve exemption procedures, and serve on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

The bill extends the MBE requirements applicable to cannabis licensees through July 1, 2031, and requires the Administration and its Office of Social Equity to consult on disparity evaluations and licensee MBE participation plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reauthorizes and extends MBE participation compliance requirements through 2031 for video lottery terminal (VLT) and sports wagering licensees, which the Commission is tasked with enforcing.

The bill extends the MBE requirements for approved offshore wind projects through July 1, 2031, and requires offshore wind renewable energy credit (OREC) holders to submit biannual MBE progress reports to the Commission.

MDOT serves as a designated certification agency in procurement regulations, the Secretary must be consulted regarding capital project subgoal guidelines, and the Secretary serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

Uncodified language in the bill requires the State Retirement and Pension System to provide information necessary to assess the need for remedial measures in the brokerage and investment management services industry.
The bill amends the composition of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation to specifically add the Secretary of Labor or the Secretary's designee as a member.
The Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation is required to report to the Governor annually, and OSBA operates within the Executive Department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory membership, chair, meeting mandates, and duties of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is a designated member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department must adhere to the new quarterly and annual procurement reporting schedules.
The Secretary of Commerce is a designated member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the agency must comply with the altered MBE/SBR reporting deadlines.
The Secretary of Health serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department is subject to the accelerated procurement reporting requirements.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the agency must submit quarterly and annual MBE/SBR data.
The Secretary of Human Services serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department is subject to the updated procurement reporting timelines.

The Secretary of Information Technology is a member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and the department is impacted by the modified procurement preference reporting deadlines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and must comply with revised quarterly procurement preference reporting.

The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is a statutory member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation, and the bill amends reporting rules for the Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise Program.

bill_summary: Transfers operational authority and project responsibilities for horse racing redevelopment projects to the Maryland Stadium Authority. Increases Maryland Stadium Authority bond authorization for Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor facilities from $400,000,000 to $425,000,000. Designates Montgomery County and Howard County as grantees under the Bus Rapid Transit Fund. Mandates a $5,000,000 appropriation in fiscal year 2028 for backstretch housing facilities at Laurel Park. Alters annual distributions from the State Lottery Fund and the Purse Dedication Account for racing facilities and debt service.
responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Transportation; State Racing Commission
stakeholders: Thoroughbred horse racing operators, backstretch workers at Laurel Park, transit riders, Prince George's County, Montgomery County, and Howard County
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million annually beginning in FY 2027 due to increased statutory lottery distributions. General fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2028 only for Laurel Park backstretch housing. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028, and Purse Dedication Account expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028. Montgomery County continues to receive $27.0 million annually and Howard County receives $2.0 million annually in local bus rapid transit grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Requested the bill and serves as the primary implementing agency; designated as the successor entity to MTROA for racing and community development projects, given oversight over Pimlico operations and financial statements, authorized up to $425 million in bonds for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor, and administers project funds.

Administers the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Grant Program, which is altered to mandate multi-year grant agreements with Montgomery and Howard counties, expands authorized uses of grant funds, and increases mandated appropriations from the Transportation Trust Fund to the BRT Fund.

Responsible for executing altered statutory distributions from the State Lottery Fund to the Racing and Community Development Financing Fund, the Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund, and issuing warrants from the Purse Dedication Account.

Transfers MEDCO's operational responsibilities for the Pimlico racing project to the Maryland Stadium Authority, while MEDCO is allocated $2 million annually from the Purse Dedication Account for debt service on a training facility site.

Directly designated under the bill to receive 10% of the thoroughbred racetrack operator's annual net income as local impact grants for community development projects under the Pimlico Area Joint Plan.
Houses the Maryland State Racing Commission, whose statutory authority regarding licensing, race-day allocations, Preakness Stakes transfers, and the Purse Dedication Account is altered.

Invests and manages proceeds in the Purse Dedication Account, and evaluates the fiscal impact of increased lottery fund distributions and transportation debt on state debt affordability and bond ratings.

Approves bond issuances by the Maryland Stadium Authority for Blue Line Corridor facilities and receives formal 180-day notification and alternative use plans if racing operations at Pimlico are no longer viable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Regulates and manages the State Lottery Fund from which increased statutory distributions are mandated for racing facilities and Blue Line Corridor debt service, directly affecting lottery coverage ratios.
Authorized to receive delegated adjudications as contested cases from the Maryland Stadium Authority regarding disputes over commercial viability or alternative use plans for the Pimlico site.
Mandated to include specific appropriations in the annual state budget bill, including $5 million in FY 2028 for Laurel Park backstretch housing and increased funding for the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.

The bill repeals Section 10-612 of the Economic Development Article, removing provisions that required MSA to notify and report to the State Ethics Commission regarding employee service on affiliated sports foundation boards.

bill_summary: Alters statutory parameters governing how public school performance is measured under the State's educational accountability program. Increases the maximum combined weight of academic indicators from 65% to 70% of the composite score. Prohibits any academic indicator of proficiency from being weighted at more than 20% of the composite score. Prohibits accountability indicators established by the State Board of Education from incorporating, referencing, or relying on teacher evaluations. Authorizes school staffing measures and completion of well-rounded curriculum measures as school quality indicators. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to submit annual reports on accountability indicators and poverty correlations through 2031.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Maryland public schools, public school students, public school educators, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: No impact on State revenues or expenditures. Any implementation costs for the Maryland State Department of Education are expected to be absorbable within existing resources, and local school system finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1582 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) that alters the statutory parameters governing the State's public school educational accountability program and school quality indicators. MSDE and the State Board of Education are directly responsible for administering the accountability system, calculating composite scores, and producing the required annual reports on accountability indicators and correlation with poverty levels.

Specifies that an electronic instant bingo machine need not print a paper ticket unless the player chooses. Exempts authorized electronic instant bingo machines from statutory prohibitions governing illegal gaming devices. Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to adopt implementing regulations. Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to submit an independent gaming expansion study by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency; State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Commercial electronic instant bingo licensees, qualified nonprofit gaming organizations, electronic bingo players, satellite simulcast facility operators, and gaming industry labor unions
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 in fiscal 2027 for the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to retain an independent consultant. State revenues and local finances in Anne Arundel and Calvert counties are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission with adopting regulations to implement changes to electronic instant bingo operations, and mandates that the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency hire an independent consultant to conduct a study and report on the impacts of potential gaming expansions by December 1, 2026, incurring up to $100,000 in general fund expenditures.

The bill explicitly requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to submit a comprehensive report detailing the potential expansion and economic impacts of electronic instant bingo, historical horse racing machines, and satellite simulcast facilities to the Governor by December 1, 2026.

bill_summary: Authorizes a racing licensee to receive a Racetrack Facility Renewal Account grant without providing a matching fund. Requires a licensee receiving grants without matching funds to conduct live racing for at least 10 years after construction completion. Directs the State Racing Commission to recapture grant funds on a pro rata basis if racing requirements fail. Requires the Commission and Department of General Services to certify completion of capital construction plans upon written request. Alters to 75% the unencumbered balance transferred between Rosecroft Raceway and Ocean Downs Race Course if either facility closes.
