bill_summary: Establishes the Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program to fund oyster propagation and replenishment projects. Establishes the Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund to assist commercial watermen and seafood industry small businesses. Authorizes the temporary transfer of up to $337,500 each from two existing loan programs to the fund. Requires notification to the Department of Natural Resources when a tidal fish licensee is delinquent on a loan. Prohibits the department from approving tidal fish license transfers until the delinquent borrower becomes compliant. Mandates an annual $2,000,000 Transportation Trust Fund appropriation for the enhancement program starting in fiscal year 2028.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
stakeholders: Commercial watermen; seafood industry small businesses; tidal fish license holders
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2,000,000 in fiscal 2027 to capitalize the new fund under a contingent budget appropriation. Nonbudgeted revenues increase by $2,000,000 and nonbudgeted expenditures increase by $2,700,000 in fiscal 2027 to provide loans and cover administrative costs, reflecting the contingent appropriation and $675,000 transferred from other loan programs. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures increase by indeterminate amounts in future years from loan repayments and reissuance. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is the primary implementing agency for the newly created Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund. It is tasked with administering the fund, setting loan terms and eligibility criteria, executing temporary fund transfers from existing programs, and notifying DNR of delinquent borrowers.

DNR houses and administers the newly codified Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program for oyster propagation and replenishment projects, receives program funding, and is prohibited from approving transfers of tidal fish licenses for borrowers delinquent on MARBIDCO loans.

The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $2,000,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) administered by MDOT to support DNR's oyster replenishment efforts, codifying a long-standing interagency mitigation agreement between MDOT and DNR.

The bill's Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program specifically funds oyster propagation and replenishment projects that mitigate the ecological impacts of transportation, dredging, and maintenance projects at the Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore, which MPA operates.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and fiscal planning, including the implementation of the statutory mandated annual TTF appropriation of $2,000,000 starting in FY 2028 and the FY 2027 contingent general fund appropriation.
The bill requires the Governor to include a mandated annual appropriation of $2,000,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund in the state budget bill beginning in FY 2028.

Synopsis: Altering a certain income limitation used to establish eligibility for a property tax credit against the county and municipal corporation property tax imposed on the dwelling house of a certain disabled veteran or surviving spouse; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Property Tax - Credit for Dwelling House of Disabled Veterans and Surviving Spouses - Income Eligibility

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Alters income eligibility limits for an optional local property tax credit on dwelling houses of disabled veterans. Limits eligible federal adjusted gross income to $150,000 for individual filers and $300,000 for joint filers. Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or county and municipal governing bodies to set additional eligibility criteria. Permits those governing bodies to base additional criteria on income and disability ratings. Takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
stakeholders: Honorably discharged disabled veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities, their surviving spouses, and county and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Potential decrease in local property tax revenues beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent local jurisdictions grant the credit and higher income limits expand eligibility. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies eligibility thresholds, including income caps and disability ratings, for local property tax credits available to disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. As the primary state agency tasked with assisting veterans and their families in accessing benefits, housing resources, and tax relief information, this legislation directly pertains to their advocacy and constituent service mission.

The bill establishes eligibility caps based on federal adjusted gross income from individual and joint income tax returns. While the tax credit is applied at the local property tax level with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller administers Maryland income tax reporting and was consulted on the fiscal and policy note.

Synopsis: Authorizing a mutual insurance holding company that, directly or indirectly, owns 100% of the capital stock of a reorganized stock insurer to convert its mutual insurance holding company system to a mutual insurer on adoption and approval of a plan of conversion; and establishing certain requirements related to the plan of conversion and its submission to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner for approval.

bill_summary: Authorizes a mutual insurance holding company owning 100% of a reorganized stock insurer's capital stock to convert into a mutual insurer. Requires approval of a conversion plan by a majority of the board and at least 75% of voting members. Mandates submitting the plan and a 5-year operation plan to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner at least 60 days before conversion. Requires the Commissioner to approve the plan if it complies with statutory standards and is equitable to members. Directs the holding company and intermediate holding companies to dissolve upon conversion.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Mutual insurance holding companies, reorganized stock insurers, and their policyholders and members
fiscal_impact_summary: No net state fiscal impact. Special fund expenditures and revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration may increase correspondingly if the agency retains an outside expert to review a conversion plan at the holding company's expense; exact amounts are unavailable. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1616 directly regulates the conversion of mutual insurance holding companies to mutual insurers, requiring approval, review, and potential hearings by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner. The Maryland Insurance Administration is also authorized to retain experts to assist in reviewing plans of conversion and adopt implementing regulations.

bill_summary: Designates the Village Council of Drummond as the governing body of the Village of Drummond special taxing district in Montgomery County. Establishes a three-member Village Council elected annually by village residents who are at least 18 years old. Requires the Village Council to appoint a mayor, a treasurer, a secretary, and necessary employees. Alters eligible uses of special tax levy funds and establishes an annual budget adoption process with public hearing requirements. Raises the competitive bidding threshold for material or work contracts to $15,000 and defines specific bidding exemptions. Authorizes the Village Council to establish, operate, maintain, and control non-State public ways in the village.
responsible_party: Village Council of Drummond; Montgomery County Council
stakeholders: residents and property owners in the Village of Drummond special taxing district in Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Village of Drummond expenditures increase minimally to purchase fidelity bonds for required officers, estimated at $1,000 to $5,000 per bond for approximately two individuals, which does not materially affect village finances.

Synopsis: Clarifying that certain requirements apply only to districts for the election of members of the Senate of Maryland and the House of Delegates; authorizing the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review the congressional districting plan of the State; and providing that nothing in the Maryland Constitution provides applicable criteria for the boundaries of a congressional districting plan.
Title: Election Districts - General Assembly and Representatives in Congress
Status: Approved by the Governor, assigned a chapter number, enactment subject to constitutional referendum - Chapter 881

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte

bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution governing legislative and congressional election districts. Clarifies that constitutional compactness, contiguity, and equal population standards apply exclusively to General Assembly legislative districts. Establishes that no provision in the Maryland Constitution provides criteria for congressional districting boundaries. Authorizes the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review congressional districting plans. Submits the proposed constitutional amendment and specific ballot question text to voters at the November 2026 general election.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections; Maryland General Assembly; Supreme Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland voters and candidates for the Maryland General Assembly and the U.S. House of Representatives
fiscal_impact_summary: The proposed constitutional amendment is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the submission of a constitutional amendment to Maryland voters at the November 2026 general election, setting specific ballot language and modifying standard statutory requirements for the ballot question administered by the State Board of Elections.

The Secretary of State is responsible for the certification of statewide ballot questions and constitutional amendments, as well as serving as the custodian of state official records and constitutional changes.

The proposed constitutional amendment authorizes the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review congressional districting plans, directly impacting judicial proceedings and appellate caseload.

The Maryland Department of Planning provides demographic and mapping support, maintains official legislative and congressional redistricting maps, and is listed as an informational source on redistricting data.

Pursuant to the bill and Article XIV of the Maryland Constitution, the official election returns regarding the proposed constitutional amendment must be transmitted to the Governor to make the official proclamation.

Synopsis: Withdrawing and repealing a certain duplicate proposed constitutional amendment relating to collective bargaining for State employees.
Title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026 - Withdraw and Repeal of Duplicate Proposed Constitutional Amendment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Withdraws and repeals a duplicate proposed constitutional amendment regarding collective bargaining for State employees. Repeals Sections 2 through 4 of Chapter 156 of the Acts of 2026. Alters the contingency clause of Chapter 156 to depend on voter ratification of Chapter 155 of 2026. Prevents identical constitutional amendment questions from appearing on the November 2026 general election ballot. Takes effect immediately upon enactment as an emergency measure.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters and State employees
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the change is technical and merely prevents duplicate language from appearing on the general election ballot.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 2101 directly impacts the ballot preparation responsibilities of the State Board of Elections by withdrawing and repealing duplicate constitutional amendment language from Chapter 156 of 2026, ensuring that the referendum on binding arbitration for State employee collective bargaining appears only once on the November 2026 general election ballot.

Synopsis: Establishing the salaries to be paid to the Governor and Lieutenant Governor, as directed by Article II, Section 21A of the Maryland Constitution, for the 4-year term of office beginning January 20, 2027.
Title: Governor's Salary Commission - Salary Recommendations for Governor and Lieutenant Governor
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 21A(d) of the Maryland Constitution Assigned a resolution number - Joint Resolution 3

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Adopts the salary recommendations of the Governor's Salary Commission for the Governor and Lieutenant Governor. Establishes the Governor's annual salary at $195,000 in year one, $202,000 in years two and three, and $210,000 in year four. Sets the Lieutenant Governor's annual salary at $175,000 in year one, $180,000 in years two and three, and $185,000 in year four. Applies the new salaries to the four-year term of office beginning January 20, 2027. Directs the Department of Legislative Services to forward copies to the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, and Secretary of Budget and Management.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland Governor and Lieutenant Governor
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $6,800 in FY 2028, $13,600 in FY 2029, $20,900 in FY 2030, and $28,300 in FY 2031 to cover salary increases and associated fringe benefits. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HJ 5 directly establishes the annual compensation and salary schedule for the Governor of Maryland for the 4-year term beginning January 20, 2027.
HJ 5 directly sets the annual salary schedule for the Lieutenant Governor of Maryland for the 4-year term beginning January 20, 2027.

As the state's principal budget and personnel agency, DBM must incorporate the adjusted executive salary figures and fringe benefits into future state budget planning, and the resolution explicitly directs that a copy be forwarded to the Secretary of Budget and Management.
The State Treasurer serves as a constitutional member of the Governor's Salary Commission which evaluated, determined, and submitted these salary recommendations.

Synopsis: Establishing the compensation of the members of the Judiciary in this State in accordance with Section 1-708 of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland.
Title: Judicial Compensation Commission - Recommendations
Status: Enacted under Section 1-708 of the Courts Article Assigned a resolution number - Joint Resolution 4

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Increases judicial salaries by $5,900 annually across fiscal years 2027 through 2030. Applies phased salary increases to judges of the Supreme Court, Appellate Court, Circuit Courts, and District Court. Grants an annual $7,500 stipend to the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland. Authorizes an annual $7,500 stipend for circuit court and District Court administrative judges.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Judges across the Supreme Court of Maryland, Appellate Court of Maryland, Circuit Courts, and District Court; administrative judges; retired recalled judges; magistrates; the State Prosecutor; the Public Defender; Workers' Compensation Commission members; and county officials whose salaries tie to judicial pay
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.3 million and special fund expenditures increase by $63,325 in FY 2027, with total annual State expenditure increases reaching $12.0 million by FY 2030. Local government expenditures increase minimally in counties that index local official salaries to judicial pay.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The resolution directly sets the compensation, annual stipends, and salary schedules for all judges across the Maryland Judiciary, which the Administrative Office of the Courts administratively supports and funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: By statute, the salary of the Public Defender is tied to that of a circuit court judge, resulting in an automatic salary and expenditure increase for the agency.
By statute, the salary of the State Prosecutor is tied to that of a circuit court judge, resulting in an automatic salary and expenditure increase for the agency.
The salaries of the commissioners of the Workers' Compensation Commission are tied by statute to those of District Court judges, resulting in an increase in special fund expenditures for the agency.

The agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Judicial Retirement System, which experiences changes in actuarial assumptions and pension liabilities resulting from the revised judicial salary schedules.
DBM oversees the state budget and personnel allocations, which must account for the general and special fund expenditure increases across impacted state positions and agencies.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to develop a uniform policy, to be used by each law enforcement agency, prohibiting the use of a face covering in the performance of duty; requiring the Commission to develop a certain uniform policy requiring the use of worn identification by a law enforcement officer in the course of duty; requiring a law enforcement officer to wear identification while in the performance of duty in the State, with a certain exception; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Law Enforcement Officers - Face Coverings and Identification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Police Conduct -see also- Ethics; Law Enforcement

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to develop uniform policies on law enforcement face coverings and identification. Prohibits law enforcement officers from wearing face coverings on duty, except as authorized by policy or during undercover operations. Mandates that uniformed officers display identification on outermost clothing and verbally disclose identifying information upon request. Bars local jurisdictions and agencies from adopting differing policies regarding officer face coverings or identification. Classifies violations as civil offenses punishable by fines up to $1,500 and as police misconduct.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: law enforcement officers and law enforcement agencies in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in general fund revenues from District Court civil penalties. Potential minimal increase in State and local expenditures to update law enforcement officer uniforms and training programs. The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can implement the policies with existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), housed within DPSCS, is required to develop two statewide uniform policies prohibiting face coverings and mandating worn identification for law enforcement officers.
The District Court must prescribe a statewide uniform citation form, establish a schedule for fine prepayments, and schedule and adjudicate civil citation trials for violations of the bill.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, its sworn troopers are subject to the face covering prohibitions and identification display mandates, and must update uniform and training protocols accordingly.
DNR employs the Natural Resources Police, whose sworn officers are subject to the uniform policies regarding face coverings, visible outerwear identification, and associated training requirements.
MDOT oversees modal administrations that employ sworn law enforcement personnel who must adhere to the new identification and face covering mandates and adjust uniforms or training as needed.
MDTA operates its own dedicated police force, whose sworn officers must comply with the uniform policies on identification and face coverings.
MTA maintains a sworn transit police force that must comply with the MPTSC uniform policies regarding face coverings and outer uniform identification.
DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, whose sworn officers are directly subject to the uniform policies prohibiting face coverings and requiring visible identification.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund, which is specified in the bill to receive court-ordered penalty payments from individuals adjudicated of civil violations under this Act.
USM institutions employ sworn campus police officers who are subject to MPTSC standards, requiring compliance with the uniform face covering and identification policies.
Morgan State University maintains an independent campus police department with sworn law enforcement officers who must comply with the bill's uniform identification and face covering requirements.
As a public institution maintaining campus public safety personnel, it is potentially affected by the statewide law enforcement uniform and identification policies.

Synopsis: Providing collective bargaining rights to nontenure track faculty of    system institutions of higher education, Morgan State University, or St. Mary's College of Maryland whose primary assignments involve academic instruction, including teachers, researchers, and department heads and those in comparable positions; and establishing a separate collective bargaining unit for nontenure track faculty.
Title: State Personnel - Collective Bargaining - Nontenure Track Faculty

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Extends collective bargaining rights to eligible nontenure track faculty at public institutions of higher education. Covers instructional nontenure track faculty at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland. Establishes a separate collective bargaining unit for nontenure track faculty at each institution. Excludes faculty at fully online institutions and faculty funded through grants, contracts, or clinical revenues. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
stakeholders: Nontenure track instructional faculty and administrations at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Reimbursable revenues and expenditures for the Public Employee Relations Board increase minimally from institutional fees. Expenditures for the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland increase minimally to reimburse the board, with potentially significant but indeterminate administrative and personnel cost increases contingent on union election results and collective bargaining negotiations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PERB is responsible for administering union elections, certifying exclusive representatives, investigating unfair labor practice charges, and resolving collective bargaining disputes for the newly created nontenure track faculty bargaining units.

USM institutions are directly required to establish a separate collective bargaining unit for eligible nontenure track faculty, negotiate terms and conditions of employment, and reimburse PERB for collective bargaining election expenses.

MSU is an affected public institution of higher education directly required to recognize collective bargaining rights for its eligible nontenure track instructional faculty and handle associated negotiation and administrative costs.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the bill's provisions, requiring it to establish collective bargaining for eligible nontenure track faculty and incur potential administrative and reimbursable costs with PERB.

OAH has delegated authority from institutions to hear employee grievances and disciplinary appeals; it will experience an operational impact from training administrative law judges on the new law and potential increases in case hearings.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from utilizing certain personal identifying information or engaging in certain conduct in order to cause physical injury, serious emotional distress, or economic damages; prohibiting a person from using certain artificial intelligence or certain deepfake representations for certain purposes; providing penalties of 5 years of imprisonment and a fine of up $10,000 or both where one victim is involved, and for two or more victims the term of imprisonment is up to 10 years and the fine is up to $15,000 or both; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Identity Fraud - Artificial Intelligence and Deepfake Representations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Expands identity fraud prohibitions to include unauthorized use of personal identifying information to cause harm. Prohibits assuming another person's identity with fraudulent intent to harm, harass, intimidate, threaten, or coerce them. Prohibits using artificial intelligence or deepfake representations with fraudulent intent to cause harm or create false records. Establishes felony penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment for artificial intelligence or deepfake identity fraud violations. Authorizes victims of artificial intelligence or deepfake violations to bring civil actions for injunctive or other relief.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Office of the Attorney General; State's Attorneys
stakeholders: Victims of identity fraud, deepfake depictions, or artificial intelligence impersonation; law enforcement agencies; individuals accused of identity fraud offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations, with any additional caseloads accommodated within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under § 8-301(p) of the Criminal Law Article, the Attorney General is explicitly granted authority to investigate and prosecute identity fraud violations under this section, possessing all powers of a State's Attorney including the use of a grand jury.

The Department of State Police is statutorily empowered to initiate investigations and enforce this identity fraud section statewide without jurisdictional limitations and adopts regulations governing investigative authority for other law enforcement entities under § 8-301(l) and (m).

The bill creates a new private right of action permitting victims to bring civil suits for injunctions and appropriate relief in the courts, and expands criminal identity fraud offenses handled by the state court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands identity fraud crimes and penalties (including new felony classifications for deepfake and AI fraud), impacting the caseload and representation duties of the Office of the Public Defender for indigent defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new and expanded misdemeanor and felony offenses carrying terms of imprisonment ranging up to 10 years, which impacts state correctional and pretrial intake and supervision operations.

The Maryland Transportation Authority Police are specifically authorized by § 8-301(m) and (n) to investigate identity fraud violations throughout the State and receive notifications of investigations occurring on MDTA property.

The Maryland Port Administration Police are explicitly authorized under § 8-301(m) and (n) to investigate identity fraud offenses throughout the State and receive investigative notifications for incidents on MPA property.

Section 8-301(n) specifically requires notification to the chief of police of the Maryland Aviation Administration when an identity fraud investigation occurs on property owned, leased, or operated by the administration.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Highway Administration to approve, deny, or return as incomplete an application for the use of a certain speed monitoring system within 120 days after receipt of the application; providing that if the Administration does not approve, deny, or return the application in accordance with the Act, the application is deemed approved; and limiting the number of applications that may be submitted to not more than 10 during any 30-day period.

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Requires the State Highway Administration to approve, deny, or return speed monitoring system applications within 120 days of receipt. Deems an application approved if the Administration fails to act within the 120-day timeframe. Applies to county requests to operate speed monitoring systems on State highways within municipal corporations. Prohibits a program administrator or contractor from submitting more than 10 applications during any 30-day period. Requires contractors to consult with the program administrator before and after submitting an application.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Maryland counties, municipal corporations, local program administrators, and speed monitoring system contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact. The State Highway Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources because internal processes already conform to the 120-day timeframe. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Highway Administration approve, deny, or return an application for the use of a speed monitoring system within 120 days of receipt, deems applications approved if the deadline is missed, and enforces application submission limits.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, the Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state highway network, capital projects, and modal administration operations impacted by the statutory application timelines.

Synopsis: Requiring a landlord to provide air-conditioning to residential rental units in apartment buildings with 10 or more individual dwelling units in a certain manner beginning June 1, 2026, for newly constructed residential rental units and beginning October 1, 2026, for residential rental units that undergo renovation that includes the replacement or substantial upgrade of electrical systems or heating systems; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Residential Rental Apartments - Air-Conditioning Requirement
bill_summary: Requires landlords of residential rental apartment buildings with 10 or more dwelling units to provide air-conditioning. Mandates landlords maintain unit temperatures at or below 80 degrees Fahrenheit from June 1 through September 30. Applies starting June 1, 2026, to newly constructed units and units previously equipped or leased with air-conditioning. Requires compliance beginning October 1, 2026, for units undergoing substantial electrical or heating system renovations. Exempts National Register historic properties and specified Housing Authority of Baltimore City developments. Preempts local laws and regulations that impose inconsistent air-conditioning requirements.
responsible_party: Judiciary; local code enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Tenants and landlords of residential rental apartment buildings with 10 or more dwelling units, including public housing authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Local government expenditures may increase, potentially significantly, for jurisdictions and local housing authorities that own or operate residential rental apartment buildings or experience increased code enforcement demand.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development is the state's principal agency for housing policy, standards, and rental housing programs. While the bill establishes statutory requirements under the Real Property Article enforced largely at the local level or through court proceedings, the department was consulted as an information source and monitors statewide rental housing standards.

The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the judicial branch administration. Landlord-tenant disputes, lease breaches, and habitability issues arising under Real Property Article statutory requirements are adjudicated within the state court system (primarily the District Court).

The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection and fair housing laws, provides legal guidance regarding tenant-landlord regulations, and served as an information source during the evaluation of the bill.

Synopsis: Altering certain alcoholic beverages license fee refund requirements to allow for certain members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service to be eligible for a refund of a portion of the license fee; etc.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - License Fee Refund Requirements - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for refunds of unearned alcoholic beverages license fees upon license surrender. Requires a refund when a license holder volunteers for or is called into the uniformed services. Replaces statutory references to the armed forces of the United States with the uniformed services. Extends refund eligibility to members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service. Applies the refund requirement to both State-issued and locally issued alcoholic beverages licenses. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; local alcoholic beverages licensing boards
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders who volunteer for or are called into the uniformed services, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller's office is responsible for collecting state revenues, administering fee payments and refunds, and historically oversees aspects of alcohol regulation and state revenue administration impacted by changes to license fee refund eligibility.

The bill expands eligibility for alcoholic beverage license fee refunds to individuals entering the uniformed services (including NOAA and the Public Health Service). The Department of Veterans & Military Families advocates for and assists service members and was an official information source on the legislation.

Synopsis: Specifying that, for purposes of earnings withholdings, the amount deducted from the obligor's earnings may not exceed 35% of the obligor's disposable earnings if the obligor's individual income for the current year does not exceed 250% of the federal poverty guidelines for a family of one; and authorizing an employee to contest the amount of an earnings withholding order based on certain limits.
Title: Child Support - Earnings Withholdings Limits
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 868

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Limits the amount an employer may deduct from an obligor's earnings under a child support earnings withholding order or notice. Caps deductions at 35 percent of the obligor's disposable earnings under specified individual income conditions. Applies this limit when the obligor's individual income does not exceed 250 percent of federal poverty guidelines for a family of one. Excludes obligors determined to be voluntarily impoverished at the time of the most recent court order. Authorizes employees to administratively contest an earnings withholding that exceeds these statutory limits. Directs the Child Support Administration to investigate timely contest requests within 15 days.
responsible_party: Child Support Administration, Department of Human Services; Office of Administrative Hearings
stakeholders: Low-income child support obligors, employers subject to earnings withholding orders, and child support recipients
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Human Services increase by $618,840 in FY 2029 ($210,406 general funds and $408,434 federal funds) for system programming enhancements, offset by $408,434 in federal matching revenues. Ongoing operational expenditures increase by $59,520 annually thereafter ($20,237 general funds and $39,283 federal funds). A potential reduction in overall child support collections may impact federal performance incentive payments by an indeterminate amount.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Child Support Administration is a division of the Department of Human Services. DHS is the primary agency responsible for administering child support services, updating the Child Support Management System (CSMS) to reflect withholding limits, investigating employee contests, and issuing relevant notices.

The bill explicitly designates the Office of Administrative Hearings as the appeals body for obligor employees contesting child support earnings withholding determinations made by the Child Support Administration.
Child support earnings withholding orders stem from court orders, and the judiciary handles underlying child support cases, voluntary impoverishment findings, and judicial contests.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and representation to the Department of Human Services' Child Support Administration and represents the agency in administrative challenges and enforcement actions.

Synopsis: Establishing that the holder of a Maryland Golden Age Pass is entitled to free day-use entry at certain State parks and is authorized to launch a boat at any State park without paying a boat launch fee; altering the days of the week on which the holder of a Maryland Golden Age Pass may camp overnight in a State park at a discounted fee; and establishing that the free day-use entry applies to everyone in the vehicle with the holder of a Maryland Golden Age Pass under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: Entitles Maryland Golden Age Pass holders to free day-use entry at any State park charging service fees. Extends this free day-use entry to everyone in the vehicle when a per-vehicle fee applies. Authorizes pass holders to launch a boat at any State park without paying a boat launch fee. Expands half-price overnight camping privileges to apply Sunday through Thursday, excluding holidays.
responsible_party: Maryland Park Service

bill_summary: Requires petition signature pages and ballot questions to include plain language summaries and statements explaining voting outcomes. Prohibits the use of passive voice, legal jargon, and double negatives in required petition and ballot statements. Advances the deadline for officials to prepare and certify ballot questions to July 1 before a general election. Requires the State Board of Elections to hold a 15-day public comment period for submitted ballot question information. Mandates that election boards publicly post the full text of specified ballot questions 90 days before the election.

SBE must establish plain language guidelines prohibiting passive voice and legal jargon for petition summaries, administer a 15-day public comment period for submitted ballot questions, and post complete texts and links to applicable legislation online for at least 90 days before the general election.

The bill directly alters statutory deadlines and responsibilities for the Secretary of State, requiring the office to prepare and certify statewide ballot questions and petitioned referenda by July 1 prior to the general election, adhere to new plain language standards, review public comments received during the 15-day comment window, and submit the certified plain text to SBE.

Covers certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, and independent outpatient providers. stakeholders: certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, independent outpatient providers, direct care staff, and individuals receiving community-based behavioral health services
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $391,974 in FY 2027 ($181,699 in general funds for MDH and $210,275 in special funds for MHCC) and by $356,100 in FY 2028 for contractual staff, data analysis, and actuarial services. The bill establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Commission, requires the Commission to staff the workgroup and assist MDH with the rate-setting study, and mandates that the Commission submit interim and annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly, resulting in notable special fund expenditures.

Mandates periodic status reports to each county board and local governing body on requested school projects.

stakeholders: local boards of education; local governing bodies; Maryland public school students
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is largely procedural and has no direct State or local fiscal impact, though administrative changes may allow the Interagency Commission on School Construction to utilize existing resources more efficiently.

responsible_party: Maryland Port Administration
stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Delegation to the General Assembly and Anne Arundel County government
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Port Administration can handle notifications using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues. Local finances and operations in Anne Arundel County are not materially affected.

The Maryland Port Administration is a modal administration under the Department of Transportation, which oversees its operational policies and land acquisition activities.

Requires these questions to address motorcycle visibility, proper lane positioning, safe following distances, and crash prevention. Authorizes the Administration to include any other motorcycle safety topic it considers relevant. Applies to examinations administered for an original driver's license or a higher license class.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: applicants for Maryland driver's licenses; motorcyclists in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) include at least one question on motorcycle safety awareness on the driver skills examination and establish a question pool containing at least five motorcycle safety awareness questions.
As the parent department overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT is directly impacted by changes to driver licensing requirements and statewide transportation safety education.

bill_summary: Prohibits counterfeiting a lease of real property or rental agreement relating to real property with intent to defraud. Prohibits knowingly possessing a counterfeit lease of real property or rental agreement relating to real property with fraudulent intent. Punishes counterfeiting these documents as a felony subject to 10 years imprisonment, a $1,000 fine, or both. Punishes possessing these counterfeit documents as a misdemeanor subject to three years imprisonment, a $1,000 fine, or both. fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State and local revenues from fines and minimal increase in State and local expenditures for incarceration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

The bill expands criminal offenses adjudicated in the State's District Court and circuit courts, which are operationally supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

bill_summary: Establishes an enforcement process for Maryland residents whose motor vehicles are improperly registered in another jurisdiction. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue a warning allowing owners 60 days to register or show an exemption. Assesses a civil fine of $7 per day for up to 60 days against noncompliant motor vehicles. Authorizes county attorneys to initiate civil actions in rem to immobilize persistently noncompliant vehicles through impoundment or booting. Prohibits title service agents from selling, offering, advertising, or facilitating out-of-state vehicle registrations to State residents. Authorizes reciprocal enforcement agreements with other jurisdictions for automated traffic enforcement systems.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Maryland residents with out-of-state registered vehicles, title service agents, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $379,400 in FY 2027 to hire five customer service agents and cover operating costs, rising to $481,700 by FY 2031. Special fund revenues increase significantly beginning in FY 2027, including an estimated $15.4 million initially from registration fees, titling fees, emissions testing, and civil fines, with ongoing annual revenues around $6.2 million. Local government revenues increase from higher highway user revenue distributions and improved collection of unpaid automated traffic citations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with issuing compliance warnings and civil fines, taking possession of improper out-of-state plates, negotiating reciprocal automated enforcement agreements, administering titling tax exemptions, and licensing title service agents.

As the parent department of MVA and SHA, MDOT is significantly impacted fiscally, with the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) incurring hundreds of thousands in operating expenditures and realizing millions of dollars in increased registration and fee revenues.
SHA operates automated traffic speed and enforcement systems on state roadways and stands to benefit from reciprocal enforcement agreements with other jurisdictions to collect outstanding citations.
MDTA operates automated enforcement systems on toll facilities and may receive nonbudgeted citation revenues collected through the new reciprocal enforcement agreements.
The District Court adjudicates contested automated traffic citations and county attorneys may bring civil in rem actions in court against noncompliant vehicles.
MSP enforces vehicle and traffic laws statewide, coordinates on automated enforcement, and was consulted on the implementation of vehicle registration enforcement measures.

The Maryland Department of Aging has a designated seat on the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board to ensure nonemergency community referral and automated 3-1-1 systems adequately serve older adults.

Synopsis: Requiring and authorizing the State Administrator of Elections to take certain actions if the State Administrator receives a credible report that election misinformation or election disinformation, including a deepfake, has been or is being communicated, disseminated, or distributed; requiring the Administrator to publicly communicate correct information; prohibiting a person from knowingly or with reckless disregard creating, using, or disseminating a deepfake to produce materially false information; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits creating, using, or disseminating deepfakes knowingly or with reckless disregard to produce materially false election-related information. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to a $5,000 fine, five years imprisonment, or both for violations. Requires the State Administrator of Elections to distribute accurate information upon receiving credible reports of election misinformation or disinformation. Authorizes the State Administrator to seek injunctions against online platforms and issue subpoenas for dissemination records. Authorizes the State Board of Elections to file civil actions to recover correction costs, damages, and attorney's fees. Exempts satire, parody, bona fide news broadcasts, and interactive computer services protected under federal law.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; State Administrator of Elections
stakeholders: voters; political candidates; political action committees; individuals and entities communicating election information; online platforms and broadcasters
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund and State general fund revenues may increase annually beginning in fiscal 2027 from criminal penalties and civil damages, but the amounts cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Administrator of Elections and the State Board of Elections with receiving reports, issuing corrective information, seeking court injunctions against online platforms, issuing subpoenas, and initiating civil actions to recover costs.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes election law violations in Maryland, receives referrals of election misinformation/disinformation from the State Board of Elections portal, and enforces criminal election fraud provisions.
The Maryland Judiciary will handle civil actions, injunction requests, subpoena processes, and criminal proceedings authorized and created under the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Board of Elections, and may represent the State in legal actions, court injunctions, and constitutional defenses of the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal misdemeanor penalty with up to 5 years imprisonment for the unlawful creation, use, or dissemination of deepfakes, which may require representation of indigent defendants by the Public Defender.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a misdemeanor offense subject to imprisonment of up to 5 years, potentially impacting state correctional facilities and parole and probation supervision.

The Comptroller is responsible for administering the state income tax system, receiving tax credit certificates from qualifying taxpayers claiming the credit, and coordinating with MDEM regarding issued certificates.
MDEM is statutorily required to submit a report on the tax credit's usage and vesting of 9-1-1 specialists to the Governor by December 1, 2028.

The bill directly authorizes units within the Maryland Department of Labor to include notations indicating veteran status on public profiles of licensees.

Title: Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund - Eligible Companions
bill_summary: Expands the purpose of the Individuals With Disabilities and Service–Disabled Veterans Boating Fund. Adds water-dependent recreational opportunities for eligible companions of individuals with disabilities or service-disabled veterans. Defines an eligible companion as an accompanying family member or direct support professional of a participant. Authorizes the Department of Disabilities to provide grants of up to $40,000 per fiscal year including companions. Maintains existing nonprofit eligibility requirements for organizations receiving fund grants.
responsible_party: Department of Disabilities
stakeholders: individuals with disabilities, service-disabled veterans, accompanying family members, direct support professionals, and qualified nonprofit boating organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The expansion is technical in nature and does not directly alter governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Disabilities is the primary administering agency of the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund, responsible for awarding grants and managing fund operations.

The bill directly impacts recreation and support services for service-disabled veterans and their family members or companions, an area aligned with the department's mission to support veterans and military families.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund separately.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily required to account for the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund.

bill_summary: Expands certain state legal protections and benefits to apply to all members of the uniformed services. Exempts uniformed services members on official leave from trout stamp requirements while angling in Maryland. Extends expedited tenant holding over repossession remedies to landlords who are active service members. Alters the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to include fees from certain non-combat uniformed services license plates. Consolidates the statutory definition of a military protection order within the State Government Article.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families; Maryland Department of Transportation; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Members of the uniformed services, including the U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps and NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps; veterans; residential landlords and tenants; Maryland trout anglers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Department of Natural Resources may decrease by up to $4,400 annually due to newly eligible individuals qualifying for trout stamp exemptions. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the composition of the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund under the State Government Article, which is overseen and administered within the department to support veterans and military personnel.

The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to expand the trout stamp exemption to all uniformed services on leave, which has a direct operational and small fiscal impact on DNR's special fund licensing revenues.

The bill amends the Real Property Article regarding expedited District Court procedures for tenant holding over actions involving active service members, as well as cross-references relating to military protection orders under Courts and Judicial Proceedings and Family Law.
The bill amends the Transportation Article concerning federal facilities and references vehicle registration plate fees designated for the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund administered through MDOT/MVA.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding eligibility criteria for individuals who withdrew from high school to enlist in military service to apply for a high school diploma.
As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the agency is impacted by statutes standardizing definitions and provisions affecting service members and the National Guard.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from possessing more than 100 images of certain child pornography or possessing or viewing images of certain child pornography depicting a minor or an individual indistinguishable from an actual and identifiable child under the age of 13 years; providing that a violation of the Act is a felony and on conviction a violator is subject to imprisonment not exceeding 10 years; and providing that a sentence under the Act may be separate from and consecutive to or concurrent with a sentence imposed for certain other crimes.
Title: Criminal Law - Child Pornography - Prohibitions and Penalties

bill_summary: Establishes felony penalties for child pornography offenses involving 100 or more images or children under age 13. Defines each still visual representation as one image and each video depiction as 20 images. Prohibits possessing, distributing, or viewing qualifying depictions of a child younger than age 13. Prohibits possessing with intent to distribute, distributing, or possessing 100 or more qualifying depictions. Subjects violators to imprisonment not exceeding 10 years. Authorizes courts to impose sentences consecutive to or concurrent with other convictions based on the same act.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Judiciary
stakeholders: Individuals prosecuted for child pornography offenses, state and local law enforcement agencies, state prosecutors, and victims of child sexual abuse
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to the bill's incarceration penalties. Local revenues and expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new felony offenses for child pornography violations involving 100 or more images or depictions of minors under age 13, carrying sentences of up to 10 years imprisonment, which directly impacts DPSCS correctional facility intake, bed days, and expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new felony prohibitions and severe penalties for certain child pornography offenses, requiring legal representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent individuals charged under these provisions.
The bill creates new statutory felony charges and sentencing structures, impacting trial court caseloads, hearings, and judicial administration across the state court system.

As the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for criminal investigations, MSP investigates internet crimes against children, computer-facilitated crimes, and violations of state child pornography statutes.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals resulting from convictions under Maryland's criminal code, including appeals stemming from these new felony offenses.

bill_summary: Transfers the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program and Fund from the Maryland Energy Administration to the Maryland Clean Energy Center. Requires the Center to manage the Program, hold the Fund, and invest its money. Repeals the authority of the Maryland Energy Administration to adopt regulations implementing the Program. Limits annual reporting on Strategic Energy Investment Fund receipts and disbursements to amounts exceeding $10,000. Alters reporting to require estimates of greenhouse gas emissions reductions instead of electricity savings.
responsible_party: Maryland Clean Energy Center; Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Eligible businesses, nonprofit organizations, local jurisdictions, and State agencies seeking energy conservation loans, as well as participating financial institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: Net State fiscal impact is $0. In fiscal 2027, the transfer of the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund balance and operations increases Maryland Energy Administration special fund expenditures by $9.0 million and decreases special fund revenues by $947,700, while Maryland Clean Energy Center nonbudgeted revenues increase by $12.3 million and nonbudgeted expenditures increase by $2.4 million. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program and the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund to MCEC, requiring the Center to manage the program, hold and invest the fund, and provide loans.

This departmental bill transfers MEA's Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program and associated special fund to MCEC, repeals MEA's regulatory authority over the program, and alters MEA's annual reporting requirements for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF).

The bill removes the statutory responsibility of the State Treasurer to hold, invest, and reinvest the moneys of the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund, shifting custody and investment responsibilities to MCEC.
The bill repeals the requirement that the Comptroller account for the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund as the fund is transferred out of the State Treasury to MCEC.

Synopsis: Establishing that engaging in sexual contact with another without the consent of the other in connection with a first-, second-, or third- degree burglary constitutes sexual offense in the third degree; and altering the definitions of "tier I sex offender", "tier II sex offender", and "tier III sex offender" applicable to provisions relating to sex offender registration to include certain acts constituting sexual offense in the third degree.
Title: Criminal Law - Third-Degree Sexual Offense - Burglary

bill_summary: Establishes nonconsensual sexual contact committed in connection with a first-, second-, or third-degree burglary as third-degree sexual offense. Subjects convicted individuals to felony penalties including imprisonment for up to 10 years. Classifies convicted individuals as Tier I sex offenders if the victim is not a minor. Designates offenders as Tier II sex offenders if the victim is a minor at least 13 years old. Classifies offenders as Tier III sex offenders if the victim is a minor under 13 years old. Applies these provisions prospectively to offenses committed on or after October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of sexual offenses in connection with first-, second-, or third-degree burglaries; victims of nonconsensual sexual offenses; state correctional facilities; local law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State expenditures from enhanced incarceration penalties and sex offender registration classifications. Potential minimal decrease in local revenues from fewer fines imposed in circuit court cases. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands third-degree sexual offense (a felony carrying up to 10 years imprisonment) and alters sex offender registry tiers. DPSCS operates the state correctional facilities housing individuals serving sentences over 18 months and oversees supervision and the sex offender registry.
Circuit courts across the state will hear cases involving the reclassified felony offenses, sex offender designations, and sentencing under the bill's amended statutes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency provides legal defense for indigent individuals charged with newly expanded felony third-degree sexual offenses and subject to sex offender registry tier enhancements.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP investigates felony sexual offenses and burglaries, and serves as the registering law enforcement entity for sex offenders in many Maryland jurisdictions.
The OAG represents the State of Maryland in all criminal appeals resulting from convictions under the revised third-degree sexual offense and sex offender registration statutes.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain persons to bring an action when the owner of a property that includes a cemetery proposes a sale, transfer, or alternate use of all or part of a certain cemetery; requiring a court to take certain actions under certain circumstances; authorizing a governmental unit to acquire property on which an abandoned cemetery is located under certain circumstances for purposes of transferring ownership of the abandoned cemetery to a descendant community, veterans, or nonprofit organization; etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Cemeteries and Abandoned Cemeteries - Sale, Transfer, or Government Acquisition and Disposition

bill_summary: Prohibits cemetery owners from selling or transferring a cemetery without approval from the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight. Requires owners seeking approval to submit an application, complete a preservation plan, and provide specified public notice. Grants standing to descendants, descendant community organizations, and other interested parties to challenge sale decisions in court. Directs courts reviewing disputes to allow, prohibit, or order alternative dispositions for proposed cemetery sales or transfers. Authorizes the State, counties, and municipalities to acquire abandoned cemeteries for transfer to qualifying descendant, veterans, or nonprofit organizations.
responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight
stakeholders: cemetery owners, registered cemeterians, permit holders, descendants of interred individuals, descendant community organizations, veterans organizations, and nonprofit cemetery preservation organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations are not materially affected; the Office of Cemetery Oversight and the Judiciary can likely implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Cemetery Oversight is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight is the primary official tasked with approving cemetery sales and transfers, reviewing preservation plans, considering public comments, and facilitating reinterments.

The bill establishes legal standing and detailed procedures for circuit courts to adjudicate actions regarding cemetery sales, transfers, alternative uses, and disposition of abandoned cemeteries within a mandatory six-month timeframe.
The bill explicitly exempts property acquired by the Department of Transportation that is necessary for a public project from the bill's cemetery sale and transfer approval requirements.

The Maryland Historical Trust, a division within the Department of Planning, is referenced in statutory provisions determining interested persons for burial sites when local advisory boards are absent, and the department contributed to the fiscal review.

bill_summary: Authorizes active service members and their spouses relocating to Maryland under military orders to practice under out-of-state licenses. Requires qualifying applicants to submit proof of orders, an affidavit of good standing, and a marriage certificate if applicable. Allows licensing authorities to issue temporary licenses if applications cannot be processed within 30 days. Prohibits licensing authorities from requiring a separate State license within the same discipline and scope of practice. Repeals the one-year post-discharge time limit defining an eligible veteran for expedited occupational licensing. Authorizes each licensing authority to adopt implementing regulations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Insurance Administration; Public Service Commission; Department of State Police; Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Active service members and military spouses relocating to Maryland; military veterans seeking expedited occupational licensing; State occupational and professional licensing boards; Maryland employers in licensed professions
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $107,900 in FY 2027 ($80,100 general funds, $27,800 special funds) for software programming updates and personnel across multiple agencies. Future annual general fund expenditures range between $43,600 and $50,300 through FY 2031. General and special fund revenues decrease indeterminately beginning in FY 2027 due to reduced licensing fee collections. Local government revenues from clerk-issued business licenses experience an indeterminate minimal decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends licensing requirements across dozens of occupational and professional boards housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, including electricians, plumbers, accountants, architects, cosmetologists, home improvement contractors, and financial regulators. MD Labor expects IT programming costs and potential special fund revenue losses.

The bill directly impacts the numerous health occupations licensing boards and MDH departmental licensing (such as medical laboratories and tissue banks), requiring them to authorize qualifying active service members and spouses to practice and adjust expedited licensing procedures.

MSDE is directly required to alter its teacher and school counselor licensure processes and expand expedited licensing for military service members and spouses, incurring fiscal impacts for system modifications and administrative staffing.

The bill alters licensing and certification requirements for veterinarians, pesticide applicators, nutrient management consultants, and milk haulers, requiring software updates and causing minimal revenue reductions for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners.

MDE and its affiliated boards (such as well drillers, waterworks operators, marine contractors, and on-site wastewater professionals) must authorize qualifying military personnel and spouses to operate under out-of-state credentials.

Clerks of the Circuit Court issue several business licenses affected by the bill (such as peddlers and traders), and the Judiciary requires general fund expenditures in FY 2027 to update its e-licensing software.

MSP certifies private detectives, security guards, security systems technicians, and vehicle inspection mechanics, all of which are subject to the bill's military license recognition and examination exemption provisions.
MVA issues professional licenses for vehicle salesmen, automotive dismantlers, title service agents, and driving instructors, which are subject to the bill's military license recognition exemptions.
MIA licenses insurance producers, advisers, public adjusters, and bail bondsmen, which are subject to the bill's authorization framework for military service members and spouses.
The PSC licenses energy salespersons and vendors and recognizes master plumber/gasfitter reciprocity, all of which are amended by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates sports wagering and video lottery terminal personnel and operators, which are amended to accommodate the bill's out-of-state license recognition for service members and spouses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS and the EMS Board oversee the licensing and certification of EMS providers, which are specifically amended under the bill.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which regulates several commercial and vehicle-related professions impacted by the bill.
DNR licenses taxidermists and tree experts, both of which are amended to accommodate military personnel and spouses licensed in other states.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS licenses private home detention monitoring agencies, which are subject to the out-of-state licensing recognition provisions in the bill.
WCC oversees the registration of rehabilitation counselors and vocational evaluators under the Labor and Employment Article, which is amended to exempt authorized military personnel and spouses.
The Comptroller issues transient vendor licenses under the Business Regulation Article, which are exempted for eligible military service members and spouses.
The bill requires service providers to provide notice of rights that are posted on the Maryland National Guard's website in connection with military contract termination protections under the SCRA.
DVMF advocates for active-duty service members, veterans, and military spouses in navigating state benefits and services, aligning directly with the bill's civil relief and licensing protections.

Synopsis: Repealing a provision of law authorizing a person holding a certain license relating to cigarettes or other tobacco products to manufacture, distribute, or sell electronic smoking devices in the same capacity as a person holding a certain license relating to electronic smoking devices; exempting the holder of a certain license who is an applicant for a license to act as an electronic smoking devices retailer or vape shop vendor from the requirement to pay an additional license fee for the license; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals authorization for cigarette and other tobacco product licensees to manufacture, distribute, or sell electronic smoking devices under existing licenses. Requires these licensees to obtain a separate electronic smoking devices license to conduct those activities. Exempts certain cigarette and other tobacco product licensees applying as retailers or vape shop vendors from additional license fees. Allows existing licensees on September 30, 2026, to operate under their current licenses until expiration. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Clerks of the Circuit Court
stakeholders: Cigarette and other tobacco products licensees, electronic smoking device manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, and vape shop vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by up to $25,100 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 from electronic smoking device license fees. Additional administrative duties can be absorbed with existing resources by the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission and local circuit court clerks.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues and is statutorily involved in tobacco industry regulation and enforcement, making the changes to tobacco and electronic smoking device licensing requirements relevant to its administrative functions.

Clerks of the circuit courts, which are part of the Maryland Judicial Branch supported by the AOC, issue county retail licenses for tobacco products and electronic smoking devices and will absorb the administrative workload of issuing separate electronic smoking device retail licenses.

MDH oversees public health initiatives regarding tobacco and youth vaping prevention and is funded in part by retail tobacco licensing fees to enforce laws prohibiting the sale of tobacco products and electronic smoking devices to individuals under 21.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the imposition or application of a method for electing the governing body of a county or municipal corporation that impairs the ability of members of a protected class to elect candidates of the members' choice or influence the outcome of an election by diluting or abridging the rights of voters who are members of a protected class; authorizing the Attorney General and any other person to bring a certain action in the county where the violation allegedly occurred for injunctive relief, damages, or other relief; etc.
