bill_summary: Prohibits county and municipal governing body election methods that impair protected classes from electing candidates of their choice. Applies to protected classes defined by race, color, or language minority groups. Authorizes the Office of the Attorney General and any person to file civil enforcement actions. Empowers courts to order tailored remedies, grant preliminary relief, and award reasonable attorney's fees to prevailing plaintiffs. Excludes statewide elections from its requirements.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Voters belonging to race, color, or language minority groups; county and municipal governing bodies; local election candidates in Maryland counties and municipalities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase to the extent the Office of the Attorney General pursues enforcement actions; the office estimated costs of $242,704 in fiscal 2027 for legal personnel and expert witness fees, though the overall extent of enforcement is indeterminate. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) to bring civil enforcement actions against counties or municipal corporations for voting rights violations, and the fiscal note outlines potential general fund expenditures for OAG personnel and expert witness fees.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action for voting rights violations in local elections, establishing specific evidentiary standards, preliminary relief procedures, and remedial powers for the Maryland court system.

The bill amends the Election Law Article to regulate local election systems and standards for county and municipal governing bodies, which interacts with the State Board of Elections' oversight of election laws and administration.

Synopsis: Altering, for a certain licensing requirement, the definition of "money transmitter" under the Maryland Money Transmission Act to exclude a certain person designated as an agent of a payor for the purpose of the agent's provision of payroll processing services under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: Excludes certain payroll processing agents from the definition of money transmitter under the Maryland Money Transmission Act. Applies to a designated agent operating under a written agreement directing payroll processing on a payor's behalf. Requires the payor to hold the agent out to employees and other payees as providing payroll processing services. Mandates that the payor's obligation to payees is not extinguished if the agent fails to remit funds. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Payroll processing service providers, employers utilizing third-party payroll processors, and employees receiving payroll disbursements
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor decrease by $6,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to lost money transmitter licensing fees. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Maryland Money Transmission Act regulated by the Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department experiences a reduction in special fund licensing revenues of $6,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 as certain payroll processors will no longer require a money transmitter license.

bill_summary: Authorizes a special enforcement officer in Baltimore City to enforce laws regulating cigarettes, other tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices. Authorizes the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to reprimand licensees or suspend or revoke licenses. Requires applicants for initial or renewal county licenses in Baltimore City to obtain a local licensure authorization. Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City to establish an authorization process and charge a fee. Requires Baltimore City to remit 50% of authorization fees to the Comptroller for the Family League of Baltimore City, Inc. Prohibits issuing licensure authorizations to initial applicants between October 1, 2026, and October 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: retailers and vendors of cigarettes, other tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices in Baltimore City; Family League of Baltimore City, Inc.
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in state special fund and general fund revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2027 from licensure authorization request fees. Indeterminate increase in Baltimore City expenditures for local enforcement and administering licensure authorizations. Minimal one-time general fund expenditure increase in fiscal 2027 for Judiciary programming.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Comptroller of Maryland to receive 50% of the licensure authorization request fees collected by Baltimore City and distribute those funds to the Family League of Baltimore City, Inc. The fiscal note also evaluates the Comptroller's administrative capacity and special fund impacts associated with managing these disbursements.

Circuit court clerks, supported administratively and technologically by the Administrative Office of the Courts, issue retail tobacco and electronic smoking device licenses. The bill requires clerks in Baltimore City to verify licensure authorizations before issuing licenses, resulting in required system programming changes and minor general fund expenditure impacts for the Judiciary.

The bill references and amends provisions governing retail tobacco licensing fees, which partially fund Maryland Department of Health enforcement activities prohibiting sales to individuals under 21. It also interfaces with Baltimore City Health Department enforcement officers carrying out tobacco use prevention and cessation oversight.

Receives operational and capital appropriations for central administration, marketing, animal health, plant and pest management, and resource conservation programs.
Serves as the central fiscal and personnel management agency administering statewide expenses, position allotments, budget execution controls, and personnel audits.
Receives appropriations for business attraction, finance programs, marketing, tourism, the Maryland State Arts Council, and workforce grant initiatives.
Receives appropriations for general administration, Telecommunications Access of Maryland, the Developmental Disabilities Council, and boating access funds.

Synopsis: Authorizing the creation of a State Debt in the amount of $1,847,099,000, the proceeds to be used for certain necessary building, construction, demolition, planning, renovation, conversion, replacement, and capital equipment purchases of the State, for acquiring certain real estate in connection therewith, and for grants to certain subdivisions and other organizations for certain development and improvement purposes; etc.
Title: Creation of a State Debt – Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2026, and the Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loans of 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025
bill_summary: Authorizes the creation of State debt through the Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2026 totaling $1,847,099,000. Allocates bond proceeds for public school construction, higher education facilities, community revitalization, healthcare, and environmental infrastructure. Reduces prior State debt authorizations across multiple fiscal years by $97,099,000. Repeals the two-year termination requirement for capital appropriations when matching funds or contracting conditions are unmet. Preauthorizes general obligation bond loans for capital projects in fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Comptroller of Maryland; State Treasurer; Department of General Services; Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Maryland public and nonpublic schools, local governments, higher education institutions, nonprofit organizations, healthcare providers, and Maryland property taxpayers
fiscal_impact_summary: Authorizes $1,847,099,000 in State general obligation bonds for capital projects, offset by $97,099,000 in prior bond loan deauthorizations, resulting in $1,750,000,000 in net new debt. Debt service payments are funded through the State property tax. Local jurisdictions and community organizations receive substantial grant funding for public schools, parks, infrastructure, and community facilities.

bill_summary: Adjusts State appropriations, revenue distributions, and statutory funding mandates to balance the State budget. Caps annual State aid growth to community colleges under the Cade funding formula at 3% for fiscal 2027 through 2029. Decouples State income tax from federal production property depreciation and limits manufacturing bonus depreciation to 20%. Increases county retirement contributions for local educators and librarians by $39.3 million annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Authorizes fund transfers to the General Fund, including $380 million from the Local Income Tax Reserve Account. Requires motor vehicles to be at least 25 years old to register as historic vehicles beginning in fiscal 2028.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Community colleges; four-year public and private higher education institutions; county governments and Baltimore City; local school systems; public school teachers, community college employees, and librarians; taxpayers claiming business depreciation or student loan tax credits; historic vehicle owners; Medicaid recipients; health care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues increase by $808.0 million in FY 2026 and $218.9 million in FY 2027, while General Fund expenditures decrease by $2.1 million in FY 2026 and $651.2 million in FY 2027. Special fund revenues decrease by $3.9 million in FY 2026 and $405.5 million in FY 2027, while special fund expenditures increase by $61.2 million in FY 2026 and decrease by $111.0 million in FY 2027. Local governments face an ongoing annual expenditure increase of $39.3 million beginning in FY 2027 for educator pension costs and direct State aid reductions for community colleges, partly offset by an estimated $29.9 million local revenue increase in FY 2027 from corporate and personal income tax decoupling.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for implementing major tax provisions of the bill, including individual and corporate income tax decoupling modifications, pass-through entity tax calculations, reporting, and stakeholder study, setting interest rates on digital advertising gross revenue tax refunds, delaying centralized collection of local hotel rental taxes, executing transfers from the Local Income Tax Reserve Account ($380 million and $37.3 million), and withholding State Aid for Police Protection from noncompliant jurisdictions.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for executing the State budget and the BRFA provisions. DBM oversees the suspension of surplus transfers to the Revenue Stabilization Account, resolves county disputes concerning noncompliance with immigration enforcement agreements, approves interagency agreements and expedited procurements for the Developmental Disabilities Administration, and processes budget amendments under the bill.

MDH is impacted across multiple divisions: it must establish Assisted Outpatient Treatment (AOT) programs with phased local reimbursements, oversee fund expansions for the Advance Directive Program Fund ($1M), Board of Physicians Fund ($2M), and Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists Fund ($500k), use Cigarette Restitution Fund and Population Health Improvement Fund monies for Medicaid expenses, update Prescription Drug Monitoring Program data retention regulations, and utilize expedited procurement/interagency agreements for DDA.

MHEC is directly responsible for administering the formulas and programs altered by the bill, including the 3% annual growth cap under the Senator John A. Cade Funding Formula for community colleges, freezing Joseph A. Sellinger formula allocations for private colleges, administering the altered caps and reporting for the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit, shifting funding for Title IX legal representation, and absorbing mandate reductions for the police officer and probation agent scholarship and loan repayment programs.

MEA administers the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is significantly altered by transfers of $259 million from the RPS/ACP account and $33 million from the Administration Account to the General Fund, along with statutory expansions of allowable uses of RGGI and ACP revenues for gap financing, clean energy grants, and interagency initiatives.

MDA experiences mandated appropriation reductions for two of its key grant initiatives in FY 2027: the Maryland Healthy Soils Program (reduced from $500,000 to $400,000 for FY 2027 and FY 2028) and the Urban Agriculture Water and Power Infrastructure Grant Fund (reduced from $500,000 to $400,000 in FY 2027).

Commerce administers the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund (expanded to support up to $5M annually in operating costs for DoSEM), the More Jobs for Marylanders Program (where final tax credit certificates are capped at $15M for FY 2027), and the Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund (which transfers $250,000 to MHBE).

MD Labor is impacted by mandated funding reductions for the Public Safety Apprenticeship Program (from $750,000 to $390,000 annually) and the Career Pathways for Health Care Workers Program (from $500,000 to $350,000 annually), and is required to reimburse the Local Reserve Account $37.3 million within two years of FAMLI contributions beginning.

DNR is affected by a $7.01 million transfer from the Waterway Improvement Fund to the General Fund (replaced by GO bonds), receives SEIF funding for the Power Plant Research Program and Environmental Review Program, has its Program Open Space land acquisition balance redefined to include the Heritage Conservation Fund, and repurposes $980,000 in unexpended capital funds for POS land acquisition.

MSDE is impacted by capping Tier II prekindergarten eligibility at 450% of the federal poverty level for FY 2027, eliminating the mandated appropriation for the Lacrosse Opportunities Program, and reducing the State's share of employer pension contributions for local school personnel by $36.2 million annually.

MDE is impacted by a $70 million fund balance transfer from the Bay Restoration Fund to the General Fund (replaced with GO bonds), receives SEIF funding for the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program ($9.485M) and a Senior Climate Advisor, and receives ongoing SEIF support for the Air and Radiation Administration.

MDOT receives $10 million from SEIF to establish leasing processes and safety guidelines for utility transmission infrastructure right-of-way, and the Transportation Trust Fund is fiscally impacted by tax decoupling provisions and historic motor vehicle registration modifications.

MVA is directly responsible for implementing the statutory change to the definition of Class L (historic) vehicles, altering eligibility to vehicles at least 25 years old rather than model year 1999 or earlier, directly impacting registration operations, VEIP exemptions, and fee collections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP's Executive Director is tasked with certifying county and municipal noncompliance with immigration enforcement agreement laws to suspend police aid funding, and the bill authorizes a $2.0 million transfer from GOCPP's Performance Incentive Grant Fund to the General Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI oversees the Maryland Corps Program, and the bill statutory reduces participation targets for the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway in FY 2027 (to 1,100) and FY 2028 (to 1,550), while setting a target of 2,000 for FY 2029.

MIA is required to order the transfer of 90% of excess ending balances from ACA-segregated abortion accounts held by commercial health insurers and HMOs to the Dedicated Purpose Account for health care access grants ($22.2M in FY 2027 and ~$2.5M annually thereafter).

MSA is impacted by an FY 2026 reduction in the mandated lottery distribution to the Racing and Community Development Financing Fund from $17.0M to $13.4M, and the redirection of $27.0M in FY 2027 lottery revenues from the Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund to designated stadium, municipal, and economic development grants.

The bill authorizes SEIF RGGI revenues to be used for resiliency efforts implemented by MDEM, including the Office of Resilience annual report, providing $400,000 in FY 2026 deficiency funding and $1.47 million in FY 2027 funding.

DGS receives a $20 million contingent special fund appropriation from the SEIF alternative compliance payment account in FY 2027 to develop Tier 1 renewable energy projects across State-owned facilities.
DHS is impacted by the prohibition on FY 2027 provider rate increases set by the Interagency Rates Committee for residential child care programs.

DoIT's Information Technology Investment Fund receives $59.3 million in FY 2026 from the Fiscal Responsibility Fund for Major Information Technology Development Projects (MITDPs), and these funds are exempted from year-end reversion requirements.

DJS is authorized to alter the use of $3.0 million in FY 2026 funds from opening the Alfred D. Noyes Children's Center as an adolescent drug treatment center to reopening it as a general facility for children and providing drug treatment elsewhere, and is subject to the IRC provider rate freeze.

MDP's African American Heritage Preservation Grant Fund is expanded to allow funding above the $5 million capital mandate to be awarded as noncapital grants, and SEIF funding is allocated for a Lead Resilience Planner position within the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is impacted by the transfer of $2.0 million from the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund to the General Fund.

MSP Aviation Command's authorization to use the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF) for general operations is extended for three additional years (FY 2027 through FY 2029) at $5.5 million annually.

BPW is impacted by a $1.5 million fund swap utilizing SEIF revenues for the Chesapeake Conservation and Climate Corps Program and maintains oversight regarding expedited procurement reviews authorized for DDA.

PSC is allocated $10 million from SEIF to conduct research into grid-enhancing technologies and advanced transmission technologies, and $5 million for utility grants to modify transmission facilities.

HSCRC is required to examine whether financial assistance to Medicare Advantage plans is needed to maintain viability and whether hospital rates should be adjusted up to $140 million, which impacts the potential reallocation of Population Health Improvement Fund monies to Medicaid.

MEDCO is designated to receive an $18.0 million grant in FY 2027 from redirected State Lottery Fund proceeds for a mixed-use development that includes a soccer stadium at the University of Maryland, College Park.

MSA provides staff support for the Maryland Reparations Commission, for which the bill alters membership, extends reporting deadlines, requires three public hearings, and extends the commission's termination date to June 30, 2029.

SRA administers the Teachers' Retirement System and Teachers' Pension System, where the bill permanently reduces the State's share of annual employer pension contributions by $39.3 million starting in FY 2027, shifting the requirement to local county governments.

IAC is authorized to reallocate $40 million in federal ARPA State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds from FY 2022 and 2023 for school HVAC upgrades to ensure expenditures are completed prior to federal expiration deadlines.

MHBE receives authorization for a $250,000 transfer from the Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund to conduct an outreach campaign and survey on health insurance coverage among child care workers.

USM institutions are impacted by higher education research grants authorized from SEIF ($42M), an $18M grant to MEDCO for a soccer stadium at UMCP, and general fund / CRF adjustments related to the HBCU litigation settlement.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive budget actions, is authorized to execute multiple statutory fund balance transfers to the General Fund totaling hundreds of millions of dollars, and manages executive appointments to the Maryland Reparations Commission.
DHCD receives special funds from SEIF RGGI auction revenues to support personnel and operating expenses for two positions within its Housing and Building Energy program.
MSLA's budget line item for the State share of TRS/TPS employer pension contributions for local library staff is reduced by $722,970 annually, with the cost shifted to local county governments.
GOC participates as a member of the Interagency Rates Committee (IRC), whose rate increases for provider placements are frozen for FY 2027 under the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is specifically named in partnership requirements with the Department of Commerce for awarding grants and loans from the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund.

bill_summary: Prohibits courts and case parties from disclosing court records to nonparties without redacting identifying information of sexual assault or stalking victims. Requires a court to redact identifying information from existing records upon written request of a victim. Permits disclosure of unredacted records if a court finds good cause by clear and convincing evidence. Authorizes health occupations boards to petition for unredacted records to investigate or discipline a defendant for sexual misconduct. Requires the State's Attorney to notify victims of board petitions and explain objection procedures. Prohibits health occupations boards from publicly disclosing records obtained under the petition process.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Offices of the State's Attorney; Health Occupations Boards
stakeholders: Victims of sexual assault, victims of stalking, defendants and respondents in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases, licensed health professionals, and health occupations boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $13,500 in FY 2027 for one-time programming costs. The bill has no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires courts to redact identifying information of sexual assault and stalking victims from court records and filings in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, handle written redaction requests, and adjudicate petitions for record access filed by health occupations boards. The Judiciary incurs direct fiscal and operational impacts for system and software programming.

Health occupations boards, which operate under and are overseen by the Maryland Department of Health to regulate health care professionals, are explicitly authorized by the bill to petition the court for unredacted records to investigate and discipline licensees for sexual misconduct.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As counsel representing indigent individuals in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, Public Defender attorneys are subject to the bill's restrictions prohibiting parties from disclosing or allowing inspection of case records containing victim identifying information to nonparties without required redactions.

bill_summary: Extends the current compensatory education enrollment funding calculation method through fiscal year 2028. Repeals the sunset on using Concentration of Poverty School Grant funds for certain required regulatory programs. Alters initial teacher certification requirements by adding state-approved portfolios and apprenticeship certificate options. Delays the National Board Certification requirement for new licensed principals from July 1, 2029, to July 1, 2034. Repeals the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Skills Standards Advisory Committee while modifying CTE Committee responsibilities. Suspends operation of the Expert Review Team Program for the 2026–2027 school year.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board; Career and Technical Education Committee; Governor's Workforce Development Board; State Board of Education
stakeholders: public school students (including low-income and dual enrollment students), public school teachers and teacher candidates, prospective and current school principals, local boards of education, county governments, and career and technical education providers and employers
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $228.5 million in FY 2027, $311.5 million in FY 2028, $170.4 million in FY 2029, $75.5 million in FY 2030, and $23.7 million in FY 2031, driven primarily by formula aid increases for compensatory education and concentration of poverty grants. Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund special fund interest revenues decrease by $4.7 million in FY 2027 and $3.0 million in FY 2028 due to lower fund balances. Local school system revenues and expenditures increase statewide, and county government appropriations increase by $6.8 million in FY 2027 and $14.5 million in FY 2028 to meet local share requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency impacted by this bill. The legislation alters school finance formulas (compensatory education enrollment calculations and Concentration of Poverty grants), modifies teacher certification and principal career ladder criteria, suspends the Expert Review Team Program for the 2026–2027 school year, redirects associated budget funding, and directs MSDE to collaborate on low-income student counting methodology.

The bill directly modifies the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee, which is an explicit unit within the Governor's Workforce Development Board (GWDB). GWDB collaborates with and approves the CTE Committee's list of priority occupations and comprehensive career pathway information.

The Secretary of Labor is a designated member of the CTE Committee, and the Department staffs the committee. The bill also requires all relevant workforce development programs, including registered apprenticeships approved by MD Labor, to align with the newly established priority occupations list and career pathways.

The Secretary of Higher Education serves on the CTE Committee, and the commission is directly impacted fiscally (requiring an additional education policy analyst position per the fiscal note) to ensure postsecondary CTE and academic programs align with the priority occupations list and career pathway frameworks.

The Secretary of Higher Education serves on the CTE Committee, and the commission is directly impacted fiscally (requiring an additional education policy analyst position per the fiscal note) to ensure postsecondary CTE and academic programs align with the priority occupations list and career pathway frameworks.

DBM is statutorily mandated to be consulted by MSDE and the Accountability and Implementation Board regarding the methodology for counting students from low-income households. The bill also carries massive fiscal ramifications across the state budget and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.

The Secretary of Commerce is designated as an ex officio member of the CTE Committee to align statewide career and technical education frameworks with Maryland's economic development goals and priority workforce needs.

The Governor jointly appoints the chair and industry representatives to the CTE Committee with legislative leaders, receives mandated annual reports on CTE and Expert Review Teams, and receives the final low-income student counting methodology report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the purpose, duties, and membership structure of the CTE Committee and repeals the CTE Skills Standards Advisory Committee.
USM institutions are affected by provisions modifying teacher preparation accreditation and certification pathways, post-CCR dual enrollment limitations, and higher education CTE alignment.

As a public university offering teacher preparation and postsecondary pathways, Morgan State University is affected by altered teacher candidate assessment standards and postsecondary career pathway alignments.

Synopsis: Establishing a certain immunity from liability for a person who donates a pet item or dispenses a donated pet item; and authorizing the State Department of Agriculture to inspect donated commercial feed and establish procedures for handling donated commercial feed.

bill_summary: Establishes civil liability immunity for persons who donate or dispense pet items, including commercial feed. Protects acts or omissions affecting the nature, age, condition, or packaging of good-faith donations. Excludes acts or omissions amounting to gross negligence or willful and wanton misconduct. Covers donations made for use or distribution by nonprofits or units of state or local government. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Agriculture to inspect donated commercial feed and establish handling procedures.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Donors of pet items and commercial feed, nonprofit organizations and government units that distribute pet supplies, pet owners, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $84,600 in fiscal 2027 to fund one agricultural inspector position, vehicle purchase, and operating expenses to inspect donated commercial feed. Expenditures range from $69,700 to $80,000 in subsequent fiscal years. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) to inspect donated commercial feed for wholesomeness and establish procedures for handling donated commercial feed. The fiscal note indicates general fund expenditures for MDA to hire an agricultural inspector to handle inspections.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish a statutory civil liability immunity defense for individuals and entities donating or dispensing pet items, directly affecting civil tort actions filed in the state court system.

Synopsis: Providing that a person who has been convicted of a crime punishable by imprisonment exceeding 1 year and is currently serving the sentence imposed for the conviction, including a term of parole or probation, or has been convicted of a crime involving or relating to perjury, witness intimidation, jury intimidation, or fraud or a related crime is not qualified for jury service.

bill_summary: Alters the circumstances under which an individual convicted of a crime is disqualified from jury service. Disqualifies individuals convicted of crimes punishable by imprisonment exceeding one year who are currently serving their sentence. Specifies that disqualification includes time spent serving a term of parole or probation. Disqualifies individuals convicted of perjury, witness intimidation, jury intimidation, or crimes under Title 8 of the Criminal Law Article. Repeals the provision qualifying individuals with a disqualifying conviction who have received a pardon. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: prospective jurors with criminal convictions, individuals currently serving criminal sentences or on probation/parole, and Maryland circuit courts
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,100 in FY 2027 only for one-time programming costs incurred by the Judiciary to update juror qualification forms. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the operational, administrative, and technological functions of Maryland's judicial branch, which includes managing jury selection and qualification. The agency incurs a direct fiscal impact of $28,100 in FY 2027 to update and reprogram online and printed juror qualification forms to reflect the altered disqualification criteria.

Synopsis: Altering the jurisdiction of the juvenile court by repealing provisions specifying that the juvenile court does not have jurisdiction over a child alleged to have committed any crime punishable by life imprisonment; requiring an intake officer to authorize detention for a child that is at least 16 years old and is accused of certain crimes; altering and establishing certain provisions relating to the detention, confinement, and transportation of certain children; etc.

bill_summary: Expands the exclusive original jurisdiction of the juvenile court over children at least 16 years old. Repeals statutory exclusions for certain handgun violations, firearm violations, and first-degree assault. Requires an intake officer to authorize prehearing detention for specified violent or handgun offenses. Prohibits holding or transporting juveniles within sight or sound of incarcerated adults, effective October 1, 2029. Establishes annual juvenile justice reporting requirements for state agencies and commissions.
responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy; Administrative Office of the Courts; Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices
stakeholders: juveniles accused of delinquent acts or criminal offenses, juvenile intake officers, State's Attorneys, public defenders, and state and local correctional facility staff
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant operational cost savings for the Department of Juvenile Services beginning in fiscal 2027. Local State's Attorneys' offices face potentially significant expenditure increases due to increased juvenile caseloads and shortened timelines. Local detention facility expenditures decrease beginning in fiscal 2030 or earlier. Maryland may avoid the loss of approximately $173,000 annually in federal grant funding by meeting sight-and-sound compliance standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DJS is the primary state department impacted by the bill. The legislation alters juvenile court jurisdiction to keep certain serious charges initially in the juvenile system, mandates that intake officers authorize pre-hearing detention for specified offenses, requires secure juvenile facility placement instead of adult jails, and establishes ongoing statutory reporting requirements for DJS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is explicitly mandated by the bill to submit an annual report detailing youth housed with adult offenders, sight and sound violations, and charges under adult jurisdiction. Additionally, GOCPP administers federal Title II Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act (JJDPA) grant funds, which are directly tied to the sight-and-sound separation and adult jail removal provisions in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is impacted by provisions restricting the detention, confinement, and transport of youth in adult correctional facilities, requiring strict sight and sound separation from incarcerated adults, and potentially seeing minor expenditure reductions due to fewer youth placed in adult state facilities.

The bill directly alters the statutory boundaries between juvenile court and criminal court jurisdiction, waiver procedures, and pre-hearing detention determinations. AOC is also explicitly required to consult with DJS on annual statutory reporting regarding juvenile court petitions, waivers, and transfers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent juveniles facing delinquency and adult criminal charges. The bill alters where cases originate and how waiver hearings proceed, which directly impacts OPD caseload distribution and contractual expenditures for psychological evaluations in transfer/waiver hearings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices is statutorily designated to receive annual reporting from DJS and GOCPP, and is mandated under Section 3 to submit an evaluation report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2027 regarding bill implementation, behavioral incidents, and DJS staffing capacity.

Requires eligible students to meet college and career readiness standards and a minimum grade point average. Requires participating institutions to waive application fees and offer conditional direct admission to eligible applicants. Authorizes participating institutions to establish additional criteria and revoke admission offers under specified circumstances. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission and the State Department of Education to study program implementation by July 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland State Department of Education; University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland public high school seniors; participating public senior higher education institutions (constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland, University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland)
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $100,000 in FY 2027 for MHEC and MSDE to conduct the required study and report. Future implementation costs beginning in FY 2028 are indeterminate but potentially significant, possibly reaching millions of dollars for IT system integration and data sharing. Institutional costs and tuition revenue impacts will depend on voluntary participation by public senior higher education institutions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is a primary implementing agency tasked with administering the direct admission program, establishing eligibility requirements through an MOU with educational partners, receiving eligible student data, generating customized admission lists, and conducting a comprehensive implementation and feasibility study in collaboration with MSDE.

MHEC is a primary implementing agency tasked with administering the direct admission program, establishing eligibility requirements through an MOU with educational partners, receiving eligible student data, generating customized admission lists, and conducting a comprehensive implementation and feasibility study in collaboration with MSDE.

MSDE is a primary implementing partner required to collaborate with MHEC on establishing direct admission eligibility criteria and executing an MOU, establishing a process to annually identify and report eligible students meeting CCR standards and GPA thresholds, and collaborating on the implementation study.

USM is specifically named as a required partner to establish direct admission eligibility standards and enter into the MOU, and its constituent institutions may participate in the direct admission program, waive application fees, and offer conditional admission to qualifying students.

MSU is explicitly mandated to collaborate with MHEC, MSDE, and other public senior institutions to establish eligibility criteria and enter into the program MOU, with the option to participate in offering direct admission and fee waivers to eligible students.

Saint Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly required to participate in establishing eligibility requirements and executing the MOU for the direct admission program, with the option to enroll direct-admission students and waive application fees.

bill_summary: Prohibits manufacturing, selling, offering for sale, purchasing, receiving, or transferring a machine gun convertible pistol beginning January 1, 2027. Expands the definition of rapid fire activators to include pistol converters. Authorizes lawful owners to sell or transfer a machine gun convertible pistol to eligible immediate family members. Requires the Department of State Police to adopt regulations and publish a list of prohibited pistols. Exempts law enforcement personnel, servicing by licensed dealers or gunsmiths, firearm surrenders, and temporary gratuitous exchanges.

Potential minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures from expanded misdemeanor penalty enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of State Police adopt regulations to implement the law, including reviewing firearm models and compiling and publishing the official list of prohibited machine gun convertible pistols, resulting in direct operational impacts and ongoing general fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates and expands criminal misdemeanor and felony penalties involving machine gun convertible pistols and pistol converters, which can lead to incarceration and supervision within State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation and expanded scope of criminal firearm offenses and associated incarceration penalties increases caseloads for public defenders representing indigent defendants charged under these provisions.
The bill establishes new prohibitions and penalties regarding firearm crimes, impacting judicial proceedings and caseload processing within the State court system.

Synopsis: Authorizing a vehicle dealer association and a vehicle manufacturer association to request an administrative hearing to resolve a dispute between entities or seek clarification or interpretation of any provision of applicable law, subject to certain requirements; and prohibiting a manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch that does not have at least one franchised dealer in the State from requesting a hearing.

bill_summary: Authorizes vehicle dealer associations and vehicle manufacturer associations to request an administrative hearing with the Motor Vehicle Administration. Allows associations to request hearings on behalf of themselves, an individual entity, or a group of members. Permits hearings to resolve statutory disputes or seek clarification or interpretation of vehicle licensing and franchise provisions. Restricts dealer association dispute requests to matters germane to their purpose not requiring individual member participation. Excludes disputes involving any manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch lacking at least one franchised dealer in Maryland.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Office of Administrative Hearings
stakeholders: Vehicle dealers, vehicle manufacturers, dealer associations, manufacturer associations, vehicle distributors, and factory branches in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not materially affected; any increase in caseload for the Motor Vehicle Administration, Office of Administrative Hearings, or Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration regulates vehicle dealers and manufacturers in Maryland and is the agency before which dealer and manufacturer associations may request administrative hearings to resolve disputes or seek statutory clarifications.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which oversees vehicle dealer licensing, franchise relations, and the administrative dispute resolution process altered by this bill.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested administrative hearings referred by state agencies, including hearings requested under Title 12 of the Transportation Article involving vehicle dealer and manufacturer disputes.

Decisions and orders resulting from these administrative hearings may be appealed to the Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County within the state judicial system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

bill_summary: Authorizes an aggrieved party or the Office of the Attorney General to sue a covered officer for federal rights deprivations. Defines a covered officer as an armed officer authorized to make arrests for federal code violations. Excludes Maryland law enforcement officers acting under a joint task force primarily enforcing federal law. Permits plaintiffs to seek damages along with declaratory and injunctive relief. Authorizes courts to award reasonable attorney's fees and expert witness fees to a prevailing plaintiff. Requires plaintiffs to file an action within five years after the cause of action accrues.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Covered officers with federal arrest authority, individuals deprived of federal constitutional or statutory rights, and civil litigation attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not anticipated to be affected, though general fund revenues may increase if the Office of the Attorney General is awarded damages, fees, or costs. Local government finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to initiate civil actions against covered officers who deprive individuals of constitutional rights, seeking damages, declaratory, and injunctive relief.

The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund and handles Maryland Tort Claims Act claims; the agency anticipates an operational impact investigating claims and filing motions regarding alleged state officer liability.
The bill establishes a new civil cause of action, standard of relief, and fee-shifting provisions within the state court system, directly affecting judicial administration and caseloads.

fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2027 for one-time IT system updates to the online application portal. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

The bill alters renewal timelines to the holder's birth month, mandates electronic notification schedules, repeals late renewal fees, and requires $100,000 in FY 2027 IT modifications to the department's licensing portal, along with causing an ongoing decrease in fee revenues.

Renames the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Young Readers Grant Program and repeals local matching requirements. Increases the mandatory annual State budget appropriation for the Young Readers Grant Program to $450,000. responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency; State Librarian; State Library Board; Comptroller of Maryland

fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.3 million in FY 2028, rising to $5.2 million in FY 2031 due to phased-in per capita formula increases and a $100,000 annual boost for the Young Readers Grant Program. The bill mandates significant increases in general fund appropriations for the Young Readers Grant Program and per capita aid formulas for public library systems and regional resource centers beginning in FY 2028.

The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $450,000 for the Young Readers Grant Program in the annual State budget bill.

fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2030 to fund the mandated appropriation. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Recovery Residence Grant Program is established and administered within the Maryland Department of Health, which awards competitive grants to certified recovery residences and submits annual reports on the program.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Alters the pay schedule for the full-time chief inspector employed by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County. Increases the position's compensation range from non-represented pay schedule NR-05 to pay schedule NR-12. Requires the Board to fix the chief inspector's annual salary within the updated schedule. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: full-time chief inspector employed by the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Anne Arundel County finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected, as the board funds operations from license fees and retains discretion over specific salary amounts.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that a forensic review board provide notice to certain individuals within a certain time period after issuing a recommendation; establishing the Community Forensic Aftercare Program in the Maryland Department of Health to monitor committed persons on conditional release and individuals with mental illness or an intellectual disability who are required to be monitored; prohibiting a court from issuing an order that authorizes or requires a Community Forensic Aftercare Program to make certain clinical decisions; etc.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - Forensic Review Boards and Community Forensic Aftercare Program

Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Establishes the Community Forensic Aftercare Program within the Maryland Department of Health to monitor individuals on conditional release. Requires the program to establish a community monitoring board to review conditional release and out-of-state travel requests. Prohibits courts from ordering the program to make clinical decisions regarding a committed person's treatment. Authorizes an authorized agent to attend forensic review board and community monitoring board meetings virtually. Repeals the requirement that forensic review boards notify committed persons within ten days of recommending court action.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Committed persons on conditional release, criminal defendants found incompetent to stand trial, behavioral health providers, and public defenders
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $97,000 in fiscal 2028 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire two part-time personnel, with annualized costs in future years. The Office of the Public Defender may incur future costs if advocacy demand exceeds existing capacity. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, which establishes and codifies the Community Forensic Aftercare Program (CFAP) and Community Monitoring Boards within the department, alters requirements for facility forensic review boards, and incurs direct general fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes specific statutory requirements for CFAP and treatment providers to disclose medical and legal records directly to public defenders representing committed individuals within 24 hours without client authorization, permits nonlegal defense staff to serve as authorized agents at board proceedings, and may affect defense social worker staffing and caseloads.

The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by prohibiting courts from issuing orders requiring CFAP to make clinical treatment decisions and establishes specific procedures regarding the receipt of release recommendations and reports of conditional release violations.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to provide legal representation and counsel to MDH during CFAP Community Monitoring Board meetings.

Synopsis: Establishing a consumption-only nonprofit swim club license in Anne Arundel County which authorizes the license holder to allow members of the swim club and their guests to bring beer, wine, and liquor onto the licensed premises for on-premises consumption during designated events; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to issue the license to a nonprofit swim club in Anne Arundel County; and providing for an annual license fee of $100.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Consumption-Only Nonprofit Swim Club License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Establishes a consumption-only nonprofit swim club license in Anne Arundel County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to issue the license to a nonprofit swim club. Authorizes license holders to allow members and guests to bring beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption. Restricts consumption to designated club areas during designated events from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. Limits events to five days per year unless the Board authorizes up to three additional days. Establishes an annual license fee of $100 and a fee of $50 for each additional day.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Nonprofit swim clubs in Anne Arundel County and their members and guests
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2027 from license fees ($100 annually plus $50 per additional day). County expenditures are unaffected. State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this legislation specifically authorizes the local Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners to issue local consumption-only nonprofit swim club licenses with no direct state fiscal impact, it amends the state's Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article under the Comptroller's general regulatory domain.

Synopsis: Prohibiting employers and their agents, representatives, and designees from taking certain actions against an employee or applicant for employment because the employee or applicant takes certain actions regarding employer-sponsored meetings during which the employer communicates the opinion of the employer regarding religious matters or political matters; authorizing an employee to file a certain complaint with the Commissioner of Labor and Industry; etc.
Title: Labor and Employment - Mandatory Meetings on Religious or Political Matters - Employee Attendance and Participation (Maryland Worker Freedom Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits employers from disciplining employees or refusing to hire applicants who decline employer-sponsored religious or political meetings. Authorizes employees to file written complaints with the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within 180 days of an alleged violation. Requires the Commissioner to investigate complaints and attempt informal resolution through mediation. Authorizes civil penalties up to $10,000 for initial violations and up to $25,000 for subsequent violations. Requires employers to post and provide new hires with a model notice developed by the Commissioner. Exempts specified religious organizations, political organizations, educational institutions, nonprofit training programs, and mandatory legal compliance trainings.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry
stakeholders: Maryland employers, employees, and job applicants
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $131,588 in FY 2027 for 1.5 enforcement and legal positions within the Maryland Department of Labor, rising to $173,100 by FY 2031. Civil penalty revenues are not expected to materially affect general fund revenues. State and local government employer expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor is the primary entity charged with implementing and enforcing the Maryland Worker Freedom Act. MD Labor is responsible for receiving complaints, conducting investigations, facilitating mediations, assessing civil penalties, issuing orders, petitioning circuit courts, and publishing required informational posters and notices. The agency requires additional general fund expenditures and staffing to handle this new workload.

The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for providing legal counsel and representation to the Commissioner of Labor and Industry for enforcement actions, orders, and circuit court petitions. The fiscal note explicitly accounts for funding a half-time assistant attorney general position to assist MD Labor in enforcing the bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a research facility or a testing facility from using certain dogs and cats for research or testing purposes; prohibiting a research facility or testing facility from performing devocalization procedures on dogs or cats; prohibiting a testing facility from using traditional animal test methods under certain circumstances; applying certain provisions of law regarding the adoption of dogs and cats used for scientific research purposes to testing facilities; etc.
Title: Research Facilities and Testing Facilities That Use Animals - Prohibitions and Adoption Requirements (Animal Research Modernization and Best Practices Act of 2026)
