bill_summary: Prohibits research facilities and testing facilities from performing devocalization surgeries on dogs or cats or using devocalized dogs or cats. Restricts testing facilities from using traditional animal test methods when regulatory agencies approve alternative methods or grant waivers. Excludes medical research from restrictions on traditional animal testing methods. Requires euthanasia of dogs and cats at covered facilities to follow American Veterinary Medical Association guidelines. Extends adoption placement mandates for dogs and cats no longer needed for research to testing facilities. Mandates annual reporting to the Secretary of Agriculture on animal use and rescue releases beginning in 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Secretary of Agriculture
stakeholders: research facilities, testing facilities using live vertebrate animals, animal rescue organizations, and licensed veterinarians
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement and enforce the requirements using existing resources. State revenues are not expected to be materially affected by penalty fines of up to $1,000 for a first offense and $5,000 for subsequent offenses. Local government finances are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary implementing and regulatory agency for the bill, which amends Title 15 of the Agriculture Article. The Secretary of Agriculture is responsible for collecting annual data reports from research and testing facilities, compiling an anonymized annual report, posting it to the department's website, and enforcing the title's provisions and fines.

Constituent research institutions of the University System of Maryland that conduct research, education, or experimentation using live vertebrate animals are classified as research facilities under the bill. They must adhere to statutory restrictions on devocalization, specific euthanasia protocols for dogs and cats, adoption placement mandates, and annual reporting requirements to the Department of Agriculture.

As an independent public research university, any scientific research or educational programs at Morgan State University utilizing live vertebrate animals are subject to the bill's requirements for research facilities, including prohibitions on devocalization, adherence to AVMA euthanasia guidelines, adoption placement procedures, and annual reporting.

Synopsis: Requiring a custodian to deny inspection of certain records pertaining to a divorce proceeding except under certain circumstances.
Title: Public Information Act - Divorce Records

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires a public record custodian to deny public inspection of records pertaining to a divorce proceeding. Covers divorce applications, submitted financial records, divorce settlement records, and custody orders. Excludes a final decree in a divorce proceeding from the inspection denial. Requires custodians to release the records to a person in interest or their representing lawyer. Mandates disclosure to an applicant authorized under a court order to inspect the record.
responsible_party: Custodians of Public Records
stakeholders: Parties to divorce proceedings, family law attorneys, public record custodians, and members of the public requesting divorce records
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Divorce proceedings, applications, financial statements, divorce settlements, and custody orders are filed with and maintained by the clerks of the circuit courts within the judicial branch. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, operational, and technological oversight of court records and case management systems (such as MDEC) that must implement these restrictions on public inspection.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state entities regarding the Maryland Public Information Act (PIA), maintains the statewide PIA manual, and advises custodians on statutory compliance and exemptions under the General Provisions Article.

The Maryland State Archives is the central repository for historical judicial and government records in Maryland, including transferred court and divorce records, making it a custodian subject to the inspection and disclosure limitations established by this bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an employer from taking certain discriminatory employment actions against a fire and rescue public safety employee based on the employee's use of medical cannabis, subject to certain conditions; and requiring an employer to report an incident of a fire and rescue public safety employee reporting for work while impaired by cannabis to the State Emergency Medical Services Board.
Title: Employment Discrimination - Fire and Rescue Public Safety Employees - Use of Medical Cannabis

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits employers from disciplining, discharging, or discriminating against fire and rescue public safety employees based on medical cannabis written certifications. Protects covered employees who test positive for cannabis components or metabolites while holding a valid written certification. Covers firefighters, emergency medical technicians, cardiac rescue technicians, and paramedics employed by state or local entities. Authorizes employers to prohibit on-duty cannabis use and working while impaired. Requires employers to report employees who report to work impaired by cannabis to the State Emergency Medical Services Board. Exempts employers from requirements that would violate federal law or jeopardize federal benefits.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; State Emergency Medical Services Board
stakeholders: Firefighters, emergency medical technicians, cardiac rescue technicians, and paramedics employed by municipal corporations, counties, the State, the State Airport Authority, or fire control districts, and their public employers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $67,800 in fiscal 2027 for the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights to hire one investigator, with ongoing annualized costs. Indeterminate potential increase in state and local expenditures from employer liability, legal challenges, and policy updates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary enforcement agency for Title 20 employment discrimination laws amended by the bill. The fiscal note explicitly allocates funding for MCCR to hire a civil rights officer to process and investigate anticipated complaints under the new provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that employers report any fire and rescue public safety employee who reports to work impaired by cannabis directly to the State Emergency Medical Services Board, which is the governing body of MIEMSS.

As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employment policies and handles disciplinary and liability impacts for state-employed fire and rescue personnel subject to the bill's anti-discrimination requirements.

The bill specifically applies to fire and rescue public safety employees employed by the State Airport Authority, which includes the fire and rescue operations at BWI Marshall and Martin State airports operated by the MAA.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Maryland Aviation Administration and serves as an employer of fire and rescue personnel operating at state airport facilities covered under the bill.
The bill relies upon the statutory framework, registry, and certification standards established under the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article administered by the MCA.
OAH administrative law judges hear and adjudicate contested employment discrimination cases certified for litigation by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

Synopsis: Establishing an exemption to the population ratio quota for certain Class A (off-sale) and Class D (off-sale) licenses in Anne Arundel County for an application filed on or after January 1, 2023, and approved by the Board of License Commissioners before July 1, 2025.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Population Ratio Quota for Class A (Off-Sale) and Class D (Off-Sale) Licenses - Exemption
bill_summary: Exempts certain alcoholic beverages license applications from the population ratio quota in Anne Arundel County. Applies to Class A (off-sale) and Class D (off-sale) license applications filed on or after January 1, 2023. Limits the exemption to applications approved by the Board of License Commissioners before July 1, 2025. Permits license issuance even if an assessment district exceeds one off-sale license for every 3,500 individuals. Takes effect July 1, 2026, and abrogates December 31, 2028.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Applicants for Class A (off-sale) and Class D (off-sale) alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County whose applications were filed on or after January 1, 2023, and approved before July 1, 2025; Anne Arundel County government
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County revenues increase by $5,160 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to the collection of license fees from three newly issued licenses. County expenditures are not affected, and there is no State fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Human Services to study the potential number of households excluded from automatic standard utility allowance eligibility for the Heat and Eat Program within the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program due to enactment of the federal One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025; and requiring the Department to submit a report of its findings and recommendations, by December 1, 2026, to the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee and the House Appropriations Committee.
Title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program - Heat and Eat Program - Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to study household exclusions from the Heat and Eat Program. Examines exclusions from automatic standard utility allowance eligibility under the federal One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025. Directs the Department to compile historical participation data and calculate benefit reductions across each county. Mandates an evaluation of administrative costs and logistics for verifying individual energy expenses. Requires the Department to report its findings and recommendations to designated legislative committees by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Households participating in or eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and the Heat and Eat Program, particularly households without an elderly or disabled member
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Human Services can complete the required study and report using existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 461 directly mandates that the Department of Human Services (DHS) conduct a study and report recommendations on households affected by changes to the Heat and Eat Program and standard utility allowance eligibility within the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

Synopsis: Providing that during the trial of a criminal case in which a defendant is charged with an assault in the second degree, a certain statement is not excluded by the hearsay rule if the statement is offered against a party that has engaged in, directed, or conspired to commit wrongdoing that was intended to and did procure the unavailability of the declarant of the statement, under certain circumstances.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Admission of Out-of-Court Statements - Assault in the Second Degree
bill_summary: Expands an exception to the hearsay rule to include criminal cases charging assault in the second degree. Permits out-of-court statements when a defendant intentionally procured the declarant's unavailability through wrongdoing. Requires the court to hold a hearing outside the jury's presence before admitting the statement. Requires the court to find by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant procured the unavailability. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Defendants charged with second-degree assault, victims and witnesses in criminal assault proceedings, State's Attorneys, and criminal defense attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands an exception to the hearsay rule to criminal trials involving assault in the second degree, requiring state court judges to hold evidentiary hearings outside the presence of the jury to determine admissibility.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts criminal defense practice by allowing certain out-of-court statements to be admitted against defendants charged with second-degree assault, affecting cases handled by public defenders.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals, which may involve defending trial court rulings on the admissibility of hearsay statements under this expanded statutory exception.

Synopsis: Providing that the creative expression of a criminal defendant or juvenile respondent is not admissible against the defendant or respondent unless the court makes certain findings, subject to a certain exception; and providing that the Act does not preclude the admission of a creative expression in juvenile cases for the purposes of evaluating, recommending, or ordering referral to mental health services or diversion programs.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Evidence - Protecting Artists' Creative Expression (PACE Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits the admission of a defendant's or respondent's creative expression against them in criminal or juvenile proceedings. Requires the court to make specific findings by a preponderance of the evidence before admitting the expression. Requires findings that the creator intended literal meaning and a close nexus exists to the alleged offense. Requires findings that the expression is relevant to a disputed fact and its probative value outweighs prejudicial effect. Authorizes admitting creative expression in juvenile cases to evaluate, recommend, or order mental health services or diversion programs.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Circuit Courts of Maryland
stakeholders: criminal defendants, juvenile respondents, criminal defense attorneys, State's Attorneys, and artists
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes statutory evidentiary standards and required judicial findings for the admissibility of creative expression in criminal and juvenile proceedings, directly impacting state court judges and court operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts defense strategies and motions practice for public defenders representing indigent defendants and juvenile respondents by restricting the admissibility of creative works such as music, poetry, and art.

The bill explicitly governs juvenile proceedings and includes an exception allowing creative expression to be considered for evaluating, recommending, or ordering referrals to mental health services or diversion programs, which fall under the purview of DJS.
The Office of the Attorney General prosecutes certain state criminal matters and represents the State in criminal appeals where evidentiary determinations made under this statute may be challenged.
The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes certain criminal matters and would be bound by these new evidentiary admissibility restrictions when trying criminal cases.

Synopsis: Establishing the Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board to advise the Secretary of Natural Resources on the operation, acquisition, regulation, and general oversight of off-highway recreational vehicle trails and recreation in the State.
Title: Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Forests and Parks -see also- MdNatlCapPkPlnCm; Plants; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board to advise the Secretary of Natural Resources. Directs the Board to advise on the operation, acquisition, regulation, and general oversight of recreational vehicle trails. Specifies the Governor appoints five State residents representing vehicle drivers and motorcycle organizations to staggered terms. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to provide staff and operational support for the Board. Mandates that the Board elect a chair annually and meet at least quarterly.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board
stakeholders: Off-highway recreational vehicle drivers, motorcycle and off-highway vehicle dealers, recreational riding associations, and counties containing state-maintained off-highway vehicle trails
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Natural Resources can provide staff and support using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Off-Highway Recreational Vehicle Recreation Oversight Board to advise the Secretary of Natural Resources on trail operations, acquisitions, regulations, and oversight. The Department of Natural Resources is required to provide staff and support services to the board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent statutory advisory and oversight body within the state executive structure.
The Governor is responsible for appointing all voting members of the newly established board and appointing successors in the event of vacancies.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor by recruiting, vetting, and recommending qualified candidates to fill the newly created gubernatorially appointed positions on the board.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Highway Administration to implement a program of safety corridor speed monitoring systems for use in areas determined to be of high risk to vulnerable road users; and authorizing a local jurisdiction to use speed monitoring systems in safety corridors under certain circumstances.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Speed Monitoring Systems - Safety Corridors (Vulnerable Road User Protection Act of 2026)

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
License Plates -see also- Motor Vehicle Registration
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Highway Administration to establish a speed monitoring system program in designated highway safety corridors. Permits local jurisdictions to deploy speed cameras on State highways within safety corridors under an Administration permit. Applies to vehicles traveling at least 12 miles per hour above the posted speed limit. Establishes escalating civil penalties from $40 up to $425 depending on vehicle speed. Requires citation revenues to cover system administrative costs before distribution to the Transportation Trust Fund. Mandates warning notices instead of citations during the first 30 days of camera operation at new locations.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Comptroller of Maryland; District Court of Maryland; Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers; vulnerable road users, including pedestrians, bicyclists, and highway work zone personnel; local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase potentially by millions of dollars annually beginning in FY 2027 to cover camera implementation and administration. Remaining revenues distribute to the Transportation Trust Fund for highway safety and system preservation. Local government revenues and expenditures increase if local safety corridor camera programs are established under permit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SHA is the primary agency authorized to establish, operate, and regulate the safety corridor speed monitoring system program, permit local jurisdictions to operate cameras on State highways, and receive special fund disbursements to cover program costs and system preservation.
MDOT is the parent department of SHA and MVA. Remaining revenues from civil penalties are distributed to the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) for highway safety and system preservation purposes.

MVA is responsible for enforcing vehicle registration suspensions or refusals to register/transfer registration when violators fail to pay safety corridor speed citations or appear for trial, and places administrative flags on vehicle records.

The District Court of Maryland has exclusive original civil jurisdiction over contested citations, with the Chief Judge tasked with adopting procedures and prescribing uniform citation forms for safety corridor violations.
The Comptroller is statutorily mandated to collect and distribute civil fine revenues generated by State-operated safety corridor speed monitoring systems into a dedicated special fund.

The bill amends the Insurance Article to prohibit insurers from considering safety corridor speed citations for auto insurance reclassification or premium increases, which falls under MIA's regulatory oversight.

Synopsis: Authorizing, beginning January 1, 2027, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide comprehensive coverage for the treatment of obesity; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide notice to Program recipients if the Department elects to provide the comprehensive coverage; authorizing the Department to apply to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services for a State plan amendment authorizing the State to provide comprehensive coverage for the treatment of obesity; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Coverage for the Treatment of Obesity - Authorization
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 866

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide comprehensive coverage for the treatment of obesity beginning January 1, 2027. Defines comprehensive coverage to include intensive behavioral therapy, bariatric surgery, and federal Food and Drug Administration-approved chronic weight management medications. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to apply to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services for a State plan amendment. Requires the Department to notify program recipients if it elects to provide the coverage. Requires the Department to report to specified legislative committees by November 1, 2027, on coverage implementation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients with obesity, healthcare providers, and managed care organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct mandatory fiscal impact because coverage is permissive, and the reporting requirement can be handled with existing budgeted resources. If the Maryland Department of Health elects to implement coverage, Medicaid expenditures could increase by up to $449.4 million annually for anti-obesity medications, with federal fund revenues increasing accordingly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill authorizes MDH to provide comprehensive coverage for the treatment of obesity, apply for a Medicaid State plan amendment with CMS, notify program recipients if coverage is adopted, and submit a report to the General Assembly by November 1, 2027.

Synopsis: Implementing the federal Workforce Pell Grant Program in the State through which Pell Grants may be awarded to students enrolled in a certain short-term program; requiring the Governor, after consultation with certain entities, to determine whether to approve short-term programs as eligible for Pell Grant funds subject to certain requirements; requiring a certain registered apprenticeship program to include certain components in the curriculum; etc.
Title: Higher Education - Workforce Pell Grant Program - Implementation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Implements the federal Workforce Pell Grant Program for short-term programs in the State. Requires the Governor, after consulting with the Governor's Workforce Development Board, to approve eligible short-term programs. Prohibits institutions of postsecondary education from disbursing program funds without state and federal approvals. Mandates minimum completion and job placement rates of 70% for short-term program approval. Prohibits institutions from charging tuition and fees exceeding the maximum available Pell Grant funds. Authorizes application evaluation fees and requires annual reporting to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Office of the Governor; Governor's Workforce Development Board; Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students in short-term workforce programs, public and private institutions of postsecondary education, and employers in high-skill or in-demand industry sectors
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $300,000 in FY 2027 to cover administrative and staffing costs for the Governor's Workforce Development Board and the Maryland Higher Education Commission, with ongoing staffing costs in subsequent years. Indeterminate increase in general fund revenues beginning in FY 2027 from application fees. Indeterminate impact on revenues and expenditures for public institutions of higher education and community colleges that voluntarily seek program approval.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Board to consult with the Governor on program approvals, collect compliance and outcome data from postsecondary institutions, establish application fees, adopt regulations, and submit an annual report to the General Assembly.

The Commission is authorized to collect application fees, verify program compliance, adopt regulations jointly with the Governor's Workforce Development Board, and submit an annual report on the program to the General Assembly.

The Commission is authorized to collect application fees, verify program compliance, adopt regulations jointly with the Governor's Workforce Development Board, and submit an annual report on the program to the General Assembly.

The bill tasks the Governor directly with determining whether short-term educational programs meet statutory and federal criteria for Workforce Pell Grants and requires the Governor to revoke program approvals under certain conditions.

The Department staffs the Governor's Workforce Development Board and oversees the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council, which approves registered apprenticeships referenced in the bill. Additionally, the department receives the contingent general fund appropriation associated with the bill's implementation.

Constituent institutions of the University System that choose to offer short-term workforce training programs will be directly impacted by the application requirements, data reporting mandates, tuition caps, and credit transfer regulations established by the bill.

The bill explicitly provides that a finding by the Attorney General under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act regarding unfair, deceptive, or abusive trade practices related to the program triggers mandatory revocation of an institution's program approval.

As an independent public postsecondary institution, the university is impacted if it seeks Workforce Pell Grant eligibility for short-term workforce programs and must comply with the bill's tuition, transferability, and reporting standards.

As a public institution of postsecondary education, the college is subject to the bill's requirements and operational restrictions should it elect to offer eligible short-term programs funded through Workforce Pell Grants.

Synopsis: Increasing the penalties for stalking to a period of imprisonment of up to 10 years or a fine of up to $10,000 or both if the victim had a protective order in effect against the defendant at the time of the offense or the defendant had previously been convicted of stalking.

bill_summary: Establishes enhanced felony penalties for stalking under specified aggravating circumstances. Applies felony penalties when an interim, temporary, or final protective order was in effect with the victim as petitioner. Extends penalties when an active court order prohibited stalking behavior involving the victim. Applies felony penalties if the offender was previously convicted of stalking in Maryland or another state. Subjects felony offenders to imprisonment not exceeding 10 years, a fine not exceeding $10,000, or both.
responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Victims of stalking, petitioners with protective orders, and individuals charged with or convicted of stalking
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund expenditures from increased prison terms. Potential minimal decrease in State fine revenues as cases shift from District Court to circuit courts due to felony classification, with a corresponding potential minimal increase in local fine revenues. Local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a felony penalty for stalking under specified aggravating circumstances, which shifts cases from the District Court to the circuit courts and impacts judicial caseloads, sentencing proceedings, and court fine revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enhances stalking penalties to a felony with up to 10 years of imprisonment, potentially increasing incarceration lengths and supervision caseloads for the Division of Correction and Division of Parole and Probation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill elevates certain stalking charges from misdemeanors to felonies with increased penalties up to 10 years, directly affecting the defense representation requirements, trial preparation, and caseload for indigent defendants.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating stalking offenses and enforcing protective and court orders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees statewide criminal justice policy and victim services funding, areas relevant to tracking intimate partner violence, protective orders, and stalking deterrence.

The bill establishes a new 90-day special enrollment period (SEP) on the Individual Exchange for individuals and dependents whose providers are terminated from a health plan's panel, requiring MHBE to administer these new enrollment opportunities.

The bill adds a section to the Health - General Article governing health systems and impacts behavioral health provider notifications and continuity of care requirements, areas closely related to MDH's regulatory oversight of health care facilities and public health programs.

DBM oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and was consulted on the legislation, though the bill does not impose direct fiscal impacts or regulatory duties on the department.

Pursuant to Health-General § 19-112, the Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund.

Requires nonprofit partners to adhere to Minority Business Enterprise requirements and submit annual reports on expenditures and outcomes. Mandates that participating nonprofits maximize opportunities for community engagement related to each service opportunity.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of Planning; Maryland Department of Transportation; Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Nonprofit entities partnering on State historic preservation, archaeology, and conservation projects; third-party historic preservation, archaeology, and conservation contractors; certified Minority Business Enterprises
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the procurement exemptions and contract requirements are expected to apply in a limited number of cases. There is no effect on State revenues or local government operations and finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly grants DGS an exemption from standard State procurement law for agreements or partnerships with nonprofits related to historic preservation, archaeology, or conservation, while requiring them to enforce specific subcontracting, reporting, and MBE requirements in those contracts.

The bill directly grants DHCD an exemption from State procurement law when partnering with nonprofits on historic preservation, archaeology, or conservation projects, and obligates the agency to enforce statutory subcontracting and annual reporting requirements.

The bill directly grants the Department of Planning (which houses the Maryland Historical Trust) a procurement exemption for historic preservation, archaeology, and conservation partnerships with nonprofits, subject to new contract clauses and reporting mandates.

As the governing body overseeing State procurement policy and approving written procurement policies and procedures for exempt agencies, BPW is relevant to changes expanding procurement exemptions.

fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Local school system expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 if vendors decline to bid, though school systems may also experience savings through reduced operational and legal risk; reliable estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article to regulate contracting terms and prohibit specific provisions in contracts entered into by Maryland public school systems, which are overseen and guided by the Maryland State Department of Education.

The Interagency Commission on School Construction oversees and funds capital improvement and construction projects for public school systems across Maryland, and its assisted local projects involve contracts governed by these new statutory restrictions.

The bill invalidates provisions requiring binding arbitration or out-of-state venues in public school system contracts, requiring disputes instead to be resolved through courts of proper jurisdiction within Maryland, which may impact state court litigation.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain line-of-duty disability allowance to be paid to a member of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System or the State Police Retirement System who is found to be totally and permanently incapacitated, either mentally or physically, for the further performance of duty, and unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity; and applying the Act prospectively.

bill_summary: Establishes a catastrophic line-of-duty disability allowance for members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and State Police Retirement System. Authorizes the allowance when a line-of-duty accident permanently prevents a member from engaging in any substantial gainful activity. Calculates the benefit as an annuity of accumulated contributions plus a pension equal to 100% of average final compensation. Requires recipients to submit annual federal income tax returns to the State Retirement Agency to maintain eligibility. Reduces the benefit if a recipient works for a participating employer or engages in substantial gainful activity. Mandates annual reporting by the State Retirement Agency to the Joint Committee on Pensions starting November 1, 2028.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and the State Police Retirement System (including Deferred Retirement Option Program participants); participating governmental units
fiscal_impact_summary: Likely no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates, as qualifying catastrophic events are expected to occur rarely. The State Retirement Agency can implement the administrative requirements with existing budgeted resources. No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). The bill tasks the agency with implementing the new line-of-duty catastrophic injury disability benefit, processing annual federal tax returns to verify gainful activity, managing benefit suspensions and restorations, and reporting annually to the Joint Committee on Pensions.

Uniformed members of the Maryland State Police are the sole active participants in the State Police Retirement System (SPRS), which this bill directly amends to establish a 100% average final compensation catastrophic line-of-duty disability retirement benefit.

Raises the maximum age to enter and participate in the Deferred Retirement Option Program from 60 to 62. Authorizes eligible active participants to extend their program participation up to age 62 or seven total years. The agency administers the State Police Retirement System and the DROP program, is responsible for providing election extension forms, and will manage the actuarial and benefit changes resulting from the altered retirement age.

As the state's primary agency for personnel and budget planning, DBM oversees state pension contribution expenditures and long-term fiscal impacts, which will see general fund savings beginning in FY 2028 due to reduced pension liabilities.

The bill references collaboration with the State Archives regarding record retention requirements and guidelines for electronic communications related to credible allegations.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees and enforces consumer protection standards relating to residential real estate transactions and was consulted regarding the bill's legal provisions.

bill_summary: Authorizes a qualified recipient to transfer legal ownership of qualified agricultural property to a limited liability company. Exempts the transfer from Maryland estate tax recapture under specified conditions. Requires the ownership of the limited liability company to consist only of qualified recipients. Requires the qualified agricultural property to be used for farming purposes for at least 10 years after the decedent's death. Directs the Comptroller to adopt regulations to implement the law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's tax collector and administrator of the Maryland estate tax, and the bill explicitly mandates that the Comptroller adopt regulations to implement the provisions governing transfers of qualified agricultural property to limited liability companies without triggering tax recapture.

The Register of Wills oversees the administrative probate of decedents' estates and coordinates with the state on estate and inheritance tax matters, making the estate tax rules on transferred agricultural property relevant to its administration of estates.

The Department of Agriculture supports the economic viability of farming and agribusiness; this legislation facilitates the generational transfer and continued agricultural use of farmland through business entities.

bill_summary: Defines "danger to the life or safety of the individual or of others" under Maryland mental health law. Applies the standard to emergency evaluations and involuntary admissions to facilities or Veterans' Administration hospitals. Requires a substantial risk based on recent and relevant conduct resulting from a mental disorder. Incorporates the individual's current condition and available personal, medical, and psychiatric history. Covers serious bodily harm or inability to provide for basic needs creating substantial risk of harm or death. Excludes inability to provide for basic needs that arises solely from indigence.

stakeholders: individuals with mental disorders facing potential emergency evaluation or involuntary admission, examining health care professionals, law enforcement officers, and psychiatric inpatient facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate general fund expenditure increase for the Judiciary beginning in fiscal 2027 if emergency evaluation petitions increase court and clerical workloads. State revenues are not affected. Operational impacts on the Maryland Department of Health and the Office of the Public Defender are anticipated to be minimal and absorbable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Health - General Article governing mental health law, emergency evaluations, and involuntary admissions to psychiatric facilities, which are directly overseen and administered by MDH.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent individuals in involuntary admission hearings and proceedings affected by the revised definition of 'danger to the life or safety of the individual or of others'.
State police officers are authorized peace officers who may petition for and execute emergency evaluations of individuals believed to present a danger to themselves or others.

fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The Maryland Department of Health can update relevant regulations using existing budgeted resources.

stakeholders: virtual currency kiosk operators, software installers and operators for automated devices, and consumers using virtual currency kiosks
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact. Small businesses operating virtual currency kiosks may incur compliance expenses related to registration requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, which oversees and enforces the registration, licensing, and regulatory requirements governing virtual currency kiosks and kiosk operators in the State.

Synopsis: Repealing the 90-day time limit within which an individual receiving services from the Developmental Disabilities Administration must appeal a loss of eligibility for services; establishing requirements related to eligibility determinations and redeterminations under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; prohibiting the Department from procedurally disenrolling individuals from the Program or home- and community-based services solely on a certain basis except under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Developmental Disabilities Administration - Home- and Community-Based Services Eligibility Determinations (Maryland Protecting People With Disabilities Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Home Care Services -see also- Respite Care
Long-Term Care -see also- Continuing Care; Nursing Homes
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: Regulates eligibility determinations and appeals for home- and community-based services under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program. Prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from procedurally disenrolling individuals solely for missing documentation without exhausting ex parte verification. Requires the department to continue services during incomplete reviews and automatically reinstate coverage following improper disenrollments. Directs the department, subject to federal approval, to reserve waiver slots for eligible individuals with developmental disabilities. Mandates quarterly reports on eligibility redeterminations, disenrollments, and application processing times through September 2029.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients, individuals with developmental disabilities receiving home- and community-based services, and service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can handle any additional workload using existing budgeted resources. The bill has no effect on state revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and its Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) administer the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and HCBS waivers. The bill directly establishes requirements for MDH regarding eligibility determinations, ex parte redeterminations, appeal timeframes, prohibitions on procedural disenrollment, waiver slot reservations, and quarterly reporting.

The Department of Disabilities is highlighted in the preamble regarding its statutory obligation, alongside the DDA, to compile data from habilitation plans and incorporate community placement barriers into the State's annual Olmstead Plan. The bill aligns directly with the department's mission to coordinate inclusive community living and services for Marylanders with disabilities.

The Department of Human Services, through its local departments of social services, participates in administering public assistance programs and eligibility determinations alongside Medicaid, and is cited as an information source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Providing that a certain unit owner is responsible for a certain cost of repair or replacement for certain portions of a condominium under certain circumstances; requiring a council of unit owners to inform unit owners annually of certain responsibilities; requiring a certain condominium unit owner to obtain a condominium unit owner insurance policy or a substantially similar property insurance policy for the unit; and requiring a certain insurance policy to include certain provisions.
Title: Condominiums - Unit Owner Responsibility for Damage or Destruction and Mandatory Insurance Coverage

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Increases a condominium unit owner's maximum liability for damage originating from their unit from $10,000 to $25,000. Sets unit owner liability at the least of repair costs, the council's deductible, or $25,000. Requires residential condominium unit owners to maintain individual property insurance policies. Exempts detached units within condominiums composed entirely of similar detached units from mandatory unit insurance. Mandates specified coverages, including at least $25,000 in loss assessment coverage. Requires owners to provide evidence of coverage annually and upon request to the council of unit owners.
responsible_party: Council of Unit Owners
stakeholders: Residential condominium unit owners, condominium councils of unit owners, and property insurers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates specific property and casualty insurance coverage requirements for condominium unit owners, including required loss assessment coverage amounts, building property minimums, and provisions relating to master policy deductible responsibility, which impact policies issued and regulated by the Administration.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically through its Consumer Protection Division, handles consumer inquiries and disputes related to common ownership communities, condominium governance, and statutory compliance under the Maryland Condominium Act.
The Secretary of State is responsible for the registration and regulatory oversight of condominiums in Maryland, which are governed by the Maryland Condominium Act amended by this legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Commerce to develop and maintain a searchable online database, to be known as the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal, to connect businesses in the State with local sources for supplies and inventory; and requiring the Department to report on or before December 31 each year on the use and effectiveness of the portal.
Title: Economic Development - Local Sourcing Database

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Commerce to develop and maintain the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal. Establishes a searchable online database connecting State businesses with local sources for tariff-impacted goods and other supplies. Requires the portal to be searchable by North American Industry Classification System codes. Makes participation in the portal by local sources voluntary. Requires the department to report annually by December 31 to the General Assembly on portal effectiveness.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Maryland businesses seeking supplies and Maryland-headquartered or locally based commercial suppliers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $142,900 in FY 2027 to hire one contractual data analyst and fund system development, with ongoing operating costs of $91,800 to $102,100 through FY 2031. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Department of Commerce is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing, maintaining, and administering the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal, as well as submitting annual reports to the General Assembly and incurring direct personnel and IT expenditures.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Commerce to coordinate with the Office of the Comptroller to identify potential local sources for inclusion in the local sourcing portal.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Commerce to coordinate with the Department of Information Technology to leverage existing digital infrastructure and minimize portal development and maintenance costs.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Growth Initiative in the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to support the growth of start-up companies; requiring the Initiative to create a certain list of companies in the State that are between certain growth phases according to a certain priority; establishing the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund to be administered by the Corporation as a special, nonlapsing fund; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget an appropriation of $5,000,000 for the Initiative; etc.
Title: Maryland Technology Development Corporation - Maryland Growth Initiative - Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Public Corporations and Instrumentalities -see also- HBE

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Growth Initiative within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to support growing start-up companies. Creates the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund to provide postseed and Series A funding for businesses scaling up. Requires the initiative to maintain a curated list of State companies between start-up and scaling phases. Prioritizes prior corporation funding recipients, minority business enterprises, and companies in economically distressed or high-need areas. Mandates an annual State budget appropriation of $5,000,000 for the initiative beginning in fiscal 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
stakeholders: Maryland start-up companies in the postseed and Series A scaling phases, minority business enterprises, and businesses in economically distressed or high-need geographic areas
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $4.0 million in FY 2027 due to a contingent appropriation, and by $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028 under the mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund increase correspondingly by $4.0 million in FY 2027 and $5.0 million annually thereafter. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency responsible for establishing and administering the Maryland Growth Initiative and the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund, creating the curated list of qualifying companies, and adopting implementation regulations.
The bill mandates the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $5,000,000 for the Maryland Growth Initiative in the annual state budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2028.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and must incorporate and monitor the mandated $5,000,000 annual general fund appropriation for the Initiative.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund separately and invest the money of the Fund in accordance with state law.
The Comptroller is statutorily tasked with accounting for the newly established Maryland Growth Initiative Fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant, by law, a credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on a commercial building that is rented or rented to own at fair market value to a small business if the commercial building is located in a designated arts and entertainment district, a Main Street Maryland community, a designated Baltimore Main Street, or any other designated business improvement district.
Title: Property Tax - Credit for Commercial Buildings Rented to Small Businesses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to grant a property tax credit on commercial buildings rented to small businesses. The commercial building must be rented or rented to own at fair market value to a small business. Qualifying buildings must be located in designated arts and entertainment districts, Main Street Maryland communities, Baltimore Main Streets, or business improvement districts. Local governments may establish the credit's amount, duration, additional eligibility criteria, and application procedures. The Act takes effect June 1, 2026, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of counties and municipal corporations
stakeholders: Owners of commercial buildings rented to small businesses in designated arts, entertainment, Main Street, or business improvement districts; small-business commercial tenants; Baltimore City, county, and municipal governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. County and municipal property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 to the extent local governments choose to grant the tax credit. The revenue loss depends on local credit amounts, duration, and the number of qualifying small businesses, which cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly conditions eligibility for the local property tax credit on a commercial building being located in a 'Main Street Maryland community designated by the Department of Housing and Community Development.'

The bill incorporates Arts and Entertainment Districts designated under Title 4, Subtitle 7 of the Economic Development Article (administered by the Department of Commerce) as qualifying locations for the local property tax credit, and the department served as an information source on the legislation.

Synopsis: Approving certain projects for the acquisition, development, and improvement of certain academic facilities for the University System of Maryland; authorizing the issuance of bonds by the University System of Maryland in a certain total principal amount for financing the projects; and providing that the bonds are not a debt or obligation of the State or any of its subdivisions.
Title: University System of Maryland - Academic Facilities Bonding Authority

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: Approves specified academic facility projects for the University System of Maryland. Authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue bonds totaling $26,000,000 for three specific campus projects. Covers projects at Towson University, the University of Maryland, College Park, and the University System of Maryland Office. Authorizes an additional $24,000,000 in bonds for systemwide academic capital facilities renewal projects. Clarifies that issued bonds do not constitute a debt or pledge of the State. Takes effect June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Students, faculty, staff, and administration across University System of Maryland constituent institutions, specifically Towson University, University of Maryland, College Park, and the Rita Colwell Center
fiscal_impact_summary: State bond revenues and expenditures increase by $50.0 million in FY 2027 for capital improvement projects. Higher education expenditures increase by an estimated $4.2 million annually beginning in FY 2028 for 20 years to pay debt service on the revenue bonds. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 769 directly authorizes the University System of Maryland (USM) to issue $50 million in academic revenue bonds to finance specific capital improvement and renewal projects across its institutions, with USM responsible for the debt service.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to establish an employment training and opportunity database for the purpose of assisting individuals in the State in finding employment training and other opportunities that may enable the individuals to become eligible and maintain eligibility for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to assist individuals in enrolling in programs listed in the database; etc.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - Employment Training and Opportunity Database

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and maintain an employment training and opportunity database. Requires the database to assist individuals in finding opportunities to become or remain eligible for Medicaid and SNAP. Directs the department to publish the database on a dedicated webpage and update it every 30 days. Requires the department to assist individuals in enrolling in listed vocational, workforce training, and job placement programs. Requires designated state agencies to establish processes for receiving and forwarding program recommendations to the department. Terminates the provisions of the act on September 30, 2029.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Department of Labor; Department of Human Services; Department of Service and Civic Innovation
stakeholders: Maryland residents seeking or maintaining eligibility for Medicaid or the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program; providers of vocational, workforce training, and job placement programs
fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures increase by $500,000 (90% federal funds, 10% general funds) in FY 2027 for system implementation, followed by maintenance costs between $51,200 and $53,600 annually (75% federal funds, 25% general funds) in FY 2028 through FY 2030. Federal fund revenues increase correspondingly. The Department of Labor, the Department of Human Services, and the Department of Service and Civic Innovation can absorb implementation with existing resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing, hosting, maintaining, and updating the Employment Training and Opportunity Database every 30 days, as well as assisting individuals with enrollment, which has a direct fiscal impact on the department.

MD Labor is statutorily mandated to coordinate with MDH, establish a process to receive recommendations for vocational, workforce training, or job placement programs, and forward appropriate recommendations to MDH.
DHS is statutorily mandated to coordinate with MDH, establish a recommendation process for programs to be included in the database, and forward eligible programs to MDH to support SNAP recipients.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI is statutorily mandated to coordinate with MDH, establish a process to receive recommendations for training and placement programs, and forward suitable recommendations to MDH for database inclusion.

Synopsis: Requiring a federal firearms licensee or law enforcement agency  operating a gun buyback program to destroy each firearm and all its component parts that are traded in as part of a gun buyback program; authorizing a licensee or agency to contract with a law enforcement agency or a business to destroy certain firearms; requiring a law enforcement agency operating a program to determine if a firearm is a crime firearm or has been reported lost or stolen before destroying the weapon; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Gun Buyback Programs - Destruction of Firearms

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Dealers -see also- Motor Vehicle Dealers and Salespeople
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
