Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: Requires a federal firearms licensee or law enforcement agency operating a gun buyback program to destroy each surrendered firearm. Mandates that destruction render the firearm and all attached components permanently inoperable and unrepairable. Excludes firearms determined by a law enforcement agency to be stolen or evidence of a crime. Requires law enforcement agencies to check databases to determine whether surrendered firearms are lost, stolen, or crime firearms. Authorizes operators to contract with a law enforcement agency or business to carry out required destruction. Requires the Secretary of State Police to revoke dealer licenses for violations of these buyback provisions.
responsible_party: Department of State Police; Secretary of State Police
stakeholders: Federal firearms licensees, law enforcement agencies operating gun buyback programs, licensed firearms dealers, and individuals surrendering firearms
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State Police is statutorily mandated to revoke the firearms dealer's license of any licensee who violates the gun buyback provisions. In addition, as a state law enforcement agency, the Department of State Police must follow the bill's protocols for firearm checks and destruction if operating a gun buyback program.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense subject to fines up to $10,000 for operating an unauthorized gun buyback program, as well as statutory civil penalties, which would be adjudicated within the Maryland District and Circuit Court systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense for operating an unauthorized gun buyback program, which could potentially require representation by public defenders for qualifying indigent defendants.

Synopsis: Altering the program the Maryland Department of Labor is required to establish for the retraining and placement of certain hospital employees; requiring the Department to allocate money from the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund to local workforce development boards under certain circumstances; altering certain workforce development programs to require inclusion of local workforce boards; requiring the Department to provide funding to local workforce boards; requiring local workforce boards to provide certain grants; etc.
Title: Labor and Employment - Workforce Development - Hospital Employee Retraining and Placement Program and Workforce Development and Local Workforce Development Boards (Local Workforce Solutions Investment Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to allocate money from the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund to local workforce development boards. Mandates that the department's dislocated worker unit forward reduction in operations notices to affected local workforce development boards. Directs the department, subject to available funding, to provide quick response program funds to local boards. Requires local workforce development boards to award grants to eligible employers under the Apprenticeship Career Training in Our Neighborhoods Program. Substitutes local workforce development boards for one-stop career centers in consultations under the Direct Care Workforce Innovation Program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: displaced hospital workers, workers affected by reductions in operations, employers undergoing reductions in operations, construction employers hiring apprentices, direct care workers, and local workforce development boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected, as the Maryland Department of Labor can implement the requirements with existing resources. Local revenues and expenditures increase for local workforce development boards that receive distributions from the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund to assist displaced workers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with administering the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund, the quick response program under the Economic Stabilization Act, and the ACTION Program in partnership with local workforce development boards.

The board is statutorily required to collaborate with the Secretary of Labor to develop mandatory guidelines for employers experiencing reductions in operations, and will assist in providing guidance to local workforce development boards.

The Secretary of Health is statutorily required to jointly adopt regulations with the Secretary of Labor to implement the hospital employee retraining and placement program, which is triggered by hospital closures, delicensing, or mergers.

Synopsis: Establishing a clinical research pharmacy permit; authorizing the State Board of Pharmacy to issue a clinical research pharmacy permit; authorizing a health care provider to hold an ownership interest in a clinical research pharmacy under certain circumstances; prohibiting an individual from being required to obtain a license, certification, or authorization to practice under certain provisions of law to own or have an ownership interest in a clinical research pharmacy; etc.
Title: Clinical Research Pharmacies and Clinical Trials - Permits and Ownership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Establishes a clinical research pharmacy permit issued by the State Board of Pharmacy. Requires a separate permit before a person may establish or operate each clinical research pharmacy in Maryland. Authorizes licensed health care providers to hold an ownership interest under specified operational and ethical conditions. Prohibits requiring professional licensure or certification merely to hold an ownership interest in a clinical research pharmacy. Authorizes relevant health occupations boards to investigate allegations of unauthorized practice by pharmacy employees. Requires the State Board of Pharmacy to adopt implementing regulations regarding operational standards, application procedures, and inspections.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: Clinical research pharmacies, clinical trial participants, licensed pharmacists, and health care providers investing in clinical research facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Pharmacy special fund expenditures increase by at least $85,600 in FY 2027 for a full-time licensing specialist, with indeterminate additional IT contractual costs. Special fund revenues increase minimally and indeterminately to the extent permit application fees are established. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Health and its State Board of Pharmacy by creating a new clinical research pharmacy permit, requiring the Board to adopt regulations, oversee applications, conduct inspections, and enforce compliance, resulting in an ongoing fiscal impact and the addition of personnel.

Synopsis: Repealing a certain provision of law exempting all persons that acquire or are assigned certain mortgages, mortgage loans, or installment loans under certain circumstances from certain provisions of law governing the licensing of providers of certain financial services in the State.
Title: Financial Institutions - Consumer Credit - Application of Licensing Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Repeals a statutory exemption from consumer credit licensing requirements under Title 11 of the Financial Institutions Article. Applies to persons that acquire or receive assignment of a mortgage, mortgage loan, or installment loan. Clarifies that the repeal corrects a provision erroneously enacted by Chapter 118 of 2025. Subjects these loan purchasers and assignees back to State consumer lending licensing provisions. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Persons and entities that acquire or are assigned mortgages, mortgage loans, or installment loans, as well as consumer borrowers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, through its Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, oversees the licensing and regulation of financial institutions and consumer credit lenders under Title 11 of the Financial Institutions Article, making it the primary implementing and regulatory agency for this licensing requirement correction.

Synopsis: Prohibiting local correctional facilities from taking certain actions related to immigration enforcement, subject to certain exceptions; prohibiting law enforcement agents from taking certain actions related to immigration enforcement, subject to certain exceptions; prohibiting State and local correctional facilities from taking certain actions against an individual based on a certain immigration status of the individual or any other person; requiring employees and agents of State correctional facilities to provide certain notice; etc.
Title: Correctional Services and Criminal Procedure - Immigration Enforcement - Prohibitions (Community Trust Act)
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 872

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Prohibits local correctional facilities from prolonging detention or transferring individuals to federal immigration authorities without a judicial warrant. Exempts covered convicted individuals, routine booking procedures, and entries into the National Crime Information Center. Requires State correctional facilities to give federal authorities 48 hours notice before releasing an individual with an active detainer. Bars law enforcement agents from providing federal immigration authorities with individual information unless required by a court order. Authorizes judges and District Court commissioners to consider immigration detainers when determining pretrial release or bail for felony defendants. Authorizes the Attorney General and affected individuals to file civil enforcement actions.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Individuals in State and local correctional custody, immigrant communities, State and local correctional personnel, law enforcement agents, and federal immigration authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant decrease in State and local federal fund revenues if Maryland is deemed out of compliance with federal immigration enforcement law. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS directly operates State correctional facilities and the Division of Pretrial Detention and Services. The bill establishes specific operational requirements and prohibitions regarding immigration detainers, inquiries, transfers, and a 48-hour release notice requirement for State correctional facilities.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to initiate civil actions to enforce compliance with the correctional facility immigration enforcement prohibitions and seek injunctive relief.

The bill directly impacts judicial operations by authorizing District Court commissioners and judges to consider immigration detainers when determining pretrial release, bail, or bond for felony defendants, as well as handling civil enforcement actions.

As the State's primary law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police officers are subject to the bill's restrictions on sharing information with federal immigration authorities during regular police duties, and the department must adopt a compliant policy.

Synopsis: Requiring hospitals in the State to adopt a policy describing the protocol of the hospital when there is an immigration enforcement action at the hospital; and requiring hospitals to make the immigration enforcement action policy available to all staff members and provide annual training to ensure the staff's knowledge and understanding of the policy.
Title: Hospitals - Immigration Enforcement Action - Policy Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires hospitals in the State to adopt a policy regarding immigration enforcement actions. Excludes hospitals operated by state or local government units subject to specified existing guidance requirements. Mandates that the adopted policy remain consistent with guidance issued by the Attorney General. Requires hospitals to make the policy available to all staff members. Directs hospitals to provide annual training on the policy to all staff members. Establishes an effective date of June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Hospitals in Maryland, hospital staff members, and hospital patients and visitors
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires hospitals in Maryland to adopt policies regarding immigration enforcement actions that are consistent with guidance issued by the Attorney General under § 6–111 of the State Government Article.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to establish operational and training requirements for licensed hospitals in Maryland, which fall under the regulatory and licensing purview of the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill as introduced originally tasked the Commission with developing and publishing a model immigration enforcement policy for hospitals; however, these provisions were struck out by amendment, leaving no active duties or fiscal impact for the agency.

Synopsis: Authorizing an individual who enrolls for coverage or enrolls a dependent for coverage during a certain special enrollment period for pregnancy to choose a certain date option on which the coverage will become effective; and requiring the carrier, if the individual fails to select the effective date, to select a certain date option.
Title: Health Insurance - Special Enrollment Period for Pregnancy - Coverage Effective Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Authorizes an individual enrolling during a pregnancy special enrollment period to choose when coverage becomes effective. Permits selection of the first day of the pregnancy confirmation month or the month following plan selection. Requires the carrier to choose between those two dates if the individual fails to make a selection. Applies to all health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed in the State on or after January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Individuals enrolling for health insurance during a pregnancy special enrollment period and their dependents; health insurance carriers
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Agency operational impacts can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates private health insurance carriers in the state. MIA will review amended policy forms and rate filings implementing the new coverage effective date options for the pregnancy special enrollment period and will receive form filing fees.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange operates Maryland Health Connection (the Individual Exchange). It will need to adjust enrollment systems and processes to accommodate the enrollee's choice of effective coverage date during a pregnancy special enrollment period.

Synopsis: Expanding the definition of "pomace brandy" authorized to be produced and sold by the holder of a Class 4 limited winery license; clarifying that the holder of a Class 4 limited winery license must report all pomace brandy distilled and bottled by the holder as a distilled spirit for purposes of the alcoholic beverage tax; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Montgomery County to issue a Class D beer, wine, and liquor license to the holder of a Class 3 winery license under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 3 Wineries and Class 4 Limited Wineries - Alterations

Alcoholic Beverages Manufacturing -see also- Breweries; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes Class 3 winery license holders to acquire bulk wine from Class 4 limited winery license holders. Authorizes Class 4 limited winery license holders to sell and deliver bulk wine to Class 3 wineries. Expands the definition of pomace brandy to include brandy not exceeding 80 proof made from qualifying wine. Requires Class 4 limited wineries to report all distilled and bottled pomace brandy as a distilled spirit. Authorizes the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class D license in Silver Spring.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Board of License Commissioners for Montgomery County
stakeholders: Class 3 winery license holders and Class 4 limited winery license holders in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that pomace brandy distilled and bottled by Class 4 limited winery license holders be reported as a distilled spirit under Title 5 of the Tax - General Article for alcoholic beverage tax purposes, falling under the Comptroller's jurisdiction as the state's principal tax collector and regulator of alcoholic beverage taxation.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions of law governing the recapture of certain amounts of the credit against the State income tax for certain individuals with student loan debt to require the recapture of the unused amount of the credit rather than the total amount; authorizing the Maryland Higher Education Commission to extend the period of time that an individual who claims the credit has to prove that the individual used the credit to repay the individual's student loan debt under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit - Alterations
bill_summary: Requires recapture of only the unused portion of the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit instead of the total amount. Authorizes the Maryland Higher Education Commission to extend the three-year deadline for individuals to use the credit. Permits extensions if SAVE plan litigation forbearance, federal understaffing delays, or buyback agreement delays prevent loan repayment. Requires the Commission to adopt procedures for individuals to apply for an extension by October 1, 2026. Applies to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: individuals with undergraduate or graduate student loan debt claiming the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit
fiscal_impact_summary: Potential decrease or delay in State general fund revenues to the extent credit recapture is precluded or delayed; specific figures cannot be reliably predicted. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary administering agency of the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit. The bill directly tasks MHEC with establishing procedures for waiver applications and authorizes the Commission to grant extensions for individuals to use the credit to repay eligible student loan debt.

As the state higher education coordinating board (MHEC), the agency is responsible for administering the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit, approving credits, adopting procedures by October 1, 2026, and granting extensions to qualified taxpayers.
The Comptroller administers Maryland state income taxes and is responsible for processing tax credits and collecting recaptured credit amounts as taxes payable to the State.

Synopsis: Requiring that a holder of a Class 8 farm brewery license engage in certain agritourism activity; altering certain standards and requirements for food service under a Class 8 farm brewery license; providing an exception to a prohibition against issuing an alcoholic beverages license for a premises that does not comply with local zoning laws; and providing that the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission has exclusive regulatory authority over the operation of a Class 8 farm brewery.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 8 Farm Brewery Licenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages Manufacturing -see also- Breweries; etc.
Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Farmers and Farming -see also- Agriculture; Farmland
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: Requires holders of a Class 8 farm brewery license to operate an agribusiness and actively engage in agritourism. Grants the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission exclusive regulatory authority over Class 8 farm breweries. Exempts farm breweries first licensed on or before July 1, 2015, from local zoning conformity requirements. Expands food service privileges to allow licensed food trucks, licensed caterers, and on-farm cottage foods. Authorizes license holders to host festivals, provide entertainment, and rent farm property for events.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
stakeholders: Class 8 farm brewery license holders, farm brewery patrons, and food service vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $196,700 in fiscal 2027 and approximately $250,000 annually thereafter for two regulatory positions and contractual health inspection services. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires Class 8 farm brewery licensees to operate as agribusinesses engaged in the production, showcasing, preparation, and sale of farm products, actively engage in agritourism, and use Maryland agricultural products grown on the licensed farm. The Department of Agriculture supports agricultural marketing and agritourism initiatives and was consulted in the bill's fiscal analysis.

The bill alters food service requirements for farm breweries by specifically referencing food establishment licensing and cottage food provisions under Title 21 of the Health - General Article, which falls under the regulatory purview of the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments.

The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for collecting state alcoholic beverage taxes and administering tax compliance for alcoholic beverage manufacturers under the Tax - General Article, which is referenced in the licensing conformity requirements.

Synopsis: Requiring certain public school personnel to notify a county superintendent or a county superintendent's designee if the individual receives notification of certain immigration enforcement at a school; expanding the definition of sensitive locations relating to a "public school" to include certain locations that distribute food to individuals in need; prohibiting public school personnel from engaging in certain immigration enforcement; requiring certain courthouses to implement a certain policy and update the policy as necessary; etc.
Title: Immigration Enforcement - Expanding Sensitive Locations, Notification, and Guidance (Maryland Values Act of 2026)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Prohibits public school security personnel from engaging in immigration enforcement at a public school. Bars personnel from sharing student educational or employee personnel records for immigration enforcement without specified legal process. Requires school personnel notified of immigration enforcement at a school to notify the county superintendent. Expands sensitive locations to include designated school bus stops, school vehicles, and certain food distribution facilities. Requires sensitive locations to deny immigration enforcement access to areas requiring security screenings without a federal warrant. Requires the Attorney General to update enforcement guidance annually and requires courthouses to implement related policies.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General; local school systems; public schools; public libraries; State courthouses
stakeholders: Maryland public school personnel, students, public school employees and their families, public libraries, State and local courthouses, and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the Attorney General to annually update comprehensive guidance regarding immigration enforcement at sensitive locations, delineate boundaries between public and nonpublic spaces, and evaluate locations requiring special consideration.

The bill establishes restrictions on public school personnel regarding immigration enforcement, prohibits sharing student records without judicial process, adds notification requirements to county superintendents, and expands sensitive locations to include school vehicles and designated bus stops.

The bill explicitly references the Center's School Resource Officer and School Security Employee Training Academy within its definitions of public school personnel subject to the bill's restrictions, and the Center tracks school safety and law enforcement coverage.

The bill directly requires courthouses to implement and annually update policies regarding sensitive locations and federal immigration enforcement, which falls under the administrative and operational oversight of the Judiciary and AOC.

Public libraries are designated as sensitive locations under the statute and are required to implement and maintain policies denying access to nonpublic areas for immigration enforcement consistent with the Attorney General's guidance.
Statutory provisions in the bill require that covered officers provide notice to the Department of State Police barrack commander prior to or upon taking enforcement actions.

Facilities operated by the Comptroller are statutory sensitive locations governed by access restrictions and required to implement policies consistent with the Attorney General's immigration enforcement guidance.
The bill requires covered officers to notify the Secretary of Natural Resources or their designee when conducting enforcement actions on property owned, leased, or controlled by the department.

The chief of police of the Maryland Transportation Authority must be notified when covered officers conduct enforcement actions on property owned or operated by MDTA, the Aviation Administration, or Port Administration.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain service agreements for residential property entered into before June 1, 2023, if the service provider is not considered in good standing with the State Department of Assessment and Taxation on or after June 1, 2026.
Title: Residential Property - Service Agreement - Defunct Service Providers
bill_summary: Voids certain residential property service agreements entered into before June 1, 2023, under specified conditions. Limits application to defunct service providers not in good standing with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation. Prohibits these agreements from lasting over two years or creating liens on residential property. Prohibits agreements from binding subsequent bona fide purchasers or assigning service rights without notice or consent. Authorizes persons holding property interests to bring circuit court actions declaring noncompliant agreements void. Authorizes persons bringing an action to seek compensatory damages, reasonable attorney's fees, and costs.
responsible_party: Circuit Courts; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Residential property owners, individuals with an interest in affected residential property, and defunct residential service providers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a specific civil cause of action allowing persons with an interest in residential property subject to an invalid service agreement or lien to file an action in the circuit court for a declaratory determination, compensatory damages, and attorney's fees. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch in managing these proceedings.

The Department of Labor regulates businesses and licensed professionals (such as real estate professionals and home improvement contractors) that execute service agreements relating to residential property maintenance, purchase, or sale. The agency was consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal note.

Synopsis: Altering certain requirements related to the development of a certain project at State Center; and establishing a State Center Advisory Group to provide community input, inform the identification of potential community benefits associated with the project in the surrounding areas, and facilitate transparency and information-sharing.
Title: State Center - Development - Contract, Plan Requirements, and Advisory Group

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the State Center Advisory Group to provide community input and facilitate transparency regarding the development of State Center. Alters development contract requirements to include anchor institutions that provide public or community services as major tenants. Requires development contracts to include a community benefit agreement with the advisory group, local hiring plans, and economic improvement plans. Repeals parking facility requirements and replaces former community alliance consultation provisions with advisory group engagement. Extends the developer construction commencement deadline from 18 months to 24 months after contract execution.
responsible_party: Department of General Services; State Center Advisory Group
stakeholders: Residents and community organizations surrounding State Center in Baltimore City, State Center developers, and local businesses and workers
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; creating the advisory group and altering development contract requirements does not materially affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of General Services manages state-owned facilities and real estate contracts. As the primary reporting agency overseeing the 28-acre State Center property in Baltimore City, DGS is responsible for implementing the development contract provisions and convening and consulting with the newly established State Center Advisory Group.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates a new advisory body, the State Center Advisory Group, outlining its membership, leadership structure, conflict-of-interest requirements, and duties to provide community input and engage in community benefit negotiations.
The University of Baltimore, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, is explicitly designated as an anchor entity entitled to appoint a member to the State Center Advisory Group.
The Board of Public Works oversees and must approve significant state procurement contracts and the lease, transfer, or redevelopment of state-owned real estate such as State Center.

DBM reviews state capital commitments, budget execution, and major procurement requirements associated with large-scale state property redevelopment plans and was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.

Synopsis: Altering requirements for providing notice to interested parties when a county or municipal corporation files a complaint for a judicial in rem foreclosure on certain vacant and abandoned property.
Title: Judicial In Rem Tax Foreclosure - Notice Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Alters notice requirements for judicial in rem tax foreclosure actions on certain vacant and abandoned properties. Requires a county or municipal corporation to serve the foreclosure complaint on each interested party under the Maryland Rules. Repeals the mandate to mail notice and the complaint by certified and first-class mail within five days after filing. Retains an interested party's right to cure delinquent taxes and liens before judgment entry. Sets an effective date of June 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Circuit Courts of Maryland; Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Counties and municipal corporations; owners, mortgagees, and interested lienholders of vacant and abandoned real property subject to tax foreclosure
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances; not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the service and notice requirements for complaints filed in the circuit courts for judicial in rem tax foreclosures on vacant and abandoned properties, requiring service in accordance with the Maryland Rules administered within the judicial branch.

Synopsis: Reserving jurisdiction with respect to certain federal land in the State under certain conditions; authorizing the Central Collection Unit of the Department of Budget and Management to collect a certain amount of delinquent federal funds; authorizing the Central Collection Unit, under a certain circumstance, to collect certain federal funds owed to the State, place liens on federal property in the State, and direct the Comptroller to withhold certain payments to the federal government; etc.
Title: State Finance - Delinquent Federal Funds (Federal Obligations Enforcement Act)

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments

bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of Public Works to determine the federal government delinquent in funds owed to the State upon court noncompliance. Requires delinquent federal funds to be referred to the Central Collection Unit of the Department of Budget and Management. Authorizes the Central Collection Unit, in consultation with the Attorney General, to collect funds and place property liens. Authorizes the Central Collection Unit to direct the Comptroller to withhold State payments to the federal government. Authorizes the Comptroller to withhold those State payments. Reserves State jurisdiction over federal land when the federal government defies court decisions upholding congressionally approved spending.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Central Collection Unit of the Department of Budget and Management; Comptroller of Maryland; Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: The federal government, Maryland State agencies receiving or remitting federal funds, and the Maryland Department of Transportation
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by up to $660,800 in FY 2027 for the Comptroller's Office and the Office of the Attorney General, with ongoing legal staffing costs. Special fund expenditures for the Central Collection Unit may increase. State expenditures across all funds may decrease from withholding payments to the federal government, but federal fund revenues may decrease if federal agencies offset funds through the Treasury Offset Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Central Collection Unit (CCU), a unit of DBM, with collecting delinquent federal funds, placing liens on federal property in the State, and directing the Comptroller to withhold payments to the federal government.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Comptroller to withhold State payments to the federal government upon referral from CCU and requires an estimated $175,000 in FY 2027 for vendor IT programming modifications.
The bill grants BPW the primary authority to determine, by a majority vote, that the federal government is delinquent in funds owed to the State and to refer delinquent funds to CCU.
OAG must consult with CCU prior to taking enforcement actions and will litigate anticipated federal challenges, requiring an estimated $485,827 and 6.0 new positions in FY 2027.

The Governor serves on the Board of Public Works deciding federal delinquency, retains authority regarding concurrent jurisdiction agreements on federal land, and receives notice regarding Maryland Defense Act proceedings.

MDOT relies heavily on federal funding ($1.5 billion of its capital program in FY 2027), which could be severely impacted or jeopardized if the federal government responds by offsetting or withholding federal grant revenues.
The judiciary may experience an increase in circuit court filings, litigation, and recordings of liens placed against federal property in the State.
The State Treasurer sits on the Board of Public Works, which is authorized by majority vote to make the determination of federal delinquency.

Synopsis: Establishing certain civil penalties for violations of law involving the employment of minors; prohibiting employers from allowing the formation of a certain organization or entity under certain circumstances; authorizing certain private employees to petition the Public Employee Relations Board to resolve certain matters under certain circumstances; prohibiting Executive Branch units from applying for a waiver of the federal Fair Labor Standards Act; etc.
Title: Labor Law - Child Labor Penalties, Private Sector Employee Labor Relations, and State Employee Labor Standards

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to assess civil penalties for violations of child labor laws. Caps initial penalties at $16,035 for standard violations and $72,876 for willful or repeated hazardous violations. Prohibits employers from permitting certain workplace organizations that are exempt from the federal National Labor Relations Act. Prohibits Executive Branch units of State government from applying for waivers of the federal Fair Labor Standards Act. Authorizes private employees to petition the Public Employee Relations Board if federal labor protections are repealed or ceded.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Public Employee Relations Board
stakeholders: employers, private sector employees, employed minors, and State Executive Branch agencies and employees
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 from new civil penalties for child labor violations. If specified federal contingency conditions are met, special fund revenues and expenditures for the Public Employee Relations Board will increase significantly to oversee private employee collective bargaining. Local circuit courts are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within MD Labor with assessing civil penalties for child labor violations and indexing those penalties to inflation. It also directs MD Labor to monitor federal actions regarding the National Labor Relations Act and notify the Department of Legislative Services if statutory contingencies are triggered.

The bill expands PERB's jurisdiction to include private sector employees under specified federal contingencies, authorizing PERB to process representation petitions, conduct elections, certify exclusive representatives, adjudicate unfair labor practices, and assess civil penalties.

As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees executive branch employee standards and policies. The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article to prohibit any Executive Branch unit from applying to the federal government for a waiver of any applicable provision of the federal Fair Labor Standards Act.

The bill provides that orders issued by the Public Employee Relations Board regarding private employees are subject to judicial review by the circuit courts, which are supported administratively by the AOC.

Synopsis: Correcting certain errors or omissions in certain articles of the Annotated Code and the Public Local Laws of Maryland; clarifying language; correcting certain obsolete references; reorganizing certain sections of the Annotated Code; providing that the Act is not intended to affect any law other than to correct technical errors; and providing for the correction of certain errors and obsolete provisions by the publishers of the Annotated Code.
Title: Annual Corrective Bill

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: Corrects technical errors, omissions, cross-references, and obsolete language across multiple articles of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Clarifies statutory terminology and reorganizes select code sections without intending substantive changes to existing law. Authorizes the publishers of the Annotated Code, subject to approval by the Department of Legislative Services, to make technical corrections. Restores omitted district residency requirements for Somerset County Commissioners.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: state agencies, local governments, legal practitioners, and publishers of the Annotated Code of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the bill is technical in nature and does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes nonsubstantive technical corrections, grammar fixes, and cross-reference updates to multiple sections of the Education Article concerning school funding, educator guidelines, special education models, and student programs.

The bill corrects statutory cross-references concerning nonvisual access procurement standards and cybersecurity incident reporting by the State Chief Information Security Officer under DoIT's purview.

The bill corrects omitted statutory definitions designating the Department of Disabilities and Secretary of Disabilities regarding the Ethan Saylor Alliance and the Assistive Technology Services Fund.
The bill corrects technical phrasing, spelling errors, and legislative committee reference names for annual reports submitted by the Department of the Environment.
The bill updates statutory provisions relating to transportation project definitions, Transportation Trust Fund accounts, legislative reporting committees, and Maryland Vehicle Law terminology.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates obsolete statutory references in the Health - General Article to reflect the agency's current name.

The bill makes technical corrections to remove redundant references to the Secretary of Budget and Management in capital project and employee incentive provisions where the term is already statutorily defined.
The bill makes minor technical language cleanups in State Finance and Procurement provisions involving DGS capital project program approvals.
The bill corrects technical agency misnomers within reporting requirements regarding reemployed contractual correctional retirees submitted to the State Retirement Agency.
The bill corrects grammatical errors and internal cross-references in the Labor and Employment Article relating to unemployment misconduct definitions and apprenticeship grant provisions.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of a "foster care recipient" to mean an individual who resided in an out-of-home placement on or after the individual's 8th birthday rather than 13th birthday for purposes of determining eligibility for a certain tuition exemption.
Title: Higher Education - Tuition Exemption for Foster Care Recipients - Eligibility

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Alters the definition of foster care recipient to expand eligibility for tuition exemptions at Maryland public institutions of higher education. Lowers the qualifying out-of-home placement age threshold from an individual's thirteenth birthday to their eighth birthday. Applies to individuals in out-of-home placements for at least one year who enter guardianship, adoption, or parental reunification. Exempts eligible students from tuition if enrolled before age 25 for a vocational certificate, associate's degree, or bachelor's degree. Requires eligible students to file for federal and State financial aid. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Department of Human Services; public institutions of higher education
stakeholders: Foster care alumni placed in out-of-home placement on or after age eight who exited through adoption, guardianship, or reunification; Maryland public four-year universities and community colleges
fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education tuition revenues decrease, potentially significantly, beginning in fiscal 2027 due to additional tuition waivers granted. Local community college tuition revenues also decrease, potentially significantly. State and community college expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount annually due to additional student enrollment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters eligibility for foster care recipients placed in out-of-home care by the Department of Human Services, requiring DHS foster care placement and exit records to determine student eligibility.

MHEC oversees higher education policies and financial assistance in the state and receives mandatory annual reporting from public higher education institutions regarding foster care tuition waivers and forms used.

The commission is responsible for establishing statewide higher education policies and receives required annual reporting from public institutions regarding students receiving foster care tuition waivers.

USM institutions are public institutions of higher education that must provide tuition waivers and on-campus housing priority to newly eligible foster care recipients, experiencing decreases in tuition revenue and increases in educational expenditures.

As a public four-year university, Morgan State must grant tuition exemptions to newly eligible foster care students, resulting in a direct reduction in tuition revenue and potential expenditure impacts.

As an independent public four-year institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland is required to waive tuition and mandatory fees for eligible foster care recipients, impacting tuition revenue.
MLDSC connects foster care data with postsecondary education outcome data and tracks college-going rates and waiver eligibility for foster youth.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2027, and altering the membership and duties of the Workgroup.
Title: Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance – Extension and Alteration of Membership and Duties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance to June 30, 2027. Alters workgroup membership by adding an actuary, mutual insurer representatives, and nonprofit research or consumer advocacy representatives. Requires the workgroup to develop concrete legislative recommendations to reduce premiums through a recorded voting process. Mandates specific recommendations regarding territorial rating and factors contributing to disparate impacts across the State. Requires an updated report to the Governor and General Assembly by January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, private passenger automobile insurers, insurance producers, and consumer advocacy organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources, though special fund expenditures for the Maryland Insurance Administration may increase minimally if its actuarial contract scope is expanded. Revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary implementing agency responsible for staffing, convening, and chairing the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance, and will oversee the development and submission of the updated report.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (or their designee) is statutorily designated as a member of the workgroup examining automobile insurance affordability and rating factors.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the duration, alters the membership, and expands the statutory charge of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance.
The workgroup is required to submit its updated findings and concrete legislative recommendations directly to the Governor by January 1, 2027.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program in the Department of Commerce to provide customized, no-cost workforce training as a business attraction tool, to recruit strategic industries and qualified business entities to the State; requiring the Department to partner with not more than two community colleges in the State to deliver training services; etc.
Title: Economic Development - Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program in the Department of Commerce. Directs the Department to provide customized, no-cost workforce training to recruit strategic industries and qualified business entities. Requires the Department to partner with not more than two community colleges to deliver training services. Mandates that community colleges own any curriculum, manuals, or instructional materials developed under the program. Requires participating business entities to reimburse training costs if they fail to meet established performance metrics. Terminates the pilot program on September 30, 2029, following an evaluation report due December 31, 2028.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: out-of-state business entities seeking to locate in Maryland, partner community colleges, and participating trainees
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million in FY 2027 and FY 2028 to support administrative staffing and training grants, with an additional $42,600 in FY 2029. Revenues and expenditures for up to two partner community colleges increase by an equivalent amount to develop and deliver customized training programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and tasks the Department of Commerce with administering the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program, including selecting and partnering with up to two community colleges, negotiating agreements with qualified business entities, distributing program funds, monitoring performance metrics, and reporting on program outcomes.

The Department of Commerce is required to submit a comprehensive report on the effectiveness of the pilot program and recommendations for statewide expansion to the Governor on or before December 31, 2028.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "rental dwelling unit" for purposes of provisions of law governing the reduction of lead risk in housing.
Title: Reduction of Lead Risk in Housing - Rental Dwelling Unit - Definition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Alters the definition of rental dwelling unit under the State's lead risk reduction in housing law. Repeals the requirement that a habitable rental unit must be independent. Includes units that have living facilities with, or access to, permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation. Maintains exclusions for unfinished basements, hotel and motel units, secured inaccessible areas, and units not offered for rent. Takes effect October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Owners and landlords of residential rental properties (including single-room occupancy and shared-housing facilities), tenants, local public housing authorities, and lead paint inspection and abatement contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Fund increase by an estimated $1,406,300 in FY 2027 and future odd fiscal years ($281,300 in even years) from biennial registration fees. Special fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $369,600 in FY 2027 and between $255,000 and $291,400 annually thereafter for three positions, outreach, and database upgrades. Local expenditures may increase for local housing entities required to pay fees and perform inspections or remediation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment administers the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program and enforces the Reduction of Lead Risk in Housing law under Title 6, Subtitle 8 of the Environment Article. The bill directly expands the definition of rental dwelling units subject to MDE registration and regulation, requiring MDE to add staff, upgrade its database, and process substantial registration fee revenues.

The Maryland Department of Health coordinates on statewide public health initiatives to prevent childhood lead poisoning and works in conjunction with lead surveillance and local health department case management for elevated blood lead levels.

The Department of Housing and Community Development oversees affordable rental housing programs, single-room occupancy (SRO) units, and residential property standards that are directly affected by expanded lead risk reduction compliance mandates.

Synopsis: Authorizing the use of stop sign monitoring systems in school zones in the 41st legislative district of Baltimore City under the pilot program authorized for Prince George's County, the 45th and 46th legislative districts of Baltimore City, and the City of Takoma Park if authorized by local law.
Title: Baltimore City - Stop Sign Monitoring Systems Pilot Program - 41st Legislative District

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: Authorizes the use of stop sign monitoring systems in school zones in the 41st Legislative District of Baltimore City. Conditions deployment on authorization by local law enacted after reasonable notice and a public hearing. Distributes 50% of collected violation fines to the local management board for Baltimore City. Requires these distributed funds to support youth programming and services in the 41st Legislative District. Imposes a civil penalty of up to $40 on recorded motor vehicle owners or drivers. Takes effect July 1, 2026, and terminates June 30, 2029.
responsible_party: Baltimore City; Baltimore City Department of Transportation; District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers and owners in Baltimore City's 41st Legislative District, Baltimore City public school students, and youth residing in the 41st Legislative District
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5,938 in FY 2027 only for one-time Judiciary programming costs. State general fund revenues increase minimally from FY 2027 through FY 2030 from contested citations. Baltimore City revenues and expenditures increase from FY 2027 through FY 2030 to the extent monitoring systems are installed and fine revenues are distributed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under the statute governing the pilot program, stop sign monitoring systems may only be used on State highways located in school zones if authorized by the State Highway Administration (SHA), and SHA is statutorily required to place signs providing notice that systems are in use on State highways.

The Administrative Office of the Courts / District Court handles contested citations issued by automated stop sign monitoring systems and collects fine revenues. The fiscal note indicates general fund expenditures of approximately $5,900 in FY 2027 for one-time judicial IT programming costs.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the State Highway Administration, which has regulatory and operational responsibilities regarding automated traffic enforcement signs on State highways.
The bill references reporting requirements under Chapter 571 of 2025 requiring pilot program progress and evaluation reports to be submitted to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to conduct a study on the use, regulation, and taxation of captive insurance companies by entities in the State and report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the Senate Finance Committee and the House Health Committee by January 1, 2027.
Title: Insurance - Captive Insurers - Premium Receipts Tax Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, to study captive insurance use, regulation, and taxation. Directs the study to examine utilization by nonprofit and for-profit entities and interstate regulatory and tax frameworks. Evaluates the feasibility and structure of establishing a State registry for out-of-state captive insurers. Protects information submitted by nonprofit health systems and hospitals from disclosure under the Public Information Act. Requires submission of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly committees by January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Captive insurance companies, nonprofit and for-profit entities utilizing captive insurance (including nonprofit hospitals and health systems), and Maryland insurance regulators.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Insurance Administration can conduct the study using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting the comprehensive study on the use, regulation, and taxation of captive insurance companies in Maryland and reporting findings and recommendations.
The bill requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to submit its final study report and policy recommendations on captive insurance to the Governor by January 1, 2027.

As the state's principal revenue and tax administrator, the Comptroller has an interest in the study's examination of tax frameworks, capital contributions, and premium receipts taxation for captive insurers.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness; requiring health occupations boards that require licensees or certificate holders to complete certain continuing education to grant at least 2 hours for every hour of continuing education for menopause and menopause-associated symptoms; requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated conditions; etc.
Title: Health Occupations, Public Health, and Insurance - Menopause - Provider Training Coverage Requirements, Policy Initiatives, and Access to Care

bill_summary: Requires certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover menopause and menopause-associated symptoms. Requires health occupations boards to grant qualifying licensees at least two continuing education credits per hour of menopause training. Directs the Maryland Department of Health to identify at least one qualifying menopause training program. Alters the membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness. Requires the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Commission for Women to evaluate policy initiatives and report findings.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Commission for Women; State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness; Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; licensed and certified health care providers who manage menopause; individuals experiencing perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal symptoms.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,300 in FY 2027 and $30,200 in FY 2028 for Maryland Department of Health contractual staff, vendors, and reporting requirements. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. Local government health care expenditures may increase for fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is directly responsible for identifying approved training programs for health occupations licensees regarding menopause, overseeing health occupations boards implementing continuing education requirements, and conducting evaluations and reporting action plans regarding community health workers and clinical education.

MIA regulates the private health insurance market in Maryland and will be responsible for enforcing the bill's mandate requiring health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans to cover the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated symptoms, as well as processing rate and form filings.

The Maryland Commission for Women is housed within DHS; under the bill, the Commission's Executive Director is added to the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, and the Commission is mandated to evaluate state policy initiatives and report findings to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory membership and composition of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, places reporting requirements on the Maryland Commission for Women, and requires consultation with the State Community Health Worker Advisory Committee.
DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must evaluate compliance and coverage standards with respect to state-mandated health insurance benefits.

MHEC serves as an informational source and coordinates higher education policy, relevant to the bill's requirement that MDH consult with institutions of higher education to evaluate methods for expanding clinical education on menopause.

USM institutions, including the University of Maryland School of Medicine, are consulted regarding clinical and postgraduate medical education opportunities related to menopausal evaluation and treatment.
Morgan State University is an institution of higher education consulted on opportunities for clinical and professional education in menopausal care.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide reimbursement for applied behavior analysis services provided by behavior technicians to Program recipients with autism spectrum disorder under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; prohibiting, subject to a certain exception, the Department from requiring as a condition of reimbursement that an individual receive a certain certification to provide applied behavior analysis services as a behavior technician to Program recipients; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Behavior Technicians - Reimbursement
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 867

NarrowSubjects.Name: Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse applied behavior analysis services delivered by behavior technicians to Medicaid recipients with autism spectrum disorder. Prohibits the Department from requiring certification from a recognized credentialing entity as a condition of reimbursement. Authorizes the Department to require technicians to obtain and maintain certification within 150 days of beginning services. Requires the Department to adopt regulations necessary to carry out the provisions. Abrogates the requirements if federal authorities declare them inconsistent with federal Social Security law by June 30, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: behavior technicians, Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients with autism spectrum disorder, and applied behavior analysis providers
fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures may increase minimally for administrative oversight to verify technician certifications, which the Maryland Department of Health can likely absorb with existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse applied behavior analysis services provided by behavior technicians under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, permits the department to enforce a 150-day certification requirement, and mandates that it adopt regulations and conduct administrative oversight.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program in the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to support the growth of companies that specialize in regenerative medicine and other advanced manufacturing by providing certain grants; authorizing grant proceeds to be used only for acquisitions, renovations or construction of certain space, infrastructure improvements, and purchase of equipment; etc.
Title: Maryland Technology Development Corporation - Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program - Established

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. Supports the growth of companies that specialize in regenerative medicine and other advanced manufacturing. Requires the corporation to establish eligibility criteria, application procedures, evaluation criteria, and grant award amounts. Restricts grant spending to space acquisition, renovation, construction, necessary infrastructure improvements, and necessary equipment. Requires the corporation to consult with the Maryland Stem Cell Research Commission on regenerative medicine items. Creates a special, nonlapsing fund to finance grant awards and administrative expenses.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation; Maryland Stem Cell Research Commission
stakeholders: companies specializing in regenerative medicine and other advanced manufacturing, equipment and service suppliers, and advanced manufacturing small businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2027. General fund administrative expenditures increase by approximately $800,000 in fiscal 2027 only. Beginning in fiscal 2028, pay-as-you-go general fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually to capitalize the fund. No effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, administering, and adopting regulations for the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program and the associated special fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the monies of the newly created Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program Fund, with interest credited to the fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily tasked with accounting for the newly created Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program Fund.

According to the fiscal note, initial PAYGO funding of $3.0 million for the grant program is held within the Department of General Services' appropriation to be transferred into the new special fund in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that TEDCO consult with the Maryland Stem Cell Research Commission on criteria, procedures, and regulations related to regenerative medicine under the program.

Synopsis: Establishing a related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City for the Kappa Alpha Psi 2027 Conclave; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a related event promoter's permit to certain applicants under certain circumstances; and requiring a holder of a State caterer's license to obtain a certain Class C per diem license from the Board before the holder may act as a participating license holder at a related event.

bill_summary: Establishes a related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City for the Kappa Alpha Psi 2027 Conclave. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue the permit to eligible event promoters. Requires applicants to submit applications at least 30 days before the event and obtain written consent from Visit Baltimore. Requires State caterer's license holders to obtain a Class C per diem license before participating. Sets permit fees at $500 or $1,500 depending on venue capacity determined by the Fire Marshal. Authorizes fines between $1,000 and $3,000 or license suspensions for staging unpermitted events.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
stakeholders: event promoters, Baltimore City alcoholic beverages license holders, State caterer's license holders, and attendees of events related to the Kappa Alpha Psi 2027 Conclave
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally in FY 2027 through FY 2028 from application fees ($50) and permit fees ($500 or $1,500). Baltimore City can handle monitoring and enforcement using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes permit requirements and enforcement provisions relating to alcoholic beverages and State caterer's licenses. The Comptroller's responsibilities include the regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry.

Synopsis: Withdrawing and repealing a certain proposed Constitutional amendment relating to temporary appointments to the Commission on Judicial Disabilities; allowing the chair of the Commission to appoint a former member to temporarily fill a certain vacancy on the Commission; and allowing the Governor, on certain request of the chair, to appoint a temporary substitute member or extend the term of an existing member of the Commission.
Title: Judiciary Department - Commission on Judicial Disabilities - Temporary Appointment
Status: Assigned a chapter number, enactment subject to constitutional referendum - Chapter 878

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution authorizing temporary appointments to the Commission on Judicial Disabilities. Authorizes the commission chair to recall a former member upon a member's recusal, disqualification, or term expiration without replacement. Authorizes the chair to request that the Governor appoint a temporary substitute or extend a current member's term. Authorizes the Governor, on the chair's request, to appoint a temporary substitute or extend a current member's term. Prohibits any person rejected by the Senate for commission appointment from serving as a temporary substitute member. Withdraws and repeals Chapters 848 and 849 of the Acts of the General Assembly of 2025.
responsible_party: Commission on Judicial Disabilities; Governor
stakeholders: Members of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities and Maryland state judges
fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances or operations, though the Commission on Judicial Disabilities experiences operational efficiencies if the amendment is approved. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 933 directly empowers the Governor, upon request of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities chair, to appoint temporary substitute members or extend an existing member's term in cases of recusal, disqualification, or term expiration.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state boards and commissions, including potential temporary appointments or term extensions for the Commission on Judicial Disabilities.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judicial Branch. The Commission on Judicial Disabilities oversees disciplinary proceedings and investigations for Maryland judges and coordinates with the Supreme Court of Maryland.

As a proposed constitutional amendment, the measure must be submitted to Maryland voters on the statewide ballot at the November 2026 general election, which is administered and supervised by the State Board of Elections.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a landlord from requiring or requesting from a prospective tenant certain information relating to criminal history and prohibiting a landlord from considering certain information when evaluating the prospective tenant; permitting a landlord to consider certain criminal history information prior to extending a conditional offer to a prospective tenant; and requiring the landlord to consider certain information provided by a prospective tenant relating to a criminal history records check; etc.
